title: Who is in the running for BBC Men's Footballer of the Year?
summary: Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal are shortlisted for the BBC's Men's Footballer of the Year award.
content: [BBC] Voting has closed for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year. Fans from the UK have been voting from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal. The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December. Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate. "Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game. "It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner." The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game. The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales). Read more on the five contenders below. Jude Bellingham Age: 23 Country: England Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament. In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway. That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958. Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player. The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts. Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe [Getty Images] Harry Kane Age: 33 Country: England Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer. His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12. Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions. Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history. Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups. Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015 [Getty Images] Kylian Mbappe Age: 27 Country: France Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history. The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine. Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before. It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament. Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer. He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid. Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots [Getty Images] Rodri Age: 30 Country: Spain Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player. By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane. His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024. Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966. His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14. Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023 [Getty Images] Lamine Yamal Age: 19 Country: Spain Club: Barcelona Position: Forward Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country. Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982. For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession. At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions. He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history. Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024 [Getty Images] Read full terms and conditions and privacy notice The SPOTY Men’s Footballer of the Year

title: Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea: Prediction, betting tips and lineups
summary: Follow our football betting tips as Chelsea travel to Nottingham Forest for some Friday night football
content: Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea tips: A score draw - 7/2 BetVictor Liam Delap to score - 23/10 SpreadEx Chelsea make the trip north to Nottingham Forest tonight, aiming to put the disappointment of back-to-back defeats to Sunderland and Leeds behind them (kick-off 8pm, live on Sky Sports). Xabi Alonso’s side went down 1-0 at the Stadium of Light before they were thrashed 4-1 at home by Leeds last weekend despite taking the lead. That was their fifth Premier League defeat in 11 games, leaving them eighth in the table and five points off the top four. Their opponents tonight have also had a tough start to the season with just two wins so far, which means they are outside the bottom three on goal difference only. One of those wins came against Manchester City a fortnight ago when Liam Delap scored twice to help his side to a shock 3-1 win and ended a five-game winless run. Both managers are under increasing pressure in their new roles, but it is Oliver Glasner, who is the favourite on betting sites to be the next manager to lose his job at 11/8, and he will know that the patience of Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis will only last so long. Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea prediction tips: The only thing we expect is goals The two sides have met 102 times, and Chelsea lead the head-to-head 43 wins to 28. This will only be the 19th meeting in the Premier League, though and in those games the Blues have won just seven to Forest’s five, while the remaining six have been drawn. The strange statistic between these sides is that both have better away records, with Chelsea winning the last three matches at the City Ground, while Forest have won two and drawn two of the last four at Stamford Bridge. Last season, Josh Acheampong, Pedro Neto and Reece James were on target in a 3-0 win at Forest, before Malo Gusto was sent off three minutes before the end. In the return match in the capital in May, Taiwo Awoniyi scored twice to help his side to a 3-1 win, which went a long way to helping preserve their Premier League status. Forest’s last home win against tonight’s opponents came way back in 1997 when Stuart Pearce and the late Chris Bart-Williams scored in a 2-0 win. Based on those stats, it’s a surprise that football betting sites have Forest as the favourites for the win at 8/5, while you can get 9/5 on Chelsea to take all three points. The Blues have scored 20 so far and conceded the same amount, so we expect goals, and you can get 3/4 on over 2.5 goals and 8/13 on both teams to score, but with both teams so out of form, we’re going for a draw. Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea prediction 1: A score draw - 7/2 Bet Victor Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea prediction: Delap to come back to haunt Chelsea After enduring a disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge, striker Liam Delap would love to get one over his former club tonight. The 23-year-old scored just one Premier League goal for the Blues last season, in 18 appearances, and he’s already improved on that number for Forest. He has three goals in nine league starts, including those two against City, and he also has a goal and an assist against Chelsea while at Ipswich. Betting apps are offering 23/10 on him scoring tonight, or you can get 16/1 on him scoring two or more as he did against Enzo Maresca’s side two weeks ago. title: Will The Agit Kabayel Era Begin on Saturday in Dusseldorf?
summary: What to Know WBC World Heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and challenger Nelson Hysa are prepared for their championship fight on Saturday, November 28 in front of 50,000 fans at the Merkur Spiel Arena in Dusseldorf. Kabayel will make the first defense of his title against the lesser-known Albanian challenger, who would be his country’s first […]
content: What to Know WBC World Heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and challenger Nelson Hysa are prepared for their championship fight on Saturday, November 28 in front of 50,000 fans at the Merkur Spiel Arena in Dusseldorf. Kabayel will make the first defense of his title against the lesser-known Albanian challenger, who would be his country’s first boxing world champion if he wins. The fight will air live in the U.S. on DAZN Boxing starting at 1 p.m. ET / 10 a.m. PT in the U.S. and 6 p.m. GMT in the UK. On Saturday, November 28, at the Rudolf Weber Arena in Dusseldorf near Agit Kabayel’s hometown, it will be 11 years to the day that Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury in the same arena. German fans who embraced the Ukrainian Klitschko brothers as their own haven’t had much to cheer since they retired. Now, their hopes have been raised by Germany’s newest champion, WBC World Heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel. Agit Kabayel says Nelson Hysa is a great trash talk, and not much else. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Kabayel would like to change his status as the boxing world’s forgotten heavyweight champion. The native of Bochum is already a star at home. His appearance against Damian Knyba in January sold out the 13.000-seat Rudolf Weber Arena in Oberhausen before an enthusiastic audience. Because of that enthusiastic response, Queensberry Promotions decided to stage Saturday’s fight in a 54,600-capacity arena. Only a handful of fighters can fill that many seats: Canelo Álvarez , Jake Paul, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua, Katie Taylor. And now, Agit Kabayel, with 50,000 tickets sold. According to Kabayel’s opponent, Nelson Hysa of Albania, thousands of those tickets were sold to his devoted Albanian fans. The fight also takes place on Albanian Independence Day. Kabayel’s Quiet Path to the Heavyweight Title Agit Kabayel got the boxing world’s attention with his win over Zhilei Zhang to win the Interim WBC World Heavyweight title in February 2025. Photo: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing Kabayel (26-0, 18 KOs), age 34, became the WBC Interim Heavyweight champion with a win over Zhilei Zhang of China in 2025. He was upgraded to full champion status after unified champion Oleksandr Usyk of Ukraine relinquished his WBC belt in June . Kabayel captured the boxing world’s attention with wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Frank Sanchez. Knowledgeable fans have gravitated to Kabayel, who is Kurdish by heritage. He speaks English, German, and Kurdish fluently. Kabayel had hoped to face Usyk. He joined Usyk in the ring after his knockout win over Rico Verhoeven in Egypt. But it didn’t materialize. With the top ten heavyweights already booked ( Fury vs Joshua , Dubois vs Parker , and a potential Benavidez vs Usyk matchup, Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) Hysa accepted the matchup with Kabayel. Hysa enjoyed a long amateur career and didn’t turn pro until age 37 in 2022, and his resume has no recognizable names. Now at age 42, he is determined to become the first-ever world champion from Albania in any division. “I want only the big fights, but none of the big guys are available,” said Kabayel. “Now I will teach (Hysa) respect. Nelson is my focus now. But after this fight, it’s a unification fight. This is my dream. I want all the belts.” Kabayel called Hysa a better trash talker, but on November 28 they would find out who is the better boxer. Agit Kabayel Proud to Represent German and Kurdish Heritage Agit Kabayel said he’s proud to represent both his German and Kurdish heritage. Photo: Queensberry Promotions “I’m proud to box under the German flag with my Kurdish roots and really happy to do that … It’s all about the unity, and it doesn’t matter what kind of religion. It’s just about the sports, and people know my country, Germany, and know the country where I derive from,” said Kabayel in German at the final pre-fight news conference in Dusseldorf on Thursday. “It will be an unbelievable feeling when I step into the ring, representing both countries. Germany gave me so much. I’m going to give it back. But I have my Kurdish roots, and I am proud to bring that to the world,” said Kabayel. Asked about his plan for the fight, Kabayel was cagey. “I’m well prepared. I’m giving nothing away about my game plan, and my coach is really happy that we don’t do training anymore. My hands are in the ice bucket, so everything is prepared.” Nelson Hysa: “I Love You, Albania!” Nelson Hysa would become Albania’s first world champion in boxing history with a win on Saturday. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Hysa acknowledged Saturday is a big fight both for him and for his country. “He’s a good boxer. He has done very good in boxing, and I’m proud that you support him,” said Hysa to the German fans. “I want to thank my people supporting me from all over the world … Albanians coming to support me. Thank you. I love you, Albania!” Hysa hinted that Kabayel has fragile hands. “I am happy for the coach of Agit that he will not have more problem with hands. But I think Agit will have problem with hands Saturday. “You need to believe, because everything is possible in life and in boxing. I will answer you: Yes, I come to win. I prepare to win, and I will win.” “We are fully prepared, and we hope we will do a good fight. And like you know, I’m every time realistic. So after we will win the match, the other match, the rematch will be in Albania. I will invite all of you to come in Albania to see how beautiful Albania is,” said Hysa. Without a doubt, Kabayel is a clear favorite among oddsmakers. But he said he knows what it’s like to be the person whose chance for success is in doubt. “I was the underdog, an underdog over and over again. Right now I’m the favorite, and there is no pressure. But I’m going to be better and improve from fight to fight. I’m Agit Kabayel. I want to be better in every fight, and I want to be improve, improve that. I want to show that to the people, and there’s no pressure for me. I’m the favorite right now. That’s it. The Kabayel Era: Inspired by Tyson Fury Kabayel declared Saturday will be the beginning of a new era: the Kabayel Era. It’s certainly going to be an era. It’s the new era of Agit Kabayel. I’m going to be the new champion. I’m writing my own chapter. I’m writing new history, and the fight 11 years ago when Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury, it was bad for Germany. “But Tyson Fury kind of inspired me, and now I got the same manager, and this was kind of the starting point, and he inspired me to keep on fighting and to bring it all on the line. It’s all about boxing. We are going to let the fists speak in the ring. It’s not about Albanian people, and it’s not about Kurdish people. It’s all about the two guys in the ring,” said Kabayel. Prediction: Albania Must Wait A Little Longer Observers claim Hysa had an outstanding training camp, running through sparring partners and doing damage. But he lacks mobility and hasn’t demonstrated the punch volume that can fend off Kabayel. Kabayel’s high-volume pressure style is built around relentless body punching and heavy combinations. His sustained bodywork to the ribs and liver wears his opponents down over rounds, rather than relying solely on a single lights-out shot to the head. Expect Kabayel to get right to work against Hysa, breaking him down and draining his spirit. He’s riding a six-fight knockout streak since 2022 and hasn’t gone more than seven rounds. He won’t make it that far against Hysa. We predict a TKO win for Kabayel in rounds five or six. Kabayel vs Hysa Undercard Lineup Four bouts have been set for the undercard at Merkur Spiel-Arena in Dusseldorf, Germany. A cruiserweight matchup features London native Aloys Youmbi (12-1, 9 KOs) facing Germany-based Artur Mann (23-6, 14 KOs) of Kazakhstan. Serbia’s Gleb Bakshi (7-0, 5 KOs) and Germany’s Serhat Parlak (8-1, 3 KOs) square off at middleweight. Germany’s Granit Shala (18-2, 7 KOs) and Iceland’s Kolbeinn Kristinsson (20-0, 14 KOs) clash at heavyweight. Simon Zachenhuber of Erding, Germany (29-2, 18 KOs) vs. Alexander Rigas of Munich (22-3, 10 KOs) in an all-Bayern super middleweight scrap.

title: Eddie Hearn: Tyson Fury backed out of fight week punch machine contest with Anthony Joshua to decide ringwalks
summary: Anthony Joshua came up with a novel idea on how to decide the ringwalk order for their December 11 super fight, but Tyson Fury would not play ball.
content: Eddie Hearn: Tyson Fury backed out of fight week punch machine contest with Anthony Joshua to decide ringwalks originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Anthony Joshua came up with a novel idea on how to decide the ringwalk order for their December 11 super fight, but Tyson Fury would not play ball. Long-time British heavyweight boxing rivals Fury and Joshua will finally meet in the ring next month after more than a decade of circling one another. As has been well documented, negotiations over various aspects – most notably securing the Welsh capital Cardiff as the location – have been fraught. Joshua's promoter and Matchroom Boxing chief Eddie Hearn puts this down to multiple stakeholders being involved in the fight, with Saudi entertainment company Sela providing separate contracts to each fighter where all the terms do not necessarily align. MORE: We now have an official Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua ring walk time for boxing fight Speaking to UK-based reporters on Friday, Hearn explained that the order in which the names of both men appear on the official fight promotional material — global streaming giant Netflix is pushing "Fury vs. AJ" — was not cleared with his team, but is relaxed about what he sees as "fun and games". "In our original contract, the championship prerequisites are to be discussed in good faith," Hearn explained. "When the fight was announced as Fury vs. AJ – which, to be honest, we weren't overly bothered about; I always felt like Netflix would want to do that anyway because of [its documentary series with Fury] and everything — we said thanks for letting us know. Was there any discussion? That's not particularly good faith…. "Before we move forward, can you tell us how all the other things are going to be resolved, particularly the ringwalks." Fury vs. Joshua: Which fighter will ringwalk second? In boxing, there is prestige attached to which fighter enters the ring second. Traditionally, this is the defending champion in a championship fight, or the fighter who is the obviously bigger name – the "a-side" – in a non-title bout. Fury vs. Joshua is complicated because both fighters are huge figures in the sport and they are set to contest the vacant WBA 'Super' title, so neither is champion. Hearn concedes they will probably toss a coin for this after revealing Joshua wanted each man to publicly test their punching power to decide who would walk second. This was written into Joshua's contract, but Fury declined. "And this was agreed with Sela. AJ's request was that there would be, on fight week, a punch machine, and the person that scored the highest punch on the punch machine would walk second," Hearn said. "AJ felt, Netflix felt this would be a great bit of TV. So we told Sela, this is what we'd like to do. They went away and said, 'love it, love it' and they signed the contract that the ringwalk will be determined in that fashion. "So, we were expecting to punch the punch machine on fight week, see who will walk second. We have been told that Tyson Fury is not willing to take part in that, so I guess the alternative for that is probably a coin toss. "But, again, another thing that was put in the contract and now, all of a sudden… oh no, that wasn't put in Tyson Fury's contract; he doesn't want to do that." Matchroom Boxing Hearn: Fury vs. Joshua not in danger over contract disputes An ongoing sore point for Hearn around the fight has been to what extent Dana White's Zuffa Boxing vehicle will be involved in the promotion. Sela is a majority shareholder in Zuffa, with White and Nick Khan's TKO Group owning the remaining 40%. But Zuffa does not have any promotional or management agreement with either Fury or Joshua directly. Hearn revealed that Fury has been undergoing pre-fight drug testing — previously a point of confusion under Sela's dual contract approach – and he insists nothing will derail things now, with the big fight just two weeks away. "Obviously there is still the contractual piece around TKO and Zuffa, that will be fun and games. The ringwalk stuff will work itself out. Ultimately it's a breach from Sela if they can't fulfil the contract. We're not going to pull out of the fight," Hearn said. "But what's in Fury's contract? I wouldn't even be surprised if in Fury's contract he's got that he walks second. Spencer Brown [Fury's manager] tells me a coin toss will be no problem, but who knows? "The gloves will be the gloves, inspected and approved by the British Board of Control. I'm sure there'll be fun and games on fight week, but nothing that's going to affect the fight from happening." MORE: New opponent confirmed for Deontay Wilder after Jai Opetaia backs out of fight on Fury vs. Joshua card Hearn lamented Netflix's lack of expertise when it comes to sports promotion, with plenty of fans complaining about the muted build-up so far. But he insists the huge stakes at play, as a career-defining rivalry approaches a resolution, have also led two charismatic fighters to studiously adopt tunnel vision. "One of the other reasons why you haven't seen people talking a load of s— is I think both guys are working their nuts off," Hearn added. "I know AJ is, because I've seen it first-hand. "And I believe Tyson is as well. I believe he's anxious about losing this fight. I don't believe he thinks he's going to lose it, but I think he really wants to win. I don't think he can be bothered being on Instagram giving it the back and forth because he's focused on winning."

title: Will Alabama continue Iron Bowl win streak vs Auburn? Our score prediction
summary: Here is The Tuscaloosa News' prediction for Alabama vs Auburn, and the storylines to watch Saturday.
content: The Iron Bowl has arrived for Alabama football . The Crimson Tide (9-2, 6-2 SEC) will host Auburn (7-4, 4-4 SEC) at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, hoping to continue an Iron Bowl win streak that started in 2020. No. 5 Alabama will take on Auburn at 6:30 p.m. CT Saturday, Nov. 28, on ABC. Can Alabama secure another Iron Bowl win? Here are the top storylines and an Alabama vs Auburn score prediction. Alabama vs Auburn scouting report Here are the biggest storylines going into Alabama vs. Auburn: Can Keelon Russell shine on Iron Bowl stage? Keelon Russell has faced big stages before, but the Iron Bowl is where the lights shine brightest. Russell's last three games have produced a 9-to-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio after throwing two interceptions against Tennessee. Can Russell, even if he's hobbled by an ankle injury, shine against one of the worst pass defenses statistically in the SEC? Can Alabama football stop Byrum Brown? Alabama knows Byrum Brown better than most, playing him twice when he was South Florida's quarterback. Brown was a dual threat, but stifled. Brown has yet to score a touchdown against the Crimson Tide . But that was two years ago, and Brown has emerged as even more of a threat with the Tigers. Can Alabama's defense continue its defensive mastery against a quarterback who knows what he's getting into? Can Alabama contain Auburn defensive rush? Auburn has one of the most ferocious defensive fronts in the SEC. DJ Durkin's group is second in the league with 81 tackles for loss. Seventeen players have multiple tackles for loss, led by Elijah Melendez and Cody Sigler. Can Alabama's offensive line, a group that has allowed 28 sacks in 11 games, protect Russell and its own backfield? Alabama vs Auburn score prediction Alabama's season always seems to come down to the Iron Bowl. With a three-spot drop in the College Football Playoff rankings, a win against Auburn seems even more imperative to the Crimson Tide's postseason hopes. This Alabama team has the tools to do that with ease: a superstar quarterback, a former in-state five-star receiver waiting to make his mark on the state's biggest rivalry and a defense which has been lights out for weeks. But Auburn has been able to feast off small mistakes, including ones that led to Georgia's only blemish of 2026. From forcing turnovers to consistency moving the ball, Alex Golesh has the recipe for success against the best and brightest college football has to offer. But that is exactly what Alabama expected, which will help the Crimson Tide secure a positive postseason fate Saturday night. Prediction: No. 7 Alabama 28, Auburn 17 Colin Gay covers Alabama football for The Tuscaloosa News, part of the USA TODAY Network. title: Among noise around Indiana football, its focus is on 'hate week,' Purdue
summary: CFP rankings, Big Ten title game scenarios flood the concerns outside the Indiana football walls. Inside? "Bragging rights for the next 364 days."
content: BLOOMINGTON — When Curt Cignetti arrived at Indiana , and a raft of transfers from James Madison and elsewhere followed him through the North End Zone facility doors, sixth-year center Mike Katic took it upon himself to clarify for his new teammates the importance of the Saturday after Thanksgiving. A Hoosier his entire career, Katic grew up in Pennsylvania but spent more than enough time in Bloomington to understand the importance of the Hoosiers ’ rivalry with Purdue . His program might be changing its face. Katic was determined to ensure that importance — of the Old Oaken Bucket game — did not fade from everyone’s collective view. It was with purpose that Katic walked into his postgame press conference, on the night of Indiana ’s historic 66-0 win over Purdue in 2024, smelling like cigar smoke. Even as IU football climbed into unfamiliar levels of atmosphere, its locker room leaders made sure it maintained a healthy relationship with its oldest and most coveted tradition. Since Katic’s departure, other Hoosiers have assumed the responsibility of impressing upon teammates the importance of their primary rivalry game, set to be renewed Nov. 28 in Bloomington. Aiden Fisher shouldered that load in 2025, before passing it off to Indiana’s first-ever national championship generation that season. Even as Indiana has expanded the spaces reserved for its compounding wealth of trophies and honors across the last two years, the oldest prize available remains deeply coveted. “You’re gonna have these bragging rights for the next 364 days,” fifth-year linebacker Isaiah Jones said. “Where’s the Bucket sitting? Is the Bucket in Bloomington, or West Lafayette? We take a lot of pride in that.” Carter Smith sets IU standard in Bucket week This week, the responsibility passed down from Katic to Fisher fell to Carter Smith. Curt Cignetti often chooses a veteran player to speak to the team, based on Cignetti’s assessment of whose leadership deserves it the most, and whose words might resonate the best. Smith did not disappoint. “This is hate week, man,” Smith said, recounting his message. “Whoever is across from you this week, as your competition in practice, they’re wearing black and gold, and you need to beat the crap out of them.” A fifth-year senior left tackle from the Columbus, Ohio, area, Smith is a disappearing species on this Indiana roster: A player who can remember the way it was before the way it has become. He committed to Tom Allen in the afterglow of the Hoosiers’ run to second place in the Big Ten, and the Outback Bowl, in 2020, then stuck with the program despite a three-year dip and a coaching change. Smith only lived two of those years in college, meaning his record against Purdue remains in the balance. He began his IU career twice a loser in the Bucket game. He’s since won it the same number of times. Which makes Saturday particularly important for Smith, and for that fading generation that can recall a time before Indiana owned seemingly too many trophies to count. “There’s a lot of tradition behind the Bucket,” Smith said. “I’m 2-2 against Purdue. I’d like to cap it off with a winning record against them.” Doyel in 2015: 3 men walk into a bar and steal Old Oaken Bucket IU football can play freely, focusing on what it controls What does this weekend mean for Indiana? The latest College Football Playoff top 25 might not lend it much weight. The Hoosiers’ precipitous fall, from No. 8 to No. 14, in this week’s rankings leave Cignetti’s team firmly on the outside looking into the field . Indiana fans will watch with interest games in Iowa City, Madison, Pasadena and Eugene. There are a wide variety of results which could both thin the Big Ten-heavy herd just ahead of IU, and also reopen a path for the Hoosiers to return to the Big Ten title game . If you want the cleanest handicap possible, it’s probably a Minnesota win over Wisconsin (helping IU with its Iowa tiebreaker), and then a UCLA loss against Southern Cal. Cignetti won’t want his players worried about any of that. Not when it needs its best against a Purdue team Cignetti suggested this week has kicked on noticeably from 2025. “Highly improved,” he said. “Wins against Illinois, Minnesota. Beat Minnesota badly, at home, the week after they beat (Michigan). “Got to be ready to go Saturday night at 7 (p.m.) and play well. That’s the focus.” From a playoff perspective, it’s also all Indiana can do. The Hoosiers cannot control those other results. They can only to an extent affect the committee’s opinion of them. That means winning Saturday, and winning well, and letting go of everything they can’t control. Bucket game part of longstanding IU football culture In the most basic sense, though, that fades when the sun comes up Sunday morning. Whether Indiana makes the Big Ten title game or doesn’t, whether Indiana makes the College Football Playoff or doesn’t, the calendar will reset eventually. Rosters will turn over, players will graduate or move on, 2026 will become 2027, and 2027, eventually, 2028. The cigar Katic enjoyed that night two years ago represented the importance of something that does not fade with dates. That does not reset. It was important for Katic to relate to his teammates then the stakes of this game to Indiana, because it would not just outlive him, or them, but every single player before, around and after them. Indiana and Purdue first played football in 1891, the same year Carnegie Hall opened, and James Naismith officially introduced a sport he’d invented called basketball. The Old Oaken Bucket was first put on the line in 1925, only 60 years after the ending of the Civil War. History: What is the Old Oaken Bucket? Who leads rivalry series between Purdue, Indiana? In the 101 years since, it’s traded hands dozens of times. It’s been stolen, beaten, borrowed and kissed. It’s seen highs and lows on both sides of the rivalry, Rose Bowls and hard times. Most recently, it’s witnessed the historic rise of a program once associated only with failure, now become college football’s inescapable phenomenon. The one constant? The one Saturday a year when all that matters is cream and crimson against black and gold, as an entire state stops to watch. That’s what Katic intended to preserve with the one year he had to do it. And that’s what he’s handed down now to players like Smith and Jones, young men who recognize that, no matter what else happens this season, one of their final jobs as Hoosiers is to make sure the generation that follows them understands. title: Arkansas Offense Faces A Top-Five Defense In Friday Clash
summary: LSU's defense ranks in the top five nationally while Arkansas struggles to score. The Razorbacks face a tough test against Blake Baker's unit on Friday.
content: Nov 15, 2025; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers cheerleaders perform during a time out against the Arkansas Razorbacks during the second half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The Arkansas offense looks lost, and LSU’s defense is ready to punish them for it. Saturday’s matchup in Fayetteville features a team that can barely move the ball against one of the best units in the country. The Razorbacks average just 19.7 points per game, which ranks 124th among teams in the nation. They struggle to gain ground, averaging only 341 total yards per game. That puts them at 108th nationally. Their passing game moves the ball better than the run game, but even that ranks a weak 70th, at 224 yards per contest. The rushing attack is a disaster, mustering only 117 yards per game, which sits at 120th. It is a clear mismatch that favors the Tigers in every way. Blake Baker’s Defensive Legacy LSU coach Blake Baker has built something special, even if some fans do not see it yet. As the season winds down, potential head coaching opportunities swirl around his name. While critics have been harsh, the numbers tell a different story about his work. If Baker leaves, he walks away from a defense that ranks in the top five nationally. That is a massive achievement for a unit that has carried the entire team all year. The Tigers have nothing left to play for but pride, and they will use that to wear Arkansas out. A dominant season can be capped with an exclamation point by the defense in this game. The sideline may see Baker in purple and gold for the last time during this final SEC matchup. Nov 15, 2025; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Dashawn Spears (10) reacts to sacking Arkansas Razorbacks quarterback Taylen Green (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Stopping the Key Players The Tigers must keep quarterback KJ Jackson and wide receiver Chris Marshall in check to win. AJ Hill was initially considered the starter before Jackson assumed the starting role. He has 2,231 passing yards this year, much of it coming from his connection with Marshall. Marshall is a former five-star recruit who finally has the success he deserves. He had back-to-back games of over 130 receiving yards, including a 136-yard effort against Georgia. The next week he destroyed Tulsa with nine catches for 195 yards and one touchdown. Arkansas allows 27 sacks this season, and LSU’s front will attack that weakness. The secondary should handle the pass coverage easily against a team that completes only 58 percent of its throws. This is a game where the Tigers should dominate from start to finish.

title: Will Auburn football pull off Iron Bowl upset at Alabama? Score prediction
summary: Will Auburn football do the unthinkable and upset Alabama and Georgia in the same season? See our score prediction for the Iron Bowl to find out.
content: It's quite a thing to fathom. Even if Auburn football opened as just over a two-touchdown underdog, a victory in the upcoming Iron Bowl would give it wins over its biggest rivals for the first time in nine seasons. Auburn last beat Georgia and Alabama in the same season during a 10-win campaign in 2017. Prior to that, the two latest happenings came in 2010 and 2013, both instances in which it played for a national championship. In this instance, Auburn is searching for its eighth win, though that's something the program can celebrate. It has already notched its largest win total since 2019, and after upsetting top-ranked Georgia in Athens last month, Auburn has a chance to deliver something similar to the fifth-ranked Crimson Tide on Saturday, Nov. 28 ( 6:30 p.m. CT, ABC ), at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa. Here's a deeper dive into Saturday's contest, including analysis and a score prediction. Our expert analysis, breakdown of Auburn football vs Alabama DJ Durkin and Auburn's defense will absolutely have its challenges containing Keelon Russell and a high-powered offense, but the Alabama defense could present a slew of problems for Auburn's offense. It is the Iron Bowl however, and happenings beyond logic could always rear their head, but the Crimson Tide look like a bonafide competitor this fall. Auburn's had high points throughout Year 1 under Alex Golesh, but an inaugural Iron Bowl in Tuscaloosa feels like too mighty an undertaking — even if that was the belief heading into Athens weeks ago. Auburn football vs Alabama scouting report: What we're watching Will Auburn be able to establish the run in Tuscaloosa? Alabama boasts a top-10 rushing defense, which is tops in the SEC. It'd be swell to get a high-impact performance from Jeremiah Cobb or Omar Mabson II, but will Byrum Brown even be effective? Does Byrum Brown play clean against Alabama defense? After throwing as many interceptions (7) as touchdowns in his first five games, Brown's TD-to-INT ratio is 8 to 1 in the six games since. Alabama leads the SEC with 13 interceptions, along with a nation-leading five defensive touchdowns. Can Auburn deliver on crucial downs against Crimson Tide? Defensive coordinator Kane Wommack's unit has clearly shined all season, as Alabama's also top-15 national in first and third down defense, both circumstances that have been problem spots for the Tigers. Our Iron Bowl score prediction for Auburn football vs Alabama Final score: No. 5 Alabama 51, Auburn 35 Expect Golesh to keep it competitive, as his teams have in three of the last four meetings, but if Alabama is anything up to its billing, it should be able to break away from Auburn late. LSU and Ole Miss, both boasting deeper talents, found their opportunities. Expect the Crimson Tide to find it eventually. Adam Cole is the Auburn athletics beat writer for the Montgomery Advertiser. title: When it comes to the national championship, why not the Utes?
summary: As the last unbeaten team in the country, and a handful of the usual suspects already with multiple losses, could this be the Utes’ year to win it all?
content: Utah running back Wayshawn Parker celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half of an NCAA college football game against Iowa State, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Ames, Iowa. | Charlie Neibergall With Utah gathering itself for the homestretch of the season, someone might as well say it: How could it look any better than this? The road to a national championship, that is. The table is set. Everything has fallen their way (another way to say it: Don’t blow this). To wit: The Utes have done their part, which is to say, win. They’re the last unbeaten team left in the country. Eleven and oh. They’ve won 17 consecutive games dating back to last season. One by one, their chief rivals have fallen, pushing the Utes closer and closer to the top of the rankings — now No. 2 for three consecutive weeks. It’s difficult to remember a year in which the top teams have (rather conveniently) lost so many games. Five of the AP Top 25 teams have four losses, including mighty Ohio State. Five more of the ranked teams have three losses. Talk about opening the door for everyone else. The Utes are a lock for a playoff spot, even if they were to lose one of their next two games. The national playoff expanded from four to 12 teams in 2024, so the Utes have room to spare a loss and won’t be left on the outside. There will be no repeat of what happened in 2008, when the 12-0 Utes got shut out of the championship game, which featured No. 1 Florida and No. 2 Oklahoma. Both were ranked ahead of the Utes despite having one loss apiece. The Utes went on to crush Alabama 31-17 in the consolation prize/Sugar Bowl to finish 13-0 and were No. 2 in the final rankings. In other words, they got robbed of a national title shot. It was a repeat of what occurred in 2004, when the Utes finished the regular season with an unbeaten record of 12-0. They were one of five teams with an unbeaten record at the end of the regular season. No. 1 USC and No. 2 Oklahoma — the Rockefellers of college football — played for the national championship. Utah was banished to the Fiesta Bowl and an inferior opponent — three-loss Pitt. The Utes won 35-7 to finish the season with a 12-0 record and a No. 4 ranking without ever being able to play for the national title. It wasn’t until 2024 that the avenues to the playoffs were realistically available to teams from the West. All that has changed, to say the least. Next season, the playoff field doubles to 24. If the Utes win Friday night’s game against lowly, but unpredictable, West Virginia, then win the Big 12 championship game on Dec. 4, they will finish the regular season with an unbeaten record for the third time in 22 years. This time, they will be enabled to play in the postseason until they lose. There might never be a better opportunity for the Utes, who have never won a national championship — or played for one, for that matter — and absolutely no one saw this coming. They weren’t even picked as a contender to win the Big 12 Conference. Texas Tech was the favorite and BYU and Houston were considered the top challengers. Which was understandable. Utah had lost many key players from the 2025 team, including their entire offensive line, to graduation or the NFL, and their top defensive players and top receiver, not to mention six coaches (including head coach Kyle Whittingham) to Michigan. The Utes had to start over with a new coaching staff and a revamped lineup, but you’d never know it. Quarterback Devon Dampier — 2,535 yards and 24 touchdowns passing, 644 yards and 11 TDs rushing — has played his way into an invitation to the Heisman ceremony with his running and passing. Wayshawn Parker has 1,034 scrimmage yards and 13 TDs, despite playing only two downs the last two games due to injury. The defense is physical and has a knack for big plays. The Utes are outscoring opponents 37.9 to 18.5. They are averaging nearly 7 yards per play. They are winning on the road and at home, they are winning high-scoring games and low-scoring defensive battles. The Utes are the real deal. Unlike most seasons, there is no clear powerhouse favorite out there — several teams have a realistic chance to win the national championship. Why not the Utes? Utah Utes head coach Morgan Scalley puts up a “U” after the Utah Utes won against the BYU Cougars in a football game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News

title: Commute: Mizzou legacy to visit this weekend
summary: The Morning Commute for Friday, November 27th, 2026.
content: Hey, did you know Justin Smith has a kid who is a 5-star defensive lineman? Wyatt Smith, a 5-star rated, consensus top 100 player in the country, is visiting Missouri this weekend. He’s a 6’6, 235 lb edge rusher who has been committed to Ohio State since May 17. NEW: Missouri is making a massive push in the 2027 cycle — and the No. 1 edge rusher in the country just scheduled an official visit to Columbia this weekend. Five-star Wyatt Smith is a verbal to Ohio State, but the Tigers aren't done. His dad played there. Drinkwitz never… pic.twitter.com/VKkZD8yMoB — Steve Wiltfong (@SWiltfong_) November 24, 2026 The connection is his dad is former Mizzou All-American Justin Smith. Smith was awesome as a Tiger and drafted in the 2001 NFL draft by the Cincinnati Bengals with the 4th overall pick. It’s not often Missouri has a chance to flip an Ohio State commitment, but you’d have to think the legacy aspect at least has some play with the family. CBS Sports analyst Tom Loy talked about this topic and seemed to imply the family, and Smith might just feel more comfortable with the future with Eli Drinkwitz at Missouri. Obviously this would be a huge get, especially coming off the heels of flipping former Florida State commit and 4-star running back Jayden Miles . Here’s some info on that from Sammy’s post yesterday: Mizzou continues to stockpile talent at the running back position as Miles is ranked as one of the top RBs in the state of Louisiana. Along with Florida State, Miles has plenty of power conference offers — including Ohio State, LSU, Arkansas, and Kentucky. Miles becomes the 19th overall addition to Mizzou’s 2027 recruiting class — and there’s potential for more commitment flips in the near future so stay tuned. Reportedly, LSU thought they were going to keep Miles in state. But perhaps some recruits are looking for a bit more stability than what can be offered in Baton Rouge and Columbus these days? Yesterday at Rock M and Rock M+ Thanksgiving means a quiet news day. But we still put out some content. You already saw the recruiting news, Matthew Gustafson previewed the game tomorrow , and just what the Tigers might face : The Sooners are averaging roughly five more points per game under Witten. As Drinkwitz alluded to, much of that improvement can be credited to their ground game. OU averaged just under 105 yards per game and an average of merely 3.09 yards per carry during conference play during its 2-3 start to conference play. Those numbers have jumped to more than 161 yards per game and 3.84 yards per carry under Witten. And much of that improvement can be seen directly in the Sooners’ signal caller. Mateer will give the ball away if you let him. But he’s still a capable QB, and of course the OU defense is stout. Force some turnovers and convert in the Red Zone and you should be able to pull out a win at home. Jaden took a look at who is rising and falling after last weeks win over Kentucky, and he can’t stop talking about Santana Banner : The case can be made that Banner was the team’s defensive MVP on Saturday with a handful of memorable plays : A PBU in the end zone on Willie Rodriguez. UK eventually settled for three, instead of scoring 7. An open-field TFL, resulting in a loss of two. On the following play, Sione Laulea intercepted Kenny Minchey. A game-sealing interception with UK driving down the field. On top of that, Banner finished with 12 tackles, a team-high. It earned him both the Walter Camp Football National Player of the Week and the Thorpe Award National DB of the Week honors. Banner has been a really nice surprise this year, not just as an on the field player but his leadership off the field has been top notch. And with 5 in 5 he could come back for another season. title: Ex-Colorado State AD, former players raise alarm over Jim Mora and staff conduct
summary: Former Colorado State players have sent a letter to the university's governing board to address concerns about Jim Mora and his coaching staff.
content: Things appear to continue to get messier for Jim Mora at Colorado State. According to The Coloradan — part of the USA TODAY Network — nearly two dozen former Colorado State players are asking the university’s governing board to address concerns in what they describe as "inappropriate behaviors" from Mora and his staff and "the lack of response by athletic department leadership." Mora is in his first season at Colorado State after being hired from UConn last offseason. Week 13 bold predictions: Rivalry weekend could wreck some playoff dreams The Colorado State players who wrote and sent the letter to the Colorado State University System Board of Governors on Nov. 25 include former Rams quarterback and athletic director Jack Graham, former defensive back Erik Olson and former linebacker Nate Kvamme. The letter does not specifically ask the Colorado State University System Board of Governors to fire Mora or Colorado State athletic director John Weber, but brings forth their worry about the "welfare of the student athletes" in the program. "As former CSU football players, we want to convey a sense of urgency and resolve to support the University in rebuilding the integrity, culture and reputation of the Athletic Department and our football program," the letter reads. "Our experiences at CSU delivered great lessons and guidance for our adult lives. "We learned to compete and win. We had support to study and succeed in our academic careers. We were given the opportunity to be part of teams that represented commitment, hard work, integrity, respect and pride. We left CSU as better people." Graham additionally brought up several "red flag" incidents that he believes are egregious enough for Colorado State to fire Mora "for cause" under the terms of the five-year contract they signed him to last December. These "red flags" include: the program’s entire equipment room staff reportedly quitting at the beginning of the season or late spring due to "abusive behavior toward them by Jim Mora," damage allegedly done to the visitors’ locker room following a loss at Texas State on Oct. 25, not believing Mora's side of the story on the firing of former Rams defensive coordinator Tyson Summers in the middle of a game against Oregon State on Oct. 3 and a physical altercation between strength and conditioning coach Shelton Bynum and offensive lineman Toriyan Johnson amongst others. REQYIRED READING: Pac-12 flex week is set: Who will Boise State, others play? "Is the University providing the culture, leadership, support and resources these athletes need to be good human beings, strong competitors and lifelong proud alumnae of CSU?," the letter reads. "... We believe not; rather, they are seeing the antithesis of these critical values." Under Mora this season, the Rams have the No.4 scoring offense in the Pac-12 at 33.7 points per game, but one of the worst defenses in the conference and country. The Rams rank dead last in the Pac-12 in both scoring defense at 47.7 points per game and total defense at 548.1 total yards allowed per game. The Rams have won just once in their last nine games and have lost each of their last four games. In their four-game losing skid, Colorado State has been outscored by opponents 217-101. Colorado State ends its regular season at 6 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 28 against No. 21 Boise State . title: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Iowa
summary: Nebraska concludes the season with the Black Friday finale with Iowa. Both teams enter the matchup looking to end the regular season on a high note.
content: Nebraska concludes the regular season with its annual Black Friday finale against the Iowa Hawkeyes . Both teams enter the matchup fresh off a crucial win and now look to end the regular season with just one more. For the No. 25 Huskers, a win would earn them their first eight-win season since 2016 and could help them finish the year in the top 25. For the No. 13 Hawkeyes, a win would provide them a chance to compete in both the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. But while this top-25 matchup presents opportunities for both sides, Nebraska’s still facing an uphill battle. Though they picked up a win over then-No. 14 Ohio State , the Huskers jumped on a few Buckeye slip-ups and had Memorial Stadium behind them. Now they head to Iowa City, where the Hawkeyes have remained dominant. Iowa’s only loss as a home team this season came to Ohio State 31-14 in early October. Though Nebraska just came off a win over the Buckeyes, it’s safe to say a lot has changed since the Hawkeyes faced them. Plus, Iowa’s got a lot of momentum coming into this contest. Iowa’s won its last four games, averaging 29 points and allowing less than nine points in that stretch. The Hawkeyes’ last win especially provided momentum. Iowa derailed Illinois 34-17 last week, shutting out the Fighting Illini in the second half, 17-0. Despite allowing over 300 passing yards on just 21 completions, the Hawkeyes generated two interceptions, including a pick-six. Iowa also suffocated Illinois’ run game, holding it to just 28 yards on 17 carries. Plus, Katin Houser did throw the ball 39 times, so the Hawkeyes’ defense overall played well. This is the brick wall Nebraska’s offense is dealing with. Though the Huskers scored 31 points against the Buckeyes, Iowa isn’t likely allowing that many points. But even if Nebraska finds success on offense, its defense is also in for a tough game. The Hawkeyes ran the ball 52 times for 263 yards and three touchdowns against Illinois and held possession of the ball for over 37 minutes. Iowa’s Hank Brown also threw 13-of-26 for 138 yards and ran for 32 yards and a touchdown on eight carries. The Blackshirts allowed Ohio State to score 28 points and Jeremiah Smith to rip them apart. Though it generated two turnovers, those did just enough to get the win. Now, they get a well-spread Iowa group that rarely coughs up the ball. The win over the Buckeyes was big for Nebraska. But the Hawkeyes aren't a team that’s going to let a historic opportunity slip through their fingers. Unless the Huskers play perfectly in all three phases or catch a few breaks, Iowa’s bound to win this. title: Florida State takes different path with Glenn Schumann hire. Who can blame 'em?
summary: For as long as anyone can remember, new FSU football coaches brought along a background on offense. That changed with the hiring of Glenn Schumann.
content: “And now for something completely different …” That is so much more fitting than you could possibly imagine on this first day of your new diet. First, let’s try to digest some history. Dating back to the 1960s and Florida State ’s first extended run of quality football — utilizing Bill Peterson’s revolutionary (for the time) offensive schemes — Seminole coaching hires have been almost entirely offense-minded men, usually former quarterbacks and/or offensive coordinators (Bobby Bowden, Willie Taggart and Jimbo Fisher among them). Mike Norvell was a former receiver and offensive coordinator, as well as a successful head coach at Memphis. He was also once a successful head coach at FSU. Remember? Where were we? Back to that opening line, borrowed from the long-ago and quite brilliant Monty Python’s Flying Circus. How fitting is it? Well, try this … New FSU leadership has charted a new course for its coaching search, and for something completely different, they’ve hired a defensive coordinator who, though just 36, has been on the staff of a combined six national champs with Alabama and Georgia . Leaning defensively worked out for Georgia since they hired Kirby Smart, you may have noticed. And FSU has now hired Smart’s defensive coordinator, Glenn Schumann. Not sure if finances played a big role, but he’ll surely come a tad cheaper than an established head coach from elsewhere (think Taggart and Norvell). Schumann: By the Numbers #NoleFamily pic.twitter.com/iK1ZHA3xC7 — FSU Football (@FSUFootball) November 24, 2026 Another “completely different” facet: Schumann didn’t play football beyond high school. No big deal, actually. Quite a few successful coaches never played college ball — Mike Leach, David Cutcliffe and Sonny Dykes among them. But Schumann was born in Georgia’s football cradle, Valdosta, which means his baptismal font was likely a Gatorade cooler. His dad, Eric, was a longtime college assistant (yes, on defense) and his mom, Sherry, was a small-college athletic director. He has soaked in college athletics since birth. And finally, there’s Schumann’s family connection to FSU, which takes us back, again, to today’s opening line. Jack Haskin, Schumann’s maternal grandfather, was the first-ever assistant football coach in school history, serving on the small staff of FSU’s inaugural football team in 1947. Jack was also a physical education instructor at FSU and had a longtime infatuation with acrobatics, gymnastics, juggling and the like. The same year he joined FSU’s first football staff, he also founded the school’s renowned Flying High Circus, now in its 80th year. Jack was inducted into FSU’s athletics hall of fame in 1979. So the current Seminoles have hired a guy who never played serious football, and whose school roots trace to the Big Top. It’s tempting to say it’s fitting by suggesting the football program has been a bit of a circus recently. But that’s not true. Circuses are entertaining. Special night at the FSU Flying High Circus. Great Halloween performances by some amazing @floridastate students. 🍢 #FlyingHighCircus pic.twitter.com/vdj4uBWh6d — Michael Alford (@M_Alford11) October 23, 2022 Rank & File Weekly ranking of Florida’s seven big-league football programs, based on results versus expectations, current trends, and in some cases, the ability to ignore those current trends. 1. Miami (10-1). Last week: (1) Beat Virginia Tech, 28-20. This week: Boston College at home. FYI: Assuming the Hurricanes don’t step on a rake this week, they’d likely clinch an eventual playoff berth even if they lose to Wake Forest in the ACC title game. Occasionally, BC brings along a rake, but it’ll take the whole garden shed this week. The pick: ’Canes 34, Eagles 20. 2. Florida Gators (7-4). Last week: (2) Beat Vanderbilt, 34-27. This week: at Florida State, Friday. FYI : Head Gator Jon Sumrall was literally quoting Van Morrison after the Vandy squeaker. The topic was mediocrity, fittingly. Where do you draw that mediocrity line? Not sure, but it might be between 7-5 and 8-4. The pick : Gators 19, Seminoles 12. 3. FAU Owls (7-4). Last week: (4) Beat USF, 35-14. This week: at East Carolina. FYI: Owls are notoriously territorial about their homes, whether it’s the cavity in a tree limb, an underground burrow, or some cast-aside nest once belonging to a hawk. However, these Owls just completed their first-ever undefeated home slate (6-0), dating back to their 2001 debut. The pick: Pirates 23, Empty-nesters 20. 4. UCF Knights (6-5). Last week: (6) Beat Iowa State, 48-17. This week: at Colorado. FYI : How do you handicap a matchup of teams that refuse to forge an identity? Well, OK, there’s this: Colorado’s two home losses were against really good teams (Texas Tech, Utah), and this ain’t that. The pick: Buffaloes 27, Knights 20. 5. FSU Seminoles (5-6). Last week: (3) Lost to N.C. State, 28-10. This week: Florida at home, Friday. FYI : 6-6 looks better than 5-7, but 6-6 could become a 6-7 with a loss in a fourth-tier bowl game no one will watch. End this and move on. The pick: Still have the Gators, 19-12. Rivalry Week. 🆚 Florida State ⏰ 3:30 PM ET 📺 ABC 🏟️ Doak Campbell Stadium pic.twitter.com/XnWYCn9xjJ — Florida Gators Football (@GatorsFB) November 23, 2026 6. USF Bulls (6-5). Last week: (5) Lost to FAU, 35-14. This week: Tulane at home. FYI: The Bulls entered November 6-2 and perhaps to assuage the autumnal gods, offensive coordinator Tim Beck was fired this week. Oh, my bad … he and the program “agreed to part ways.” Last game at Raymond James, by the way. The new campus ballpark opens next fall. The pick : Bulls 26, Green Wave 20. 7. FIU Panthers (4-7). Last week: (7) Lost to Kennesaw State, 35-24. This week: Sam Houston at home. FYI : I’m glad Sam Houston ain’t here to see this. Just two years ago, his Bearkats were 10-3 with a bowl win. They’re 3-20 since. Why Bearkats with a K? Long story and not really a good one. The pick: Panthers 38, ’Kats 16. Other picks Man, what a downer. So many of those ancient rivalries on this weekend’s slate, and nary a one with a pair of evenly matched foes battling for something important. Except for those delicious possibilities of upsetting highly ranked rivals and ruining their postseason plans. Can you hear us, Aggies? How about you Tuscaloosa-bound Tigers? Wait, hold the phone. What’s this? At the Rose Bowl of all places? That’s right, for the first time in ages, there’s importance hanging on the USC-UCLA game. Forget that it’s laughably a “battle of Big Ten rivals” and hear me out. UCLA is clinging to its playoff hopes while Southern Cal is hoping to give that fickle playoff committee something to think about. It seems to hinge on a hinge — UCLA’s quarterback was stretchered from the field last week with a hip injury, so ... Trojans 30, Bruins 23. ELSEWHERE: Texas over the Aggies; Dawgs big over Tech; ’Bama probably beats Auburn, but there’s a brain worm suggesting trouble; Indiana takes it out on Purdue; Tennessee handles Vandy; Wake by 12 over Duke; Louisville over reeling Kentucky; Clemson beats S. Carolina in OT; Irish comfortably over Syracuse; Belichick beats N.C. State; Michigan upsets Ohio State; and the Hampden-Sydney Tigers, at home in the middle of Virginia, over the Mariners of the Merchant Marine Academy. Little slice of central Virginia heaven HSC is all all dudes school “D3 Hampden-Sydney College beats rival Randolph-Macon for the first time since 2013 to clinch the ODAC title!” pic.twitter.com/RgiJI2zPFw — Quarter Zip Sports (@TheQuarterZip) November 15, 2026 BTW: Hampden-Sydney College is in unincorporated Hampden Sydney and I know what you’re thinking: “Why the hyphen discrepancy?” In the late 19th century, the U.S. Postal Service, for some good reason (maybe), dropped all punctuation from official town names. While many towns kept using the hyphen on signage (both Wilbur and Carmel-by-the-Sea, among other hot spots), Hampden Sydney, which was actually platted after the college and named after it, apparently didn’t miss its hyphen. Saves on paint, you know. BTW II: Great Americans Patrick Henry and James Madison were among the school’s founders in the 1770s, and to further agitate the lording Brits, they named it after a pair of earlier anti-royalist English statesmen. History also labels John Hampden and Algernon Sydney as martyrs, but you probably assumed that. title: 'Football 101' gives OSU international students a crash course on America's sport
summary: Football 101, an event was hosted by Ohio State's Office of International Affairs, gives foreign students a crash course on college football.
content: With her graduation date on the horizon, Mengxi Sun decided that she needed to watch at least one Ohio State football game. Sun – an Ohio State senior from Wuhan, China, majoring in city and regional planning – came to the U.S. to get a well-rounded college education, not necessarily to spend Saturdays at the Shoe. But after years of watching her friends go all out for game day, she decided to see what American football was all about. So Sun and a dozen other international students attended a Football 101 watch party back in October to learn the ins and outs of Buckeyes football and game day traditions. The event was hosted by Ohio State's Office of International Affairs to give foreign students a crash course on college football. Caroline Omolesky, assistant director of global engagement at Ohio State, said a lot of international students are excited to learn about football and experience the game day atmosphere when they arrive in Columbus. "Even if they don't grasp the finer details of what's happening on the field," Omolesky said. An estimated 1.17 million international students were enrolled at U.S. colleges and universities this academic year. Ohio State alone enrolled 5,234 students from more than 100 different countries. It's been a challenging time for some international students studying in the U.S. as the Trump administration has tightened visa policies and travel restrictions. Earlier this year, the Trump administration finalized a new rule limiting foreign students to four-year stays. But game day is a quintessentially American college experience, something that can bring people together across state lines and international borders to cheer on their teams. "American football is really special," Sun said. "It's not just about football, but also about socializing." The Football 101 watch party included student leaders to help explain the rules and traditions during the game. Football is unlike many other sports in its complexity. The difference between a "first down" and "touchdown" isn't inherently clear to the novice. Paul Kuteyi remembers what it's like to be new to football. Kuteyi, an Ohio State junior finance major, was born in Nigeria and lived in London and other U.S. cities before moving to Columbus about eight years ago. He wasn't always big on football, but he got hooked after watching former Alabama head coach Nick Saban take the Crimson Tide to the College Football Playoff National Championship in 2016. His friends taught him the rules and he's been a fan ever since. When he enrolled at Ohio State, Kuteyi said he saw a student job posting at the Office of International Affairs and offered to lead the Football 101 watch party. "These students are getting thrown into football culture, and I thought no one would be better to teach them than someone who has also experienced it," Kuteyi said. This year's watch party was during an away game against the Iowa Hawkeyes. Students from China, India, France, Denmark and Spain attended, as well as a few scholars from Brazil. Outside of the U.S., Brazil is the NFL's second-largest international market behind Mexico. Kuteyi pulled up a few YouTube videos to give attendees a quick run through of the rules. Then he answered questions as they came up once the game started. The biggest questions? What's up with all of the lines on the field? Which lines are real, and which ones are just on the TV broadcast? And why are they changing? Kuteyi has perfected his simple explanation for watching American football: You have to get the ball to the yellow line in four tries. Sun said that explanation helped her a lot. Before the watch party, she thought American football was more like soccer and that the ball moved more freely between the teams. The number of strict rules surprised her, she said. "If I watched this by myself, I wouldn't know what's going on," she said. Sun said she was happy to learn about end zones and touchdowns, but she also enjoyed learning about the social side of football. Football isn't just about the game, she said. It's a full day of Skull Sessions, tailgates, stadium traditions and after parties. Back home in Wuhan, Sun said people are passionate about sports like table tennis and badminton, but nothing compares to the all-encompassing game day atmosphere. Kuteyi agreed. Having lived in London for a while, he said American football fandoms feel different than European soccer clubs. Where you can have multiple different fan bases in a single European city, Kuteyi said football fans in America rally for the home team. "If you're in Columbus, chances are you're a Buckeyes fan," he said. Kuteyi always encourages international students to find a connection between American football and their home countries, often finding a player they can root for. But more than anything, Kuteyi said he tells students to go to a game in person. Even if you don't care about what's happening on the field, he said, there's always something to enjoy. Sun said she plans to move home to China after graduating in December and take some time off before applying to master's programs in the U.S. She'd love to come back to America, this time with a little more knowledge about football. "Maybe I will even attend a tailgate," Sun said. Higher education reporter Sheridan Hendrix can be reached at shendrix@dispatch.com and on Signal at @sheridan.120. You can follow her on Instagram at @sheridanwrites. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: 'Football 101' gives OSU international students a crash course on America's sport

title: Georgia vs Georgia Tech predictions, odds for Week 13 college football game

content: Georgia football’ s rivalry with Georgia Tech has been decided by 7, 2 and 8 points the last three games with one of those matchups going to eight overtimes. Things look quite different this year for Saturday's game in Athens. Georgia is ranked No. 1 and its defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann was just plucked by Florida State to be its head coach. He’s still with the team coaching. Georgia Tech fired four assistant coaches Nov. 9 during a 3-8 season. Athletic director Ryan Alpert in a message to fans wrote last week: "Quite simply, the results this season have not met the standard that we have come to expect for Georgia Tech football, nor have they matched the investments that the Institute and our supporters have made in the program. …We have to do better to meet the standard of excellence that is reflected across our world-class Institute.” Georgia coach Kirby Smart said he still expects a battle. “The physicality in this game's unmatched,” he said. “I think that's what you look for in a rivalry game. You look over the history of the last three, four, five years, it's really been one of the most physical games we've played. They're physical at the point of attack. They believe in running the ball just like we do, so both teams are built very similarly in terms of the culture and the way they want to strike people and block people.” Georgia vs. Georgia Tech odds, money line, over/under Odds courtesy of BetMGM as of Wednesday, Nov. 25. title: Can Iowa make the CFP? Media reactions to Hawkeyes' statement vs. Nebraska

It sets the stage for the 13th-ranked Hawkeyes to potentially qualify for the 2026 Big Ten championship game. Many around the nation think it was enough of a statement from the Hawkeyes to earn a College Football Playoff berth whether Iowa reaches the Big Ten Championship Game or not. Iowa quarterback Hank Brown had a sensational performance against the Cornhuskers , scoring three rushing touchdowns and finishing with four total touchdowns on a 13-for-18 passing day. Tight end DJ Vonnahme led the team in receiving yards, reeling in three grabs for 61 yards and a score. LJ Phillips Jr. finished with 76 rushing yards on 14 carries. Defensively, Phil Parker's unit stiffled the Cornhuskers, forcing two fumbles and one interception. Iowa limited Nebraska to 260 yards of offense. The Hawkeyes shut out the Huskers in the second half, marking the sixth time this season that Iowa has posted a second-half shutout. title: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year
summary: After a nine-year hiatus, the Missouri State Media Player of the Year award has returned. Jared 'Bird' Lloyd has earned the honor after an historic season.
content: SPRINGFIELD — The Missouri State Media Player of the Year award has returned. Linebacker Jared "Bird" Lloyd was named the 2026 Media Player of the Year on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The Media Player of the Year award had been given to the top Bears player from 1982-2017 and was revived in 2026. “This means a lot. I really appreciate you guys covering me and I’m very appreciative of you guys just getting my name out there more,” Lloyd said. “You guys reporting on me, doesn’t just help me. It helps my teammates, it helps the university and it helps the football program.” Missouri State football: Bears snag its top in-state recruit in the program's history Entering the final game of the season, Lloyd leads the nation with 127 total tackles. He also ranks No. 1 in tackles per game with 11.55. This is the best season by a Missouri State player since 2016, when Dylan Cole set the mark. This is the third-most tackles in a single Missouri State season since 2004. Lloyd also has two sacks, one forced fumble and three pass deflections. The Daytona Beach, Florida, native will finish his career with more than 275 tackles in his five seasons in Springfield. “Bird will go down in history as one of the most important players in Missouri State football history, shepherding this team into the FBS era. He has been one of the best tacklers in college football in 2026,” the News-Leader's Liam Keating said in a press release. “Instead of competing for individual accolades, he's always been a team-first player. This is what makes him a special player and worthy of the first media-given award in almost a decade.” Lloyd is the seventh linebacker to win the award. Ken Braden (1986), Matt Soraghan (’87), James Turnage (’88), DeLaun Fowler (’94-95), P.J. Jones (’01) and Cole (’15-16) were named winners. Missouri State: How star Kaemyn Bekemeier has mastered the NIL era "There's something satisfying about seeing the fruits of one's labor play out before your very eyes," Collingwood said. "Lloyd made a concerted effort to get leaner and quicker in the offseason, and it's translated into him being the country's most prolific tackler. Between his hard work, matter-of-fact disposition, productivity, and rare five-year allegiance to the same school, Lloyd is certainly deserving of this award." Missouri State (4-7, 3-4 CUSA) will host No. 21 Liberty (10-1, 7-0) at 1 p.m. for senior day on Saturday, Nov. 28. This will be Lloyd’s final game representing the Bears inside Plaster Stadium. Keating and the Daily Citizen’s Ryan Collingwood voted on the winner. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. Send stats or information to him at Lkeating@usatodayco.com This article originally appeared on Springfield News-Leader: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year

title: Kansas State vs Iowa State score prediction: Picking a Farmageddon winner

content: AMES, Iowa — The end of Kansas State football's disappointing 2026 season will arrive Saturday once the clock hits zero against Iowa State . The Wildcats and Cyclones will play at 1 p.m., Nov. 28, at Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, Iowa. It will mark the 110th straight season K-State and Iowa State have played the Farmageddon rivalry game . That streak is scheduled to end in 2027. Kansas State (4-7, 1-7 Big 12) has lost its last five games, including last week's 35-28 overtime collapse against Arizona. Iowa State (5-6, 3-5 Big 12) needs a win to achieve bowl eligibility in its first season under Jimmy Rogers. If they continue that level of play this week, they'll have a shot. Outside of Iowa State's run game, the Cyclones don't do much that's special. The Cyclones don't force too many turnovers; their quarterback play isn't the best; their defense is vulnerable. They allow 29.2 points per game, they allow 176.9 rushing yards per game, and are bottom 10 in the country in opposing quarterback efficiency. Why Iowa State has an advantage: Running back Aiden Flora leads the nation in rushing, while Kansas State has been dreadful against the run all year. One of the best all-purpose backs in the country, he should have a big day as he averages 7.2 yards per carry. Iowa State's run game and red zone offense have ranked among the nation's best. Those are the only two areas they've been super consistent. The Cyclones should be motivated, being the lone team in this game with bowl hopes. Kansas State's health at quarterback continues to be a question; they've lost all five games since Avery Johnson's season-ending injury.
