title: UCF football hopes to close strong vs Deion Sanders, Colorado: Preview, predictions
summary: The UCF Knights can earn their first winning season in the Big 12 Conference if they can topple Colorado on the road.
content: ORLANDO — Last week's dominant win over Iowa State offered a glimpse at what a fully healthy UCF football team could accomplish. The Knights cruised to a 48-17 win behind Alonza Barnett III 's four touchdown passes, Josh Derry's hat trick of TD catches and a four-takeaway performance by their defense. What they have not done, though, is string those type of performances together. That's the challenge that lies ahead for the Knights in their regular-season finale. UCF (6-5, 4-4 Big 12) visits Folsom Field for the first time for a Nov. 28 date with Colorado (4-7, 2-6). Kickoff is set for 2 p.m. on TNT. "Seems like it's been a little bit of a roller coaster," Knights coach Scott Frost said. "What a great opportunity to play our best and see what happens. They've got good players, they've got really good coaches, we're on the road, tough environment, right after Thanksgiving — just an awesome chance for us to go and get another opportunity to be around each other and play another game." The Knights will go bowling , securing the all-important sixth win on senior night. Colorado, meanwhile, guaranteed a third losing season in Deion Sanders ' four-year tenure with a 35-28 defeat at Cincinnati last Saturday. Sanders could be on the hot seat , considering the school's recent change in athletic directors; Fernando Lovo arrived from New Mexico in January. Can the Knights clinch their first winning Big 12 season? The News-Journal panel of Chris Boyle, Chris Vinel and Ken Willis deliver their analysis and predictions. UCF vs. Colorado tale of the tape It's easy to forget Barnett's first pass against Iowa State should have been intercepted by two defenders. The redshirt senior turned in a strong performance otherwise, completing 17 of 27 attempts for 255 yards with four touchdowns, plus another 43 yards and a score on the ground. UCF stayed on schedule, producing a first-down success rate of 49.1% and creating 11 explosive plays. Duke Watson 's return from a foot injury certainly helped the cause as he rushed for 113 yards, his first 100-yard day since Sept. 19. Derry, now up to 25 career touchdown receptions, has three straight 100-yard receiving games — the first Knight to do so since Kobe Hudson in 2023. If the Knights can retain him, Tyren Hornes , Duane Thomas Jr., Waden Charles and Caden Piening, they should boast one of the most formidable groups of pass-catchers in the Big 12 next fall. Antione Jackson continued a strong senior season with a forced fumble and an interception, adding to his three pass breakups the week before against Arizona State . According to Pro Football Focus, opposing quarterbacks are completing just 52.2% of their passes with Jackson as the nearest defender with a 61.3 NFL passer rating. Isaac Wilson, the younger brother of former New York Jets quarterback Zach Wilson, is the starter behind center for the Buffaloes. He has thrown for 1,941 yards but has four multi-interception games in nine appearances. Joseph Williams is one of just two Big 12 receivers with more than 1,000 yards entering Thanksgiving weekend. Two weeks ago, Colorado rushed for 249 yards, the most in the Sanders era, in a 42-32 upset of then-No. 14 Houston — the program's first win over an AP Top-15 team since 2007. Lehigh Acres native Richard Young paced the Buffs with 99 yards and two touchdowns on 21 attempts, DeKalon Taylor ripped off a 67-yard TD run and JaQuail Smith added 44 yards and a score. Defensively, Colorado ranks near the bottom end of the Big 12 in scoring (29.3 ppg allowed) and total yards (391.1 ypg allowed). However, the Buffaloes are fourth in the league with 29 sacks — with Gideon ESPN Lampron, Lamont Lester Jr. and Toby Anene recording at least five apiece. That could pose a problem for UCF's offensive line, which has conceded 25 sacks. UCF vs. Colorado scouting report: What we're watching Chris Boyle: Can UCF generate takeaways on the road again? It squandered a 19-point lead in Kansas, saved at the last second by Barnett's touchdown pass to Caden Piening, but the defensive unit dominated the first 35 minutes or so of action. UCF recovered a pair of Jayhawk fumbles and held them to 2.8 yards per play through the 9:52 mark of the third quarter. UCF improved to a tie for 18th among the nation's 138 Football Bowl Subdivision teams with 18 takeaways. Colorado ranks second-to-last with 23 giveaways, including 12 interceptions by redshirt sophomore quarterback Isaac Wilson. It's a mismatch on paper, one which the Knights need to exploit. Chris Vinel: Can UCF's offense look alive again? It has oscillated for the past month. Thirty-nine points against BYU, nine against Baylor. Thirty-three against Kansas, 13 (including a garbage-time touchdown) against Arizona State. Last week, the Knights posted their best performance of the season against an FBS team. They rushed for 205 yards, their most since September, and Barnett tossed four touchdown passes in a 48-point outburst. And if there was ever an opponent to stop the negative pendulum swing, it's Colorado. The Buffs allowed crooked numbers to Northwestern (41), Oklahoma State (57), Houston (42) and Cincinnati (35). Ken Willis: I dare you to pretend to know how this game might play out. Even a rough estimation. From week to week in today's college game, you simply don't know which version of any team will show up. UCF epitomizes that, and Colorado sorta does, too. Except while UCF teeters between good and bad, the Buffs have mostly swung between bad and worse. Still, the Knights have yet to put together two weeks of mere decency against real competition this year. And they were decent last week. Do the math. This is looking like a matchup of the resistible force versus the moveable object. UCF vs. Colorado injury updates Redshirt senior safety Demari Henderson was the lone starter sidelined for the Iowa State game. The Sanford native has missed more than a month, last appearing in the upset win over BYU. Tackett Curtis' status will be worth monitoring throughout the week; he played just 32 snaps against Iowa State, per PFF. He leads the Knights with 69 tackles, notching four TFLs, two sacks and two picks. Tight end Caden Piening and right tackle Preston Cushman received treatment during the game, with the former spending time in the medical tent. However, both returned and finished the game against Iowa State. For Colorado, safety Naeten Mitchell has missed the last three games, with Ben Finneseth drawing into the lineup in his place. Wide receiver Danny Scudero, who topped 1,000 receiving yards last year at San José State, has not been available since mid-September. UCF vs. Colorado score predictions, picks Chris Boyle: UCF 24, Colorado 19 Chris Vinel: UCF 31, Colorado 24 Ken Willis: Colorado 27, UCF 20 This article originally appeared on The Daytona Beach News-Journal: UCF football hopes to close strong vs Deion Sanders, Colorado: Preview, predictions

title: Will UNC football beat NC State? Players to watch, prediction for Tar Heels vs Wolfpack
summary: A bowl bid and bragging rights are up for grabs in the UNC football vs. NC State game at Kenan Stadium. Here's our preview and prediction.
content: It’s win or onto next season for UNC and NC State football. The Tar Heels (5-6, 2-5 ACC) host the Wolfpack (5-6, 3-5) on Saturday, Nov. 28, at Kenan Stadium in the regular-season finale. Kickoff is set for noon ET and the game will be televised on ACC Network. The winner will be bowl eligible. It’s been all NC State this decade, with the Pack winning eight of the last 10 games in the rivalry matchup, including five straight in the series. If it wins a sixth, it would be a program record. BOWL PROJECTIONS: Will it be UNC or NC State football in bowl game? Latest projections FINALLY THE YEAR?: No UNC football player has beaten NC State. Now a bowl bid depends on it FOUR-LETTER WORD: Philip Rivers is a four-letter-word hire for NC State football Bill Belichick’s Tar Heels are trying to avoid consecutive losing seasons for the first time since 2017-18 and NC State is aiming for a seventh consecutive bowl berth before the Philip Rivers era gets underway in Raleigh. Here are some stats to know, players to watch and a score prediction for the Tar Heels vs. Wolfpack . Will Bill Belichick start Billy Edwards Jr. or Travis Burgess at quarterback vs NC State? For the second week in a row, UNC has questions at quarterback. True freshman Travis Burgess got his first start in the Tar Heels’ 41-24 loss at Virginia, showing some promise but racking up a lot of yards in garbage time. Burgess had 354 passing yards and 106 rushing yards with two touchdowns, but also threw a pair of interceptions. Billy Edwards Jr. led UNC to its five wins before leaving the Louisville game with an injury. Edwards was playing his best football before the setback and missed the Virginia game. He wasn't listed on the initial ACC availability report for the NC State game, so it looks like Edwards is good to go. Still, it could be an interesting choice for Belichick, who needs this win to validate the progress made this season. NC State QB CJ Bailey is undefeated against Tar Heels NC State quarterback CJ Bailey is 2-0 against UNC, completing 70% of his passes for four touchdowns and an average of 221.5 passing yards with just one interception. Bailey also averaged nearly 60 rushing yards in those games against the Tar Heels, looking comfortable in a close game at Kenan Stadium in 2024 before leading the Pack to a blowout win last season at Carter-Finley Stadium. Bailey had 292 passing yards and 3 TDs in a 28-10 win at Florida State last week, so UNC better be ready to bring its best effort. Wolfpack running back Davion Gause vs UNC defense Known as “Bullet,” NC State running back Davion Gause played his first two seasons at UNC. Gause is having the best season of his career, logging 536 rushing yards on 4.1 yards per game with 3 TDs to go with 303 receiving yards on 33 catches. He’s also coming off the best game of his career, racking up 134 rushing yards and 71 receiving yards at FSU. UNC’s defense struggled against running backs in space at Virginia, allowing eight explosive plays, with most of those coming from the Cavaliers' running backs. If those Tar Heels struggles carry into this weekend, Gause will have quite a reunion with his former team. UNC vs NC State score prediction NC State 29, UNC 26 : The Tar Heels have one win at home against an FBS opponent under Belichick and the Pack has lost three of its four road games this season, so something’s gotta give. Considering the recent history of the rivalry and the success of CJ Bailey against UNC, NC State is the safer bet. title: US Merchant Marine Academy looking to make more history in Division III football playoffs
summary: They’re sea-sing the day at the United States Merchant Marine Academy.
content: They’re sea-sing the day at the United States Merchant Marine Academy. It’s a historic year for the 8-1 Mariners, who will play in the second round of the Division III football playoffs for the first time in Kings Point history. “It’s really a special team and how close-knit they are,” head coach Jameson Croall told The Post. “Really, when times get difficult … we lean on each other and respond to that adversity together.” A U.S. Merchant Marine Academy player runs up field during his team’s 42-14 blowout win over the Coast Guard Academy on Nov. 14, 2026, in the Secretaries’ Cup at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. Matt Kaminsky/ZUMA Press Wire The Mariners face No. 25 Hampden-Sydney on the road Saturday at noon after a first-round bye. The USMMA returns to the playoffs for the first time since 1994, the academy’s only other berth. It’s a unique situation for midshipmen on the team who were slated to begin their term at sea — where they can be deployed anywhere around the globe — right after the regular season ended. Several players are spending their mornings on the academy’s flagship vessel, the Kings Pointer, as an interim solution while they wait for long-term stationing after the playoffs. They come back to land and practice in the evening, ready to work, Croall said. “Their ability to compartmentalize all of those things and be able to focus on what they need to focus on in the moment is really a pretty special quality that I think embodies our team. “We really don’t have many bad practices.” The Mariners have also been sailing to victory thanks to dual-threat junior quarterback Bubba Mustain, who averaged 100 rushing yards per game and threw for 16 touchdowns in nine weeks. “He’s really just a complete player with a team around him that’s fully bought in and able to make plays for him as well.”

title: USC Band Benched After Bruins Campus Prank Backfires
summary: USC's marching band sits out the UCLA rivalry game after students vandalized a campus sign. President Kim cites respect and discipline for the move.
content: Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports USC President Beong-Soo Kim ordered the Trojan marching band to skip its traditional pregame and halftime shows this Saturday. The decision comes after students removed letters from a sign at UCLA’s Wasserman Football Center to spell a crude message. Kim sent an email to students on Wednesday stating the group would stay on the sidelines “out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university’s values.” This isn’t the first time the two Los Angeles schools have played tricks on each other before a big game. Fans remember the 1958 incident where a helicopter dropped manure on the Tommy Trojan statue, or the 1989 prank where USC fans released 20,000 painted crickets into a UCLA library. Those stunts were wild, but they did not stop the music from playing at the Rose Bowl. This time, the university leadership decided the prank crossed a line that cost the band its spot in the game. Kim made it clear that the students involved will face real consequences for their actions. He stated that any student found responsible for the vandalism “will be subject to discipline under university policy.” The president called the behavior unacceptable, noting that “This conduct runs contrary to USC’s values and is unacceptable.” The school wants to show the entire UCLA community that it takes this rivalry and mutual respect seriously. Stakes Rise at the Rose Bowl The game on Saturday carries massive weight for both teams as they fight for a spot in the College Football Playoff. No. 10 UCLA enters the matchup with a 10-1 record and a chance to clinch the Big Ten title with a win. A conference championship berth would secure an automatic berth in the playoff field for the Bruins. They are looking to prove they can run Los Angeles and dominate the conference. No. 15 USC sits at 8-3 and needs a victory to keep its slim playoff hopes alive. Head coach Lincoln Riley admitted his team has faced struggles, but he gave credit to the opposing squad. Riley said, “They’ve done a great job, I’ll give them a lot of credit,” while comparing the current season to his own debut year in 2022, according to the New York Post . He noted that the situation feels familiar, even if the outcome has been different so far. Bob Chesney, the UCLA coach, predicted a massive crowd for the showdown at the Rose Bowl. He told fans at a pep rally that between 75,000 and 80,000 people were expected to attend the game. This would mean the removal of the end-zone tarps and full stadium shots that have been common this year. The sign outside the UCLA football center is currently undergoing repairs after the band members altered the name. The game kicks off at 12:30 p.m. on Saturday with Big Ten title and playoff implications on the line.

title: UTSA ignores outside noise, tops Tulsa to earn home field in American championship game
summary: With emotions high and rumors swirling about coach Jeff Traylor's future, UTSA responded with its best game, delivering in all three phases to beat Tulsa.
content: The UTSA Roadrunners football head coach Jeff Traylor is picked up by UTSA Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown (2) and other teammates after a win between UTSA and Tulsa at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Friday, Nov. 26, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) With rumors swirling about coach Jeff Traylor's future, an American Conference championship berth at stake and a group of seniors preparing for their final home game, UTSA quarterback Owen McCown knew his team was grappling with "a lot of possible distractions." The whirlwind unfolded quickly over an abbreviated week, as the Roadrunners faced an 11 a.m. Friday kickoff against perhaps the hottest team in the league, as Tulsa entered riding a three-game winning streak. But amid all the noise, UTSA delivered perhaps its best performance of the season, beating Tulsa 28-22 in the Alamodome to secure the right to host the American Conference championship game at 7 p.m. next Saturday. "We didn't really hear no noise," wide receiver AJ Wilson said. "We just tuned that stuff out, and we just put our head down and work." The chatter about Traylor's future with the Roadrunners has rarely been louder, as speculation mounts that he could be just days away from accepting the open head coaching position at Baylor. The Roadrunners have held on to Traylor for seven years despite overtures and speculation involving programs like Texas A&M, Texas Tech and Houston, but his name has continued to show up near the top of the list for every Power Four opening in the state. Rather than offer any insight on his future after Friday's win, Traylor said his focus was on next week's opponent in the conference championship game. "Whoever it is, that's where all my attention is going to be," Traylor said. "I'm not going to get distracted by anything else that's being talked about." UTSA Roadrunners tight end Brandon Young Jr. (89) reacts after making a catch during a game between UTSA and Tulsa at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Friday, Nov. 26, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) UTSA finishes the regular season alone atop the American Conference at 10-2 overall and 7-1 in the league, set to meet with Memphis, East Carolina or North Texas depending on the results of this weekend's games. The Roadrunners will be seeking their third conference championship and first as a member of the American, previously claiming Conference USA titles in 2021 and 2022. UTSA hosted both of those matchups, too, with 41,412 fans on hand to watch a 48-27 win against North Texas in 2022 and 41,148 packed into the Alamodome for a 49-41 win against Western Kentucky in 2021. The Roadrunners faced a tougher path in the American, finishing their first year 9-4 before posting 7-6 campaigns the past two seasons. "The last couple years have been sluggish, but this all started in January," linebacker Cam Cooper said. "We talked about it, and now we get a chance to do it, and I'm just very happy." The Roadrunners opened Friday's matchup with a pair of explosive passing scores, as quarterback McCown found Wilson for touchdowns of 64 and 79 yards within the first three plays from scrimmage. Less than four minutes into the game, McCown had eclipsed his passing total from either of the past two games, as his combined 197 yards in wins against North Texas and UAB the marked the lowest total for a two-game stretch in his three-year career as the Roadrunners' starter. McCown hadn't hit a pass of 50 yards or longer in any of UTSA's previous seven conference games this season. "Last week, I put it out there, that was one of my worst performances, and it was," McCown said. "So, I think I kept my mindset all week. Just watch the film, learn from it and then get ready to roll again." UTSA's defense allowed Tulsa to answer with a 75-yard touchdown on its opening possession, but the Roadrunners kept the Golden Hurricane off the board through the next nine drives, allowing just 63 yards through that stretch. UTSA forced safeties on back-to-back drives and set a new season high for sacks in a game with four in the first half alone. Since giving up 563 yards and 60 points in a blowout loss to Florida Atlantic on Nov. 5, UTSA's defense has shut down three straight opponents, holding North Texas, UAB and Tulsa to averages of 18.3 points and 286.3 yards per game. "Anger, if I'm being honest," Cooper said. "That game right there (against FAU), we were very mad about how we played. Since then, it's just the emotion on defense is anger, and that's how we've been ever since." Traylor called Friday's win "the most dominant we've been in all three phases," as the Roadrunners outgained the Golden Hurricane 526-274. McCown finished 22-of-32 passing for 353 yards with two touchdowns and an interception, while Will Henderson picked up 105 yards on the ground. UTSA's defense allowed Tulsa to march for long touchdown drives on its final two possessions, but the Roadrunners' offense drained the final 3:27 off the clock, sending UTSA back to its long-awaited spot in a conference championship game. "It's what we do this for, man," linebacker Darion White said. "Everything since the spring, man, I can just see it now. This is what we do it for, man. It means everything. This is what we practice for." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: Vanderbilt football vs Tennessee score prediction for Week 13 SEC game

content: Vanderbilt football beat Tennessee last year in Knoxville and is looking to follow that up with a home win at FirstBank Stadium for a Nov. 28 matchup. Why Tennessee has an advantage: Tennessee's defense seems like a nightmare for Vanderbilt, which has been prone to turnovers playing a freshman quarterback. title: Vernell Brown III to undergo surgery amid extended Florida absence
summary: Following his extended absence this season, the Florida Gators have announced that Vernell Brown III will undergo surgery for his PCL sprain.
content: Florida football will remain without one of its young offensive playmakers as the 2026 regular season comes to a close. The Gators announced Tuesday that sophomore wide receiver Vernell Brown III will undergo surgery to address a knee injury that has kept him sidelined since Florida's Week 4 victory over Ole Miss. According to a statement released by the university, Brown will be out "for the immediate future" as he recovers from the procedure, leaving his potential return date uncertain. "During the Ole Miss game, Vernell Brown III suffered a PCL sprain. In ramping up to return to play, he suffered a setback during Georgia week. After exhausting every non-surgical option, with medical consultation, it’s been advised that the best course of action is that he undergo surgery to correct the issue for good. He will be out for the immediate future,” UF stated. “Vernell has worked tirelessly since suffering the sprain to return to play for the team this season. Despite extensive rehab and two procedures, persistent swelling and limited range of motion have prevented him from returning this season. We look forward to his return for the 2027 season.” An update on Vernell Brown III pic.twitter.com/UnJjJB5XOg — Florida Gators Football (@GatorsFB) November 24, 2026 Before suffering the injury, Brown recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns through Florida's first four games of the 2026 season. The sophomore also made an impact on special teams, averaging 34.6 yards per punt return and returning two punts for touchdowns against Campbell in Week 2. His performance earned him SEC Co-Special Teams Player of the Week honors. After Florida announced that Brown would undergo knee surgery, his father and agent, former Gators defensive back Vernell Brown Jr., released a statement on social media about the news. “If you know (Vernell Brown III), you know his love for the game of football, his relentless work ethic, his competitive spirit, and his love for his teammates. Before questioning his commitment or credibility, understand his character, work ethic, and pedigree. Never confuse his inability to play with an unwillingness to play!” Brown Jr. said. “His goals remain unchanged: a successful collegiate football career, becoming a Top-10 NFL Draft pick, and having a long, successful, and lucrative NFL career. Accomplishing those goals requires playing on Saturdays. There was ZERO chance he would voluntarily sit out if he could play! Our motto is SHOW UP & SHOW OUT! His freshman season and the first four games of 2026 speak for themselves. MINOR SETBACK FOR A MAJOR COMEBACK!” Follow us @GatorsWire on X, formerly known as Twitter, as well as Bluesky , and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Florida Gators news, notes and opinions. title: Virginia Tech football vs. Virginia: Preview, betting odds, how to watch
summary: Previewing the 2026 Commonwealth Clash.
content: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - NOVEMBER 29: Thomas Williams #23 of the Virginia Tech Hokies and Jahmal Edrine #7 of the Virginia Cavaliers come together during a game between the Virginia Cavaliers and the Virginia Tech Hokies at Scott Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images It’s hard to believe the 2026 college football regular season ends on Saturday. That means the Virginia Tech Hokies face off against bitter in-state rival Virginia in the Commonwealth Clash. We don’t have to get into the numbers; Virginia Tech has dominated this series. However, Virginia won last season’s matchup, 27-7. The Hokies have won 19 of the previous 21 meetings, and 23 of the last 26. UVa’s last win in Blacksburg came back in 1998. This Saturday’s game ends what feels like a little bit of a disappointing season for both teams. After Virginia’s surprise run last season, the Cavaliers loaded up their roster in the transfer portal again. They’re 6-5, 4-4 in ACC play, while the Hokies are also 6-5 (3-5). Virginia Tech’s record isn’t the disappointing part. Remember, the Hokies won three games last season. It’s some of the losses. Penalties cost the Hokies against Pittsburgh, but they played horribly in shocking losses to Cal and Stanford. Still, Virginia Tech is much better than it was a year ago and is headed in the right direction under head coach James Franklin. Speaking of Franklin, this is his first game against Virginia. He’s already learned how important this game is to players, fans and alums. Virginia enters Saturday’s game on a two-game winning streak, having beaten Cal and North Carolina over the last two weeks. Meanwhile, the Hokies are 0-3 since a huge road win at Clemson last month. After ugly losses to SMU and Stanford, Tech took No. 7 Miami to the wire last week. One of the many storylines in this game is Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula. Pribula, who began his career at Penn State under Franklin, wanted to transfer to Virginia Tech last winter, but the Hokies preferred Ethan Grunkemeyer. Franklin spoke this week about how much Pribula means to him personally. Pribula has had a solid season for the Hoos, completing 67% of his passes for 2,024 yards, with 19 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. He’s also rushed for 285 yards and two touchdowns. His legs could play a critical role in Saturday’s game. UVa’s leading rusher is Jekail Middlebrook, who has 561 rushing yards (4.8 ypa) and four touchdowns. While the Cavaliers don’t have a dominant lead back like J’Mari Taylor last season, they have four players, including Pribula, with 269 or more rushing yards. Virginia’s top receiver is junior Da’Shawn Martin, who leads the Cavaliers with 34 receptions, 472 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. UVa’s defense is anchored by senior Kam Robinson. A four-year starter, Robinson does a little bit of everything. He’s the leading tackler, but he can also make plays in coverage, as evidenced by his 3 interceptions. Meanwhile, for the Hokies, Grunkemeyer, running back Jeffrey Overton, wide receiver Que’Sean Brown and tight end Luke Reynolds are the players to watch. Grunkemeyer is in a bit of a funk over the last few weeks, although he played well in the first half last week at Miami. The key for Tech is getting Overton and Reynolds involved early. The passing game should go through Reynolds, then extend to Brown and others. Reynolds is a matchup nightmare for opposing defense. Overton needs less than 100 yards to reach 1,000 for the season. It’s an impressive feat, considering he has split time with Marcellous Hawkins and Virginia Tech’s run blocking woes. Watch out for true freshman Messiah Mickens to be more involved when Overton gets a breather. 3 keys to victory Keep Pribula in the pocket : Pribula is at his best when he’s on the move. The Hokies have had some trouble stopping mobile quarterbacks this season. If Tech can keep Pribula in the pocket, their chances of winning go way up. Establish the run early : We say it often, but Tech needs to be able to run the ball. Virginia’s pass defense is better than its run defense, so why not find ways to get Overton and Mickens going early. It will also open up more opportnities in the passing game later. Win turnover margin : When the Hokies turn the ball over, they lose. Most teams do actually, but it’s ugly when Tech turns it over (see Pitt and Stanford games). The defense has struggled to force turnovers, but had two against Miami. Get a couple on Saturday and the Hokies will be in good shape. Tech needs to make some plays early to keep the crowd involved and not leave at halftime. How to watch, betting odds When: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Where: Lane Stadium, Blacksburg, Virginia Time : 3:00 p.m. ET TV : The CW Network Announcers : Thom Brenneman (play-by-play), Jason Cabinda (analyst) and Wes Bryant (sideline) Radio : Virginia Tech Sports Network Radio. You can find a list of affiliates here . Streaming options : fuboTV [try it free] , ESPN Unlimited Series history : These longtime rivals first met in 1895. Overall, the Hokies have are 62-39-5 against the Cavaliers in 106 all-time meetings. Odds : Virginia Tech is a 3.5-point favorite, per FanDuel .

title: How to watch Grambling vs Southern in the Bayou Classic: TV, live stream, storylines for Saturday's game
summary: It's the 53rd annual showdown between the HBCU powerhouses.
content: The Grambling State Tigers and Southern Jaguars will meet Saturday in the 53rd annual Bayou Classic in New Orleans in a national broadcast on NBCSN and Peacock . The game will also be broadcast live on NBC stations throughout Louisiana. The national programming schedule was adjusted because of the rescheduling of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday . pic.twitter.com/SsXIuJlTti — NBC Sports PR (@NBCSportsPR) November 26, 2026 In what's known as the grandaddy of HBCU classic matchups, Southern leads 27-24 in the series since the annual meeting was moved to New Orleans in 1974, and the Jaguars have won four consecutive and seven of the past eight. The rivalry between the Louisiana schools dates to 1932 when Southern beat Grambling 20-0 and won the next seven meetings before Grambling's first victory in 1947. Southern leads the overall series 43-34, and the teams have played annually since 1959 when Grambling joined the SWAC. There have been 25 games in the series decided by one score or less, including last year's 28-27 win by Southern (4-3 SWAC, 6-5), which leads HBCU schools with a record 613 wins. The Jaguars also have 19 SWAC championships. Grambling (3-4 SWAC, 5-5). has a record 26 SWAC titles and ranks third all time with 6-4 victories. The marching bands from Grambling and Southern will compete Friday night in a Battle of the Bands before both perform at halftime. How to watch Southern vs. Grambling State: When: Saturday, Nov. 28 Where: Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana Time: 2 p.m. ET TV: NBCSN (NBC on stations in Louisiana, because of the rescheduled Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade reair) Live Stream: Peacock Announcing team : Chris Lewis (play-by-play), Anthony Herron (analyst) and Lewis Johnson (sideline reporter). Grambling State preview Under third-year coach Mickey Joseph, Grambling seemed on the way to back-to-back winning seasons after six consecutive from 2014-19. But the Tigers lost three in a row after a 4-2 start. Grambling has the SWAC's No. 5 scoring offense at 34.1 points per game. Three quarterbacks have rotated tjhrough the system: Jacobe Robinson (224 passsing yards, 61 rushing and four passing TDs in the team's most recent game) Reginald “RJ” Johnson (the primary QB for two games before taking an indefiinte leavve for a health issue) Ashton Frye (30 of 58 passing for 406 yards, seven total TDs — four passing, three rushing) Grambling has no players with at least 400 rushing yards but have has eight with at least 100 rushing yards. The Tigers have had a different leading rusher and a different leading receiver in each of their last 4 games. Southern preview Pro Football Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk has guided Southern to a 6-5 record in his first year as head coach while emphasizing accountability and discipline Faulk benched starting quarterback Christian Johnson and his backup quarterback Ashton Strother on Oct. 3 in a 41-10 loss to Arkansas-Pine Bluff, citing “conduct detrimental to the team” and later confirmed it was for academic reasons. "I’ve told (my players), I sat down everybody that was recruited, and was like, ‘If you don’t go to school, you’re not going to play here,' " said Faulk, a New Orleans native whose previous coaching experience was as Colorado's running backs assistant in 2005. "And you had a handful of them … my bluff got called. So I had to push the chips in.” Redshirt junior running back Trey Holly leads the SWAC in rushing yards (1,402) and touchdowns (14), and his 1,402 rushing yards are the second most in a single season in program history (behind Lenard Tillery's 1,665 rush yards in 2016). Faulk is expecting Holly to transfer next year to a Power 4 school. “Next year, he’ll be somewhere helping somebody contend for a national championship," Faulk said. "Unless he decides to stay. But I know we don’t have enough. We don’t have the money to keep him.” Bayou Classic history, results This is the 53rd installment of the Bayou Classic. Since the two teams moved the annual meeting to New Orleans in 1974, Southern holds a 28-24 edge in the Bayou Classic, including wins in four consecutive years and seven of the past eight meetings. Last year, Southern beat Grambling 28-27. What is the Battle of the Bands at the Bayou Classic? The marching bands from Grambling and Southern will compete Friday night in a Battle of the Bands before both perform at halftime. Grambling's “World Famed Tiger Marching Band” (which started in 1926) has appeared in six Super Bowl halftime shows, and Southern's "Human Jukebox" outfit has performed at four Super Bowls. The bands also will perform during halftime of Saturday's game. How can I watch college football on Peacock ? title: Why Cambridgeshire derby could be season-defining
summary: Peterborough United and Cambridge United are set for a potentially season-defining local derby at London Road.
content: Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road [Getty Images] History, tradition, bragging rights. Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT). Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads. At stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season. As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift. 'It's all about winning' The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's. They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline. Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990. Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record. "We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he said. "We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter. "It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game." The victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February. "This game is at the top of the mountain," he said. "No doubt about it. The players will be up for it, we've shown them videos of the previous games, we've got fans sending messages. "We're doing everything we can to make them realise how big this game is. It's not another game, it's the derby. A great game. "Neil knows what it means. We're two passionate managers. He's done far better than me as a manager so far, so hats off to him. But we both want to win. "They will bring 1,600 fans and we need to show Cambridge that we want to county to be blue." While this derby is new territory for Savage, Harris comes armed with the memory of defeat in his only previous taste of the tie in a season than ultimately ended with relegation for the U's. After securing a return to the third-tier in 2025-26 - and having made a competitive start to this campaign - there is no shortage of motivation to deliver a long-awaited win for his side. "It is a one-off fixture," he told BBC Look East. "There is a slightly different feel and mentality to it, but it means a hell of a lot to a hell of a lot of people. "It means a lot to get bragging rights over a direct opponent. It's important to get back to our highest standards." Posh have lost just one of their past 12 league games against Cambridge United, winning their past four in succession. But with Savage's side in a precarious league position, there is optimism among fans that their 36-year long wait to celebrate a league win at London Road could finally arrive. "It's about playing with heart and emotion, but brains as well," added Harris. "We understand the importance of the fixture, I understand it as a driven manager. It's about trying to make sure we make our fans proud." All the latest Peterborough United news All the latest Cambridge United news

title: Why a rivalry-week win might not save your College Football Playoff bid
summary: Rivalry week arrives with College Football Playoff chaos: About 10 teams are fighting for four spots, and even winning may not guarantee a berth.
content: How good is this current chaos? Rivalry week and we still don’t know who the last four teams (7-11) are going to be in the final year of the 12-team College Football Playoff . If this were next year (24-team playoff), there would be a scarcity of interest, but with just 11 spots for grabs and one game left, about 10 teams are on eggshells. Having said that, even winning your last game and being in the top 11 doesn’t guarantee anything from the CFP. Just ask Notre Dame after last year’s shocker. More on that later. The ACC final is set. Wake Forest (10-1), with no signature victory but an impressive resumé, playing a rematch against 10-1 Miami (a 33-20 loss) with the loser not assured of a CFP berth. No. 2 Utah (11-0) is in the Big 12 final and No. 11 Texas Tech is in with a victory over TCU, while No. 10 BYU (10-2) wouldbe still alive if the Red Raiders were to lose. The Big Ten is a mess. If UCLA defeats USC, they’re in. No. 13 Iowa has finally found an offense this year after thumping Illinois, 31-17, and a victory combined with a UCLA loss probably would get them there. No. 12 Oregon (8-3), which looked in complete disarray early in the season, controls its own destiny with a win over Washington. No. 14 Indiana, falling six spots after losing in OT at Washington, 27-24, proves the CFP committee is either incompetent or influenced by Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti’s criticism. The Big Ten, the conference of influence and affluence, is facing a possibility of only their conference champion in the CFP. The SEC is also a mess because of its equally ridiculous tiebreaking rules. But its teams are ranked higher. If No. 7 Tennessee (9-2), No. 3 Texas (9-2) and No. 5 Alabama (9-2) all win — all tied at 6-2 — and they’re all favored, it depends on the results of common opponents against other teams as to which team meets No. 1 Georgia (10-1) in the CFP Final. If one loses, then other tiebreakers apply. Who makes this crap up? Heisman race is over Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith has clinched the Heisman Trophy. Even on a current four-loss team, Smith has amassed 86 receptions for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns. His starting quarterback, Julian Sayin, was injured for the season. He’s done that in double and triple coverage and should be a unanimous selection. LSU keeps doing LSU things In case you missed it, LSU blinked again and pulled basketball guard RJ Louis Jr. after one game, thus complying with the SEC’s position not to allow former collegians who have signed professional contracts to come back to play in college. Too late. The SEC scheduled a meeting to discuss their “expulsion.” Yeah, right. More like a total waste of time. Expect a letter of admonishment and a fine. Expulsion? Fuhgeddaboudit. LSU is the most disappointing story this year — for Lane Kiffin’s hiring and the money poured into name, image and likeness payments. For some reason, the unranked 6-4 Tigers were slight favorites against No. 8 Tennessee (8-2) in Knoxville. They lost, 27-13, and finished 0-5 against currently ranked teams. Kiffin also embarrassed the university by dropping the F-bomb on live radio and tried to knock the football out of bounds from a Tennessee back while out of bounds. Sure, it wasn’t Woody Hayes punching a Clemson player and Ohio State firing him in response, but what gives with this childish and inappropriate behavior. Ohio State (7-4), a school with a reported $50 million payroll, is a close second. About face at TCU TCU (5-6) fired head coach Sonny Dykes seven months after giving him an extension. In April, TCU athletic director Mike Buddie said: “Competing for national and Big 12 requires the right leadership, and Sonny has proven he’s that person. His track record, … standing in the community and the decisions he’s made to position this program to pursue those goals speak for themselves.” This week, he said: “TCU investment in football has led to dramatic growth … and we cannot allow that investment to fall short of its due return.” Either he’s a hypocrite, not transparent, or both. Either way, they owe Dykes $20 million. Fortunately for him, he’s not being held accountable. Wins keep ticking away Another inexplicable example of clock management, 9-2 Boise State lost on a 42-yard field goal on the final play to San Diego State (6-5). Only problem was, it shouldn’t have come to that. With a 20-18 lead, 1:36 left and facing third and 8 from midfield, Boise completed a pass out of bounds, stopping the clock even though the Aztecs had no timeouts, meaning they lost a 40-second runoff. They compounded that egregious error by being stopped on fourth and 3, handing San Diego State a short field and a justified result. Pure stupidity. Boise head coach Spencer Danielson makes $2.1 million a year. If he hired a clock-manager coach, Boise would still be heavy favorites for a CFP berth and almost definitely would have defeated the Aztecs. Shades of Mario Cristobal, Mike Riley, etc., coaches who can’t count. All this money and no clock manager. I’m here again; ready, willing and able. Email me. Party's over at UNC What's up with Bill Belichick? What are you doing? The experiment is over. You’re another year older. You’re not a college coach and North Carolina (5-6) supporters have come to the realization that the program is going nowhere with you as head coach. Do us all a favor and sever ties the way you did with that other relationship (Jordon Hudson). My Top 25 pick No. 15 USC (8-3) +7 at UCLA (10-1): You know the drill. Bruins win and they’re in the Big Ten championship. USC also has an outside shot. You know coach Lincoln Riley can’t win on the road but this is in LA. It’s the same time zone and a 26-mile drive to the Rose Bowl. It looks like Bruins quarterback Ty Deiffenbach will play. I love the UCLA defense but Deiffenbach must play turnover-free football. Does Riley finally win a road game against a Big 10 opponent? Nope. Bruins salvage their season with a close victory. title: Young Couple Appears To Break Up at Georgia Football Game
summary: ESPN's Jesse Palmer explained his view on what was happening live.
content: X A couple attending a Georgia Tech and Wake Forest playoff college football game has gone viral for what appears to be a breakup (or a passionate argument) that the game’s commentators analyzed live. With a quarter left in the game and Wake Forest up 50 to 22, the game was practically settled — causing ESPN’s analyst Jesse Palmer, host of The Bachelor and The Bachelorette , to turn his attention to the stadium during a dead-ball situation. That’s when he caught a young man and woman in an intense conversation that seemingly had all the markings of a public breakup. “This playoff game is intense, but not as intense as this conversation, though,” said one commentator. “That’s a lot of eye contact.” A Georgia Tech couple appears to have a breakup live on air and the commentators analyze and break it down #StingEm #GoDeacs pic.twitter.com/CQukZ1DRJD — Carter Lowe (@carterl0we) November 21, 2026 COMPLEX SHOP: Shop the brands you love, anytime and anywhere. Uncover what's next. Buy. Collect. Obsess. The commentator continued, egged on by his peers, reviewing the emotions on display as if they were plays on the field. In particular, he focused on the body language of the guy who looked pretty pissed off. “He’s locked in,” the commentator said. “He’s holding her to court right now. title: Boston College Men’s Hockey Preview: Notre Dame & Harvard
summary: Who & When: Friday, November 27Boston College Eagles (6-5-2) vs Notre Dame Fighting Irish (7-7-1) Sunday, November 29Boston College Eagles (6-5-2) vs Harvard Crimson (4-4-0) Where: FridayCompton Family Ice Arena, South Bend, IN SundayBright-Landry Hockey Center, Allston, MA Puck Drop Time: 3pm EST on Friday, 4pm EST on Sunday How to Watch: Friday’s game will […]
content: LOWELL, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 5: Louka Cloutier #1 of the Boston College Eagles makes a save against the UMass Lowell River Hawks during NCAA men's hockey at the Tsongas Center on December 5, 2025 in Lowell, Massachusetts. The Eagles won 3-1. (Photo by Richard T Gagnon/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who & When: Friday, November 27 Boston College Eagles (6-5-2) vs Notre Dame Fighting Irish (7-7-1) Sunday, November 29 Boston College Eagles (6-5-2) vs Harvard Crimson (4-4-0) Where: Friday Compton Family Ice Arena, South Bend, IN Sunday Bright-Landry Hockey Center, Allston, MA Puck Drop Time: 3pm EST on Friday, 4pm EST on Sunday How to Watch: Friday’s game will be live on NBCSN / Peacock, while Sunday’s game will be on ESPN+. Notre Dame Preview: The Eagles travel to South Bend right after Thanksgiving for their matchup against Notre Dame. The Fighting Irish are red hot this month under second year head coach Brock Sheahan, going 5-1-1 after a 2-6-0 record in October. They’ve swept Penn State, Ohio State, and won the weekend series against Michigan State in November, before dropping a game to Bowling Green right before the holiday. Offensively, senior Danny Nelson leads the Irish with 15 points in 15 games, followed closely by senior Paul Fischer who has 13 points in 15 games. In net, freshman Patrick Quinlan has an .896 save percentage in 10 games, while junior Nicholas Kempf has a .916 save percentage in 5. The Irish power play is clicking at 19.5%, while their penalty kill is 64.3%. Harvard Preview: As all the Ivies do, Harvard started their season at the end of October, with new coach Rob Rassey at the helm, going 1-1 against UMass before turning the calendar to November. This month, they have gone 3-3, with wins against Brown, BU, and Princeton, and games dropped to Yale, Quinnipiac, and most recently Bentley. Harvard will have a game against Dartmouth on Friday before the Eagles face them on Saturday. On offense, senior defenseman Matthew Morden leads the Crimson with 7 points. Sophomore Aidan Lane and junior Mick Thompson are tied for second with 6 points each. In net, junior Ben Charette and freshman Rudy Guimond have essentially split time equally; Charette has a .904 save percentage in 5 games, while Rudy Guimond has a .884 save percentage in 4. The Eagles are coming off a huge weekend after sweeping Maine for the first time in 26 years. Louka Cloutier earned Hockey East Goaltender of the Week honors, while Casey Mutryn earned Hockey East Rookie of the Week honors for their play up in Orono. While the Eagles should be really proud of themselves for their strong play last weekend, their memory also needs to continue to be short — games right after Thanksgiving are always a little sluggish regardless. They’ll have to really focus and dictate play from the beginning in order to maintain this streak that they’re on.

title: Chelsea are in the race to sign South American wonderkid
summary: Chelsea Transfer News: Simon Escobar Battle Grows as Brighton and Barcelona Track Argentine Left-BackChelsea are among the clubs closely tracking Simon Escobar, with the teenage Argentine emerging as ...
content: Chelsea are in the race to sign South American wonderkid Chelsea Transfer News: Simon Escobar Battle Grows as Brighton and Barcelona Track Argentine Left-Back Chelsea are among the clubs closely tracking Simon Escobar, with the teenage Argentine emerging as one of the more compelling long-term defensive prospects in South America. According to TeamTalk , the 17-year-old left-back is firmly on the radar at Stamford Bridge, while Brighton and Barcelona are also following his progress. Escobar, currently with Vélez Sarsfield, has built strong momentum over the past year. He has already collected senior experience in Argentina’s top flight and enhanced his reputation through international exposure with Argentina’s under-17 side. The report states that “Simon Escobar has become as one of South America’s most closely watched teenage defenders”, which reflects the level of attention now surrounding his development. Simon Escobar Emerging as Chelsea Target What stands out in this case is the profile. Escobar is described as a “dynamic full-back” who has shown “composure in possession, an ability to carry the ball, contribute in the final third and brilliant defensive reliability for his age”. For clubs such as Chelsea, where recruitment increasingly looks towards ceiling and adaptability, that combination will naturally appeal. There is further value in the fact that he “can also operate further forward”, strengthening his standing as a flexible left-sided option. The source adds that “his versatility has only strengthened his appeal to clubs seeking long-term options on the left, rather than immediate first-team regulars”. That detail feels important. This is a player being considered as part of a broader strategy, rather than a fast-tracked senior solution. Brighton and Barcelona Also Monitoring Situation Brighton’s presence in the race is no surprise given their established model in South American recruitment, while Barcelona’s interest underlines the calibre of talent involved. TeamTalk reports that “Barcelona have also been mentioned with interest in Escobar”, with Spanish attention focused on adding “young defensive profiles”. Vélez have already moved to strengthen their position, extending Escobar’s deal until December 2028. That gives the Argentine club control and patience. It also means any future negotiations are likely to begin from a position of strength. Transfer Timeline Points to Patient Chelsea Approach There is no immediate move on the cards. As the report makes clear, “Any move remains in the future” because “FIFA regulations mean a move to Europe would have to wait until he turns 18 in the summer.” Chelsea and Brighton are therefore focused on monitoring, not pushing towards a rapid agreement. For now, “the priority is continued scouting and reporting rather than an immediate bid”, while Vélez “are in no rush to sell and view him as a key part of their project in the short to medium term”. The situation is clear, the interest is real, the timeline is longer, and Chelsea will need to decide whether Simon Escobar is a player worth pursuing when the market opens for him. Our View This feels exactly like the sort of move Chelsea should be exploring, provided the pathway is thought through properly. The talent sounds obvious, the market interest is serious and the age profile fits a club that has repeatedly tried to get ahead of the curve. When a player is already being described as one of the standout teenage defenders in South America, it makes sense to be in the conversation early. There is also something encouraging about the patience here. It would be easy to turn every promising teenager into a transfer sprint, but this sounds more measured. Continued scouting, proper background work and a clear understanding of where he would fit are all essential. If he arrives eventually, it has to be with a development plan, not simply as another name added to a crowded list of young prospects. The Brighton angle is worth noting as well. When they are in for a player like this, it usually signals strong groundwork and conviction. Barcelona being mentioned only sharpens that sense. Chelsea cannot assume reputation alone will carry weight in these situations. If Escobar truly offers quality in possession, attacking thrust and defensive reliability, then the attraction is obvious. The key question is whether Chelsea can present the best football route. If the answer is yes, this is the kind of deal that could look very smart in a few years.

content: Nov. 26—GRAND FORKS — UND forward Josh Zakreski missed four months last season after a practice injury required leg surgery. Zakreski was in and out of the lineup early this season, but landed on UND's top line Saturday night. Zakreski spoke to the Herald about his recovery and shared some of his off-the-ice favorites. Q. Coach Dane Jackson said Saturday night that your injury lingered into the summer and you were unable to skate a lot. What was your summer like? A. I didn't skate from basically when we lost to Wisconsin (in April) until when I came back here in July. I took a lot of time off to try to give my ankle some rest. It seemed to have helped, but I kind of got behind other guys on the team. I've been try to work as hard as I can, skating a lot, getting into the gym and trying to catch up. It kind of seems like I've started to catch back up slowly, so I've been feeling really good on the ice. I'm just kind of excited where I'm going, trending in the right direction. Q. What did it feel like Saturday night on a line with Cole Reschny and Mac Swanson? A. Playing with Resch and Swanny was awesome. Just getting the opportunity to play with those guys. . . they're such gifted hockey players. It was a tight game, but I felt like I played my role well. Q. You beat out a couple of icing calls Saturday. Did it feel like you were playing fast? A. I felt like I had some good momentum. My legs felt really fresh, even though we played Friday. But I felt good out there. I was just trying to use my speed and play my game and play how I was last year before my injury. Q. Why did you start playing hockey? A. Definitely my dad. I started late. I didn't start playing until I was 7 or 8. I was playing floor hockey before. That's what got me into it. I started to enjoy it. Then, my dad put me in skates and I've been in it ever since. Q. If there's one current or former hockey player you could have dinner with, who would you choose? A. This is going to be a weird one, but I'd say Tyson Kozak. I used to room with him in Portland, so I think it would be good to get back and have a nice dinner with him, catch up and see how he's doing. Q. What are your pregame rituals? A. I like to take a nap, for sure. I like to get a good pregame meal in, shower, pretty basic. I would definitely say when I get to the rink, I have a pretty big superstition where I just like to focus on talking to myself and doing a little bit of breath work and visualizing what's going to happen on the ice. Q. What's the most memorable goal you've ever scored? A. I'd say double OT against Everett in the playoffs my last year in Portland. We ended up beating them and they were the top-ranked team in the league that year, so that was my most memorable, for sure. Q. What game was it? A. Game 4. We were down 2-1 in the series. We tied it up, then went to Game 7 of that series and ended up beating them. Q. What's something you're competitive in besides hockey? A. Probably golf. My golf game got a lot better this summer. I was able to shoot my first 80. I almost shot 79, but blew it on the 18th hole. I'd definitely say golf. I'm really starting to get into it. Q. What's your dream vacation spot? A. Somewhere over in Europe like Greece or Italy. . . just somewhere cool I've never really thought about going, somewhere I can enjoy and take a break. I like the food in Italy, so that would be a big one. Q. What's your favorite meme? A. I don't use a whole lot of memes, so I'm not sure I can answer that one. Q. What's your favorite childhood memory? A. Probably playing baseball. My dad and I would always go work in the baseball cages. I managed to hit two home runs in one game, and it kind of taught me that hard work really does pay off. I loved playing baseball growing up. Q. What's the best food spot in Grand Forks? A. I really like that Joe's Italian place. You also can't go wrong with Harry's. Q. If you had to sing karaoke, what would be your go-to song? A. Mr. Saturday Night by Jon Pardi. Q. What's the best meal your mom or dad cook? A. My dad can cook up some good burgers. My mom makes this spaghetti pie. I really like that. She whips up some good pierogies, too. Q. What's your favorite part about your hometown, Saskatoon? A. I'd say seeing my friends and family. I don't get to see them a lot.

title: Lille join race for 18-year-old Barcelona winger as club weigh January loan exit
summary: According to French outlet Foot01 (h/t SPORT), Lille are the latest club to express an interest in signing Barcelona winger Jesse Bisiwu on loan in the January transfer window.The Belgian starlet is r...
content: Lille join race for 18-year-old Barcelona winger as club weigh January loan exit According to French outlet Foot01 (h/t SPORT ), Lille are the latest club to express an interest in signing Barcelona winger Jesse Bisiwu on loan in the January transfer window. The Belgian starlet is regarded as an important prospect by the Catalan giants, who must now decide whether remaining with the reserve team or gaining experience in senior football would be better for his development. Interest growing in Bisiwu As already reported , Bisiwu is already attracting interest from clubs like Ajax, Rangers, and Walfoot in Belgium. Now, Lille, too, have thrown their hat in the ring, becoming the latest club to express an interest in bringing the 18-year-old starlet in on a temporary deal. Interest growing in Bisiwu. (Picture credit: x/@FCBarcelona) The Ligue 1 club have a track record of identifying and developing young players and could offer the Barcelona winger an opportunity to compete at a higher level rather than him waiting for a pathway into Hansi Flick’s first team. Barcelona’s stance on Bisiwu However, Barcelona are not yet convinced that a move away for Bisiwu is the right decision. The Blaugrana invested significantly in his signing last summer and have high hopes for his future and intend to weigh his situation carefully before taking a final call. According to the report, the La Liga champions would be open to considering a loan departure, but one condition is non-negotiable: the agreement must not include an option to buy. Will Bisiwu stay or leave? (Picture credit: x/@FCBarcelona) Barça do not want to risk losing control of a player they view as a strategic investment for the future. As such, any temporary departure would have to ensure that he returns to the club at the end of the loan spell. Staying at Barça Atletic would allow him to continue learning Barcelona’s style of football and adapting to the demands of the club. On the other hand, a loan could expose him to a more physically demanding level of competition at the first-team level and provide experience that may be difficult to obtain within the club at this stage. However, Barcelona will not want Bisiwu to leave simply for the sake of playing elsewhere. The move must come with a guarantee of regular minutes and offer him a genuine opportunity to develop.

title: Red Wings Prospect Check-In Part 1: College Takeover
summary: We’re just over a quarter of the way through the Red Wings season with 24 games played at the NHL […]
content: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect We’re just over a quarter of the way through the Red Wings season with 24 games played at the NHL level. The rest of the hockey world finds itself at a similar point, and for some of the Red Wings top prospects, it’s been a productive season so far. In part one of Detroit Hockey Now’s Prospect Check-In Series, we’ll be taking a look at how the team’s top college forwards are doing this year. Detroit’s prospect pool at the college level is deep, and a couple of the players on this list could very well make the jump to the NHL at the end of the year. So, make sure you’ve got your coffee brewed and a comfortable seat. Michael Hage The newest addition to the Red Wings prospect system, Michael Hage was the centerpiece of the trade haul sent back in exchange for Dylan Larkin from the Montreal Canadiens. The 20-year-old center for the University of Michigan is leading the nation in scoring with a 2 point per game pace at 26 points in just 13 games played. While many outlets project Hage to come up in the NHL more as an all-purpose forward, Shawn Horcoff has made no bones about his plans for his son’s roommate. “He’s a centerman. As clear as day, he’s a very smart, skilled centerman.” Horcoff said after acquiring Hage. Detroit is thin down the middle and are relying on Hage to continue his breakneck pace in the NCAA. It’s early in the year still, but Hage is putting together a season that might see him become just the second Red Wings prospect to win the Hobey Baker Award. JP Hurlbert The Red Wings have probably been keeping a much closer eye on 2026 first round pick JP Hurlbert than they might usually be able to, for a variety of reasons. Not only is the gifted young winger playing at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor like, but Detroit likely doesn’t pull the trigger on a trade for Hage without having watched him in person extensively. So far Hurlbert has five goals and four assists in 13 games this year Hurlbert and Hage don’t usually skate on the same line, but Hurlbert has steadily been climbing the depth chart on a loaded roster. Hurlbert started the season on the fourth line and was the only freshman to get bumped up to the second line after the Wolverines’ saw their roster get temporarily reduced after a line brawl in their matchup with Michigan State. Fireworks in the third period, Michigan up 5-1 and havoc at the bench pic.twitter.com/kyr0EvrgV1 — Max Bultman (@m_bultman) November 21, 2026 On a roster as laden with “NHL talent” as Michigan’s (14 of 23 players already drafted by a team), Hurlbert has to work hard to stand out. He and the Wolverines are the top ranked team in the country and can steamroll a lot of the opponents on their schedule. Getting more ice time over these next few games should help him make that case. The Plante Brothers Usually when making a prospect check in, one tries to avoid grouping two players into one section, however, in the case of Max and Victor Plante , there’s some reason to besides the obvious that the brothers are on the same roster. Unfortunately for the elder of the two Plantes, Max has missed 14 games with a shoulder injury. Max had two assists in his two games before coming out of the lineup while playing on the top line with both Victor and their elder brother, Zam. In the meanwhile, Victor has taken to the NCAA like a fish to water with three goals and eight assists in 16 games played. More importantly, he has managed to completely stay out of the penalty box so far this year. The young Bulldogs forward collected 71 minutes in the sin bin in the USHL but has managed not to stray afoul of Johnny law in the NCAA. Victor’s aggression on the forecheck hasn’t taken a back seat, however. With Max set to come back into the lineup sometime in the next weeks, he could see a little more offensive production on the stat sheet as well. Brent Solomon Brent Solomon isn’t having quite as productive a year as some of the rest of the Red Wings’ prospects in the NCAA, but the freshman forward does have four goals in his 11 games with the Wisconsin Badgers. Solomon is a solid-bodied winger at 6-feet tall and 180 lbs., and has used that size well so far this year to put opponents in the boards, though he’s still having to learn how to use it properly in some areas. The Wisconsin Badger has 19 penalty minutes so far, starting the year off with a bang with a game misconduct penalty after hitting an opposing player in the head. Solomon had 53 points in 54 games while playing in the USHL last year, but in a much deeper prospect pool and slightly older than a lot of his compatriots in the freshman class at 19, he hasn’t quite adjusted to the speed of college hockey. Still, the as evidenced by players like Dylan James, there’s still plenty of time for Solomon to develop into a more well-rounded prospect, especially at the college level. At 6-foot-1 and 193 lbs, Edwards has also been showing some skill defensively with four blocked shots this year. -In his fourth year at Notre Dame, senior winger Brennan Ali has two goals and five assists in 11 games so far. Ali projects to far exceed his output from last year, finishing his season with eight goals and seven assists in 35 games for the Fighting Irish in the 2025-26 season. The young winger has quietly been improving his production year-over-year, though if he will be able to eclipse the 20 point mark in his senior season is yet to be seen. -Owen Mehlenbacher is playing for his third college team in as many years, now with the Ferris State Bulldogs after starting his college career at the University of Wisconsin and playing at University of Massachusetts. The senior forward has nearly matches three goal total from last year with two goals and three assists in his first 12 games with the Bulldogs. -20-year-old Austin Baker has a goal and an assist in 14 games for the Miami Redhawks. The former 2024 seventh round pick by the Red Wings played in 14 games for the Michigan State Spartans last year.
