title: Cricket Australia widens 'Sandpapergate' forum to 2017-2018 Ashes
summary: Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public.In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0.
content: Australian fielder Cameron Bancroft (R) is questioned by the umpires after using sandpaper in the third Test against South Africa in 2018 (GIANLUIGI GUERCIA) Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public. The governing body has ruled out reopening its investigation into the explosive 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa that blew up again this month. Instead, it proposed a forum for players, coaches and staff on the tour to share their versions of events. In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0. The hosts' consistent ability to get reverse swing in that series had England's bowlers scratching their heads. In the wake of the South Africa fallout, England great Alastair Cook, who was part of the Ashes side, was asked whether the team suspected Australia of ball-tampering. "Yes a little bit, certainly in Perth when the outfield was wet with rain they got the ball-reversing," he said. The issue went no further. Experienced senior counsel Fiona McLeod will lead the forum, which will be open for six weeks and is voluntary. Players' accounts, which can be written or verbal, will be confidential. She will investigate the Ashes, all four Tests of the South Africa tour, the events of March 24, 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper, and the conduct of the 2018 Cricket Australia probe. McLeod will provide a report detailing the principal themes and her recommendations. But what players say will not be published, no new sanctions will come out of it and she is not charged with determining any individual responsibility. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," said Cricket Australia interim chairman David Boon. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn," added Boon. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." - Reignited - The issue was reignited this month by Usman Khawaja, who claimed in his autobiography that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town. He also claimed the practice was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth. A Cricket Australia probe at the time concluded only skipper Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft were in the know. They were sent home in disgrace and banned for between nine and 12 months. Khawaja's version of events was backed by Warner and Bancroft, but strenuously denied by current captain Pat Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. The bowling group at the time -- which also included Nathan Lyon -- released a joint statement in 2021 denying any involvement. Cricket Australia last weekend said Cummins had their "unanimous support" to remain Test captain and rejected any suggestion his integrity had been compromised, while praising him for changing the culture of the team. Australia are preparing for four Tests against New Zealand, starting in Perth on December 9. mp/pst

title: Cricket-'Stan Stan' the man for Christchurch amateurs as Pant stars with incognito innings
summary: (Corrects paragraph 9 to reflect that Open House Swingers won the match by 12 runs, after organisers updated the result on their website.
content: (Corrects paragraph 9 to reflect that Open House Swingers won the match by 12 runs, after organisers updated the result ‌on their website. Earlier they reported that Chosen Ones had ‌chased down the target on the final ball.) Nov 27 (Reuters) - The clean hitting and calm ​at the crease may have looked familiar to some of those watching "Stan Stan" smash a 21-ball half-century for a Christchurch amateur side this week, but few would have guessed the mystery batter was India's Rishabh Pant. Playing under ‌a false name, the ⁠India wicketkeeper, who scored a century in the drawn first test against New Zealand in Wellington, was drafted in ⁠as a last-minute replacement for Open House Swingers in an eight-a-side Twenty20 match on Wednesday. Pant, the world's sixth-ranked test batsman, made 72 off 26 balls, ​including eight ​sixes, before being run out. Organisers of ​the Last Man Stands tournament ‌revealed Stan Stan's true identity on Thursday. Open House player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald he had seen Pant on an electric bike in Christchurch, the venue for the second test, and asked if he would play as they were a player short for the match ‌against The Chosen Ones. New Zealand captain Tom ​Latham was surprised to learn about Pant's ​incognito innings. "Did he play? How'd ​he go? That's brilliant," Latham told a press conference ‌before the second test in Christchurch. "He's ​obviously a real ​character of the game is Rishabh." Pant's heroics helped Open House Swingers secure a 12-run win over their opponents. The 29-year-old made a strong start to ​the second test on ‌Friday, however, taking two catches behind the stumps in the second ​session to dismiss Latham and Rachin Ravindra. (Reporting by Chiranjit Ojha ​in Bengaluru; Editing by Peter Rutherford)

title: India’s Rishabh Pant makes surprise appearance for New Zealand club under fake name
summary: The India wicketkeeper stepped in to help an amateur side who were short on numbers
content: Wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant opted for an unusual method of preparation for India’s second Test against New Zealand, making a surprise appearance for a club team in Christchurch under a false name. Fresh off a century in the first Test, ‘Stan Stan’ scored 54 off 21 balls for amateur side Open House Swingers as they scored a 16-run victory against The Chosen Ones on Wednesday. Organisers of the Last Man Stands tournament revealed his true identity on Thursday, the day Pant returned to action at Hagley Oval. Open House player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald he had seen Pant on an electric bike in Christchurch and asked if he would step in as they were a player short. Safi said Pant managed to keep a low profile, with few players immediately recognising him, and had to borrow kit after showing up to the match in a purple tracksuit. New Zealand captain Tom Latham was amused to hear of Pant’s antics, responding to the news in a press conference before the second Test. He said: “Did he play? How'd he go? That's brilliant. “He is obviously a real character ‌of the game, is Rishabh. It's great for him to be giving his experience back to LMS (Last Man Standing) teams!” Pant scored 128 in the drawn first Test, with India posting a score of 720-9 declared. The 29-year-old made a strong start to the second Test on Friday, taking ​two catches behind the stumps ‌in the second session to ​dismiss Latham and Rachin Ravindra . He has scored 3,853 runs in 53 Tests for India, averaging just under 45.

title: Nathan Lyon faces Australia axe with bowler accused in fresh ball tampering allegations
summary: The 39-year-old bowler has been unmasked as the previously unnamed player who suggested using mints to shine the ball
content: Nathan Lyon is set to be dropped by Australia for their next Test match and the spin bowler has been accused in fresh ball tampering accusations in the aftermath of Sandpapergate . Reports emerged that the 39-year-old spinner is set to be dropped when the squad for next month’s first Test against New Zealand is announced on Saturday. Having previously been squeezed out of the first XI on several occasions recently, he is now tipped to lose his squad place to Corey Rocchiccioli. Lyon is the sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 wickets and had worked hard to recover from a hamstring injury last summer in order to return to the Test side. The news comes as Code Sports alleged Lyon was the previously unnamed player who suggested using mints to shine the ball against Pakistan in the first match after South Africa only to be angrily shot down by new head coach Justin Langer. Lyon has yet to respond publicly. Meanwhile, Australia’s conduct during the 2017/18 Ashes is back under the microscope after the independent forum set up to explore the ‘sandpapergate’ scandal was handed an expanded brief. Earlier this month, Cricket Australia reacted to a barrage of claims and counter-claims from former players by announcing that all players and staff members would be invited to share their recollections of the ill-fated 2018 South Africa tour in a ‘safe space’. Lyon is the sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 wickets and had worked hard to recover from a hamstring injury last summer in order to return to the Test side (PA Archive) CA has now formalised the terms of reference and opted to add the previous home summer – when Australia beat England 4-0 to reclaim the urn – to its scope. A statement confirmed the forum would hear accounts related to “ball-management practices in the Australian Men’s Team during the 2017/18 season, all four Tests of the 2018 SA Tour, the events of 24 March 2018, (and) the conduct and scope of the 2018 CA investigation”. Usman Khawaja, whose autobiography reopened the historic drama, has alleged that ball-tampering methods were being utilised prior to South Africa and Cameron Bancroft – who was caught red-handed in Cape Town with sandpaper – has written about being urged to manipulate the quarter-seam on his Test debut against England in Brisbane. Those claims have brought to light a passage in Sir Alastair Cook’s own memoir, published in 2019, in which he alleges David Warner admitted during a post-series drink to using substances in his finger strapping to deteriorate the ball. Warner has admitted his involvement in the sandpaper episode but responded to subsequent reporting about his using superglue and grit, by stating: “I would suggest establishing the facts rather than perpetuating speculation”. England have maintained near total silence on the subject during their recent white-ball tour of Australia. Ahead of the ODI series Joe Root, who captained the 2017/18 tour, stated: “We obviously have no idea (about it). “It’s all speculation. I wasn’t in that dressing room. I don’t know what went on.” Australia captain Pat Cummins during the press conference following allegations by former player Usman Khawaja on the 2018 ball-tampering scandal (Reuters) CA has announced that senior barrister Fiona McLeod will oversee the forum process, which will invite but not compel squad members and support staff from the South Africa tour to share their recollections and experiences. CA has reiterated its previous commitment that no new sanctions or punishments will be handed down, while the confidentiality of all participants has been guaranteed. After a six-week evidence period, a report will be published within 30 days covering “principal themes” and “recommendations for future improvements” rather than specific testimony or direct apportioning of blame. CA chair David Boon said: “This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation. “We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn. “Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate.”

title: Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes
summary: Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England.
content: Australia won the 2017-18 Ashes series against England 4-0 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England. The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0. Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged. Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them. All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out. The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town. The four frontline bowlers in that 2018 team - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and current Test captain Pat Cummins - have always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Cummins has called Khawaja's recollection of events "nonsense". However, former team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of three players who were banned for their part in the scandal, alongside Steve Smith - have backed Khawaja's version of events. "All participants in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa, including players and support staff, will be invited to take part in the Independent Forum, as will CA management and directors at that time," Cricket Australia said. "While all involved will be encouraged to participate, there will be no compulsion to do so. All materials supplied will be treated as confidential unless otherwise stated by the participant and no sanctions will be retrospectively applied. "Participants can choose to attend the Independent Forum in person, online and/or provide information via written accounts or through relevant documents and materials." The forum will be open for six weeks. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," CA chair David Boon said. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. "It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." Khawaja hinted the team had tampered with the ball before the South Africa series on The Grade Cricketer podcast, saying sandpaper "didn't just magically happen" and the team "didn't go from zero to 100". Writing in his autobiography in 2019, former England opener Sir Alastair Cook - who captained England in the 2017-18 Ashes - alleged Warner admitted during post-series drinks that he had previously used strapping on his finger to tamper with the ball. The final Ashes Test in Sydney was just two months before the start of the South Africa series. "Our suspicions had been aroused in Perth, when they managed to get the ball reversing an inordinate amount when the outfield was still wet, following three hours' rain," Cook wrote. "When the series was complete, and we had lost 4-0, the teams shared a beer in the dressing rooms at the SCG. "Warner, a couple of beers into his celebration at the time, mentioned to a group of England players that he had used substances attached to the strapping on his hand to accelerate the deterioration of the ball during a first-class match. "I looked at Steve Smith, who shot a glance that said 'ooh, you shouldn't have said that'." Cummins retains Cricket Australia support as captain The sandpaper plot - who was there, who said what? Warner accuses Cricket Australia of 'cover-up'

title: 'One bad day for us': Tilak Varma admits India A's bowling let them down after Sri Lanka A's stunning chase
summary: After their defeat to Sri Lanka A, India A's captain Tilak Varma shared his frustration regarding the bowling effort. Though the team posted an impressive 317 runs, it wasn’t enough as Sri Lanka A chased it down, thanks to centuries from Lasith Croospulle and Sineth Jayawardene. Varma encouraged the bowlers to reflect on their performance while praising the debutants' contributions, hoping the team will learn and emerge stronger next time.
content: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma admitted that his side's bowling failed to deliver when it mattered after a crushing eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semifinal on Thursday. Despite putting 317 on the board, India A were knocked out after Sri Lanka A chased down the target with 9.3 overs to spare, powered by centuries from openers Lasith Croospulle and Sineth Jayawardene. Calling it “one bad day” for his side, Tilak credited the Sri Lankan batters but acknowledged that India A would need to introspect on their bowling after failing to defend a challenging total. “Yeah, credit goes to them. Both the openers played really well. But at the same point again, I was trying all the bowlers, but one bad day for us. I couldn’t get any help. But it’s fine. One odd bad day, but credit goes to Sri Lankan batsmen,” Tilak said after the match. The India A skipper also felt that the batting unit had done well throughout the campaign, while identifying bowling as an area that needed attention. “If you see as a batting group, we have done really well. But I think in bowling, we’ll go into the dressing room or go back home and introspect things, and we’ll come back stronger,” he added. 'We haven't executed': Tilak on India A's failed bowling plans India A had hoped that 317 would be enough to put Sri Lanka A under pressure, particularly with the pitch expected to slow down as the innings progressed. Tilak revealed that the plan was to keep the scoring rate in check during the first 15 overs and make batting more difficult later. “Yeah, I was telling my boys that initially the first 15 overs will be very crucial. If we restrict them to anything six per over, it will be very good for us. Later on, the wicket gets slightly slower side. That’s what we planned, but unfortunately we haven't executed,” he said. Tilak believed India A had a competitive total after recovering from a middle-order wobble, with Shahbaz Nadeem and Tanush Kotian adding valuable runs towards the end. “Honestly, we thought that around 320, 330 will be a good score on the board. But, you know, the wicket was slightly slow after the 20 overs. Initially, first 20 overs, it was nicely coming onto the bat. But after that, slightly slower side. Few balls were gripping and staying low. So, but there again, we got like three wickets back to back we got out. So after that, coming back to Tanush and Shahbaz, the way they played, and 318 (317) was good on the board,” he said. Sri Lanka A openers dismantle India A attack India A's plans unravelled almost immediately as Croospulle and Jayawardene made the most of early reprieves. Jayawardene hammered 105 off 70 balls, while Croospulle scored 116 off 107, the pair adding 174 for the opening wicket to take the game away from India. Nishan Madushka remained unbeaten on 58 and shared an unbroken 53-run stand with Pavan Rathnayake (31 not out) to complete the chase at 318 for two in 41.3 overs. Earlier, Abhishek Sharma's 78, Tilak's 53 and Sooryavanshi's 40 gave India A a flying start. But after the top order lost momentum, Nadeem's unbeaten 54 and his 73-run partnership with Kotian helped lift the total to 317 for eight. Tilak also highlighted the positives from the campaign, pointing to the contributions of debutants and the depth they brought to the side. “Yeah, it is really positive things. You know, there are so many youngsters who have first time playing, especially Shahbaz and Tanush. Tanush himself has debuted and also Shahbaz. You have seen he has handy bowling and also he can bat down the order. It’s really positive thing. And also Tanush, he’s also an allrounder coming back again,” he said.

title: Pakistan A beat Bangladesh A by five wickets to storm into Asia Cup Rising Stars final
summary: Pakistan A clinched their place in the 2026 ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars final after overcoming Bangladesh A by five wickets during the thrilling second semifinal in Doha. Bangladesh A aimed high with a target of 233 runs, thanks to an impressive unbeaten century from Shahadat Hossain. However, Hasan Nawaz's solid 62 propelled Pakistan A to victory in a swift 45 overs.
content: Pakistan A defeated Bangladesh A by five wickets in the second semifinal of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 to secure a place in the final, where they will face Sri Lanka A in Doha on Sunday. Chasing a target of 233, Pakistan A reached 233/5 in 45.2 overs, with Hasan Nawaz leading the way with a crucial 62-run knock. The victory also kept Pakistan A's unbeaten run in the tournament intact. Bangladesh A, meanwhile, were left to rue their inability to defend a competitive total despite a brilliant unbeaten century from Shahadat Hossain. Shahadat Hossain's unbeaten ton guides Bangladesh A to 232 After winning the toss and electing to bat, Bangladesh A endured a disastrous start as Ali Raza struck twice inside the first five overs. Captain Saif Hassan and Mahmudul Hasan Joy also departed cheaply, leaving the side struggling at 15/4. Shahadat Hossain then took charge of the innings, building a crucial 95-run partnership with Mahidul Islam Ankon to revive Bangladesh A's hopes. Ankon contributed 42 runs, while SM Meherob added 28. Shahadat remained unbeaten on 103 off 118 deliveries, striking seven fours and three sixes, as Bangladesh A finished with 232/8 in their allotted 50 overs. For Pakistan A, Sufyan Moqim was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets for 29 runs. Hasan Nawaz and Ali Raza claimed two wickets each. Hasan Nawaz leads Pakistan A's successful chase Pakistan A made a steady start to the chase but lost wickets at regular intervals, allowing Bangladesh A to remain in the contest. Hasan Nawaz, however, anchored the innings with a composed 62-run knock. His contribution proved crucial in keeping Pakistan A on course as they negotiated the target. Pakistan A eventually reached 233/5 in 45.2 overs to seal a five-wicket victory and advance to the final. Pakistan A to face Sri Lanka A in final Pakistan A will now take on Sri Lanka A in the title clash on Sunday, November 29, at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha. Sri Lanka A had booked their place in the final with an eight-wicket victory over India A in the first semifinal. They chased down India's 318-run target in just 41.3 overs, setting up a clash with Pakistan A for the tournament title.

title: What Did Formula 1 Drivers Think of the FIA's Surprise Kahoot Quiz in Qatar?
summary: Formula 1 drivers sat down with the FIA’s stewards in Qatar on Thursday, November 26, for their yearly talk about racing rules, and the governing…
content: Formula 1 drivers have their say after the annual meeting with the FIA stewards in Qatar. (Source: @evrythngformu1a/X) Formula 1 drivers sat down with the FIA’s stewards in Qatar on Thursday, November 26, for their yearly talk about racing rules, and the governing body turned it into a game. With drivers teed up to give answers on multiple choice questions via their phones, the FIA ran through a host of incidents that had taken place over the year, asking each driver what penalty they would have given. It’s an odd sight, a room full of the world’s fastest drivers tapping answers into a classroom quiz app. Kimi Antonelli , the newly crowned champion, came out of it happy. The Mercedes driver said “most of us in the room were all aligned” on the incidents they watched, and that the session helped the stewards “to see how we see certain scenarios”. The FIA held its annual meeting with Formula 1 drivers and stewards in Qatar on Thursday to review controversial incidents and penalties from the 2026 season. This year, the meeting took an unusual approach, with the FIA using Kahoot! to present multiple-choice questions about… pic.twitter.com/PX4Ov1RVgN — | ⁶³ | Kris | (@krisg7gr63) November 26, 2026 Max Verstappen agreed, telling reporters “It’s good to do that,” because it let stewards hear “our voices of what we think a penalty should be”, according to The Race . The turnout had its own storylines. Fernando Alonso was unwell and Lance Stroll chose not to attend, while Lewis Hamilton showed up after skipping the meeting the previous year. The seven-time champion was blunt about it: “I didn’t go last year but I’m going to go tonight, yes.” How the FIA Turned a Rules Meeting Into a Game The setup was simple. Options included different time penalties or no sanction, and drivers voted on each clip. Some of the incidents triggered unanimous agreement from drivers and stewards over the punishment handed out, while others left opinion more divided. Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen were happy with how the stewards’ meeting went. (Source: MEGA) The FIA had a clear reason for doing it this way. The format was meant to let drivers give more candid opinions than they might voice openly, and to show that some incidents are not clear-cut. Frankly, it’s a smart move: a driver who won’t criticize a rival’s penalty in front of 19 peers will happily do it with an anonymous tap. Antonelli said the split votes proved a point. Some cases are “so borderline that it’s so hard to establish who is at fault”, he said, and in those moments the call should “just need to be a racing incident and no penalty.” Antonelli believes Formula 1 drivers should just give back the position if they overtook off the track. (Source: MEGA) That fits a mood that had been building all week, and the real talk soon turned to what happens next. Formula 1 Drivers Push for Quicker Fixes on Corner-Cutting Before the meeting, Oscar Piastri had questioned where the penalty system was heading, saying some decisions looked especially harsh while others arguably warranted stronger action. Still, nobody walked out demanding a rewrite. No major rule changes were called for next year, though some change may come on track-limit advantages gained by cutting corners. Lewis Hamilton believes Formula 1 can improve a lot when it comes to policing on-track action. (Source: MEGA) Antonelli wants the fix to be fast. On drivers who cut a corner to pass, he said the best move is to “just tell the driver to drop the position straight away”, adding “if you give straight the position back is more fair as well.” Another idea on the table was a new sanction that would drop a driver from a guaranteed position at the end of a race, instead of a time penalty. Hamilton framed his return as a chance to “help the racing be better and the ruling system I’m sure we can improve.” Verstappen was more realistic about who holds the pen. After the drivers have their say, he said, “of course they make their minds up and they decide what they’re going to do next year”. That’s the catch with any feedback session. The votes are counted, but the drivers only find out if anyone listened the next time a steward’s decision lands on them in the heat of a race.

title: Gasly amused by Verstappen and Russell feud: 'I'm just eating my popcorn'
summary: Pierre Gasly has weighed in on the latest chapter of the bitter rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell, admitting that he is thoroughly enjoying watching the drama unfold from the sidelines. Tensions between Verstappen and Russell resurfaced during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend following an on-track altercation in the third and final free practice session, during which the pair made contact.
content: Pierre Gasly has weighed in on the latest chapter of the bitter rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell , admitting that he is thoroughly enjoying watching the drama unfold from the sidelines. Tensions between Verstappen and Russell resurfaced during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend following an on-track altercation in the third and final free practice session, during which the pair made contact. The incident reignited a rivalry that reached boiling point at the end of the 2024 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, when the two drivers publicly traded accusations following a controversial qualifying incident in Lusail. Verstappen added further fuel to the fire following his victory in Las Vegas, claiming that Russell was "so far below my level" and remarking that "karma is a bi**h" following the Mercedes driver's difficult evening. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Russell was subsequently given the opportunity to respond to the Dutchman's remarks ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, describing the situation as unnecessary. The Mercedes driver stood by his criticism of Verstappen following their practice clash but insisted that he had no intention of prolonging their feud, acknowledging that he might have been too open when speaking to the media. Verstappen, meanwhile, refused to be drawn into another exchange of words with his rival during his media commitments in Qatar, insisting that everything that needed to be said off track had already been said. Gasly enjoys watching Verstappen and Russell's rivalry unfold The ongoing feud has also attracted the attention of several other drivers on the grid, including Gasly, who briefly partnered Verstappen at Red Bull in 2019 and has known both drivers since childhood. The Alpine driver admitted that he was enjoying the spectacle, suggesting that neither the altercation in Las Vegas nor the subsequent war of words came as a surprise to him: "Not the first time, not the last time these two are going to go at it. From my side I'm just sitting and eating my popcorn laughing about it." Gasly also offered an insight into how he approaches disagreements with his former teammate, explaining that he prefers to address any issues directly with the Dutchman. "I think it was best with Max just to tell him right up in his face! He's someone that just takes anything," the Frenchman told Sky Sports. "You can have opinions, etcetera. I like both of them, obviously [they are] very different. We all know each other, we know each other since we were kids."

title: Hamilton reveals if he and Leclerc are still free to race after Las Vegas clash
summary: Lewis Hamilton has confirmed that he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other in the final two rounds of the season, despite their controversial collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The two Ferrari drivers were involved in several wheel-to-wheel battles throughout Sunday's race in Las Vegas, with their fight eventually resulting in contact.
content: Lewis Hamilton has confirmed that he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other in the final two rounds of the season, despite their controversial collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The two Ferrari drivers were involved in several wheel-to-wheel battles throughout Sunday's race in Las Vegas, with their fight eventually resulting in contact. Hamilton was sent into a spin following the collision with his teammate, while Leclerc subsequently received a 10-second time penalty for causing the incident. The seven-time world champion eventually crossed the finish line in seventh place, while Leclerc had to settle for tenth, bringing an already difficult weekend for the Maranello-based outfit to a disappointing conclusion after both drivers failed to progress to Q3 on Saturday. The incident prompted a strong reaction from Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur, who immediately requested a meeting with Leclerc over the team radio after the chequered flag. The Frenchman subsequently expressed his frustration with how the situation between his two drivers had unfolded. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Hamilton confirms freedom to race Leclerc Speaking to Sky Sports F1 ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Hamilton confirmed that Ferrari did not impose any new restrictions on its drivers, reiterating that avoiding contact remains their primary responsibility. “We're still free to race, and I think that's the ultimate goal of being here. We want to race, but of course we don't want what happened last week to ever happen.” Hamilton also reiterated that avoiding collisions between teammates had always been the number one rule at Ferrari, rather than a new instruction introduced following the events in Las Vegas. The Briton went on to discuss the outcome of his conversation with Leclerc in Qatar, having previously revealed details of their latest private talks earlier on Thursday: “Charles and I had a good sit-down earlier on and had our chat. And I think moving forwards, I think we can be fine.” Hamilton plays down intensity of Ferrari tensions Despite the events in Las Vegas and the subsequent scrutiny surrounding Ferrari's driver pairing, Hamilton insisted that he and Leclerc enjoy competing against one another. The seven-time world champion also suggested that the situation between the two Ferrari drivers appears considerably more intense from the outside than it actually is behind closed doors. “We do enjoy racing together and we do have a really good relationship. It's obviously intense. On the outside, it seems a lot more intense than it really is.”

title: Kimi Antonelli sets the pace in Qatar GP FP1 with commanding display
summary: Kimi Antonelli has topped the timing charts in the first practice session at the Qatar GP, finishing ahead of George Russell and Isack Hadjar. Antonelli’s lap time of 1:23.
content: Kimi Antonelli has topped the timing charts in the first practice session at the Qatar GP, finishing ahead of George Russell and Isack Hadjar . Antonelli’s lap time of 1:23.217 - set early on in the session on the medium tyres - was enough to pip Russell to top spot in FP1 at the Lusail International Circuit, hosting the penultimate Grand Prix of the 2026 F1 season. While only one aerodynamic upgrade has been brought to the Qatar GP - that of Audi, who bring an updated front brake duct deflector - practice will be crucial for understanding tyre performance on a weekend in which the FIA have imposed a 27-lap maximum limit on each tyre set for Sunday's race. Qatar GP FP1 - as it happened With cars quick as ever to get out for FP1, a lack of grip at the final corner was already causing problems in the opening stages. With drivers running wide on numerous occasions and gravel being dragged onto the circuit. Antonelli, however, started on good form - his 1:24.057 putting him just over eight tenths up on Charles Leclerc after just 10 minutes of FP1 action. The new world champion went quicker still after another five minutes - with teammate George Russell soon joining him at the top, albeit half a second down. Red Bull suffered a few teething problems in the first session, with Max Verstappen running sixth after the first 20 minutes. The Dutchman had immediately complained about a dark visor, while his teammate Isack Hadjar - who was up to third - appeared to clip a Red Bull mechanic after an early pit stop, but was told there were no major concerns. At the halfway stage, Antonelli had extended his lead on his Mercedes teammate to seven tenths with his 1:23.217 - now over a second ahead of Red Bull's Hadjar, whose teammate Verstappen had risen to fourth just prior to the soft tyre running. Even with the softs bolted on, however, the grid struggled to match the Italian, with Russell's best effort on the softs still putting him half a second down on his teammate, who had failed to go faster himself despite switching to the softs. In third again came Hadjar, 0.6s down on Antonelli, while Oscar Piastri took P4 ahead of Verstappen and the Ferrari duo - the latter over a second behind the young Mercedes driver. A frustrated Lando Norris then pipped his teammate to fourth, but was still eight tenths down from Antonelli. Here are the full results from FP1 at the Qatar GP:

title: Lando Norris Reveals Why He Sometimes Deletes Instagram amid ‘Chaotic’ F1 Season (Exclusive)
summary: “I don’t have TikTok. I’ve never had TikTok. I don’t even know what it looks like, thankfully,” the McLaren driver told PEOPLE exclusively at F1 Las Vegas
content: Lando Norris. Credit: Hector Vivas/Getty NEED TO KNOW Lando Norris says he deletes Instagram occasionally to disconnect during the demanding Formula 1 season The McLaren driver enjoys streaming sports and playing chess but avoids TikTok entirely Norris looks forward to the offseason, calling the season “pretty busy and pretty draining” Lando Norris knows how to unplug. The McLaren star, 27, opened up to PEOPLE exclusively about staying connected with his loved ones during the “chaotic” Formula 1 season , but shared why he “sometimes” has to delete social media from his phone. “I’m on my phone way too much,” Norris told PEOPLE at the T-Mobile Signature Store on the Las Vegas Strip ahead of his second-place finish behind Red Bull Racing star Max Verstappen at the 2026 Las Vegas Formula 1 Grand Prix on Saturday, Nov. 21. Lando Norris. Credit: Jayce Illman/Getty A natural competitor, the European driver is drawn to games, “playing chess,” specifically. Streaming also monopolizes Norris’ screen time when he’s not zooming around a track. “My friends stream as well,” he says, noting that he also watches “football or sports around the world.” “Whether it’s golf or MotoGP, football games, I watch a lot. I’m streaming a lot when I’m traveling, but sometimes I’ll doom scroll a little bit,” Norris continues. Although Norris has Instagram, TikTok does not occupy space on his phone. “I don’t have TikTok. I’ve never had TikTok... I don’t even know what it looks like, thankfully, I think,” he says with a laugh. “Instagram, I have every now and then. Sometimes I’ll delete it to stay away from it, but sometimes I also keep in touch with my friends and things online.” Lando Norris in action at the 2025 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. Credit: James Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty As for what Norris’ Instagram algorithm looks like? “It’s like golf swings and dogs or something,” he reveals. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Next, Norris will make his way to the Middle East to compete in the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit on Sunday, Nov. 29, followed by the final race of the F1 season, the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix at Yas Marina Circuit on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lando Norris with father Adam and mother Cisca pose on the grid during the F1 Grand Prix of Belgium on July 28, 2024. Credit: Kym Illman/Getty Norris has his sights set on the finish line — literally — joking that he’s been “looking forward ” to it since the start of the F1 season in early 2026. “I’ve been looking forward to December since January. I’ve been looking forward to a nice holiday. We didn’t have the longest offseason this year, so it was very, very short, only a couple of weeks,” Norris shared. “So I’m looking forward to it, especially because the end of the season is pretty chaotic,” he added, referencing the 20-plus Grand Prix races that take place within 10 months. “It’s pretty busy and pretty draining, so I need a good break.” Read the original article on People

title: Why Fernando Alonso reported a "broken engine" in Las Vegas – but Honda can’t find an issue
summary: Alonso retired in Las Vegas due to a suspected power unit problem, but engine supplier Honda says it cannot see anything in the data
content: Motorsport photo On his final lap of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Fernando Alonso called it a day. The two-time world champion locked up at the end of the long straight before telling the team over the radio: “Box, box, broken engine.” In the media pen afterwards, the Spaniard reiterated that something was wrong with the power unit in his Aston Martin: “The engine was down from the beginning of the race, I think. We saw already in qualifying that the engine was down and I think it was down the whole race as well. “So I was losing a lot of time on the straights, not only to the rest of the field but also to Lance. I think in the last two laps the engine completely gave up.” In the days that followed, engine supplier Honda examined all the data, but remarkably, chief engineer Shintaro Orihara revealed in Qatar that no problem had been identified. “After the weekend, we have checked all the data that we have now and also in the maintenance we have checked the engine physically. At this moment, we haven't found any issue on the engine from the data and also from the maintenance check, but again, we will check on Friday to see how the engine works at this track,” Orihara told media including Motorsport.com on Thursday. The latter is not only to see how the power unit performs at the Lusail International Circuit – a completely different type of track – but also to obtain more feedback from Alonso himself to determine whether this particular unit is still fit for use or whether an engine change is needed. “Yes, we carefully analysed his comments and we also respected his comments,” Orihara continued. “That's why we checked all the data and why we checked the engine condition. From the data, at this moment, we haven't seen any issue, but as I mentioned, we will check again on Friday to get some feedback from Fernando.” Shintaro Orihara, Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer of Honda Racing Corporation Shintaro Orihara, Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer of Honda Racing Corporation Orihara added that it was difficult for the drivers to feel exactly what was happening in Las Vegas, precisely because the circuit was extremely power-sensitive and energy-poor. “In Las Vegas, it was difficult to analyse how engine performance affected car speed, because there was a lot of torque effect and also different energy management across the two cars. Our metrics say that the power itself is okay, but we should probably check carefully at this track again.” Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack underlined the complexity of the situation and explained that the poor feeling Alonso experienced – which led him to believe there was a power unit problem – could also be related to MGU-K deployment and difficulties in that area. “I think we need to be careful because the MGU-K part is so much higher. And that means that as soon as you have a small variation in MGU-K [deployment], it could be felt like a problem with the internal combustion engine. And you have different MGU-K power in different places. So very often, it's much more difficult for drivers to judge than it used to be in the past, and I think some of it is coming from there.” Although some of the confusion may indeed stem from uncertainty surrounding MGU-K deployment, Orihara acknowledged that another part of it could simply come from sheer frustration. Both Alonso and Lance Stroll stressed that they were losing two seconds per lap purely due to a lack of power, meaning that, according to Orihara, Alonso's retirement could also be related to that frustration. “Please ask Fernando. From the data viewpoint, we haven't seen any issue, but probably this year our engine performance is not enough to give satisfaction or confidence to the driver and then probably they feel some, how to say, feeling that the engine performance is not great.” Stroll once again expressed that frustration during media day in Qatar, stating that under these circumstances the Aston Martin drivers cannot even put up a fight, particularly at a circuit such as Las Vegas. Read Also: George Russell: Max Verstappen comments "amusing", but I stand by what I said Max Verstappen without Gianpiero Lambiase at Qatar GP as Tom Hart steps in “We know the areas we're going to work on with the car, and what we have to improve on the chassis side, but going to races like Vegas and missing like two seconds with just the engine, there's really not much we can do. We just need a lot more power, and hopefully we get that next year.” Stroll is optimistic that Aston Martin will make progress on the chassis side for 2027, but immediately pointed out that such progress will be worth little unless the power unit improves considerably. “Everyone at Silverstone is pushing flat out to hit our targets. And then, like I said, the engine, it doesn't matter how good of a chassis you have, if you're missing two seconds of power on the long straights. I mean, then it's going to be almost impossible to compete. That's where we are, so we really hope we get a lot more power next year.” To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

title: Parker Washington Being Ruled OUT With Injury Opens The Door For A Jaguars' Fantasy Football Sleeper
summary: The latest injury update on Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington and the fantasy football impact.
content: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) runs upfield during the first quarter during an NFL football matchup at EverBank Stadium, Sunday, November, 1, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. [Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect In a brutal blow to fantasy football owners, the Jacksonville Jaguars will be without star wide receiver Parker Washington this week and perhaps beyond this week. After re-aggravating an AC joint injury in practice this week, the team has ruled him out, and he is considered week-to-week. BREAKING - The Jaguars have ruled out WR Parker Washington (shoulder) for Sunday's game, per @AdamSchefter He's considered week-to-week. - SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) November 27, 2026 Fantasy Impact WR Parker Washington, Jacksonville Jaguars This is a crushing injury for Washington, who is in the midst of a breakout season. He has already caught 44 passes for 748 yards and six touchdowns this season. An AC joint sprain in his shoulder will likely cost him at least two weeks and will make him susceptible to re-injury for the remainder of the season. All fantasy owners can do is hope he heals up and that this doesn't derail his season. We are going to need him for the fantasy football playoffs. QB Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars Losing his top target is going to be rough for Lawrence, who could see his fantasy value drop while Washington is sidelined. We wouldn't expect a drop significant enough that we would bench him, but this will cap his upside a bit. The Jags offense is hurting right now, with Bhayshul Tuten also looking very questionable this week with an ankle injury. Lawrence has a lot to overcome this week and perhaps the next few weeks, but he should still be a starting-quality fantasy quarterback. WR Jakobi Meyers, Jacksonville Jaguars Meyers is the wideout we expect to step into the lead receiver role. He should lead this offense in targets. The issue is that he lacks the big-play ability that Washington has. Look for Meyers to get a nice bump in PPR leagues, raising his floor, but he's still not a ceiling play. WR Brian Thomas Jr, Jacksonville Jaguars Even with Washington being inactive, we still aren't overly interested in starting BTJ. Granted, this certainly does make him a more intriguing flex option, but not intriguing enough that we want to start him. His floor is non-existent. WR Josh Cameron, Jacksonville Jaguars This is the player who could legitimately break out if given the opportunity with Washington sidelined. We have seen him flash a few times this season, and this rookie has looked good. By no means are we looking to start him this week; however, if you have the roster space, stash him now because he could be a hot waiver-wire target by the time we get to Tuesday. title: Eastleigh to keep Hill, Bristow & Bartram in charge
summary: Eastleigh confirm that Richard Hill, Jason Bristow and Vince Bartram will continue to oversee first-team affairs.
content: Richard Hill is in his fourth spell in charge of Eastleigh, having guided them to promotion to the National League in 2014 [Shutterstock] Eastleigh have confirmed that Richard Hill, Jason Bristow and Vince Bartram will continue to oversee first-team affairs for the foreseeable future. The trio have been in charge of the side on an interim basis since Matt Gray was sacked earlier this month. Former manager Hill had conducted post-match media affairs after Eastleigh's past two games - a 3-1 win at Tamworth and a 3-1 home loss to Yeovil Town. The club had won just one of their final eight matches under Gray and are currently 18th in the National League. The news comes days after owner Stewart Donald confirmed to fans he will leave the club at the end of the season. "Given the ongoing uncertainty surrounding the club's ownership, the board believes it is right to manage the first team within our existing resources," a statement released by Eastleigh read. "Our priority remains securing our place in the National League. "We also want to put together a strong run in the FA Trophy and carry that momentum into our league performances." The club has also confirmed Gray's assistant Jason Goodliffe has left the Spitfires by mutual consent.

title: Eight-time MotoGP champion Marc Márquez announces surprise retirement
summary: Eight-time MotoGP world champion Marc Márquez has announced his retirement at the age of 33, calling time on his 13-year career.
content: Eight-time MotoGP world champion Marc Márquez has announced his retirement at the age of 33, calling time on his 13-year career. Márquez is coming off a successful title defense in Portugal last week, where he claimed the 2026 MotoGP World Championship, tying Giacomo Agostino with eight championships each. In a nod to the iconic cue-card scene from the movie "Love Actually," Márquez announced his retirement on Thursday, Nov. 27 by turning over five sheets of paper, each displaying part of his message, during the broadcast of the first Free Practice at the Valencia Grand Prix – the final race of the season. The cards, shown in sequence, read: “We’ll talk later, but first … Thank you to everyone who’s been part of this journey … I hope you’ve enjoyed it as much as I have. … This will be my last race in MotoGP. … We made history.” MARQUEZ LAST RACE IN MOTOGP?!?! 😳Marquez breaks the news with a Love Actually message 🫶#MotoGP | #ValenciaGP | Live on TNT Sports and HBO Max https://t.co/JqTsHn1Rij — TNT Sports Bikes (@bikesontnt) November 27, 2026 The decision came as an even greater shock given that Márquez had signed a two-year contract extension with Ducati as recently as June, leading many to believe he would continue racing for several more seasons. "I arrived in MotoGP in my own way, and I will leave in my own way," Márquez said in a news conference. "From 2013 until now, I enjoyed it a lot. Many people in the paddock helped me to enjoy it." "I enjoyed my journey" ❤️Marc Marquez hosts an special press conference following the news 🎙️#MotoGP | #ValenciaGP | Live on TNT Sports and HBO Max https://t.co/h3KJmRLEQ2 — TNT Sports Bikes (@bikesontnt) November 27, 2026 Although Márquez referenced his arm during the press conference, he did not elaborate on whether injuries or other factors influenced his decision to retire. Márquez joined the Honda factory team in 2013 and, over the next decade, secured six championship titles. In 2024, he transitioned to Ducati, racing alongside his brother Álex Márquez before moving up to the factory team, where he captured two more championships. title: ILT20: Sherfane Rutherford's explosive fifty powers MI Emirates to 36-run win over Abu Dhabi Knight Riders
summary: Sherfane Rutherford produced a stunning batting display, scoring 51 off just 18 balls, while Nicholas Pooran remained unbeaten on 42 off 33 deliveries. Their efforts helped MI Emirates post a massive 207/4 in 20 overs. The bowlers then stepped up to restrict the Knight Riders to 171/7.
content: MI Emirates registered their second win of ILT20 Season 5 after beating Abu Dhabi Knight Riders by 36 runs at the Zayed Cricket Stadium on Thursday. Sherfane Rutherford produced a stunning batting display, scoring 51 off just 18 balls, while Nicholas Pooran remained unbeaten on 42 off 33 deliveries. Their efforts helped MI Emirates post a massive 207/4 in 20 overs. The bowlers then stepped up to restrict the Knight Riders to 171/7. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Zahoor Khan picked up two wickets each, while Rashid Khan kept things tight with figures of 1/13. Sunil Narine was the standout bowler for the Knight Riders, taking 1/11, including a maiden. Rutherford, Pooran power MI Emirates to 207 After being asked to bat first, MI Emirates got off to a flying start. Openers Kusal Perera and Muhammad Waseem attacked the bowling and added 77 runs for the first wicket in 52 balls. Perera scored 33 off 23 balls, while Waseem contributed 41 off 37 deliveries. The opening pair helped MI Emirates reach 57 without loss in the powerplay. Sunil Narine provided the Knight Riders with their first breakthrough in the ninth over when he dismissed Perera, who was caught behind. Abdullah Tarakhail, making his ILT20 debut, then struck twice to bring his team back into the contest. The Afghanistan pacer removed Waseem and Tajinder Singh (10 off 8), leaving MI Emirates at 124/3. The scoring rate slowed down for a while, with MI Emirates managing just one run in the 17th over. However, Rutherford and Pooran changed the momentum with some powerful hitting. The pair collected 17 runs each in the 18th and 19th overs to take the score to 177/3. Rutherford then took the attack to Knight Riders captain Jason Holder in the final over. He smashed three consecutive sixes off the first three deliveries to bring up his half-century in just 17 balls. However, he was caught on the fourth delivery. Kieron Pollard joined Pooran in the middle and made an immediate impact, hitting two more sixes. He scored 12 off just two balls as MI Emirates finished with a massive 207/4. Holder had an expensive outing, conceding 62 runs in his four overs. The last three overs alone cost the Knight Riders 64 runs. Farooqi, Zahoor lead MI Emirates' bowling attack Chasing 208, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders began aggressively and collected 17 runs from Farooqi's opening over. However, the MI Emirates pacer bounced back quickly. He bowled Andre Fletcher (16 off 12) in the third over before dismissing Gulbadin Naib (5 off 6) in the fifth. The Knight Riders were reduced to 50/2. Zahoor Khan then removed Finn Allen (26 off 21) in the eighth over to put further pressure on the home team. Alishan Sharafu and Moeen Ali tried to revive the chase with a 45-run partnership off 27 balls. Both batters scored 36 runs, but Rashid Khan broke the stand by bowling Sharafu in the 13th over. Zahoor returned to dismiss Moeen in the 16th over, making the chase even tougher for the Knight Riders. Sunil Narine (4 off 15) retired out on the final ball of the 17th over. Andre Russell (6 off 3) was then bowled by Chris Jordan in the 18th over. Jason Holder (14 off 8) and Tarakhail (11 off 7) added some late runs, but the Knight Riders could only manage 171/7 in their 20 overs. Player of the Match Sherfane Rutherford spoke about his conversations with Kieron Pollard and Nicholas Pooran during the innings. "(Kieron) Pollard and I had a chat about how you have more time than you think, and Pooran and I spoke about taking it deep. We were looking at 179-180, but the last two overs changed the game. I enjoyed it a lot, and I didn't realise it was three sixes in a row. It was good of Pollard to come in and finish it off." Abu Dhabi Knight Riders captain Jason Holder admitted that his team did not play well enough and failed to finish the bowling innings strongly. "We were outplayed and a little flat. We bounced back nicely in the middle phase of our bowling innings but lost it at the back end. It's about executing better with bat and ball, and we didn't take a couple of chances early. We are a lot better than what we showed today, and I'm not worried. We'll assess when we review the game, and I wouldn't change anything I did today." Brief scores MI Emirates: 207/4 in 20 overs (Sherfane Rutherford 51, Nicholas Pooran 42*, Muhammad Waseem 41; Sunil Narine 1/11, Abdullah Tarakhail 2/44). 136214746 Abu Dhabi Knight Riders: 171/7 in 20 overs (Alishan Sharafu 36, Moeen Ali 36, Finn Allen 26; Zahoor Khan 2/38, Fazalhaq Farooqi 2/43). Player of the Match: Sherfane Rutherford.

title: Newcastle United star banned from driving after being caught using phone at the wheel
summary: The court heard the international footballer was filmed by a cyclist while he was stationary in traffic
content: Newcastle United star Sven Botman has been banned from driving after he was caught using his mobile phone at the wheel. The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) confirmed that Botman, 26, pleaded guilty at Newcastle Magistrates Court on Wednesday. The Dutch international defender was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued. The MoJ said Botman was fined £900 and ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 surcharge. Court documents show that Botman was in a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone. Sven Botman joined the Magpies in 2022 and signed a four-year contract extension in January 2026 (Getty) According to The Sun, the court heard he was filmed by a cyclist while he was stationary in traffic. The Dutch centre-half was signed by Newcastle in a £32 million deal from French club Lille during the summer of 2022. Since signing for the Magpies, Botman has made 124 appearances and was part of the squad that won the League Cup in 2025, their first major trophy in decades.

title: Runners brave wind for Thanks for Giving Day Run
summary: Nov. 27—KINGSTON — Impending winds and rain may have postponed the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, but the forecast did little to deter the more than 500 runners and walkers who came out bright and early Thursday to participate in the Friedman JCC's annual Ben August Thanks for Giving Day Run. Runners of all ages were bundled up against the cold, with many dressed up for the ...
content: Nov. 27—KINGSTON — Impending winds and rain may have postponed the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, but the forecast did little to deter the more than 500 runners and walkers who came out bright and early Thursday to participate in the Friedman JCC's annual Ben August Thanks for Giving Day Run. Runners of all ages were bundled up against the cold, with many dressed up for the holiday in festive shirts, colorful tutus and hats shaped like turkeys. Inside the Friedman JCC, runners were offered a brief reprieve from the chilly morning air, both before and after the run. There was a coffee station set up, t-shirt pick-up, and plenty of snacks and water to fill up on once the race was finished. Monte Kester, 16, of Ellettsville, Indiana was the first person overall to finish the run Thursday. "I'm visiting family here for the holiday," he said, breathless after crossing the finish line. All proceeds from the race benefited Sara's Food Pantry. Additionally, those who brought donations for the food drive earned a free raffle ticket. "The community just makes this so much fun," said Crystal Wright, the JCC's director of programming and marketing. "It really kick-starts the holiday season." Thursday's memorial run was 28-year-old Nicole Grant's first run ever. "My friends were doing it and I wanted to be healthier too," said Grant, the Harveys Lake resident. Ellen Meehan of Kingston and Shaelan Brown of Wilkes-Barre love participating in the run every year. "It's just a great way to get out and get the blood flowing," Brown said. For Meehan, the run was a way to honor one of her best friends, Joe Soprano Jr., the Times Leader's longtime executive editor who died in 2025. "He was in my run group, and this was one of my last races with him before he got too sick," she said. "I run every race in his honor now." Runner Caroline Straus, 38, of Silver Spring, Maryland, was also visiting family Thursday. Straus, who grew up in Northeastern Pennsylvania, was excited to finally run a race she had long known about. "I'm glad the weather held off for it. It was windy for sure, but at least it wasn't raining," Straus said. "It felt good once you got going." Local journalism matters, and your support makes it possible. title: Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 in Australia despite hitting ‘the worst shot’ he has ever hit as a pro
summary: Cam Smith vaulted himself back into contention at the Australian PGA Championship on Friday. Smith shot a superb round of 64, one that even featured a bogey.
content: Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images Cam Smith vaulted himself back into contention at the Australian PGA Championship on Friday. Smith shot a superb round of 64, one that even featured a bogey. The 33-year-old Australian carded seven birdies and an eagle during his second round at The Lakes on Friday. Cam Smith is now sitting just four shots adrift of the leader, Nicolai von Dellingshausen, with 36 holes left to play. Smith is looking to win his fourth Australian PGA Championship this week, and if he carries on playing like he did on Friday across the weekend, he will have a great chance to do just that. Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 at the Australian PGA Smith wasn’t entirely happy with his opening round in Australia on Thursday, so he would have been delighted to see such drastic improvements on day two. The former LIV Golf star spoke to reporters after shooting a second-round 64 and responded when asked to give his verdict on his current form. “Yeah, I think so, it’s definitely going to be a different year. I’m excited. I haven’t done the European stuff before, and just starting at home is pretty special,” Smith said. “I got in a bit of a groove and rhythm today, which is what we’ve been looking for. We’ve been searching for that and it finally kind of all came together today.” However, not everything went swimmingly for Smith. The 2022 Open champion hit what he described as probably the worst shot he has ever hit as a professional on the par-three 15th hole. However, after leaving himself a full wedge shot into the green, he holed a 25-foot putt to salvage his par. “That might have been the worst shot I’ve ever hit as a professional,” said Smith. “It wasn’t a shank, but it was close. It definitely kind of kept the momentum going, for sure.” Cam Smith will be hoping to avoid any more card-wrecking shots like the one he hit on the 15th hole on Friday. If he manages to post two rounds in the 60s over the weekend, he may well have a chance of winning the fourth Australian PGA Championship of his career.

title: Jackson Koivun Doubles Career Earnings After Dramatic Win Over Brooks Koepka
summary: Jackson Koivun has doubled his career earnings after winning the 2026 Farmers Insurance Skins Game at Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida. The young American defeated Brooks Koepka in a closest-to-the-pin playoff on the 18th hole to claim the final skin worth $2 million. Koivun produced a better shot from 118 yards, with his …
content: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun Jackson Koivun has doubled his career earnings after winning the 2026 Farmers Insurance Skins Game at Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida. The young American defeated Brooks Koepka in a closest-to-the-pin playoff on the 18th hole to claim the final skin worth $2 million. Koivun produced a better shot from 118 yards, with his ball finishing just inside Koepka’s. Koivun finished the event with $2.375 million after collecting four skins. The win gave him another big moment in a year that has already seen him make his mark on the PGA Tour. ALSO READ: Phil Mickelson Tips Jackson Koivun as Golf’s Next Big Star Jackson Koivun Beats Brooks Koepka for $2 Million The final hole produced the biggest moment of the competition after the value of the skin had carried over to $2 million. Koivun, Koepka, Justin Thomas and Wyndham Clark were all in contention as the event reached its closing stages. The players could not settle the final skin during regular play, which meant the contest went to a closest-to-the-pin playoff. ALSO READ: Nick Faldo Calls on Former LIV Golf Stars to Help Pay Unpaid Suppliers Thomas and Clark failed to find the green with their shots. Koepka then hit his ball close to the hole, putting pressure on Koivun to produce something better. The 21-year-old responded with a shot from 118 yards that finished just inside Koepka’s. That was enough to give him the victory and the $2 million prize. Koivun had already won three other skins during the event, taking his total earnings to $2.375 million. Koepka finished with $700,000, while Thomas collected $475,000 and Clark earned $450,000. ALSO READ: Brooks Koepka Reveals Frustration With Former Teammate Ahead of The Skins Game Jackson Koivun Continues Impressive Year The victory adds to what has been a successful year for Koivun. He turned professional after a standout college career at Auburn and quickly made an impression on the PGA Tour. Koivun claimed his first PGA Tour victory at the 3M Open in July , beating Scottie Scheffler by three shots. The win also helped him earn a place on the United States team for the Presidents Cup. He went on to finish the competition unbeaten, recording two wins and one tie. His performances have helped establish him as one of the young players to watch on the PGA Tour. The Skins Game gave Koivun another opportunity to compete against established players, and he made the most of it by beating Koepka in the final playoff. His $2.375 million payout also added a significant amount to his career earnings. Koivun will now look to build on his recent success as he continues his PGA Tour career. After winning the 3M Open and now claiming the Skins Game title, the 21-year-old will hope to carry that form into the next stage of his career. Main Photo Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

title: Eau Gallie faces Merritt Island, Holy Trinity eyes region championship
summary: Eau Gallie and Merritt Island square off for Class 3A, Region 2 title while Holy Trinity hosts Santa Fe Catholic for spot in Independent title game.
content: Eau Gallie, Merritt Island and Holy Trinity are still standing in the state football playoffs and they’ll compete for a regional championship Nov. 27. In Class 3A, Eau Gallie heads to Merritt Island in a rematch for a spot in the state semifinals. The Commodores seek their second state semifinal appearance in the last three years. Merritt Island eyes its first final four appearance since 2021. Holy Trinity, making its first-ever appearance in a regional final, hosts Santa Fe Catholic for a place in the Independent League Pool B state championship game. Here’s a preview of the two regional finals. Class 3A, Region 2 (2) Eau Gallie (8-4) at (1) Merritt Island (12-0). 7:30 p.m. When the season began, Eau Gallie and Merritt Island were expected to be the last two teams standing in Region 2. That came to fruition Nov. 21 after both teams won at home. Merritt Island defeated Santa Fe 49-32 behind 534 total yards of offense. It averaged 15.7 yards per play. Mustangs senior Kevin Verpaele threw five touchdowns on 11 completions racking 305 yards. He also rushed for a 41-yard touchdown. Verpaele spread out his 11 completions to five different pass catchers. Junior Tim Sedaros caught four balls for 85 yards and one touchdown. Sophomore Elijah Mitchell caught two touchdowns for 83 yards. Senior Drew Sarver recorded a 55-yard touchdown reception and senior DeShaun Thomas scored one touchdown. On the ground, junior Zaylan Chapple rushed for 146 yards and one touchdown. He scored the final Mustang touchdown on an 80-yard run. Chapple also tallied 67 receiving yards. Merritt Island’s defense limited Santa Fe’s run-heavy offense to six first-half points as it finished with four players with at least 10 tackles. Mustangs senior Elijah Floyd produced 15 tackles, seniors Alain Adams and Tory Love posted 11 tackles and senior Nathan Schafer recorded 10 tackles. Mustangs junior Amarri Hamilton sacked Raiders quarterback Gavin Peterson twice. Schafer and Love finished with one sack. Eau Gallie took down previously unbeaten The Villages Charter 42-35 behind a breakout performance from sophomore X’Zavier Corbin. Corbin, who missed eight straight games with an injury, returned to the field for the first time since Sept. 4 and ran the ball 21 times for a career-high 321 yards and two touchdowns. Commodores junior Troy Silberzahn caught eight passes for 110 yards and one touchdown. Senior Joseph Allen finished with 179 passing yards and one touchdown. On Oct. 9, Merritt Island rallied from an eight-point deficit with 2:01 remaining in regulation to tie the game with 41 seconds left. In overtime, Verpaele scored on a 4-yard touchdown run. Eau Gallie senior Donovan Richardson scored on a 1-yard run, but Allen was stopped shot of the end zone on a two-point conversion attempt in a 36-35 win for the Mustangs. Eau Gallie outgained Merritt Island 411-389 as Allen threw for 248 yards and Richardson rushed for 88 yards. Allen threw two touchdowns to junior Yusef Francis and ran for one. Richardson scored one touchdown on the ground. Verpaele recorded 186 passing yards and Chapple gained 71 yards to pace the Mustangs. The pair combined for all five Merritt Island touchdowns. Commodores junior Gabriel Player returned an interception for a 25-yard touchdown. Senior Kayden Jaquez totaled 12 tackles and senior Zay Floyd finished with 10 tackles. Mustangs junior Jonas Walters led the team with 11 tackles and Hamilton recorded one sack. A key factor in determining who wins could be penalties and special teams. Eau Gallie committed 19 penalties for 171 yards in the regular-season defeat. It also had two PATs blocked. Independent League Pool B, South Region (2) Santa Fe Catholic (10-2) at (1) Holy Trinity (9-2), 7 p.m. Holy Trinity will look to extend its history-making season by one more game in the regional final versus Santa Fe Catholic. The Tigers defeated Central Florida Christian Academy 44-21 in the regional semifinals on Nov. 21. After CFCA made it a one-score game at the half, Holy Trinity shut out the Eagles 16-0 in the second half. Despite allowing 521 yards, Holy Trinity’s defense came up with critical stops in the red zone. It forced CFCA into two turnovers on downs and one fumble when the Eagles were inside the Tigers’ 5-yard line. Tigers freshman Jadiel Corbin posted 10 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and one sack. Senior Brady Wright also recorded 10 tackles. Holy Trinity seniors Ben Silsbee and Chandler Hendley intercepted one pass. Corbin and junior Zach Curran recovered one fumble. Holy Trinity sophomore Jacorey Mills anchored the offense with 23 rushes for 290 yards and four touchdowns. Sophomore Jackson Mobley threw an 18-yard touchdown pass to freshman Ayden Williams and rushed for a 3-yard score. Santa Fe Catholic advanced to the final following a 24-14 win over Evangelical Christian on Nov. 19. The Hawks’ two defeats came to Class 1A regional finalist Lakeland Christian on Aug. 21 and Class 1A state playoff qualifier Zephyrhills Christian Academy on Oct. 23. The Hawks’ offense goes through their running game as they’ve rushed for 2,333 yards this season. Santa Fe Catholic senior Reagan Korlacki leads the team with 1,536 yards and 18 touchdowns. Korlacki posted eight games of at least 100 yards rushing. On defense, Santa Fe Catholic junior Bertran Bates is tied for eighth in the state with 17 sacks this season. He also sports a team-high 72 tackles and 27 tackles for loss. The Hawks recorded 19 takeaways with 10 interceptions and nine fumble recoveries. Sophomore Jeremiah Dunn posted a team-high three interceptions and three fumble recoveries. title: Lumen Christi's Herb Brogan sets MHSAA football record for coach wins
summary: Jackson Lumen Christi football coach Herb Brogan set the MHSAA career wins record in the 2026 Division 6 state finals Friday at Ford Field.
content: A new coach stands alone at the top of the all-time wins leaderboard in Michigan high school football . Legendary Jackson Lumen Christi coach Herb Brogan won his 444th career game on Friday, Nov. 27, with the Titans' 50-22 win over Almont in the MHSAA Division 6 state final at Ford Field. Brogan, 77, passed former Farmington Hills Harrison coach John Herrington for the most career wins by a coach in Michigan high school football history. Brogan is now 444-98 in 47 seasons, starting in 1980, with 14 state titles. With the win, Lumen Christi also earned a fifth straight state title (three in Division 6, two in Division 7), tying the state record for the longest consecutive title streak. THE GAME: Jackson Lumen Christi wins 5th straight title vs Almont Lumen Christi football now has 16 state championships, three more than Harrison in second place, and remains tied with Novi Detroit Catholic Central for the most state title appearances (19) in state history. Watch MHSAA football finals live/on demand Lumen Christi's two-headed rushing attack of Ayden Gatewood and Brennan Brogan was on full display Friday, with Gatewood getting 10 carries and Brogan getting four on the 14-play drive. Gatewood finished off the nearly eight-minute drive with a 2-yard touchdown run, giving Lumen Christi the early lead. After Almont answered to take a brief 8-7 lead early in the second quarter, Lumen Christi stormed back with 28 straight before halftime to take command. title: Smithson Valley stops Medina Valley's triple option in 52-10 playoff win
summary: Smithson Valley reeled off four straight touchdowns in the second quarter to break open the game and advance to the state quarterfinals for the fourth straight season.
content: Smithson Valley's Caleb Peagler reacts to a second half touchdown versus Medina Valley during their clash of undefeated teams in the Class5A Division 1 Regional semifinal game Friday afternoon at Farris Stadium. (Robin Jerstad/Contributor) Smithson Valley shut down Medina Valley's triple-option attack to post a 52-10 victory in a Class 5A Division I regional semifinal Friday afternoon at Farris Stadium. The Rangers limited the Panthers to 230 yards on the ground, 180 below their average, to advance to the state quarterfinals for the fourth straight time. "We came out every day, trusting our coaches and just doing our jobs," Smithson Valley junior defensive lineman Kipton Grabhorn said. "Assignment football. That was pretty much it." Smithson Valley scored 49 unanswered points to take a 52-3 lead early in the fourth quarter. Senior running back Caleb Peagler led the Rangers with 171 yards and three touchdowns on 25 carries. The Rangers outgained Medina Valley 376-269 in total yardage. "It's one thing to be unconventional, but to be unconventional and be that good at it, that's a tribute to Medina Valley," Smithson Valley coach Larry Hill said of the Panthers' offense. "But, it's a tribute to our kids today. They paid attention in film. They knew what kind of precision and discipline it was going to take to always be in the right place at the right time because if you are a foot late, they score." Smithson Valley (12-0) faces either Boerne Champion or Austin Anderson in the next round. Smithson Valley defeated both during the regular season. Medina Valley (12-1) finished its first season back in Class 5A ranks with a second straight district championship. The Panthers won their most games in a season since going 16-0 in its 1984 Class 3A state championship season. The Rangers burst for four touchdowns in the second quarter that turned a 3-3 tie into a 31-3 halftime lead. Peagler rushed for touchdowns of 39 and 12 yards during that span. His 39-yarder broke the 3-3 tie and his second score made it 31-3 with 13 seconds left in the second quarter. Medina Valley's Mason Kennedy grabs the facemask of Smithson Valley's Caleb Peagler during their clash of undefeated teams in the Class5A Division 1 Regional semifinal game Friday afternoon at Farris Stadium. (Robin Jerstad/Contributor) Gunnar Shoquist scored on a 20-yard run, and Ty Knutson reached the end zone from 14 yards on a keeper for the other two touchdowns. The Rangers extended their lead to 38-3 when Knutson connected with sophomore Schaeden Davis for an 8-yard score in the third quarter. That was enough to force Medina Valley out of its triple-option base and into its little-used passing attack. And, the Panthers found success with it when quarterback Hunter Hurtado passed to Brady Fillinger for 21 yards. However, he fumbled and the Rangers returned the ball to the Medina Valley 46. That led to Shoquist's 23-yard scoring run and a 45-3 lead at the 4:56 mark of the third quarter. Peagler closed out the Rangers scoring with a 1-yard run to extend the lead to 52-3 lead early in the fourth quarter. Smithson Valley extended its winning streak to 25 games - a run that included last year's Class 5A Division I state title 28-6 victory against Frisco Lone Star. The Rangers are halfway to earning a chance for a state-title three-peat. "Any time you go out there, you get a little more experience," Hill said. "All of our guys are getting ready to play the 14th one this year. We've got a handful of guys who've been in some even bigger games, and I don't know if that's a dominant factor, but it sure as heck can't hurt."
