title: Pablo Torre points to real reason LeBron James didn’t attend Kobe Bryant’s funeral
summary: NBA legend Kobe Bryant’s impact on basketball is still felt today, years after his life was tragically lost in a California helicopter crash. In fact, Bryant’s signature Nike shoes are still the most worn sneakers in the NBA, leaving behind his wife, Vanessa, and three daughters. However, one question has lingered since the celebration of…
content: Credit: David Richard-USA TODAY Sports, The Adam Friedland Show NBA legend Kobe Bryant’s impact on basketball is still felt today, years after his life was tragically lost in a California helicopter crash. In fact, Bryant’s signature Nike shoes are still the most worn sneakers in the NBA, leaving behind his wife, Vanessa, and three daughters. However, one question has lingered since the celebration of his life: Why wasn’t LeBron James seen attending? James was a member of the Los Angeles Lakers at the time, and throughout their careers, the two battled each other to be recognized as the best player in the NBA, and they seemed to even hae a friendly, if not all that close, relationship. In a recent appearance on The Adam Friedland Show, investigative sports journalist Pablo Torre, who noted at the time that James’ attendance wasn’t confirmed, broached the subject again. “That’s just one of these like, look, the whole thing is it was like a state funeral. It was the highest, it was a royal wedding funeral kind of thing,” Torre said. “One of the big criticisms was, why are you policing whether someone is at their, you know, colleague’s funeral or not? And the whole point was not that I care or am policing or am saying that LeBron should have mourned in such a way. It was merely the fact that this was so public… Like, it was at Staples Center. Yeah. And so it’s this like giant thing where there are a thousand, literally thousands of people there.” “And it was the one time we saw Michael Jordan not be a prick,” Friedland interjected. “In the entire time we’ve known him. He was crying and he was in pain.” “Michael and Kobe and LeBron, there is this triangle of egos and feelings,” Torre said. “And why did LeBron feel like he wanted perhaps people to think, or why was he okay with people thinking he was there while he wasn’t? “Because he didn’t want to say that Vanessa Bryant didn’t want him there?” Friendland proposed. “And that’s the subtext,” Torre responded. “On a human level, for Bron to watch that, my understanding is that, you know, Jordan does not really acknowledge him. Him and Kobe saw themselves in one another. And imagine you were 23 your whole life, and this guy’s crying over this other guy, and he won’t, like, talk to you,” Friendland said. “And understanding that story, I think, puts into context LeBron in a way that I would be sympathetic to.” Torre agreed, responding, “Yes.” The post Pablo Torre points to real reason LeBron James didn’t attend Kobe Bryant’s funeral appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

title: Pacers vs. 76ers Prediction: Preview, Injury Report, Advantages, X-Factors
summary: LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey lead the Philadelphia 76ers against Indiana Pacers with NBA Cup knockout stage qualification at stake.
content: Nov 25, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts after his three pointer against the Miami Heat during the second quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Indiana Pacers welcome the Philadelphia 76ers to Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Friday, November 27, for an NBA Cup matchup carrying big stakes for the visitors. Tipoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET. The Sixers lead the Eastern Conference at 15–4 after beating the Miami Heat 111–104 on Wednesday. Indiana is 6–12 and coming off Monday’s 125–120 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder , which snapped a four-game losing streak. Philadelphia has won both previous meetings this season, including a 131–124 victory on November 15. A win clinches East Group B for the 76ers; a loss eliminates them. The Pacers still have a narrow route to qualification. Injury Report Pacers T.J. McConnell: Questionable (Left hamstring injury management) Larry Nance Jr.: Questionable (Right ankle bruise) Kelly Oubre Jr.: Questionable (Right hand laceration) Tyrese Haliburton: Out ( Left hamstring strain) Johnny Furphy: Out (Right ACL surgery) Ben Sheppard: Out (Left meniscus surgery) 76ers Joel Embiid: Questionable (Illness) Jaylen Brown: Out (Left hamstring injury management) Why The Pacers Have The Advantage? Indiana’s clearest advantages are extra rest, home court, and a favorable interior matchup. The Pacers last played Monday, giving them three days off before facing a Philadelphia team that played Wednesday. Indiana ranks fourth in pace at 101.2 possessions per 48 minutes. Its 111.3 offensive rating ranks 21st, its 114.1 defensive rating ranks 16th, and its -2.8 net rating ranks 20th. The Pacers need to turn their speed into efficient opportunities rather than simply adding possessions. Pascal Siakam leads the team with 22.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.7 assists, shooting 50.7% overall and 37.0% from three. He can attack mismatches and provide a reliable scoring option when Indiana’s initial action breaks down. Andrew Nembhard adds 16.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 7.6 assists, shooting 42.9% from the field and 41.6% from outside. His decision-making will be essential against Philadelphia’s experienced defenders. Ivica Zubac averages 11.0 points and 9.1 rebounds on 55.0% shooting. If Joel Embiid sits, Indiana should involve Zubac through screens, rolls, and offensive rebounding opportunities to test Philadelphia’s smaller frontcourt options. Philadelphia ranks 23rd in rebounding at 42.3 per game. Indiana should attack that weakness through purposeful cuts and committed rebounding, rather than asking its struggling perimeter shooting to carry the entire offense. The Pacers rank eighth in assists at 27.7 per game but 29th in three-point percentage at 33.3%. Their passing must produce better shots, especially when Philadelphia crowds the paint. Why The 76ers Have The Advantage? Philadelphia’s strongest advantage is its ability to create quality possessions through experienced decision-makers. The Sixers rank 10th in offensive rating at 115.4, 15th in defensive rating at 113.6, and 12th in net rating at plus-1.8. Those numbers give them a stronger overall foundation than Indiana. Ball security is another strength. Philadelphia commits a league-low 11.9 turnovers per game and ranks sixth in free-throw attempts at 26.5. Protecting possessions and generating trips to the line can help the 76ers control a road game even when their rotation is depleted. Tyrese Maxey averages 25.9 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 5.7 assists, shooting 49.7% from the field and 37.4% from three. His acceleration creates problems for defenders trying to stay attached through screens, and Philadelphia will need him to maintain that pressure with Brown unavailable. LeBron James contributes 17.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 6.9 assists, shooting 48.5% overall. His ability to organize possessions and find cutters becomes especially valuable when Philadelphia has fewer established scorers available. X-Factors For Indiana, Obi Toppin averages 11.9 points and 4.2 rebounds, shooting 48.9%. Quenton Jackson adds 8.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 2.8 assists. Their activity can help the Pacers maintain pressure when Siakam or Nembhard rests. VJ Edgecombe becomes more important with Brown sidelined. He averages 13.9 points, 6.3 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 1.7 steals, shooting 46.2% overall. Anfernee Simons supplies 10.5 points and shoots 40.2% from three, giving the Sixers another potential source of offense. Jabari Walker averages 6.9 points and 4.6 rebounds, while Dominick Barlow has supplied 9.0 points and 4.7 rebounds across three appearances. Prediction The Sixers have a narrow edge despite their injury concerns. Indiana can exploit the interior and its rest advantage, but Philadelphia still has the stronger late-game creation through Maxey and James. Embiid’s return would strengthen that pick considerably. Without him, the 76ers will need disciplined rebounding and meaningful support from their reserves. I expect a competitive game, with Philadelphia protecting the ball and producing the better possessions in the closing minutes. Prediction: Pacers vs. 76ers 112-116

title: Spurs vs. Lakers Prediction: Preview, Injury Report, Advantages, X-Factors
summary: Lakers' Luka Doncic and Spurs' Victor Wembanyama headline a blockbuster showdown between the Western Conference's top two teams.
content: Mandatory Credit: Ed Szczepanski-Imagn Images The San Antonio Spurs host the Los Angeles Lakers at Frost Bank Center on Friday, November 27, in a meeting between the Western Conference’s top two teams. Tip-off is scheduled for 9:30 p.m. ET. The Lakers lead the West at 15–3, while the Spurs are second at 15–4. Los Angeles beat the Utah Jazz 109–94 on Monday and has won 11 of its last 12 games. San Antonio is looking to recover from Wednesday’s 116–111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers despite Victor Wembanyama’s 44 points and 16 rebounds. Both teams are 2–1 in NBA Cup play, tied with the Golden State Warriors and Portland Trail Blazers in West Group C. A loss eliminates either side. Injury Report Spurs De’Aaron Fox: Questionable (Right shin contusion) Dylan Harper: Questionable (Left hip external rotator strain) Tobias Harris: Out (Left calf strain) Jayden Quaintance: Out (Right knee surgery) Lakers Austin Reaves: Questionable (Left heel contusion/bone bruise) Why The Spurs Have The Advantage? San Antonio has been the more complete team statistically. The Spurs rank fourth in offensive rating at 118.3, third in defensive rating at 106.8, and first in net rating at +11.4. The biggest difference is rebounding. San Antonio leads the NBA with 48.4 rebounds per game, while Los Angeles averages 41.3, ranking 26th. The Spurs also lead the league in blocks at 6.5 per game. Extra possessions and difficult finishes could offset some of the Lakers’ offensive firepower. Victor Wembanyama averages 30.7 points, 12.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 3.8 blocks, shooting 54.3% from the field. His influence extends beyond blocked shots: the Lakers must account for his reach when attempting layups, throwing interior passes, and attacking the offensive glass. San Antonio also allows a league-low 19.3 free-throw attempts per game. Maintaining that discipline matters against a Los Angeles offense that regularly generates trips to the line. The Spurs need to challenge shots without turning difficult possessions into easy points. If De’Aaron Fox or Dylan Harper returns, San Antonio can spread its creation across more players and reduce the pressure on Wembanyama to manufacture every important basket. Fox is averaging 12.4 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 5.8 assists in 28.9 minutes per game, shooting 47.1% from the field and 26.5% from three-point range, while Harper is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 4.5 assists in 31.7 minutes per game, shooting 50.5% from the field and 31.5% from three-point range. Why The Lakers Have The Advantage? Los Angeles brings a stronger shooting profile and additional rest. The Lakers have had three days off since playing Monday, compared with one for San Antonio. The Lakers rank third in offensive rating at 119.2, 11th in defensive rating at 112.4, and sixth in net rating at +6.8. Their 119.4 points per game rank third, while their 48.6% field-goal shooting ranks second. The Lakers also rank second in free-throw attempts at 29.8 per game. That creates a direct contest between their ability to draw contact and San Antonio’s defensive discipline. Getting Wembanyama into foul trouble will change the entire game. Luka Doncic leads the NBA in scoring at 36.6 points per game, adding 6.6 rebounds and 7.7 assists. He shoots 46.0% overall and 36.5% from three. His combination of scoring and passing gives the Lakers a reliable creator when the game slows down. If Austin Reaves returns, he would be of great help. Reaves is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 4.7 assists in 35.3 minutes per game, shooting 51.3% from the field and 40.9% from three. The Lakers also shoot 36.6% from three, ranking seventh, compared with San Antonio’s 28th-ranked 33.4%. A great perimeter showing could nullify the Spurs’ superiority on the glass. X-Factors Stephon Castle averages 16.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 6.3 assists, shooting 37.7% from three. His creation becomes especially important if Fox and Harper remain unavailable. Devin Vassell adds 11.9 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 2.8 assists, although his 39.9% field-goal shooting leaves room for improvement. Julian Champagnie supplies 11.1 points and 4.3 rebounds while shooting 40.3% from three. Keldon Johnson contributes 8.6 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.5 assists. San Antonio needs their complementary production to prevent the Lakers from concentrating entirely on Wembanyama. For Los Angeles, Walker Kessler averages 14.0 points, 10.8 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks on 66.9% shooting. His ability to finish Doncic’s passes and compete for rebounds is central to the Lakers’ chances. Quentin Grimes adds 12.4 points and 3.2 assists while shooting 40.3% from deep. Matisse Thybulle averages 7.8 points and 2.3 steals, with 40.5% three-point shooting. His defensive activity could disrupt San Antonio’s creators. Prediction I’m taking the Lakers. This is a statement game for Los Angeles, and I expect them to answer questions about their championship credentials with a road win over one of the West’s strongest teams. The Lakers’ extra rest, superior perimeter shooting, and ability to generate free throws give them a clear route to victory. I trust Doncic to control the tempo, draw San Antonio’s defense toward him, and create quality opportunities for his teammates. The Spurs’ rebounding and rim protection will test them. The Lakers must finish defensive possessions and limit careless turnovers. I expect Los Angeles to execute better down the stretch and deliver a performance that quiets the critics. Prediction: Spurs vs. Lakers 115-123

title: ‘Can’t Make This Up,’ ‘They Always Come Back for the Lakers’ — LA Fans Lament Familiar Pattern As Spurs’ Dylan Harper Receives Early Injury Status Upgrade
summary: The San Antonio Spurs upgraded Dylan Harper to questionable for Friday’s showdown with the Los Angeles Lakers, opening the door for the 20-year-old guard to return just 10 days after injuring his hip. The timing drew attention from Lakers fans, who have theorized for years that injured opponents tend to get healthy just in time to face their team, sometimes ahead of schedule.
content: 'Can't Make This Up,' 'They Always Come Back for the Lakers' — LA Fans Lament Familiar Pattern As Spurs' Dylan Harper Receives Early Injury Status Upgrade The San Antonio Spurs upgraded Dylan Harper to questionable for Friday’s showdown with the Los Angeles Lakers, opening the door for the 20-year-old guard to return just 10 days after injuring his hip. The timing drew attention from Lakers fans, who have theorized for years that injured opponents tend to get healthy just in time to face their team, sometimes ahead of schedule. The Lakers enter Friday’s matchup against the Western Conference’s second-place Spurs (15-4) boasting the league’s best record (15-3), with both teams vying for an NBA Cup quarterfinal berth. Dylan Harper’s Injury Update Fuels Long-Running Lakers Fan Theory Harper suffered a left hip external rotator strain during the Spurs’ 105-93 home loss to the Detroit Pistons on Nov. 17, finishing with 20 points in 35 minutes. San Antonio has gone 3-1 in Harper’s absence, with Julian Champagnie moving into the starting lineup. The Spurs could also get De’Aaron Fox back Friday, as the star guard is listed as questionable after missing the last two games with a bruised right shin. However, Harper’s potential early return raised the most eyebrows. “Dylan Harper (hip) was reported likely to miss 2 weeks with a 1-3 week range. Friday’s game (against the Lakers) is 10 days out from his injury,” Underdog NBA pointed out Thursday. A Friday return would fall within Harper’s reported recovery window but come four days earlier than the two-week estimate. LA fan page LakeShowYo was quick to flag the news, quipping, “Dylan Harper upgraded to questionable tomorrow vs. the Lakers even though he was supposed to miss 3 weeks. Welcome back.” One fan aimed squarely at the doubters who dismiss the conspiracy: “People swear Lakers fans are crazy to think this always happens.” “They always come back for the Lakers,” another reacted. “Lakers on the schedule has the healing powers of God,” a third fan joked. For one more fan, the timing was simply too suspicious: “LOL you can’t make this up.” Even LA superstar Luka Dončić weighed in on the subject in March 2025. “I didn’t believe it before, but they say if somebody is out a long time, then they play against the Lakers,” Dončić acknowledged . “So I didn’t believe it at the time, but obviously it’s the Lakers, so I think that’s normal.” READ MORE: ‘Must Win,’ ‘Big Game’ – Victor Wembanyama Makes Feelings Clear on Spurs’ Massive NBA Cup Matchup vs. Lakers Of course, Harper has yet to be cleared to play. The Spurs will provide another update on his status in Friday’s injury report. If Harper suits up, San Antonio will regain its second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama (30.7 points per game). Through 15 appearances, the sophomore guard is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 4.5 assists a night, shooting an efficient 50.5%. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Today in Boston Celtics history: 2nd-highest point total vs. Baltimore Bullets
summary: Today in Celtics history, the storied club matched their own record for the most points scored in an NBA game taking place in a regular season contest.
content: Today in Boston Celtics history, the storied ball club matched their own record for the most points scored in an NBA game taking place in a regular season contest since the start of the shot clock era. The record was equaled with a 153-107 blowout of the (then) Baltimore Bullets (now, Washington Wizards ). The win tied identical high scores by the Celtics against the Philadelphia Warriors (now Golden State) in 1962, and against the Detroit Pistons two seasons prior, trailing only a nearly impossible to believe 173-point total scored against the (then) Minneapolis Lakers (now, Los Angeles) in 1959. Hall of Fame wing John Havlicek led the Celtics with 33 points, 10 assists, and as many rebounds. Point guard Jo Jo White added 25 points, 5 boards, and 9 assists, while Steve Kuberski and Don Chaney chipped in 22 points apiece. Hondo's triple-double was joined by double-doubles from Kuberski and big man Dave Cowens, and the Celtics had seven players score in double figures in the win. Historic milestones It is also the date of a Celtic completing the rarest play in professional basketball, the four-point play (a foul on a made 3-pointer) by former Boston center Kelly Olynyk. Oddly enough, it also came in a win against the Wizards -- this time 111-78. This article originally appeared on Celtics Wire: Today in Boston Celtics history: 2nd-highest point total vs. Baltimore Bullets

title: 10 Eagles things I think I think after incredible comeback vs. Cowboys
summary: One of the most improbable wins in Eagles history.
content: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field with the Madden Thanksgiving MVP trophy after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Incredible. There’s no other way to describe the Philadelphia Eagles’ comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys — which was way more enjoyable than any meal you could consume on Thanksgiving. This is an Eagles game that’s going to be remembered forever, just like the Christmas Day win over the Cowboys in 2006 and the Miracle at the Meadowlands comeback in 2010. The victory is that improbable, especially when the Eagles were down 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter. They had no business being in this game, yet they found their way back to make it a game — and stole a victory away from the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. This was a game the Cowboys should have won handily. Instead they choked it away, thanks to the hands of a resilient Eagles team that didn’t let their 3-7 record stand in the way of what seemed to be an insurmountable deficit. No matter how the rest of this season goes, that was one heck of a win. This victory will be talked about amongst generations of Eagles fans. A Thanksgiving miracle — that may have ended the Cowboys season. The Eagles are good at ruining seasons all of a sudden. 1. What else can you say about Joe Milton? Milton delivered one of the greatest performances my a quarterback in Eagles history. What Milton did against the Cowboys was absolutely incredible, and this was more than a quarterback showing off his ridiculous arm talent. The final stat line: 21-of-31, 311 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT, 10.7 YPA — 121.8 rating. 3 carries, 15 yards, TD. There are only two quarterbacks in Eagles history with 300+ passing yards, 3+ passing TD, 1+ rushing TD, and average 10+ YPA in a game — Milton and Michael Vick (2010 at Commanders). That’s how well Milton played on Thanksgiving — in just his third career start. Once the Eagles trailed 31-10, Milton went 11-of-16 for 181 yards with 2 TD, 1 INT and a 120.1 rating (averaging 11.3 YPA). He also had 15 yards and a rushing touchdown in that stretch to bring the Eagles back from three scores. This level of play was throughout the game. Milton used his arm strength to keep the Eagles offense moving, going 11-of-19 for 278 yards with 3 TD, 1 INT and 14.6 YPA on throws that traveled 10+ air yards — finishing with a 120.1 passer rating. He was 2-of-6 for 95 yards and 2 TD with 0 INT for a 121.5 passer rating on throws that traveled 25+ air yards. Any completion on passes that traveled 25+ air yards was a touchdown. The Eagles had some exciting performances from Jalen Hurts over the years, but that was arguably the most exciting passing performance by a quarterback since Nick Foles threw for 471 yards against the Houston Texans in 2018 (and that was an Eagles’ win too). Impressive performance by Milton, finally giving life to an Eagles offense that badly needed it. 2. The most impressive feat of Joe Milton’s day? Milton had a touchdown pass that traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, and that wasn’t the most impressive aspect of his performance. He threw an interception into triple coverage with 7:14 to play when the Eagles were trailing 38-3, which seemed to be the backbreaker with how the defense was playing. The Eagles got the ball back and Milton goes 4-of-4 for 70 yards and a 24-yard touchdown to Makai lemon on the ensuing drive — netting a perfect 158.3 passer rating. The poise and ability to forget that interception immediately following the interception spoke more volumes about who Milton is as a player than anything else he accomplished on Thanksgiving. When Milton made a boneheaded play, he responded in the way winning quarterbacks respond. He hasn’t even been on his team for two months and was able to shake that play off and perform at an even higher level. Since the interception, Milton finished 6-of-9 for 84 yards with a touchdown and a 133.6 passer rating. He led the Eagles to victory with a touchdown drive and set Jake Elliott up with his game-winning field goal. Want to know how to stick around as a starting quarterback in the NFL? Moments like that. 3. Joe Milton might have locked up QB2 One of the few things I wanted to see in the remainder of the season was if Milton could play well enough to be the QB2 next year. Judging Milton through two starts was tough, given the state of the offense and the changes the Eagles were making to accomondate his game. Milton didn’t get to throw the deep ball much, and he missed when he had his opportunity last week to DeVonta Smith. He didn’t miss any of those opportunities on Thanksgiving, hitting two of them for 95 yards and two touchdowns. On throws that traveled 20+ air yards, Milton went 6-of-11 for 188 yards and 3 TD with 0 INT — a 139.2 passer rating. The arm strength was clearly on display, along with the accuracy on the deep ball. Milton was relentless facing pressure too, finishing 7-of-10 for 154 yards with 3 TD and 0 INT for a 152.1 passer rating — while also being sacked five times. He was 6-of-8 for 145 yards with 3 TD and 0 INT on throws from outside the pocket — 156.3 rating. Backup quarterbacks don’t have games like this. QB5’s — which is what Milton was when he signed — really don’t have games like this. This performance may have locked up QB2 for Milton next year. If Milton can stack up good-to-solid performances, he’ll be the QB2 on the Eagles (at least). Milton may get a starting opportunity elsewhere too (he is a restricted free agent), but the Eagles can control his fate there as well. The situation needs to play itself out, but Milton is certainly on the radar around the league. He’s earned it. 4. That victory had to be bittersweet for Joe Milton When Milton was making incredible throws against the Cowboys, I couldn’t help but think of his journey to get to this point. Over the last four months, Milton was cut by the Cowboys after losing the QB2 job to Sam Howell —toiling on the practice squad for five weeks. Any team could have claimed Milton when he was waived, and no team did. Any team could have signed Milton from the Cowboys practice squad to the active roster, and no one did. The Eagles signed Milton to the active roster when Jalen Hurts was lost for the season due to blood clots in his lungs. If Hurts wasn’t done for the year, the Eagles wouldn’t have brought in Milton. He literally was their QB5, the fifth quarterback to make the active roster. Tanner McKee got three starts before the Eagles turned to Milton, Andy Dalton told the Eagles he had a better opportunity with the Atlanta Falcons. Milton wasn’t considered by the Cowboys and 31 other teams until the Eagles needed a quarterback. To have a performance like that against a team that cut him and chose Sam Howell over him had to be bittersweet — especially since he led the Eagles to a 21-point comeback on the road against that team on Thanksgiving in just his third start. Certainly Milton will soak that all in at some point, but the battle to succeed and have a moment like that are why sports are so great. Even when Milton was counted out, he wasn’t. 5. Legendary performance from DeVonta Smith There were questions whether DeVonta Smith was a WR1 earlier this season. There shouldn’t be any following Thanksgiving. Smith finished with 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns in the win over the Cowboys, the first Eagles’ player to get 200+ receiving yards in a game since DeSean Jackson in 2010. He had the most receiving yards on Thanksgiving since 1945 — and the second-most by any player on the holiday in NFL history. Smith had two touchdown catches of 45+ yards, the first player to do that on Thanksgiving since Randy Moss in 1998. He had more receiving yards on Thanksgiving (200) than A.J. Brown has the whole season (128). How good was the Milton-Smith connection? Milton was 11-of-14 for 200 yards with 2 TD, 0 INT and a 158.3 passer rating when targeting Smith — 14.3 yards per attempt. He hit Smith on throws of 24, 50, 45, and 23 yards of those 11 completions, and also hit him six times on throws of 10+ air yards. When Smith is healthy, he’s very good. He wasn’t even fully healthy in this one, injuring his lower back trying to make an insane catch in the fourth quarter on a Milton deep ball. Smith could barely run at full speed the rest of the way, yet still was able to go out and make plays. Smith has 42 catches for 551 yards and 4 TD in six games. He’s averaging 91.8 receiving yards per game, a 17-game pace of 1,561 yards. With the injuries, Smith is still on pace for 851 receiving yards (and those numbers will go up if he’s good enough to play). Milton has an excellent chance to stick around with Smith on the field. That connection was brilliant on Thanksgiving. 6. The Eagles play hard for their coach Hard to state the claim the Eagles have given up on Nick Sirianni based on the last two games. A win against the Pittsburgh Steelers to end a seven-game losing streak is a gut-check victory. Stealing a game on Thanksgiving against the Dallas Cowboys is in unchartered territory. The Eagles were down 21 points with 3:35 left in the third quarter. They had eight plays in the quarter that went for 1 yard at that point, while the defense allowed 31 points on seven possessions and 6.7 yards per play. They could have packed it in and allowed Dallas to continue to roll. They didn’t. The Eagles not giving up in a season that has experienced injury after injury (including the multiple starters that left the game), team captains and long-time starters getting traded, the handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, and the uncertain future of the coaching staff speaks volumes of how Nick Sirianni prepares his team during the week. No matter what Sirianni does during a game (and after), his players are still playing for him. The message is still getting across to the players in that locker room and the Eagles don’t believe their playoff chances are dead yet. If Sirianni is back after this season, this is the reason why. This locker room has no checked out on him, and they are demonstrating that with their performance on the field. Any team could have called it a day down 31-10 late in the third quarter. Not the Eagles, who had their biggest comeback in 16 years. 7. About that Nick Sirianni postgame fan interaction I understand why Sirianni acts like he does. Sirianni is a very emotional individual and a competitor who puts his heart and soul into coaching. Going on a seven-game losing streak took its toll on Sirianni, who spent weeks trying to figure out what was going on with his football team. This is a head coach who was 59-26 (.694 win percetatge) after his first five seasons, making the playoffs all five years and winning a Super Bowl while appearing in another one. Sirianni is fighting for his team — and his job. The last two months have been brutal. The Eagles head coach gets caught up in the moment with fans a little too much. He lets his emotions get the best of him. I’m not even sure if he was interacting with Eagles fans or taunting Cowboys fans, but it was enough where he had to be pulled away by Dom DiSandro. Sirianni shouldn’t be putting himself in that situation, and he’s done it far too much. I like that he’s authentic, but that is taking it too far. The Eagles head coach shouldn’t care what the fans think of him, good or bad. It’s clear Sirianni hears what’s said of him and acts on it when he wins. Sirianni gets over the top with this stuff, a silly distraction after the massive win. The Eagles have enough issues to worry about inside the Jefferson Health Training Complex. 8. Jake Elliott — stone cold Can’t speak enough on how good Jake Elliott has been all season. Elliott’s two field goals on Sunday were the reason the Eagles won, and he gave the Eagles their first lead of the game on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left — and the kick would have been good from 65 yards. Elliott had ice in his veins when making that kick, just like the majority of clutch kicks he’s made in his career. Elliott is 14-of-14 on field goals in the final minute of a game in regulation or overtime, 5-of-5 on kicks of 50+ yards in one-score games. He’s 2-for-2 in those situations this season, and 1-of-1 on game-winning field goals. Elliott has improved to 5-of-5 on 50+ yard field goal attempts, after being 5-of-15 (33.3%) on those kicks over the previous two seasons. Elliott is 8-of-9 (88.9%) on 40+ yard kicks this season after going 20-of-34 (58.9%) on those kicks over the previous two seasons. The comeback is incredible, and why the Eagles chose to adamantly defend Elliott this offseason. Just an amazing season from Elliott, who might be in line for an All-Pro campaign. 9. Hats off to Ty Robinson This Eagles comeback doesn’t happen without Robinson, who made the most of his opportunity when his number was called. Robinson had three pressures in seven pass-rushing snaps, an insane pressure rate of 42.9%. One of those pressures was the fourth-down sack on Dak Prescott on 4th-and-1 with 55 seconds left — the first one of Robinson’s career. This was a player who wasn’t even guaranteed to make the roster once training camp started, and earned his way onto this team with his play in training camp. That play set the Eagles up to steal the game, and set off a fire in Dallas on whether Brian Schottenheimer should have punted or went for it — enough where his job is in question. Robinson was able to make that massive of a presence as a pass rusher, and deserves more playing time going forward. Oh, and Robinson also blocked a punt that was recovered by Kenny Moore for a touchdown. That play was massive in the Eagles’ comeback, and cut the deficit to 31-24 with 13:53 left in the game. Robinson should have been credited with a forced fumble in this game too, but I digress. Robinson is the first player in Eagles history to record a sack and a blocked punt in the same game. This is a player that logged just 73 defensive snaps this season prior to Thursday. The Eagles have something with Robinson. They traded Jordan Davis for multiple reasons. 10. It was nice to see this team move the ball in the second half The Eagles entered this game with the worst second-half offense in football. The 4.6 point average in the second half was last in the NFL. So was the yards per play (3.6), average yards in second half (110.1), and net yards per attempt (4.3). The only major statistic that wasn’t 32nd was yards per carry — 30th at 3.3. This week was significantly different. The Eagles scored 22 offensive points in the second half (29 total), averaging 6.9 yards per play and gaining 200 yards of offense. They averaged 5.4 yards per carry and 8.5 net yards per attempt — all this while only converting 20% of third downs. This was the worst team in football in the second half, and they’re still last in the league in offensive points scored (6.2), yards per play (3.9), and average yards in second half (118.3). yards per carry moved up to 29th (3.4) and net yards per attempt improved to 31st (4.8). The Eagles even scored in the third quarter! Milton’s touchdown pass in the third quarter was just the second touchdown scored by the Eagles in the third quarter all season — the other one was against the Cowboys. They improved their third quarter scoring average to 30th in the league (2.1 points). This offense in the second half underwent a complete 180, and it didn’t start out that way (first eight plays went for a yard). Amazing turnaround once Milton hit Smith on that 45-yard touchdown with 24 seconds left in the third quarter. Can the Eagles build off this? Hopefully. Bonus: Enjoy this win (enjoy all of them). This is one the city of Philadelphia will talk about for a long time, even better since this season has been a disaster and this matchup seemed like a easy victory for the Cowboys (I didn’t even think the Eagles could score 20 points when I was watching Dallas film on Monday). You’ll remember where you were and who you were with when the Eagles pulled off this comeback. The Eagles are 4-0 against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving and Christmas — all games in Dallas. Happy Thanksgiving everyone!

title: 3 Titans to watch vs. Jaguars in Week 12
summary: Three Tennessee Titans players who need to play well versus the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 12.
content: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 22: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans looks on before the game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans are severe underdogs versus the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday . It represents another tough outing for a 1-9 Titans team that has recently played these same Jaguars, Dallas Cowboys, and Cincinnati Bengals. We’ve got three Titans players who need big-time performances in Week 12. QB Cam Ward Titans quarterback Cam Ward has played three quality games consecutively. Last time out versus the Jaguars, he was 28-of-39 for 231 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. Ward also scrambled for 39 yards. Anthony Campanile’s defense limited explosive plays. Ward was tasked with taking what an elite defense gave him, and he did an excellent job staying patient and efficient. The Jaguars will adjust defensively. We’ll see if Brian Daboll’s offense can replicate the success from the first matchup. WR Carnell Tate Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate returned to the lineup versus the Dallas Cowboys last weekend following a two-game absence (three weeks with the bye) due to a shoulder injury. Tate’s day wasn’t volume-heavy, but he did produce a highlight-worthy moment. He caught a short Cam Ward slant pass, noticed he was untouched, got up and ran the ball into the end zone for a 59-yard touchdown. Tate missed the Jaguars contest from Week 10. Ward still managed to play pretty impressively. The offense is looking forward to a do-over with Tate in the lineup. LB Anthony Hill Jr. It was a fairly uneventful return to the starting lineup for rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. against the Cowboys. He missed the Jaguars game with a neck injury. Hill only had six tackles in Dallas, and allowed three catches for 63 yards (21.0 YPC). The Titans started Cedric Gray and Dorian Mausi at linebacker versus the Jags. Hopefully getting Hill back is a boost versus a Jaguars rushing attack that could be without starting RB Bhayshul Tuten. Hill is due for a bounce-back showing.

title: 4 things that stood out in Bills' wild Thanksgiving win over Chiefs
summary: Here are Sal Maiorana's observations following Thursday's night thrilling 13-10 victory over the Chiefs.
content: ORCHARD PARK - Outside of pulling off one of the ugliest yet most important victories in their recent history, perhaps the most important thing that happened Thursday night for the Buffalo Bills is that they proved to themselves, and to a football nation watching on Thanksgiving, that it isn’t always just about Josh Allen. There is a widely held perception that the Bills would be lucky to be a slightly above-.500 team if not for their superstar quarterback, and there’s probably some truth in that because he is, without question, a transformative player. However, for one cold, crazy, rainy, and windy night at Highmark Stadium, Allen played about as poorly as he’s ever played, yet the Bills found a way to beat arguably their No. 1 rival, defeating Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on a simply incredible game-winning walk-off 57-yard field goal by Tyler Bass. "We’ve got to play better, but look: I think it’s important you find different ways to win football games," coach Joe Brady said. "If your fastball is not on, do you still have another pitch in your arsenal? ... If we can win football games when our best football player isn’t having to be Superman, it’s only going to pay dividends as we go, because we know what Josh Allen is capable of being." When Allen was asked about the premise that he carries the team on his broad shoulders week after week he said, “You can look at it that way. But I didn't play great tonight. I didn't play great last week, so I got to continue to get better and continue to elevate my game and find ways to help this team win because right now I'm putting this team behind the eight-ball. Two turnovers in the red zone. That's not going to be winning football all the time.” The weather was abysmal and it had a major impact on both Allen and Mahomes, and really, the entirety of both offenses. Ball handling was as difficult as the footing and neither team was functioning anywhere close to its expected level. But Allen was particularly bad. He misfired several passes, made some bad decisions, and the two red-zone interceptions took at least six points off the board, and maybe 14. The first one was particularly damaging because the Bills were set up to possibly take a 14-0 lead before he tried to hit Dawson Knox in the end zone and George Karlaftis got a finger on the ball and sent it fluttering into the arms of safety Alohi Gilman. The second pick came after the Chiefs had taken a 10-7 lead in the third when Allen threw a terrible pass to Khalil Shakir who had the ball slip through his arms and go right to Nohl Williams. “That was one of the grossest weather games I think I've ever played,” Allen said. “I've played in cold games, I've played in rain games, but cold rain games are tough. But everyone's got to play in it, myself included. The other teams’ got to play in it. T-Bass’ got to play in it, and he made two of the best kicks you'll see. So everybody's doing their part. I got to do mine.” Here are a few observations from the game: The Bills’ defense was outstanding There will be no asterisks attached to this victory because this wasn’t Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Cade Klubnik or Kyle McCord who they shut down - it was a future Hall of Famer and three-time Super Bowl champion. “It feels great, man,” cornerback Dee Alford said of the defense holding the Chiefs to 10 points, 13 first downs, 241 yards, and 2-for-11 on third downs. “I think as a group, we don't really care who we're playing against. We can go out and do our job and execute. Everyone doing their 1/11th. We try to block out the outside noise. Obviously we've seen a lot of people saying backup quarterbacks, so you got to take stuff like that personal. Continue to grow.” What was impressive is how the defense shut down the Chiefs at the end. Kansas City marched to a go-ahead touchdown on its first possession of the third quarter and from there on, they went three-and-out three times and had one good drive where they made three first downs, only to see struggling kicker Harrison Butker miss a 46-yard field goal. In their 10 possessions, the Chiefs punted seven times, five of those of the three-and-out variety. “I mean, it builds on the confidence we already had,” linebacker Terrel Bernard said. “We knew we were a good group. We've been playing good football. We just wanted to come out here and do it again.” A huge instant replay went the Bills’ way Who knows how this game would have turned out had a pass originally ruled to be a first-down catch by Rashee Rice not been overturned by replay. There was 1:51 remaining when Rice appeared to make a great catch after getting hammered by Amani Hooker which would have been a first down at their own 20. Instead, replay showed the ball just barely touching the ground when Rice crashed to the soggy turf. "We were first told that they were reviewing the spot, so I didn't even know that we were reviewing the catch," Mahomes said. "From my angle, when I threw the ball, I thought his hand was under the ball." Ed Oliver had a different opinion. "He was all excited, like, 'Yeah, they caught it,'" Oliver said of center Creed Humphrey. "I watched it back and I was, like, 'Aw, he dropped it.' He was still in disbelief, but I knew. Soon as I (saw) the ball hit the ground, I knew it. That just the defense a boost of energy, a boost of life, getting off the field." And then the defense had to get off the field again. Despite starting at the Chiefs 47 with a chance to win the game, the Bills’ offense went backwards and punted, but Mahomes could do nothing and that’s what led to the game-winning field goal. Greg Dortch made a great play Of course, there would not have been a heroic moment for Bass without the heads-up play by Dortch, the best punt returner the Bills have had in years. Ex-Bill Matt Araiza took the snap with 15 seconds left and lofted a 45-yard punt to the Bills 44 where Dortch made the catch, then maneuvered his way 17 yards to the KC 39 where he was tackled with four seconds left. It felt like it wasn’t enough because it left Bass with a 57-yarder, but as it turned out, it was more than enough. Dortch has been quite a find for the Bills , signed after training camp when the Lions released him after Ray Davis proved that punt returns were not really his thing. The Rochester native leads the NFL with 23 punt returns while his 9.5-yard average is 12th, right around league average. However, he has given the Bills an extra benefit on kickoffs, something he only really started doing full-time in 2025 when he was with the Cardinals. On 25 kickoff returns he has averaged 28.0 yards to rank sixth. “That last sequence there, the punt (by Tommy Doman) to get them down there, defense to go three and out, obviously G-baby (Dortch) with the return getting us into a position where we can go out there, and T-Bass nails it,” Allen said. James Cook had another big game With the awful weather conditions, the Bills knew they had to rely on Cook to run the ball, and man, did they ever rely on him. Cook tied his career-high with 32 carries and every one of his 117 yards was a grind against a stout Kansas City defense led by coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. Cook’s performance helped the Bills possess the ball for nearly 37 minutes, always a good strategy when you’re playing against Mahomes. And when he scored the Bills’ only touchdown in the second quarter, Cook tied an NFL record with 10 straight games with a rushing TD and at least 75 yards gained. He’ll have a chance to break the mark he now shares with Terry Allen (1995-96) next week, but Cook’s achievement is a record for one season. One issue that became evident Thursday night, though, is with Cook’s workload pacing to be an all-time high, he has no help when he needs a breather. Ray Davis did nothing with his four carries, gaining just six yards and there might be a case to give Frank Gore Jr. a chance off the practice squad because Ty Johnson is specifically on the team to be the third-down back, not Cook’s immediate backup. Sal Maiorana has covered the Buffalo Bills for more than four decades including 37 years as the full-time beat writer/columnist for the D&C. He has written numerous books about the history of the team, and he is also co-host of the BLEAV in Bills podcast/YouTube show. He can be reached at maiorana@gannett.com, and you can follow him on X @salmaiorana and on Bluesky @salmaiorana.bsky.social. This article originally appeared on Rochester Democrat and Chronicle: 4 things that stood out in Bills' wild Thanksgiving win over Chiefs

title: 49ers Get Positive Injury Update on WR Mike Evans Ahead of Seahawks Game
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are preparing for a massive divisional showdown against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium. And while the 49ers have some concerning names on their injury report as of Thursday, including quarterback Brock Purdy, who’s missed the last two days of practice, they did get some positive news on veteran […] The post 49ers Get Positive Injury Update on WR Mike Evans Ahead of Seahawks Game appeared first on HEAVY.
content: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with Jake Brendel #64 after scoring a two-point conversion against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are preparing for a massive divisional showdown against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium. And while the 49ers have some concerning names on their injury report as of Thursday, including quarterback Brock Purdy, who’s missed the last two days of practice, they did get some positive news on veteran wide receiver Mike Evans. 49ers Get Positive Update on Evans After sitting out Wednesday’s practice as he continues to deal with Achilles tendinitis, which caused him to miss the three previous games before last Sunday’s win over the Minnesota Vikings, Evans returned to practice Thursday in a limited capacity. That will likely be the routine for the 33-year-old moving forward. He probably won’t see much action during Wednesday’s practices, with the goal of logging at least limited work Thursday and Friday. That should put him in a good position to be ready to play each Sunday. 49ers practice report for today: Limited: Mike Evans (Achilles) Dre Greenlaw (neck) Deommodore Lenoir (foot) Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) Carver Willis (illness) No practice: Brock Purdy (ankle) Jordan Watkins (groin) Siran Neal (knee, foot) https://t.co/Uiy6xgRlUP — Coach Yac 🗣 (@Coach_Yac) November 26, 2026 Evans’ 2026 Season With 49ers While Evans has battled some injuries in his first season with the Niners, he’s been dominant in his connection with Purdy whenever he’s been on the field. Against Minnesota, he led the team in receiving with six catches for 109 yards and a touchdown, adding to his season totals of 33 receptions for 529 yards and four touchdowns in seven games. Evans Speaks About Dealing With Injury In Mexico City last weekend for the game against Minnesota, Evans spoke about dealing with Achilles tendinitis. “If any of you have tendinitis in any area, you know it just takes awhile too get warmed up,” Evans said after the 49ers’ Week 11 win. “So that’s all it was. I had a really great warm up and I didn’t feel it much throughout the game.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post 49ers Get Positive Injury Update on WR Mike Evans Ahead of Seahawks Game appeared first on HEAVY .

title: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI in Week 12
summary: As Week 12 in the NFL marches on, these 7 teams are best positioned to hoist the Lombardi Trophy.
content: Waiting until Friday for this week’s NFL Super Bowl rankings ABSOLUTELY paid off. We just got the greatest slate of Thanksgiving Day finishes ever. Rome Odunze beat Detroit with three seconds left. Philadelphia erased a 21-point deficit and beat Dallas on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Then Buffalo tipped a punt and gave Tyler Bass just enough room to beat Kansas City from 57 as time expired. Early in the season, a dozen teams can look like they belong near the top of a list like this. By Thanksgiving, the ones that separate have shown what they do when the game stops going to plan. A champion fights for the next yard, claws for one more possession, and finds a way to win with whatever still works. Some of those wins look ugly in the box score. The W counts just the same. Now grab that leftover turkey, and throw it on a sammich with this stack. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 12 of 2026 NFL season 7. Denver Broncos Nov 22, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) hands the ball to running back Jonah Coleman (20) against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first quarter at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Previous: Unranked | Back in the top seven Denver let a 17-point lead disappear against Las Vegas, then gave the ball to Jonah Coleman. The rookie ran for 111 yards and three touchdowns in a 38-24 win. One afternoon against the Raiders is a thin basis for counting on it in January. But Coleman gave Denver a way to close on the ground, and the Week 8 win over Kansas City gives the Broncos the edge over Cincinnati. Pittsburgh’s run defense makes Friday afternoon a better gauge of what Coleman can give Denver on an ordinary first down. On Christmas, the assignment flips. Denver has to account for Allen keeping the ball without giving James Cook a crease. 6. Los Angeles Rams Previous: Unranked | Back in the top seven Tied at halftime, the Rams spent eight minutes driving Green Bay back to its end zone. Blake Corum finished with 184 rushing yards, and the defense shut the Packers out after the break. A defense that ranks second in EPA allowed per play gives Sean McVay room to keep calling runs. Chasing a two-score deficit without Puka Nacua would ask considerably more of Matthew Stafford’s receivers. Kansas City comes to Los Angeles December 3 with the defense to put Stafford in third-and-long. Ten days later, San Francisco can make McVay abandon the handoff just by scoring. Those are two different ways to find out who gets Nacua’s targets when everybody knows Stafford has to throw. 5. Jacksonville Jaguars Previous: No. 3 | Down 2 The Giants had been allowing touchdowns on 80% of opponents’ red-zone trips. Jacksonville went one for six there in a 23-18 loss. New York pressured Trevor Lawrence on 45.1% of his dropbacks and picked him off twice on blitzes. Four straight games scoring at least 30 and the league’s most efficient defense keep one ugly Sunday in perspective. Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen were both limited Thursday. Against Tennessee, watch whether the tackles give Lawrence time to throw and whether Jacksonville comes away with touchdowns when it reaches the red zone. Field goals could get expensive December 6 in Chicago. 4. Kansas City Chiefs Oct 18, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Previous: No. 5 | Up 1 Kansas City intercepted Allen twice in the red zone and got its only touchdown from the all of a sudden all-world Emmett Johnson. What cost the Chiefs in Buffalo was field position. Twice late, Patrick Mahomes took over inside his 15. Twice the Chiefs went three-and-out. Just one first down might have put Tyler Bass’ winning kick out of reach. Kansas City rises because Jacksonville and Cincinnati slipped while the Chiefs remain fifth on both sides of the ball by EPA per play. The Rams get first crack at pinning them deep again. At Cincinnati on December 13, the more interesting matchup is the secondary against Burrow once he works past Chase and Higgins. 3. Chicago Bears Previous: No. 6 | Up 3 T.J. Edwards deserves a share of Williams’ winning drive. After Chicago wasted a fourth-quarter interception, Edwards stopped Gibbs on fourth down. Williams took it from there – 68 yards, 13 plays and a touchdown to Rome Odunze with three seconds left. Chicago won 39-35 despite losing tight end Colston Loveland to a knee injury with Cole Kmet already out for the season. Jacksonville visits December 6 with a defense that can make Williams work for every first down. Buffalo on December 19 poses the bigger concern for Chicago. A unit that struggled to tackle Gibbs will have to track Cook while keeping somebody free for Allen. 2. Buffalo Bills Previous: No. 2 | No change Both of Allen’s interceptions ended red-zone possessions. In driving rain, Cook supplied 117 yards and Buffalo’s only touchdown. The defense forced the punt that Greg Dortch returned into range for Bass to win it from 57. Buffalo had that many ways to beat Kansas City and needed every one of them. New England comes first, then a trip to Green Bay. Chicago at home and Denver away on Christmas give Allen good reason to clean up those red-zone decisions. Buffalo can win a playoff game on the ground. 1. San Francisco 49ers Nov 22, 2026; Mexico City, MEX; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) passes against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Estadio Banorte. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Previous: No. 1 | No change Flores wanted Brock Purdy to hurry. On throws released in under 2.5 seconds, Purdy went 12 of 13 with two touchdowns in a 35-10 win. The concern is protecting him now. Purdy finished on a sprained left ankle and missed practice Wednesday and Thursday. Right tackle Colton McKivitz is on injured reserve. Seattle comes to Santa Clara before the 49ers visit the Giants, whose rush just wrecked Jacksonville’s afternoon. Both can make Purdy’s mobility matter. San Francisco stays ahead of Buffalo because the league’s most efficient offense just faced a defense built to dictate when the ball comes out – and Purdy threw it exactly when he wanted. And now, a few participation trophies. Just missing the cut Nov 8, 2026; Madrid, ESP; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) reacts after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Estadio Santiago Bernabéu. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Cincinnati Bengals Washington held Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 74 yards combined, and Joe Burrow still threw for 300. That’s why Cincinnati is the toughest omission. The Bengals lose expected points when they hand off, and their defense gave Jayden Daniels two deep completions with 46 seconds to protect a lead. Detroit Lions Jahmyr Gibbs ran for three touchdowns against Chicago, plenty of firepower to take into January. Holding the lead looks harder. With Aidan Hutchinson and team sacks leader DJ Wonnum missing, Detroit couldn’t get off the field during Chicago’s 13-play winning drive. Seattle Seahawks Five straight second-half three-and-outs gave Drew Lock room to beat the Raiders before Seattle’s bye. Jaxon Smith-Njigba accounted for 171 of his 240 passing yards. Sam Darnold practiced fully Wednesday and Thursday, an encouraging step for an offense that needs a second place to go with the ball in San Francisco. Minnesota Vikings Brian Flores still has the sixth-ranked defense by expected points allowed per play. The trouble comes when an opponent can score through his pressure. Minnesota totaled 31 points in losses to Detroit, Buffalo and San Francisco, with a different starting quarterback in each. That problem runs deeper than Kirk Cousins’ pick-six in Mexico City. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

title: Aaron Rodgers’ brother sad to see it all go down like this
summary: Aaron Rodgers will no longer be a part of the Steelers' Black Friday gameplan.
content: The Pittsburgh Steelers will take on the Denver Broncos in a standalone game on Friday that figures to go a long way in settling the AFC playoff picture. A few days ago the world expected Aaron Rodgers to be under center for Pittsburgh as the club looked to snap back into form with a key victory. So much can change in a matter of hours. MORE: Mike Tomlin sounds off on Steelers ‘dumpster fire’ amid Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy fiasco Rodgers is no longer with the Steelers after getting benched in favor of Mason Rudolph and, more importantly, going full scorched earth on coach Mike McCarthy to his friend Pat McAfee. It is one of the most stunning incidents in NFL history even if our ability to process the bizarre has made is slightly numb. McCarthy has managed to keep his job for the moment and gets an opportunity to shock the world by pulling off an upset today. This whole thing is a mess and it’s impossible to predict the future and how McCarthy fits in. Jordan Rodgers’ reaction Jordan Rodgers, Aaron’s brother and far from a neutral voice, shared his thoughts during a Friday morning interview on Good Morning America . And he sees the organization going a different way in the coaching department. “I think I would be surprised if he continued to be the head coach moving forward, whether that’s short term, long term, whatever it is,” Rodgers said. “I think having been in locker rooms, having been a third-string quarterback on a practice squad, somebody who knew if I even looked like I was nodding off, I’d be cut in a second and to have that happen from the head coach, the play-caller, you can’t play football that way and there’s too many jobs at stake to put up with that type of behavior. I think the Steelers are looking into this, but seemingly the accusations, allegations are confirmed in a lot of ways, and he didn’t rebut them. Crazy world we’re living in but, yeah, weird way to see it end.” Rodgers also shared some other observations from the strange fallout. “That was something we all weren’t preparing for when we were getting ready for our tryptophan slumbers that we all got into yesterday,” Jordan said. “It was a crazy couple days for the Steelers and Aaron. I think the first and foremost — it was kind of sad to see it end this way in Pittsburgh here with so much good vibes and hope about the reuniting of McCarthy and Rodgers and the potential to make a playoff run, one last dance. Unfortunately, it didn’t happen that way.” Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) To be fair, the McCarthy era does feel on borrowed time. But the Rodgers era feels completely over outside of a team deciding to take a flyer on him down the stretch. So it’s tough to assign winners and losers in this situation. A lifetime of being around sports has convinced me the Steelers are going to win today to make this wild week even wilder and no amount of legitimate evidence will move me off that take. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

title: ‘Absolutely hate this dude’ – Cowboys fans lose it after Eagles HC Nick Sirianni’s mocking gesture
summary: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has angered Dallas Cowboys fans after the Thanksgiving Day clash. The Dallas Cowboys ended their NFL Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles in a shocking defeat.
content: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has angered Dallas Cowboys fans after the Thanksgiving Day clash. The Dallas Cowboys ended their NFL Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles in a shocking defeat. After all, the Cowboys led by as many as 21 points and seemed all set to register a dominant win against the Eagles. However, the Cowboys crumbled late in the game as the Eagles made a stunning comeback and finished the night with a memorable 39-38 victory. Nick Sirianni teasing infuriates Dallas Cowboys fans after Philadelphia Eagles’ win Eagles head coach Sirianni was understandably excited about the win and, after clinching the win, decided to rub salt in the Cowboys fans’ wounds. How? Sirianni mocked Cowboys fans in the stands after the 21-point comeback. So much so that security had to hold back the Eagles’ head coach to avoid causing further havoc after the game. Cowboys fans on social media had a similar reaction to how Dallas supporters in the stands reacted – they were furious. “I would have jumped the railing and whooped this crybaby,” a Cowboys fan claimed. While another added, “I absolutely hate this dude… and he probably just saved his job.” “You’re still not safe from getting fired, buddy!” a third fan reminded Sirianni. “Well someone had to make sure Jerry wasn’t the biggest fool there. What an idiot,” a fan compared the Eagles HC to the Cowboys owner Jerry Jones. “Winning the game wasn’t enough, bro wanted to win the parking lot too,” a fifth fan announced. While a sixth fan stated, “He was going after his own team’s fans too, he’ll fight theirs or his own fans. My coach has a few screws loose.” Heading into the Thanksgiving Day clash, the Eagles had a 3-7 record, and many believed Sirianni’s job was on the line. Well, with his back pushed against the wall, Sirianni led the Eagles to a famous victory. But as many Cowboys fans pointed out, Sirianni’s job is still not safe, as the franchise is still just 4-7 for the season. title: Adam Schefter shares the Aaron Rodgers theory that is now going around the NFL
summary: Aaron Rodgers’ Pittsburgh Steelers career came to an end earlier this week and the quarterback has not been shy about airing his opinions in public. The issues were initially brought to light on Tuesday when the Steelers confirmed that Rodgers was benched for the game against the Denver Broncos this week.
content: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ Pittsburgh Steelers career came to an end earlier this week and the quarterback has not been shy about airing his opinions in public. The issues were initially brought to light on Tuesday when the Steelers confirmed that Rodgers was benched for the game against the Denver Broncos this week. But that decision was confirmed just one day after coach Mike McCarthy said that the four-time NFL MVP is ‘our quarterback’. Being dropped seemingly did not go down well with Rodgers, who went on the Pat McAfee show and wasn’t exactly overly complimentary about McCarthy. People around NFL feel Aaron Rodgers wanted to bring Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers down with him That interview took place shortly before the 42-year-old was released and Adam Schefter has now shared that people around the NFL feel the player already knew he was going to lose his role and ‘figured that, on the way down, he would bring Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers’ along with him. Speaking via NFL on ESPN, he said: “Well, when you talk to people around the league, they feel like Aaron Rodgers knew he was going down. He was losing his job, he was leaving Pittsburgh, and he figured that, on the way down, he would bring Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers along with him for the ride.” For the time being at least, it doesn’t appear as though Rodgers’ interview has thrown McCarthy under the bus. It has not been suggested that the higher ups will change their coach right now and he, as of writing, is set to lead them against the Broncos in Week 12. Instead, Steelers owner Art Rooney II has come to back McCarthy this week, saying: “I just want to say that I have 100 per cent confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond.” Addressing Rodgers’ actions, he added: “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure.” Read more: ‘What a joke’ – Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany calls out NFL’s bias against Chiefs after Bills loss ‘No one worse’ – Cowboys fans are furious with Jerry Jones’ hesitation to change despite Eagles loss Colin Cowherd gives Caleb Williams a Michael Jordan compliment after latest win

title: Will Anderson Jr. Named AFC Defensive Player of the Week, Continues to Set the Tone for Houston
summary: The league-leading pass rusher dominated Indianapolis to secure his second career weekly honor, proving he is a generational centerpiece fueling DeMeco Ryans’ elite defensive transformation in Houston.
content: If there is one thing Houston Texans fans can appreciate about Will Anderson Jr., it's that the man understands the assignment. Being named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week is another indication that the Texans have something special in their young defensive end. But beyond the individual recognition, this award speaks volumes about what Anderson means to Houston's defensive identity and the culture DeMeco Ryans has been building. For me, Anderson receiving this recognition isn't necessarily a surprise. It's more of a reminder to the rest of the NFL that Houston has a legitimate defensive difference-maker who deserves to be mentioned among the league's elite pass rushers. Will Anderson Jr. is on top for the 7th straight week 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Mp0T1NkNSG — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 Anderson Put the Colts on Notice Coming off Houston's dominant 26-3 Thursday night victory over the Indianapolis Colts, Anderson earned his second career AFC Defensive Player of the Week award after accumulating five tackles, four quarterback hits, two tackles for loss and a sack that resulted in his first career safety. The interesting thing about Anderson's performance is that the stat sheet doesn't necessarily tell the entire story. His presence alone disrupted the offensive rhythm of Indianapolis and made things extremely uncomfortable for quarterback Daniel Jones. Houston surrendered only 167 yards of total offense and 38 rushing yards. The Colts were held scoreless throughout the final three quarters. That's the type of defensive football Texans fans have been waiting to see consistently this season. Anderson was at the forefront of it. More Than Just a Pass Rusher What I appreciate most about Anderson is that he isn't a one-dimensional defensive end. Everybody loves seeing quarterbacks get slammed to the turf, but Anderson's ability to defend the run, collapse the pocket and force opposing quarterbacks into uncomfortable situations makes him extremely valuable. Through 10 games this season, Anderson has registered 44 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and a league-leading 11.5 sacks. He also leads the NFL with 60 quarterback pressures and a pressure rate of 19.3%. Those numbers are ridiculous when you consider the amount of attention opposing offensive coordinators have to dedicate to containing him. When Anderson commands additional blockers, opportunities open up for other members of the defensive front. That pressure also makes life a little easier for Houston's secondary. That's where his impact goes beyond individual statistics. Anderson makes the players around him better, and that's a characteristic you want from a franchise defensive player. Is It Time to Talk Defensive Player of the Year Why not? I think it's time we start having a more serious conversation about Anderson potentially bringing the NFL Defensive Player of the Year award back to Houston. According to the NFL, Anderson joins Von Miller and former Texans great J.J. Watt as the only players since 2000 to produce at least 10 sacks and 15 tackles for loss in three separate seasons before turning 26. That's some pretty impressive company. I'm not necessarily ready to start comparing Anderson's entire career to Watt's, but the trajectory is certainly encouraging. Houston has witnessed what a generational defensive talent can do for a franchise, and Anderson is beginning to establish his own legacy. The biggest factor moving forward will be maintaining that production while helping Houston climb back into playoff contention. Despite the inconsistencies surrounding the Texans this season, Anderson has remained one of the team's most dependable assets. My Two Pennies As a football fan, I thoroughly enjoy watching Anderson because his motor never seems to shut off. Whether he's fighting through a double-team, chasing down a running back or putting pressure on a quarterback, the effort is consistently there. Being named AFC Defensive Player of the Week is well-deserved, but I believe Anderson has his sights set on something much bigger. Now, it's up to the rest of the team to match that energy. Individual accolades are great, but watching Anderson lead this defense into the postseason would make his remarkable 2026 campaign that much sweeter. And quite frankly, I wouldn't be surprised if there's some additional hardware waiting for No. 51 when this season is all said and done.

title: Andy Reid didn’t like the refs overturning the late Rashee Rice catch
summary: The Bills beat the Chiefs, but one late replay review is under scrutiny.
content: Nov 26, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills defensive back Amani Hooker (22) breaks up a pass intended for Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (4) during the fourth quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Late in the Buffalo Bills win over the Kansas City Chiefs, a turning point in the game was decided by replay. On third down inside two minutes, Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice over the middle of the field and Rice was popped by Bills safety Amani Hooker. As he fell to the ground, the ball moved. On the field it was ruled a catch. Because it was inside two minutes, the replay official had to call for a review and not Bills head coach Joe Brady. After replay, it was ruled an incomplete pass. After the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the play, saying he didn’t like the call. “Not one that I agreed with,” said Reid of the replay review. “This came from New York,” Reid said. “They called it a completion. I’m not quite sure what they saw, I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it has to be clear obvious. To me that was not clear and obvious.” The NBC broadcast spent a lot of time on it during the game and again in the postgame. Rules analyst Terry McAulay thought it was a catch and the Chiefs should have moved the chains. Cris Collinsworth talked about the laces on the ball, and when Rice hit the ground his hand moved down those laces while the ball touched the turf. I think it’s pretty clear the ball moved. I think it’s pretty clear the ball hits the ground. You be the judge: WOW… Refs called this a catch on the field but after review overturned the call and ruled this an incomplete catch for the Chiefs… Very little movement on this ball to overturn that pic.twitter.com/5yZ6sMQqTr — Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) November 27, 2026

title: Bears and Ben Johnson wake up to more great news after win over Lions
summary: The Chicago Bears are riding high after a win over the Lions on Thanksgiving.
content: Bears and Ben Johnson wake up to more great news after win over Lions originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson and the team pulled off a wild win on Thanksgiving over the Detroit Lions on the road. Even though the Lions were winning for most of the game, at the very end, with three seconds left, the Bears pulled off a last-minute win to take it 39-35. During those final moments, Rome Odunze made a touchdown catch that cost the Lions the game. On third-and-goal at the Lions' six-yard line, Odunze snagged the catch for a game-winning touchdown. What a thriller. The win itself was great news for the Bears, but after the tally came in from the Thanksgiving games, the Bears got even better news. Bears take sole possession of first place in the NFC North after Thanksgiving win It's not a surprise at all, because everybody knew this was what was on the line for this game, but after the matchup, the Bears are now the sole No. 1 in the difficult division known as the NFC North. The Lions and Bears were both at the top before the game, and now, the Bears are clearly the frontrunners. "This year, they can celebrate Caleb Williams' first-ever win over Detroit, as well as Ben Johnson's first victory over his former team while visions of hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in February dance in their heads," notes Dan Parr of the NFL's official website . Williams completed 30 of his 44 pass attempts during the game to collect 345 yards and two touchdowns. So he put on a show. The Bears are now No. 1 in the NFC North, and that only helps their playoff probability , which is currently a whopping 96% thanks to that win. title: Bears, Eagles and Bills win as NFL serves up Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a winning touchdown with three seconds remaining to lift the Chicago Bears to a 39-35 victory over Detroit on Thursday as all three NFL Thanksgiving games came down to the wire.Bears quarterback Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave Chicago their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions.
content: Chicago's Rome Odunze celebrates his game-winning touchdown catch with Bears teammate Kalif Raymond after the team's NFL win over the Detroit Lions (Gregory Shamus) Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a winning touchdown with three seconds remaining to lift the Chicago Bears to a 39-35 victory over Detroit on Thursday as all three NFL Thanksgiving games came down to the wire. The Buffalo Bills edged the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a heavyweight AFC matchup thanks to a 57-yard Tyler Bass field goal as time expired. In Dallas, Philadelphia's Jake Elliott drilled a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining to give the Eagles a 39-38 victory over the Cowboys in a classic NFC East division clash. Bears quarterback Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave Chicago their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions. "We knew we needed a big one," Odunze said. "Luckily the O-line held up for me. Caleb delivered the ball exactly where it needed to be, and I was able to make a play in the back of the end zone." Williams connected on 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns -- both to Odunze. The Bears had two rushing touchdowns from Kyle Monangai and one from D'Andre Swift to help offset a monster game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who ran for 205 yards and three TDs. The Bears erased an early 10-point deficit, knotting it at 10-10 on Monangai's first touchdown with 4:07 left in the first half. Jared Goff hit Sam LaPorta with an 11-yard scoring pass to push Detroit's lead to 19-10 going into halftime, but Monangai's two-yard TD had the Bears back within two, minutes into the third quarter. Gibbs motored 70 yards for a touchdown that gave Detroit a 35-24 lead with 8:20 remaining. Chicago responded with a three-play, 71-yard drive capped by Williams's 41-yard scoring pass to Odunze. Detroit came up empty on two possessions before the Bears put together their game-winning drive. - Marquee matchup fizzles - In Buffalo, cold, rainy weather put a damper on the marquee matchup between Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Bills counterpart Josh Allen. Allen connected on 10 of 21 passing attempts for 81 yards with two interceptions and no touchdowns. But James Cook ran for 117 yards and a touchdown and Bass booted a pair of field goals as the Bills improved their AFC-best record to 10-1 and the Chiefs slipped to 8-3. Mahomes threw for 174 yards, piloting a seven-play 56-yard drive capped by Emmett Johnson's one-yard TD run that put the Chiefs up 10-7 minutes into the second half. The Bills tied it on Bass's first field goal. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker, who booted a 26-yard field goal in the first half, missed a 46-yarder with six minutes to play before Bass came through again. "I was just trying to stay fully present," Bass said. "Just telling myself: trust your preparation and go out there and soak it all in and have fun. "It was fun being able to do that for my team." - Milton's Eagles soar - The Eagles erased a 21-point third-quarter deficit to hand the Cowboys another heartbreaking defeat. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another TD. Milton, claimed by the Eagles after he was cut from the Cowboys practice squad in October, said his meticulous work when he was still in Dallas had paid off. "You never know when your opportunity is going to come," said Milton, who was brought in to shore up Philadelphia's quarterback ranks after Jalen Hurts was lost for the season with blood clots. bb/pst
