title: Ben Johnson goes viral for ‘Stanky Leg’ celebration shot at Amon-Ra St. Brown after Bears win
summary: The Chicago Bears head coach got the last laugh after Amon Ra St. Brown tried to make fun of his ‘stanky leg’ celebration during the Thanksgiving clash.
content: Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images The Chicago Bears head coach got the last laugh after Amon Ra St. Brown tried to make fun of his ‘stanky leg’ celebration during the Thanksgiving clash. Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears faced off against his old team on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears have been flying high under Johnson’s leadership, but his offensive mind first came to the forefront with the Detroit Lions. As the offensive coordinator between 2019 and 2024 for the Lions, Johnson is quite familiar with a lot of their stars and best players. This includes star wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. The Lions man and Johnson have both been integral to one another’s careers, but it seems there’s a bit of rivalry there too. St. Brown pulled out Johnson’s ‘stanky leg’ dance celebration during the game, but it was his former OC who got the last laugh at the end. NFL fans love that Ben Johnson gave it back to Amon-Ra St. Brown after the Chicago Bears won Chicago pulled off an incredible comeback during the game. Despite trailing 35-24 with just about eight minutes left in the game, the Bears offence managed to put up 15 points in that time to get the victory. Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze connected for two touchdowns, including the incredible game-winner. Johnson hadn’t forgotten that his former WR had copied his celebration earlier in the game either. While giving an electric postgame speech in the locker room after, he did the dance himself, shouting, “If you want a f****** Stanky Leg, you’ll get a Stanky Leg.” And fans absolutely loved it. “OWN HIM BEN, St. Brown is such a cornball,” one fan commented. “Everyone saying Amon-Ra and Ben are corny are dumb. Sports need more rivalries like this. I love the pettiness. It makes the game better,” a second fan claimed. “Nah ts hard cause the Lions were doing it all game lmao,” a third fan pointed out. “Yeah they’re winning it all this year. Electric energy from that whole entire team,” a fourth fan commented. “I love this guy and the Bears are not even my team,” a fifth fan said. “Everyone wants him as coach and Caleb as their QB… That’s why we hear so much hate,” a Bears fan wrote. Thanksgiving brought a lot of epic moments for NFL fans, and this was absolutely one of them. The NFC North is extremely competitive this season, and this win was massive for Chicago to claim the top spot for now. If these two teams meet once more in the playoffs, it would make for must-see TV. title: Brittany Mahomes blasts refs after Chiefs loss to Bills: 'WHAT A JOKE'
summary: Patrick Mahomes' wife sounded off on the officials once again after a controversial overturned catch on Thanksgiving.
content: Brittany Mahomes blasts refs after Chiefs loss to Bills: 'WHAT A JOKE' originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Both the Bills and Chiefs had chances to win down the stretch on Thursday night, but Buffalo, backed by a special teams advantage, managed a 13-10 victory in the rain. In the eyes of Brittany Mahomes, one of those chances was stolen from the Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes' wife sounded off on the officials after what was initially ruled a catch by Rashee Rice was overturned by replay , ending Kansas City's drive and giving the ball back to Buffalo in the crucial final minutes of regulation. Here's a look at Mahomes' comments. MORE: How Bills' win over Chiefs impacts race for No. 1 seed Brittany Mahomes blasts refs Brittany Mahomes took to Instagram to rip the decision to overturn Rice's catch. "HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE," Mahomes wrote on her Instagram story. "Guess we can't even play football without getting it called against us...not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s— anymore from anyone." Brittany Mahomes, wife of Patrick Mahomes is back on Instagram complaining about the refs from Chiefs-Bills https://t.co/7Ixl6xrDWp — NFL Memes (@NFLMemes) November 27, 2026 Mahomes also reposted several posts sharing the same sentiment, including one that called the decision "one of the worst calls of all time." The decision caught NBC's Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth by surprise as well, as they initially thought the play was being reviewed to see whether Rice had the first down. While replay showed the tip of the ball hit the field, it didn't move much at all, and there is a strong case to be made that Rice had control the entire way. The overturn decision forced the Chiefs to punt the ball away. While the Bills didn't score on the ensuing possession, it did end a threat from Kansas City and help Buffalo win the field position battle that would play a key role in the final sequence of a 13-10 win. MORE: How NFL's Thanksgiving slate became the best ever This isn't the first time Brittany Mahomes has taken aim at the officials this season. After a loss to the Broncos earlier in November, she said on Instagram that the Chiefs were the victim of the "weakest call I have ever seen" — a false start call against Jaylon Moore that changed the complexion of a failed attempt by Kansas City to win the game. With the Rams and Bengals next up for the Chiefs, the stakes are only getting higher in Kansas City; Brittany Mahomes will have a watchful eye for any officiating controversies. title: Broncos must build on recent offensive success

Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense are starting to peak at the right time. And the biggest reason is rookie running back Jonah Coleman. It is a cliché, but when an offense can run the ball consistently and effectively, it sets up the rest of the offense for success. But more than that, Nix is taking care of the ball, the offense is taking shots down the field, and tight end Evan Engram is making an appearance. Over the last four games, Denver has averaged 30 or more points. Now it’s about staking these games. “Just off the top of my head, I think we’ve done a better job on third downs,” Nix said to the media earlier this week. “I think we’ve prolonged drives when we’ve gotten to extend some of those drives that we’ve had. At the same time, we’ve had more success in the run game and explosive plays. That’s going to help an offense score more points. “For us, we just have to continue to find ways to find explosives, continue to do well on third downs. I think one area we’ve really done well really all season is in the red zone; we’ve scored touchdowns. We’ve kept (kicker Wil) Lutz off the field until a PAT. We have to continue to do that. We feel like we’re in a good spot to continue to improve. Now we have the confidence that we can do it, we’ve done it for a couple weeks. Just have to stay on that track.” One of the most important developments is Engram. Getting the veteran tight end involved in the offense, as he was in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders, makes the Broncos that much more difficult to defend. Engram finished the game against the Raiders with six catches for 74 yards. More of that heading into the rest of the season will be massive for Denver. “He had a great game blocking and then catching,” Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb said to the media. “I think he might’ve been a leading receiver. You definitely noticed him if you were in the stadium, and he made some big-time catches on third down. Even the one that got the fourth-and-1 was an unbelievable catch. I think all of our guys are that way. “They’ve been ones everywhere they’ve been, in college and a lot of pro teams. So whatever the matchups allow you to have. That defense last week, we felt confident he was going to get the ball, and he played pretty well.” Added Broncos head coach Sean Payton: “Yes, those were some big plays that you’re getting some of that deep zone coverage. It’s hard sometimes to say, ‘Well, they have to get past the sticks.’ Well, that’s not really the case. Sometimes you’re going to have to throw it under, and he did a great job of that.” For the Broncos, it’s now about keeping the offense peaking. “It’s part of playing long seasons,” Nix said to the media. “You have to limit the distractions. Starve the distractions and feed your focus. That’s something that (Oregon head) coach (Dan) Lanning taught me a long time ago at Oregon. For us, it’s just about the next game and how we can win it.” New Jonah Coleman shirt BreakingT released a new Jonah Coleman shirt just in time for Black Friday. Coleman has taken to the history of running backs, namely Hall of Famer Terrell Davis and the Mile High Salute. The shirt? Coleman Mile High Salute . Broncos links

title: Will the Buccaneers sweep Carolina? Five storylines to watch
summary: Five storylines to follow as the Buccaneers prepare to host the Panthers on Monday Night Football.
content: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers return home for Monday Night Football against the Carolina Panthers , facing one of their most consequential games of the season. Despite being 3-7, Tampa Bay remains within two games of the NFC South lead, with a chance to complete a season sweep of Carolina and secure the head-to-head tiebreaker. The Buccaneers defeated the Panthers 43-13 in Week 7, but Carolina has since changed its defensive coaching staff and enters Monday night atop the division. Tampa Bay can't assume the rematch will unfold similarly. Here are four Buccaneers and a position group to watch as the Buccaneers look to close the gap in the NFC South. QB Baker Mayfield Mayfield needed just 11 attempts in Tampa Bay's first meeting with Carolina, completing seven for 64 yards and a touchdown. However, the Buccaneers cannot expect the same production from their rushing attack against a Carolina defense now operating under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash. Pass protection will be particularly important. According to the Buccaneers' official game preview , Tampa Bay ranks 30th in sacks allowed per pass attempt, while Carolina ranks 31st in defensive sacks per pass attempt. After being sacked four times against Detroit, Mayfield has an opportunity to establish a rhythm against a defense that has struggled to consistently get after opposing quarterbacks. RB Bucky Irving Irving enters Week 12 just 107 rushing yards shy of reaching 1,000 for the season and has scored a rushing touchdown in four consecutive games. The third-year running back recorded 106 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries in his first meeting with Carolina . Tampa Bay finished that afternoon with 258 rushing yards, with Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker also contributing. Carolina enters the rematch ranked 26th in rushing defense, allowing 127.3 yards per game. Establishing Irving early could force Carolina to commit additional defenders near the line of scrimmage, creating opportunities for Tampa Bay's receivers downfield. Tampa Bay's wide receiver room Despite having the NFL's leading rushing attack, Tampa Bay ranks last in passing offense. Emeka Egbuka leads the Buccaneers with 33 receptions for 296 yards but was held to two catches for 18 yards against Detroit last week, and Chris Godwin Jr. contributed just 13 receiving yards. Meanwhile, rookie receiver Ted Hurst III led the Buccaneers with five receptions for 56 yards and two touchdowns against the Lions. The Buccaneers could also be getting healthier at the position. Jalen McMillan has returned to practice, opening his 21-day activation window after spending time on injured reserve with a knee injury. He was listed as a full participant on Thursday's estimated injury report , although his activation remains pending. With Egbuka unavailable during the first Carolina matchup, Tampa Bay could have a considerably different receiving corps for the rematch. How the Buccaneers distribute targets among Egbuka, Godwin, Hurst, Tez Johnson and potentially McMillan will be worth monitoring. EDGE Yaya Diaby Diaby accounted for three of Tampa Bay's five sacks against Bryce Young in Week 7, including sacks on consecutive third-quarter plays. Carolina ranks 25th in sacks allowed per pass attempt, giving Diaby another chance to disrupt the Panthers' passing attack. His production could also have implications beyond the defensive front. With injuries creating uncertainty throughout Tampa Bay's secondary, generating pressure with four rushers would let Todd Bowles dedicate more defenders to coverage rather than relying as heavily on blitz packages. S Tykee Smith Smith intercepted Young and blocked an extra point in Week 7, with Zyon McCollum returning the blocked kick for two points. His performance helped Tampa Bay score points outside its offensive possessions, a key for the Buccaneers this season. However, Carolina also found success attacking the middle of the field, highlighted by Darren Waller's 50-yard touchdown reception. The Panthers enter Week 12 ranked ninth in passing offense, averaging 250.6 yards per game. With Antoine Winfield Jr. and Benjamin Morrison listed as nonparticipants on Thursday's estimated injury report and Jacob Parrish listed as limited, Smith's responsibilities in coverage become increasingly important. Limiting explosive receptions while staying aggressive around the football could help Tampa Bay compensate for its secondary injuries. title: Chargers rule out Justin Herbert to set up DJ Uiagalelei for Week 12 start
summary: The Chargers will be down their starting QB just like the Patriots in Week 12.
content: Chargers rule out Justin Herbert to set up DJ Uiagalelei for Week 12 start originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Chargers lost in Week 11 to the New York Jets , but after a win in Week 10, there's finally a bit of optimism for the Chargers right now. Unfortunately, that optimism might not last with the latest update on quarterback Justin Herbert. He's been in concussion protocol all week, and the injury update on Friday gave the Chargers the expected bad news. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chargers have ruled out Herbert for Week 12, meaning that DJ Uiagalelei is now set to make his first start in the NFL against the New England Patriots on Sunday. Chargers rule out Justin Herbert, DJ Uiagalelei set to start Week 12 "Chargers ruled out QB Justin Herbert, who is in concussion protocol," Schefter reports. "Chargers QB DJ Uiagalelei now is expected to make his first NFL start vs. the Patriots." During his collegiate career, Uiagalelei was a highly touted player who had experience in plenty of big games. Most recently, he was with Florida State last year, although it was a bit of a disappointing season. However, now in the NFL, Uiagalelei is set to make his NFL starting debut in Week 12 against the Patriots, who also happen to be starting a backup at quarterback with Drake Maye hurt, and Tommy DeVito lined up to start. This season, coming into the game against the Houston Texans in relief of Herbert, Uiagalelei completed two of his seven passes for 24 yards and a touchdown. That's his only NFL experience. MORE : Updated 2027 NFL Draft order: What Jets win over Chargers in Week 11 means for No. 1 pick race During the preseason, Uiagalelei completed 57.1% of his 42 passing attempts for 341 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, good for a 99.4 QB rating. While there are a lot of questions about how well Uiagalelei will play in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that can be tricky, it will be interesting to see this Chargers offense with a different quarterback under center. Herbert and the Chargers have struggled mightily this season, so maybe Uiagalelei is able to provide a spark for this offense. Week 12 has already featured backup QBs leading their teams to victory, with Joe Milton and Mason Rudolph winning this week. So maybe Uiagalelei can join them and get the Chargers' 2nd win of the year. title: Chiefs' Andy Reid flags key detail officials missed on costly Rashee Rice catch reversal
summary: Chiefs coach Andy Reid criticizes the NFL after an overturned Rashee Rice catch stalls Kansas City's final drive in a 13-10 Thanksgiving loss to the Bills.
content: Chiefs' Andy Reid flags key detail officials missed on costly Rashee Rice catch reversal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs suffered a 13-10 defeat to the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on Thanksgiving. Kansas City led 10-7 entering the fourth quarter. The Chiefs then did not score again, while Buffalo added six points. Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal won it for the Bills. Chiefs coach Andy Reid was not happy with the NFL's officiating office in New York over a crucial call involving receiver Rashee Rice. Andy Reid questions reversal after overturned Rice catch stalls drive With the game tied 10-10 and two minutes left, Patrick Mahomes appeared to connect with Rice for 11 yards and a first down. The on-field officials ruled it a catch but the NFL's officiating office in New York overruled them. The referee announced the result: "After review, the ball hit the ground, it's an incomplete pass." Kansas City had third-and-10 at their own 9-yard line with 1:51 left. The reception would have given them first-and-10 at the 20 with all three timeouts. The reversal left them with fourth-and-10 at the 9, and they punted. Reid, 68, addressed the sequence after the game. "Not one that I agreed with, but they said it came from New York," Reid said. "It's not from these guys, our guys called it a completion — the guys who were working the game." Reid explained that he saw Rice maintain possession throughout the fall. "I'm not sure what they saw," he said . "I saw he had control of the ball, then his elbow hit, then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it's got to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious." #Chiefs HC Andy Reid on the Rashee Rice catch being overturned: “Normally, in those kind of situations, it needs to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious.” https://t.co/AlF5IAazdJ — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 Rice finished the night with two receptions for 19 yards on five targets. He didn't appear interested in arguing the call. When the question came up about whether the catch should have counted, Rice kept a straight face. "Yes, I did," Rice said. He is still looking for an explanation because officials didn't tell him why the play was overturned and ruled incomplete. Bills fans in the stands cheered as the reversal was announced. Patrick Mahomes said he had very little idea about what the NFL’s officiating office was reviewing during the stoppage. "We were first told that they were reviewing the spot, so I didn't even know that we were reviewing the catch," Mahomes said, per ESPN. "From my angle, when I threw the ball, I thought his hand was under the ball."​‌ The Chiefs have seven days before they play their next game on Dec. 3. They will visit the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium in a Week 13 matchup. Prime Video will broadcast the "Thursday Night Football" game live at 8:15 p.m. ET. title: Chiefs’ Harrison Butker’s confidence is still high after latest miss
summary: Kansas City has trusted its longtime kicker through thick and thin this season.
content: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the fourth quarter of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills , with six minutes remaining while the score was tied, kicker Harrison Butker took the field to attempt a 46-yard field goal. The potential redemption moment for the criticized kicker could have put Kansas City in front. Since missing a 51-yarder in perfect conditions at home against the New York Jets in Week 9, Butker has made all 18 kicks he’s been tasked with (three field goals and 15 extra points). Yet, this one was pushed right, just like it has on too many occasions this year. After the game, head coach Andy Reid was asked about Butker and potentially making a change at the placekicking position. “I’ll go back and go through all of it again,” Reid said. “But I’m not going to make any decisions right this minute.” Full postgame sound from #Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker following the loss to the Bills @KSHB41 pic.twitter.com/mTUQAjFsFk — Matt Foster (@MattFosterTV) November 27, 2026 In the locker room, Butker answered questions from reporters and faced the music. “Obviously, you want to do what you can to help the team, and I didn’t do that,” Butker acknowledged. “It’s a tough loss; I’m not happy with the result, and I’m not happy with the performance.” However, as a three-time Super Bowl champion and long-time professional athlete, Butker remained poised and continued to show ultimate belief in himself. “I think my confidence is always high,” Butker shared. “I just try to focus on the process and how I approach every kick. Obviously, you want them all to feel good, and I was hitting some good balls lately, the last couple of games; that miss just showed up again on that kick, unfortunately.” When asked about the potential impact of the bad weather in Buffalo, Butker made sure to acknowledge that wasn’t a viable excuse on a day where the opponent made two kicks from over 54 yards. “No,” Butker responded. “Obviously, Tyler Bass did a great job handling it, and you have to make the kicks.” Earlier in the game, Butker hit a 26-yard field goal. He also made an extra point. He felt the difference between the misses and makes. “The one I made felt good,” Butker said. “It hit higher up on my foot. The miss, it was just toey and I pushed it off to the right.” “I can’t explain it,” Butker finished. “I’m missing kicks and you don’t want that to happen.” Butker wasn’t the only Chiefs special teams player to have a blunder in Buffalo. The latest game filled with mistakes from the third phase prompted Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star to ask Andy Reid about the special teams leadership after the game. “We have to do better,” Reid said. “But the leadership, I feel comfortable with.” While Butker may have to look over his shoulder at a potential practice-squad elevation in the future, special teams coordinator Dave Toub seems to be just fine with the head coach.

title: Chiefs most to blame for Thanksgiving loss to Bills in ugly rainstorm
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have spent the 2026 season feasting on inferior competition. Thanksgiving night in Orchard Park, though, exposed every flaw that separates them from the AFC’s true elite. In a driving rainstorm, Steve Spagnuolo’s defense delivered a masterclass. They held Josh Allen to 81 passing yards and two red-zone interceptions. Sadly, […] The post Chiefs most to blame for Thanksgiving loss to Bills in ugly rainstorm appeared first on ClutchPoints.
content: Chiefs most to blame for Thanksgiving loss to Bills in ugly rainstorm appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs have spent the 2026 season feasting on inferior competition. Thanksgiving night in Orchard Park, though, exposed every flaw that separates them from the AFC’s true elite. In a driving rainstorm, Steve Spagnuolo’s defense delivered a masterclass. They held Josh Allen to 81 passing yards and two red-zone interceptions. Sadly, the Chiefs’ offense and special teams flushed it all away in a 13-10 walk-off loss . Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired, but the game was lost long before that kick split the uprights. This was a self-inflicted wound of the highest order. The culprits are painfully obvious. Flawed contender Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Chiefs’ Week 12 showdown against the Bills was less a showcase of offensive fireworks and more an old-school trench war. It was dictated by sleet, swirling winds, and sloppy execution. Spagnuolo’s defense did everything possible to steal a road victory against an AFC powerhouse. They intercepted Allen inside the twenty-yard line twice via Alohi Gilman and Nohl Williams. That kept the scoreboard within reach. Running back Emmett Johnson carried a heavy load with 72 rushing yards and a second-quarter touchdown. Travis Kelce hauled in four passes for 71 yards to eclipse 1,300 career receptions. However, Kansas City’s offense sputtered repeatedly. They managed just 241 total yards and endured five three-and-outs. Harrison Butker pushed a potential go-ahead 46-yard field goal wide right with six minutes remaining. Another late three-and-out and a partially tipped Matt Araiza punt set up Bass’s decisive boot as time expired. Special teams Kansas City’s special teams unit usually serves as a reliable stabilizer in tight contests. However, it turned into an absolute liability when Kansas City needed precision most. The most glaring failure belonged to Butker. His wide-right miss from 46 yards out with six minutes left left critical points off the board. Sure, Butker remained automatic inside 39 yards. That said, his miss dropped him to a dismal eight-of-sixteen on attempts from 40 yards or longer this season. That’s a glaring contrast to Bass drilling kicks from 54 and 57 yards on the exact same soggy turf. To make matters worse, punter Matt Araiza endured a nightmarish evening. It was capped by a partially tipped punt in the final fifteen seconds. That allowed Greg Dortch to return the ball seventeen yards to Kansas City’s 39-yard line. It handed Buffalo effortless winning field position. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Offensive line Head coach Andy Reid lamented afterward that an offense cannot repeatedly move backward against an elite opponent. The Chiefs’ offensive line committed the exact infractions that killed promising drives. Guard Kingsley Suamataia endured a brutal outing in the trenches. He drew three separate penalties . Those included a devastating unnecessary roughness flag on a crucial second-half third down. That immediately torpedoed momentum. Operating in driving rain without injured feature back Kenneth Walker III already compressed Kansas City’s offensive playbook. That made clean pre-snap and post-snap discipline non-negotiable. Instead, sloppy blocking assignments and avoidable flags constantly forced Patrick Mahomes into predictable third-and-long passing situations. Against a ferocious Buffalo front, that just did not cut it. Patrick Mahomes Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Speaking of Mahomes, not even he is immune from accountability when the passing game completely stalls out. Mahomes openly admitted afterward that he takes immense pride in conquering any weather condition. Still, he conceded that he simply did not execute well enough. Finishing with just 174 passing yards and zero touchdowns, Mahomes looked out of sync with his perimeter weapons all evening. Trade-deadline acquisition Josh Downs and vertical threat Xavier Worthy failed to generate meaningful separation against Buffalo’s disciplined secondary. That left Mahomes holding the ball or settling for conservative checkdowns. Notably, all three of Kansas City’s losses this season have now come against teams boasting winning records. That should raise uncomfortable questions about whether this offense can consistently manufacture points when elite defenses take away easy rhythm throws. If the Chiefs intend to reclaim control of the AFC West, their biggest stars must deliver when the storm hits hardest. title: Has Commanders OC David Blough finally figured out the 2026 running game? - Daily Slop
summary: Yes, Bill Croskey-Merritt returned on MNF, but Washington’s run blocking scheme changes started a week earlier, against the Giants in Week 10
content: The Daily Slop – 27 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders shift to Duo run scheme pays off vs Bengals They entered the year looking to become more of a zone run team and while they had a promising start, they soon had issues that took a while to figure out. But in the second half against the Giants, they found some success switching up the run scheme and using more duo runs instead of zone runs . Offensive coordinator David Blough took that success and leaned into it even further against the Bengals on Monday night. The Commanders ran almost exclusively duo schemes and variations of duo against the Bengals and had one of their best rushing performances of the season. Running backs Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler had combined stats of 20 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown at an average of 4.75 yards per carry. There was a clear cohesive plan with the duo run schemes, with Blough mixing in a few different variations. The Commanders found some success shifting their base run scheme from zone to duo vs the Giants a few weeks ago. They continued that trend with even more success vs the Bengals. I broke down the layers of their duo run schemes: https://t.co/N9sfam01kd pic.twitter.com/LRvLxzi1AE — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 27, 2026 [ Note: The play discussed below is the same one embedded in the tweet above ] Patrick and Cosmi do a great job against Lawrence again here, Lawrence tries to get aggressive and split the double team, but almost jumps in the air trying to break through. Patrick makes initial contact and prevents Lawrence from breaking through but Cosmi comes in and supports him too. The pair of them effectively catch Lawrence in the air and are able to almost lift him and drive him backwards. Ekeler runs up the middle initially, following behind Chirs Paul and Brandon Coleman, who work a good double team on Jonathan Allen before Paul works up to the linebacker. I think Ekeler could have just hit this run right behind Paul the whole way, but he sees a potential lane behind Cosmi to cut into. He initially makes his cut before then deciding to hit the run inside behind Paul. He is a bit late to hit the hole but he gets in there and manages to pick up another seven yards before being brought down. It was a nice game plan from Blough, implementing a bunch of different variations of duo to keep the defense honest while still leaning into those strong double teams inside. Those double teams were very effective all game long, even against two premier defensive tackles in Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. Full credit to Blough and the coaching staff for identifying duo as a scheme that might work better for them than zone and leaning all the way into it very quickly. It was impressive to see them layer in the different variations so quickly, though it helped that these were all schemes that this group ran last year under Kliff Kingsbury. To Styles, that was a tell that Gesicki was meant to clear space for Chase, who’d be the intended target on an underneath route. Styles was so convinced that, after briefly glancing to his right to make sure Chase hadn’t moved, he ran full speed in his direction as soon as the ball was snapped. Sure enough, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow stared down Chase, who was running a short curl route. When Burrow let the ball fly, Styles was right there. The ball went through his outstretched arms, but even if he didn’t come up with the interception, it remained an impactful pass breakup. title: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer Breaks Silence on Calls for His Firing
summary: The Dallas Cowboys had a 31-10 lead over the Philadelphia Eagles late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving. They still found a way to lose. The Eagles stormed back for a 39-38 win — the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history. That dropped Dallas to 5-7 and put its playoff hopes on life support. […] The post Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer Breaks Silence on Calls for His Firing appeared first on HEAVY.
content: Fans want Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer fired after Thursday's loss to the Eagles Getty Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the game against the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) Getty The pressure is on Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer Getty The Dallas Cowboys had a 31-10 lead over the Philadelphia Eagles late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving. They still found a way to lose. The Eagles stormed back for a 39-38 win — the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history. That dropped Dallas to 5-7 and put its playoff hopes on life support. It also has Cowboys fans demanding that head coach Brian Schottenheimer be fired — some of them before he even got home for Thanksgiving dinner. Brian Schottenheimer’s Job Security Suddenly a Hot Topic Getty Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is firmly not he hot seat after losing to the Eagles When he was asked about his job security after the game, the second-year head coach kept it short despite the growing pressure from fans for owner Jerry Jones to make a coaching change. “I don’t worry about that,” Schottenheimer said, per The Athletic’s Jon Machota. “I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn’t affect me.” He did admit he was “very disappointed,” and he made it clear he isn’t going anywhere on his own. “I’m disappointed in the outcome of this game,” Schottenheimer said. “I’m disappointed in the fact that we’re 5-7. I’m a worker. That’s what I do. The grit and the fight with those guys in that locker room, I believe in it. I believe it’s real. So, I’m gonna stand with them shoulder to shoulder.” That might not be enough to win over the fan base though. The biggest mistake of the night was arguably Schottenheimer’s. With a two-point lead and 55 seconds left, he went for it on fourth-and-1 from the Eagles’ 39-yard line instead of punting, and quarterback Dak Prescott was sacked. Philadelphia was out of timeouts at the time. A short punt could have pinned the Eagles deep in their own end. Instead, Joe Milton got them in range for Jake Elliott’s game-winning 60-yard field goal. For now, Schottenheimer still has the backing of his boss. Owner Jerry Jones told reporters that firing his coach is “certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time.” “We’ve got several more games to go and we’ve got to have our mind on that,” Jones added. Cowboys Fans Want Brian Schottenheimer Gone Getty The pressure is on Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer Cowboys fans didn’t hold back with their frustration toward Schottenheimer. “If Jerry doesn’t fire Schottenheimer tonight, then he is not a serious owner,” one fan wrote. “Fire Schottenheimer. Fire CP. Fire Pettine. Fire everyone except Dak, Javonte, GP, CeeDee, and JPJ,” another fan commented. “FIRE BRIAN SCHOTTENHEIMER BEFORE HE GETS ANY THANKSGIVING DINNER,” one user posted. “We are witnessing one of the worst head coaches in Dallas Cowboys franchise history in Brian Schottenheimer,” remarked another. It’s easy to understand their frustration. The Cowboys went 7-9-1 in Schottenheimer’s first season, and Year 2 has been even rockier. Dallas blew a game to the Arizona Cardinals in a 33-30 overtime loss. Then it gave up 46 points in a 40-point effort against the San Francisco 49ers, which dropped the team to 4-6. After that loss, Schottenheimer took defensive play-calling duties away from first-year coordinator Christian Parker and handed them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. It didn’t matter on Thursday. The Cowboys gave up 29 points after the 31-10 lead, including 22 in the fourth quarter alone. Schottenheimer still has just one win streak since taking over as head coach last year. The second-year coach, however, maintained that he does not stress himself about his job security , as reported by The Athletic’s Jon Machota. “I don’t worry about that. I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn’t affect me,” said Schottenheimer. His remark grabbed attention on X. “The fact that he doesn’t worry about his job is the main reason he keeps making crappy coaching mistakes,” said @jv2151343776. “He knows Jerry (Jones) won’t do anything,” added @NORFTEXAS. “Obviously, it doesn’t affect him. He works under a culture of no accountability thanks to his senile, prideful owner,” echoed @Adam_Paul_T. “Cool, so pack your bag and leave,” suggested @KoZmoh. “Think we’d be better off if he fell asleep in offensive team meetings,” wrote @BettysNoCrock. After the painful loss to the Eagles, Jones reiterated his support for Schottenheimer , whom he promoted in 2025. The clamor for Schottenheimer’s firing has only gotten louder since the Cowboys had a 2-4 start. Some of the names being thrown around as Schottenheimer’s possible replacement include Brian Flores, Sean McDermott, Chris Shula, Klay Kubiak, and Aden Durde. title: Cowboys lose fourth game while scoring 30 points
summary: The Greatest Offense There Is needs to be a little greater.
content: The Greatest Offense There Is needs to be a little greater. The Cowboys have scored 30 or more points in eight games this year. They're 4-4 in those games. Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles became the fourth loss for Dallas while scoring 30 or more points. That matches the all-time single-season record, set by the 2002 Chiefs and matched by the 2024 Bengals. And the Cowboys have six chances to do it a fifth time. This one was the most stunning. Up 31-10 with 3:35 to play in the third quarter, the Cowboys should have won the game. To the Eagles' credit, they didn't give up. They didn't accept the outcome. And, at some point, a "here we go again" vibe may have infected the Dallas sideline. Because they've seen this movie. They've lived this nightmare. Over and over again. They've also extended a franchise-record 19-game streak of allowing 20 or more points. Which is bad but not nearly as bad as losing four times while scoring at least 30 points. Or while losing twice at home in the same season while leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter. Via Doug Clawson of CBS, that had never happened for any NFL team — until this year . What will owner and G.M. Jerry Jones do about it? He'll do what he always does. He'll shed a crocodile tear or two, wipe his eyes, and then count his money.

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day
summary: The Cowboys are a national embarrassment
content: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is tackled by Andrew Mukuba #24 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now? First Quarter The Eagles won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense to work first. Dak Prescott and the group did not waste the opportunity. Javonte Williams was served seconds, thirds, and then some as the team marched down the field, partly thanks to a huge 3rd and 18 conversion from Dak to CeeDee Lamb, but it was Williams who capped it off with the touchdown to give the home team an early 7-0 lead. JAVONTE TD pic.twitter.com/IFq12RHEEy — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Things were looking rather impressive for Joe Milton and the Eagles. I’d imagine that many Cowboys fans were starting to assume a score was happening any minute across the first drive. Thankfully that was not the case. Right around field goal range the Eagles chose to roll the dice on fourth and short… and Quinnen Williams said no! QUINNEN!!! pic.twitter.com/Yz2K1cZsqi — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Weirdly a sequence occurred on the next drive that did the first. Dak Prescott scrambled for a first on a third down, but the gain was negated by a penalty. This brought up third and long (16 here, 18 before) and Prescott connected with a star receiver (George Pickens here, CeeDee Lamb before) for the first down. After that KaVontae Turpin had a stellar catch where he turned on the boosters and reached the endzone in a flash. Dallas was up 14-0 early. TURP TD!!!! pic.twitter.com/8ihtwLzjs2 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The quarter ended with Philly holding the ball right after. Second Quarter The Eagles punted shortly after teams flipped the field which put the Cowboys offense back up. Given that they were already leading 14-0 this was a chance to really blow things open. Unfortunately they could not and wound up punting the ball for the first time in a while. A big 3rd and 12 conversion from Philadelphia put them within striking distance and while they were unable to fully get home they did give Jake Elliott a chance at a 48-yard field goal. It was good and the visitors had their first points on the day. The Cowboys offense did not miss this time around. KaVontae Turpin was involved again, this time on a jet sweep, and there was a big conversion from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb. But it was Javonte Williams who cased in yet again. This marked his second score on the day and gave Dallas a 21-3 lead. JAVONTE WILLIAMS AGAIN pic.twitter.com/mbe4qovd3I — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The dam finally broke, though. Joe Milton had been showing moments of promise to this point in the game and at long last he delivered. It was a classic Joe Milton throw… meaning it traveled quite a long ways. JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys received the ball with just over four minutes to go. It felt like an important possession as it would likely be their last one before the half and they received the ball to start the game. Points were essential. In all honesty it was a pretty penalty-filled drive. Officials were calling them left and right, many of them helping the Cowboys, but Dallas was moved back after an apparent touchdown to Brevyn Spann-Ford. On third and goal from the 12-yard line… Dak Prescott found Javonte Williams for a score to close the half. It also marked a hat trick of scores on the day for Williams specifically. JAVONT3 pic.twitter.com/9lMQ1ebII8 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took a knee and it was Miranda Lambert time. Third Quarter Philadelphia went three and out to start the second half which is always great to see. The Cowboys took the field and once again with an opportunity to stretch their lead. Dallas punted it back themselves. This game truly felt over, but obviously with a lot of time left that was not the case in any real way. Football had to be played. Shemar James sacked Joe Milton which helped to ensure the punt streak continued. Philly booted it back and the Cowboys offense returned to the field. It was a little bit of the same for the Cowboys offense in terms of not being able to fully convert. They did score, but only 3 points by way of Brandon Aubrey. This was notable though as it was a 59-yard field goal that he drilled with ease which was great to see given how this season has gone. The FOX broadcast also noted that this was the longest ever field goal made on Thanksgiving all-time. Pretty neat. The third quarter ended right as Philadelphia crossed the 50-yard line… and then Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith again to get another touchdown on the board with 15 seconds left. It was suddenly 31-17, good guys. Fourth Quarter Things did not go particularly well for the Cowboys offense to start the fourth quarter. They faced a fourth and short on their side of the field and left the offense on the field. It was bold, but nobody really thought they were going to run a play. Thankfully they just fished for offsides and punted. Or so we thought. The Cowboys tried to punt… but it was blocked and returned for a Philly touchdown. Out of nowhere it was 31-24 with basically the entire fourth quarter left. EAGLES BLOCKED PUNT TD PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1mrM5lDeTK — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 It goes without saying that the pressure was high. The Cowboys were on the verge of blowing this game. Something had to happen. Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb specifically played like that was the case. They hooked up for a pair of big gains along the drive and then Dak put the exclamation point on things himself by running it on for a touchdown… thanks to some serious hops. DAK!!!! pic.twitter.com/1GdrVEJ8Ls — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 It seemed like this was going to essentially end the game. Have you seen the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, though Philadelphia traveled 42 yards in 3 plays to match the touchdown. Joe Milton literally did by rushing it in himself. Joe Milton takes it in himself! PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ERZiu9S8Kr — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 The Eagles missed the two-point conversion so it was 38-30 Cowboys. In the blink of an eye it was 3rd and 14 right past the team’s own 15-yard line. It appeared as if the Cowboys had pulled off something truly incredible. Dak Prescott found George Pickens for a modest gain, but then he threw a lateral across the field to Hunter Luepke and the fullback took it all the way to the house. He even jumped into the Salvation Army kettle. Unfortunately it was deemed to be a forward pass from Pickens and therefore a penalty which resulted in the loss of the down. Bryan Anger successfully got the punt off this time and the Eagles returned it past midfield. There was still half the fourth quarter remaining. It was then that the Cowboys defense made a play. On third and forever they picked off Joe Milton. Cobie Durant was the hero in question. COBIE DURANT pic.twitter.com/1WmfLgtNqk — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 You would think that this would have given the Cowboys the opportunity to ice the game. You would think that the offense that had been on fire for so long would have scored to fully put things away. They wound up settling for a field goal attempt from 40 yards out. Brandon Aubrey missed. It was unbelievable. Dak's reaction to Aubrey's missed field goal. 📺 FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/PCmN1dFmj9 — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 27, 2026 Fine. Mistakes happen. Surely the Cowboys defense would lock in. It took the Eagles just 4 plays to travel 70 yards and score. Seriously. Given the failed two-point conversion earlier though the Eagles had to have one here. They failed again so Dallas retained a slim lead at 38-36. The Cowboys got past midfield. In fact, they got all the way to the Philadelphia 39-yard line. They were facing 4th and 1. Instead of letting Brandon Aubrey try a field goal, he had just missed obviously, the Cowboys chose to go for it. Dak Prescott was sacked. It felt grim. You know what happened. The Eagles pulled off a 60-yard field goal to win 39-38. The Cowboys’ season is over. Unbelievable.

title: DeVonta Smith’s 200-yard game vs. Cowboys comes with a historic twist
summary: DeVonta Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards against Dallas, making Next Gen Stats history with fewer than 20 of those yards coming after the catch
content: DeVonta Smith didn’t need long runs after the catch to deliver the biggest receiving performance of his career. He did most of his damage before Dallas could bring him down. Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns Thursday as the Eagles erased a 21-point deficit to defeat the Cowboys 39-38. The performance also produced an unusual statistical first. According to Next Gen Stats, Smith became the first player since tracking began in 2016 to record 200 receiving yards with fewer than 20 after the catch. That distinction captures how Philadelphia attacked Dallas. Smith’s production came primarily through gains downfield, with Joe Milton finding him for touchdowns of 50 and 45 yards. Those two receptions accounted for nearly half of Smith’s receiving total and gave the Eagles badly needed scoring plays while chasing a substantial deficit. Smith delivers throughout the comeback Smith entered halftime with four catches for 95 yards, then added seven receptions for 105 yards after the break. Philadelphia needed both halves of that performance after Dallas built a 28-10 halftime lead and stretched the margin to 31-10 in the third quarter. His second touchdown helped start the comeback. Philadelphia followed it with a defensive stop and Ty Robinson’s blocked punt, which Kenny Moore II recovered for a touchdown. Suddenly, a game Dallas had controlled was within reach. Smith briefly left in the fourth quarter after being shaken up while attempting a difficult reception but returned as the Eagles finished the rally. Injuries put more on Philadelphia’s passing game Dallas Goedert was ruled out with a shoulder injury, and Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger, leaving Philadelphia without two central pieces of its offense for much of the afternoon. With the Eagles managing 68 rushing yards, Smith and Milton supplied the production needed to keep the offense moving. Smith accounted for more than 60% of Milton’s 331 passing yards, and his two touchdown catches covered a combined 95 yards. Philadelphia improved to 4-7 with its second consecutive victory. For an offense working through injuries and a quarterback change, Smith’s performance offered something concrete to build on: a receiver who can turn downfield opportunities into substantial gains without needing extra yardage after the catch. title: What Dolphins’ Kyle McCord is doing well, and what he can improve in third start
summary: MIAMI GARDENS — If Miami Dolphins backup quarterback Kyle McCord is going to lead the team to a victory while playing for injured starter Malik Willis, he’ll have to be better than he was last week against the Buffalo Bills. There’s no way around it, even if he was victimized by a few key drops from his wide receivers last time out at Highmark Stadium. Ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. kickoff back at ...
content: MIAMI GARDENS — If Miami Dolphins backup quarterback Kyle McCord is going to lead the team to a victory while playing for injured starter Malik Willis, he’ll have to be better than he was last week against the Buffalo Bills . There’s no way around it, even if he was victimized by a few key drops from his wide receivers last time out at Highmark Stadium. Ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. kickoff back at Hard Rock Stadium against the New York Jets , McCord and his coaches are working to make sure he puts something together better than his 12-of-33 passing for 102 yards and an interception, without finding the end zone. “Just sticking to the same process that I always have,” said McCord, who had great success in his final college season at Syracuse in 2024 and this past preseason with the Green Bay Packers before getting traded to Miami. “Obviously, it’s constantly evolving and you’re learning on the fly and getting better and sometimes learning from mistakes. But sticking to the same things that got me here and staying true to that process.” Coach Jeff Hafley wants to take the approach with the second-year passer, who goes into his third NFL start, of highlighting the positives. “We say it’s not the best performance, but let’s go through every single play with him and show him what he did well,” Hafley said. “Sometimes, things he did well, the result wasn’t very good, but the process was, and it just might have been execution on the other end of it that maybe made the result not so good. “I think he did a lot of really good things in that game, but it’s going to be constant learning and it’s going to be the same thing in practice. He’s going to have good moments and he’s going to have ones to learn from as he continues in his career.” While there were some passes that just missed their mark, slightly out of the reach of McCord’s intended target, or throws batted at the line of scrimmage, Miami’s offensive coaches like that the young signal-caller at least gets to the snap on a strong starting point. “I think he owns the operation really well,” offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik said. “The operation part of quarterback is really a non-issue for us, which is saying something considering that’s a second start. Related Articles Ragtag Dolphins defensive line holding together through slew of injuries Perkins: Dolphins’ Sean Duggan honors brother, Ryan, in NFL’s My Cause, My Cleats Who has the edge? Dolphins vs. Jets, looking for season sweep Perkins: Dolphins have right to revoke season tickets, but I don’t agree in this case Things to watch for in Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets on Sunday “Outside of that, I thought he did some really good stuff pocket-movement-wise, like the subtleties of getting to the soft spot of where the pocket is open for us and available. I thought he had some throws down the field that were really nice. I know he had some that he would want back, as well, but he threw some balls in there that deserved to be big plays for us.” The downfield throw in the first quarter to wide receiver Chris Bell, which was dropped, makes his final stat line look a little different. The same can be said if fellow rookie wideout Caleb Douglas doesn’t drop the ball on an in-breaking route inside the 10-yard line, which could’ve gone for a touchdown after the catch. But there’s still a lot for McCord to improve once he’s processing the play from the pocket. “I know he’s still working through having everything hammered out to where he’s confident and just knowing when it’s not the time and we just got to take a completion and move on,” Slowik said. “There’s a lot of room to still grow, but there were some from Week 1 to Week 2, regardless of what it looks like, his process is going up, it’s going forward. I’m excited to see what he does this week.” The Bills deflected 12 passes of McCord last Sunday. He’ll have to keep the ball away from defenders, which was also a theme of his first start against the Indianapolis Colts. “So much of it, in his first two starts, is finding those throwing lanes,” quarterbacks coach Bush Hamdan said. “You look at Indianapolis, I do think that was a strength of their D-line. When they felt they maybe couldn’t get a rush, just anticipating where his eyes were, where the balls were. Again, I think it’s, second start, it’s the learning process that he’s going through and certainly something we’re working through.” Said McCord: “I always think a perfect ball and a good read will beat good defense, regardless of what they run. So I pride myself on a lot of that. And there’s obviously plays that I wish I could have back and put the ball in better positions.” Willis had success against the Jets, so he has been in McCord’s ear this week, relaying things he found were effective in the late-October matchup. “He’s been there every step of the way,” Hamdan said of Willis as he recovers from his groin/core injury. “He just wants to win as bad as everybody else does, and I think he and Kyle have had a great relationship. Just (Wednesday) he was in there talking to him about what he saw in this first game versus the Jets and some things that I think will benefit him. So, he’s been outstanding.”

title: Drake Maye's teammate, who had a similar injury, comments on prognosis
summary: Patriots rookie quarterback Behren Morton knows more about what Drake Maye is going through than most.
content: New England Patriots backup quarterback Behren Morton understands the challenges Drake Maye faces with his fractured fibula, having experienced a similar injury during his time at Texas Tech. According to MassLive's Mark Daniels, Morton recently weighed in on the injury that Maye sustained and gave a prognosis on how he anticipates his recovery process will go. “It’s a bone that will heal itself," Morton said. "It just takes time.” Morton suffered the same injury during his final season with the Red Raiders in 2025, explaining that the recovery process requires patience. Maye fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions in Week 10 after star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson delivered a sack that brought him down and caused the injury. The third-year quarterback is expected to be out for at least six weeks as a result of the injury. Before getting hurt, he had accumulated 2,330 passing yards, 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. With Maye sidelined, Tommy DeVito will take over as New England's starting quarterback, while Morton will serve as his backup. Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook . summary: Many people are focusing on the Dallas Cowboys’ inexcusable implosion rather than the Philadelphia Eagles’ miraculous comeback, as is quite common in society, but The Birds deserve to take center stage. content: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Eagles legend Jason Kelce has 3 words for everyone after shocker vs. Cowboys appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Many people are focusing on the Dallas Cowboys’ inexcusable implosion rather than the Philadelphia Eagles ’ miraculous comeback, as is quite common in society, but The Birds deserve to take center stage. Teams that watch their starting quarterback experience a serious health challenge and plunge into last place are not supposed to have much fight left in them. Lane Johnson’s abrupt retirement, Jalen Hurts’ blood clots and a seven-game losing streak should have brought Philly to a point of no return. Instead, on a day that emphasizes gratitude and unity, the Eagles overcame a 21-point deficit on the road versus their divisional rival. This 39-38 win does not change their last-place standing in the NFC East. A playoff berth remains unlikely. But this heroic effort, which was capped off by an amazing Jake Elliott field goal, shows that this squad will still battle in the midst of dismal circumstances and public discontent. Those who share a kinship with the Eagles needed to see this type of tenacious performance in AT&T Stadium. Jason Kelce was feeling especially cheery after Philly scored 22 points in the fourth quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Happy Thanksgiving America!!!” the all-time great center remarked on X. No matter how happy Kelce is with life after football, it is surely painful to see the franchise he represented for 13 years struggle for so much of the season. Any discomfort was displaced, at least temporarily, by Thursday’s thrilling conclusion. Joe Milton posted the greatest game of his NFL career , throwing for 331 yards and three touchdowns against a still-vulnerable Cowboys defense. DeVonta Smith pushed through a tailbone injury and racked up 200 receiving yards and two TDs. The defense made a massive stop on fourth-and-1 late, sacking Dak Prescott and gaining possession near midfield. This team came together in clutch time, and it now has a powerful experience to draw upon during the remainder of the campaign. The Eagles (4-7) will head northwest for a Week 13 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals (3-8) and then host the Indianapolis Colts (3-8) the following Sunday. In other words, they are not dead yet. Jason Kelce and other Philly supporters will now approach December with renewed optimism. title: Eagles mount furious comeback, beat Cowboys 39-38 in Thanksgiving classic
summary: What looked like a blowout turned into a great one, as Philadelphia stormed back to win in Dallas.
content: It was a Thanksgiving Day classic in Dallas. In a wild game that went from an apparent blowout to a thrilling comeback, the Cowboys jumped out to a 31-10 lead and then lost 39-38 when Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton played by far the best game of his career, throwing for 331 yards, with three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. We've always known Milton had a strong arm, but he showed today that he's more than just a thrower. He can lead an NFL offense as a quarterback. But Dak Prescott is a good quarterback, too, and he turned in a big game of his own. He threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Prescott's favorite receiver was CeeDee Lamb, who finished with 134 receiving yards, and running back Javonte Williams ran for two touchdowns and also caught a touchdown pass. The Eagles, however, got a monster game from wide receiver DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was sensational while the Eagles were coming back in the fourth quarter. Special teams miscues killed the Cowboys: The Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown, and Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Aubrey, who became the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason, is having the worst season of his career. The loss drops the Cowboys to 5-7 and is devastating to their playoff hopes. The 4-7 Eagles aren't contenders, but they played like contenders today.

title: Forget Patriots and Ravens, Cam Newton says there’s now only one NFL team Aaron Rodgers can sign for
summary: Aaron Rodgers has cleared waivers after his release by the Pittsburgh Steelers, and speculation continues over his future. When speaking to the Pat McAfee Show on ESPN this week, Aaron Rodgers expressed his anger at his benching by the team.
content: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has cleared waivers after his release by the Pittsburgh Steelers, and speculation continues over his future. When speaking to the Pat McAfee Show on ESPN this week, Aaron Rodgers expressed his anger at his benching by the team. He vowed never to play for the Steelers again, and was quickly waived. Rodgers did not indicate whether he wanted to continue playing in the NFL. For now, the 42-year-old’s intentions remain a mystery. There has been speculation over what will come next for Rodgers. Two AFC teams in need of a quarterback have been tipped by fans and media. The New England Patriots are looking for a quarterback after Drake Maye suffered an injury. While many have suggested that the chance to join the Steelers’ rivals the Baltimore Ravens would appeal to Rodgers. The Ravens still have to play the Steelers twice this season, and they are without Lamar Jackson due to injury. However, speaking to 4th & 1, former quarterback Cam Newton believes the only option for Rodgers is to sign with NFC South team the Atlanta Falcons. Newton said: “I think the only move Aaron Rodgers has now is if the Atlanta Falcons want him. “The only reason I’m saying the Atlanta Falcons is because there’s no denying Aaron Rodgers can still throw the football at a high level. But Aaron Rodgers is not the same player who can take on the task of carrying a team. You don’t need that. “No, I don’t think Michael Penix is the quarterback they drafted him to be. That’s just me personally. I think, take Bijan Robinson out of the situation, I don’t think Michael Penix has success in this NFL.” Newton says Aaron Rodgers can thrive with Atlanta Falcons Cam Newton says that he believes Aaron Rodgers could be successful with the Falcons, because they have so many other weapons in their offense. The Falcons are on a three game losing streak and are now 3-7 for the season. But they are only two games back from division leaders the 5-5 Carolina Panthers. Newton believes Rodgers could turn it around: “You insert Aaron Rodgers into a situation where now you have Kyle Pitts, you have Drake London, and you add in a Bijan Robinson, along with that defence. Because Tommy Rees, offensive coordinator for the Atlanta Falcons, as well as Kevin Stefanski, they’ve had success. “But is it worth it, though? And if you don’t have… If you don’t go to a team – and the reason I say the Atlanta Falcons is that they still have a possibility of making the playoffs. “If you don’t go to a team that has a possibility of making the playoffs, wrap it up.” Both the Ravens and Patriots could still make a late surge with Rodgers too, but as far as Newton is concerned, Atlanta is the only option. title: ‘That was freaking insane’: Chicago Bears stay ‘super resilient’ to rally and pull off a 39-35 win
summary: When Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze toe-tapped in the end zone for a 6-yard go-ahead touchdown catch with 3 seconds left Thursday, it transported Sam Roush back to the frenzied fourth-quarter rallies of last season — and the rookie tight end wasn’t even on the team then. “I remember being in college (at Stanford) watching (the Bears) last year and being like, ‘How is this even ...
content: When Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze toe-tapped in the end zone for a 6-yard go-ahead touchdown catch with 3 seconds left Thursday, it transported Sam Roush back to the frenzied fourth-quarter rallies of last season — and the rookie tight end wasn’t even on the team then. “I remember being in college (at Stanford) watching (the Bears) last year and being like, ‘How is this even possible?’” he said after the Bears’ 39-35 comeback thriller over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day at Ford Field. “And now I get to be a part of it.” Odunze’s score was the first time the Bears led all game. “Obviously, I’m not the guy that made those big plays today, but seeing Rome do that was incredible at the end of the game,” Roush said. “And (quarterback) Caleb (Williams), like, that’s why they call Caleb ‘Ice Man.’ Like, that was freaking insane. “We just got some dogs in the game.” If there’s a word that describes the Bears on Thursday, it’s “dogged.” There were several points in the game that looked like backbreakers, and some of the setbacks that seemed almost insurmountable. • Midway through the first quarter, tight end Colston Loveland lost a fumble after his only catch. • Later in the first, the Bears lost Loveland for the rest of the game after he injured his knee while blocking on a run play. • The Bears’ chance to mount a 2-minute drill before halftime ended with Williams taking a strip-sack and a safety. • When Jahmyr Gibbs sprinted 70 yards for a fourth-quarter touchdown, it looked like a wrap. Bears running back D’Andre Swift said they remained unfazed, even as the Lions built an 11-point advantage after Gibbs’s scamper pushed Detroit’s lead to 35-24 with 8 minutes, 20 seconds left in the game. “We (were) always in the game, and I feel like the game never really got away from us,” Swift said. “We gave up some stuff early on and kind of made it hard for us. “But it was a heavyweight fight. Back and forth, back and forth. Went down to the wire.” Swift had a 30-yard touchdown run, and Kyle Monangai ran in 1- and 2-yard touchdowns, scores that helped keep the Bears engaged in a seesaw battle in the second and third quarters. Odunze’s two touchdown receptions both came in the fourth quarter. The Bears defense coughed up 205 rushing yards and three touchdowns to Gibbs, but also came up with a pair of crucial plays. “Defense came up in critical situations,” Swift said. “It’s how we fight as a team. “That’s the one word I would use for that win is just ‘fight.’” Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman caught his third interception of the season (and second in consecutive games) after Jared Goff’s fourth-quarter pass bounced off receiver Jameson Williams’ hands and into Thieneman’s chest. The offense couldn’t convert that pick into points, but it didn’t stall a Lions drive that reached the Chicago 34-yard line and likely cost Detroit at least a field goal try. “I felt like that was a big change, and then giving it to the offense and all them to build some more momentum with that,” Thieneman said. “I felt it was really important.” On another crucial defensive play, T.J. Edwards wrangled Gibbs to the ground after a 1-yard catch on fourth-and-4, where nothing was backing up Edwards but a lot of green turf. Edwards’ stop forced the Lions to turn the ball over on downs. The offense then marched 68 yards on 13 plays in 2 minutes, 14 seconds, with Odunze’s toe-drag touchdown capping it off. Like Roush, Thieneman isn’t used to these kinds of wild finishes. “It’s awesome, he said. “Definitely a lot of ups and downs. You gotta control yourself, gotta stay level in it all.” Throughout the game, various players and coaches would make uplifting comments such as “don’t forget we’ve got a game to win, we’re still in this,” Kalif Raymond said. “I remember, I want to say, (quarterbacks coach) J.T. Barrett came out on the sidelines, like, ‘Hey, man, we’re in this. This game is down to the wire.’” Last season, the Bears engineered seven late-game comebacks between the regular season and playoffs. This season, they’ve taken more leads and spent more time fending off comebacks, so Thursday’s game was the first true nailbiter. “Man, I’m really proud of our guys,” Ben Johnson said. “I think about how far we’ve come since we’ve been in the building the last year and a half. Just the professionalism with which they conduct themselves, the hard work they put in all season long, but certainly on a short week like this. “And then the belief that they had in a game like that, particularly when we gave them some momentum at halftime. And yet to be able to weather that storm.” Linebacker D’Marco Jackson said the team had heard the chatter about the Bears’ struggles in the NFC North (2-6 under Johnson heading into the matchup), so to steal a win on the road against a division opponent, under those circumstances, was “super huge.” “I think a lot of people wrote us off thinking we weren’t going to be able to come in here and pull it off,” Jackson said. “We did just that and we put everybody on notice.” Roush also learned about the makeup of the team. “Super resilient,” he said. “Lot of playmakers. … It really is incredible. We’re still hungry.”

title: Friday's game gives Steelers fans a chance to chime in on recent events
summary: Much has been said from the folks at the middle of the current clusterfudge at the confluence of three rivers.
content: Much has been said from the folks at the middle of the current clusterfudge at the confluence of three rivers. One very important constituency has yet to chime in. Later today, Steelers fans will get a chance to make their voices heard when the home team hosts the Broncos in a Black Friday game. One option for Steelers fans will be to not show up. And we've heard some anecdotal evidence indicating that some fans have decided not to go to the game. That may be better than the alternative. Steelers fans aren't blindly loyal. If they see something they don't like, they'll make it known. Loudly. The dynamic adds extra pressure to the situation. If things start poorly, you'll hear the boos on the Prime Video stream, as clearly and plainly as we heard Rodgers’s comments during the Thursday night Prime Video game in Cleveland. Last year, they booed during Renegade . Today, if the Steelers respond to the recent drama with a subpar showing, the booing will start a lot earlier than that strategic moment in the fourth quarter when they press "play" on their trademark rallying cry. It's just another reason to tune in at 3:00 p.m. ET, and to watch — and listen — closely.

title: Instant analysis: What went right, what went wrong in the Bills' win over the Chiefs
summary: An analysis of Buffalo's performance vs. the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12.
content: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a waterlogged, defensive-minded affair. Tyler Bass made a 57-yard field to give the Bills the victory as time exprired. The weather completely impacted this game, neutralizing the Bills aerial attack. Buffalo's offense could only total 81yards through the air. James Cook became the focal point for the Bills offense, earning 33 touches on the evening. Cook scored the Bills only touchdown in the game. Buffalo's defense did enough to keep the Chiefs offense from gaining consistent momentum. Kansas City moved the ball fairly well in the conditions. However, the Bills defense held the Chiefs to only one touchdown. Here is an instant analysis of what went right in the Bills victory over the Chiefs. What went right? James Cook: Cook rushed the ball 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown. Buffalo's passing attack was nonexistent, so the ground game picked up the slack. Cook fought hard for yards, often grabbing an extra yard or two per rush to give Buffalo better field position. Special teams: Tyler Bass was the star in the fourth quarter. Bass hammered two long field goals in the fourth quarter, including the game-winning 57-yard field goal in the substandard conditions. Tommy Doman pinned the Chiefs deep in their territory multiple times and averaged over 45 yards per punt (even after one shanked punt that only traveled 25 yards). On the final Kansas City punt, upback Joe Andreessen appeared to tip the punt. Greg Dortch returned the punt 17 yards to put the Bills in field goal range for the win. Greg Rousseau: Rousseau was a menace once again, registering four tackles, a sack, and three quarterback hits. Buffalo's defense: The Bills defense kept the Chiefs from hitting any big plays. The unit locked down the Chiefs offense, forcing multiple field goal attempts when Kansas City entered scoring range. In addition, the Bills defense forced seven punts during the night. The Chiefs converted only two-of-eleven third-down attempts. What went wrong? The passing attack: It didn't exist in the game. Josh Allen did not look comfortable passing the ball in the game. The conditions limited his accuracy all evening. Allen completed only 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards. In addition, Allen threw two interceptions in the red zone, which is not ideal in a game where points are at a premium. Second-half struggles: The Chiefs scored quickly on the first drive of the second half. Kansas City completed a seven-play, 56-yard drive in three-and-a-half minutes, culminating with an Emmett Johnson touchdown. Buffalo's offense started the half with two 12-play drives. However, the first ended with a turnover, while the second stalled out and finished with a field goal. The bottom line Buffalo won its seventh consecutive game. The victory keeps the Bills at the top of the AFC playoff standings. The win also gives the Bills an advantage if a tie-breaking scenario occurs with the Chiefs, as the Bills have the head-to-head advantage. It's a big win for the Bills, as the team did it without the best, or even adequate play, from their MVP candidate. Josh Allen struggled mightily, so Buffalo became a one-dimensional offensive attack. Cook carried the load, and the offensive line won the battle in the trenches. Buffalo's defense was solid. The Chiefs had moments where their offense looked good. However, Buffalo's defense shut things down when they needed it the most. It's promising that the unit can keep the game in check, espeically when the offense is not producing points. What's next? Buffalo travels to Foxborough to take on the New England Patriots on December 6. Buffalo's loss to New England in Week 5 is the Bills only blemish on their record this year. New England lost its previous two games leading into Week 12. The Patriots have struggled since the loss of Drake Maye due to a long-term injury. New England squares off against the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday.
