title: The J.J. McCarthy improvement that could get Giants to the next level
summary: The deep balls were flying from the right arm of J.J. McCarthy, but the connections were tough to come by.
content: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) passes over Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker (44) in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. The deep balls were flying from the right arm of J.J. McCarthy, but the connections were tough to come by. Deep to rookie Malachi Fields, incomplete. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW Deep to Malik Nabers, incomplete. Deep to Darnell Mooney, incomplete. Another one deep to Fields, interception overturned upon review to an incomplete pass. Deep to Mooney over the middle, incomplete. Yet another deep shot to Mooney on third-and-17, not close, and some boos ensued from the crowd at MetLife Stadium. “At the end of the day, I just missed them,” McCarthy said. “The big thing that kind of stood out to me was just put some more air on the ball and let the receivers be able to track it a little bit better, but that’s an easy fix and we’ll get it fixed.” These down-the-field attempts from McCarthy were part of his 20 incomplete passes in the 23-18 upset victory over the Jaguars, showing that the Giants have to be really good, but not perfect, to beat a quality opponent. McCarthy has been a godsend since arriving in a trade with the Vikings — that 2027 fifth-round pick was draft capital well spent — and he takes a 3-1 record as the Giants starting quarterback into Sunday’s game with the Colts in Indianapolis. Ever since his arrival Sept. 29, it has been a full-speed-ahead crash course for McCarthy, as far as learning a brand-new offense and trying to fast-forward his comfort with the unfamiliar players around him. Building chemistry with wide receivers and tight ends takes time, and that was not on McCarthy’s side. The reputation for having a strong arm and a nice feel for the deep ball preceded McCarthy to his second NFL stop. That is the next bit of firepower to add to his arsenal as the Giants look to secure and build on their first-place lead in the NFC East. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) passes over Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker (44) in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Adam Hunger “For me, personally, just having more time on task with my guys being able to hit the ones that are there, especially the deeper shots,” McCarthy said. “Just being able to get in here and work with the guys just constantly and just be able to get those reps over and over again. “But I’m going to make those. Those are things that are going to come and have shown up, but sometimes you just miss. In this league, you can’t miss too many times. So just being able to be ready for that next opportunity and nail it.” McCarthy has not pushed the ball into the end zone as often as the Giants would like. He has only two touchdown passes in his four starts. Some of this is happenstance — the Giants had four rushing touchdowns in McCarthy’s first start, a 27-21 overtime victory in Houston. Some of this is McCarthy at times still looking a bit uncertain within the offense, as far as going through his progressions. Making the timely throw, and finding a way to win, though, are McCarthy hallmarks. That is how he went 27-1 at Michigan. His stats were often mid-level — the Wolverines were largely a running team during his time in Ann Arbor — but when a throw or a run was needed to keep a drive alive, McCarthy delivered with impressive regularity. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) speaks at a press conference in East Rutherford, N.J., Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post McCarthy was spraying the ball down the stretch against the Jaguars as the Giants fell into a second-half rut, with four consecutive possessions failing to pick up a first down. When it came time to close out the game or else hand it back over to Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars offense, McCarthy came through with his most clutch throw. He wanted to find Nabers on the left side, but Nabers was shadowed by two defenders. No opening there. McCarthy instantly pivoted and fired a strike to Fields for a 19-yard completion. That alleviated a great deal of pressure. After two 5-yard runs from Cam Skattebo, McCarthy could kneel down three times to end it. “That was my second read,’’ McCarthy said of the pass to Fields. “There are so many things that you could really look at from your perspective and everyone has — they’re entitled to their own perspective and their own opinion, but if you’re not really in the room and you don’t understand what the progressions are. Sometimes it’s zone-based or man-based coverage reads where it’s like, yeah, it might be your first progression, but it’s really the second in your thought process of what the defense has given you. It’s little things like that where you just can’t really focus on and just got to worry about doing your job as a quarterback, which is throwing to the open guy, and sometimes, a lot of the times, with good defenses, that is going through your reads.” And, sometimes, those reads lead to deep throws down the field. “Come back and make the next throw, and that’s a confident guy, and he’s been in a lot of huge games,” coach John Harbaugh said. “And we’re going to start hitting some of those deep passes. We wanted to take some shots, we wanted to go after them downfield and we did, and those are going to start happening. We’ll start making those plays for sure.”

content: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Javonte Williams joins Emmitt Smith in Cowboys’ history with monster Thanksgiving appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams scored three first-half touchdowns against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, joining Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith in franchise history. Williams reached the end zone twice on the ground and once through the air as the Cowboys took a 28-10 halftime lead at AT T Stadium. It was Williams’ second game with three touchdowns this season. He rushed for all three of his scores in the second half of a 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4. Dallas won that game on a late touchdown by CeeDee Lamb. NFL Researcher underscored the milestone Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, noting that Williams and Smith are the only Cowboys players in the past four decades to score at least three touchdowns in more than one game in a single season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Cowboys players with 3+ TD in multiple games in a single season over the last 4 decades: “ Javonte Williams (2026) Emmitt Smith (1992, 1995, 1996, 1998)” Williams opened the scoring with a 1-yard run, his 13th touchdown of the season. He added a 12-yard rushing touchdown and caught a 12-yard scoring pass from Dak Prescott before halftime. The running back had 64 rushing yards on 15 carries and 22 receiving yards on three catches at the break. KaVontae Turpin added a touchdown on a jet sweep, giving the Cowboys four trips to the end zone in the first half. The Cowboys entered Thanksgiving at 5-6 and held a 31-17 lead with 14:10 left in the fourth quarter. Philadelphia had cut into the deficit in the third when Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith for a touchdown. Williams brought his season total to 15 touchdowns, a rare bright spot in another tough season for the Cowboys. title: Jerry Jones says he still believes in Brian Schottenheimer despite mounting meltdowns by Cowboys
summary: ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Jerry Jones says he still believes Brian Schottenheimer is the right coach for the Dallas Cowboys.There was a significant qualifier from the owner and general manager after yet another meltdown in a 39-38 loss to Philadelphia on Thanksgiving.
content: ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Jerry Jones says he still believes Brian Schottenheimer is the right coach for the Dallas Cowboys. There was a significant qualifier from the owner and general manager after yet another meltdown in a 39-38 loss to Philadelphia on Thanksgiving. “I do,” Jones said when asked if he still believed his second-year coach could lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl. “I do, but on the other hand, these are setbacks and they’re damning setbacks.” Fans surely will see the most damning of all as Schottenheimer's decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line with a two-point lead and 55 seconds remaining. Dak Prescott was sacked for a 9-yard loss, leaving the Eagles just 11 yards from the spot for Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds remaining. Jones didn't want to pin the latest loss on that decision either, even though Ty Robinson, the defensive lineman who sacked Prescott, was surprised Dallas snapped the ball. And WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark seemed similarly puzzled . “I’m not going to take any one thing because one thing shouldn’t have done it,” Jones said. “We really had a combination of things that we miscued on.” The Cowboys (5-7) will have to sit on a stunning loss for 11 days before they return for a Monday night game at Seattle on Dec. 7. Playoff hopes aren't realistic at the moment. Here are some of the realities for Dallas: — No other home team in NFL history has lost four home games in the same season when scoring at least 30 points, or averaged at least 30 points in the first 12 games (31.3) of a season and had a losing record. — The largest blown fourth-quarter lead in franchise history was 14 points. The Cowboys matched that twice in November — both at home. — Schottenheimer botched the final seconds of a 34-31 loss to Baltimore in Rio de Janeiro and has his latest baffling decision to go with it. Those aren't the only two questionable moments with game management. — Regardless of how they're happening, the losses are mounting. Dallas is 12-16-1 and has spent just one week over .500 under Schottenheimer (6-5-1 last season). The coach insists he isn't listening to the noise about his job security. “I don’t worry about that,” Schottenheimer said. “I worry about the guys in that locker room, and it doesn’t affect me.” The Cowboys have already made the midseason hire of Mike Pettine as a senior assistant for first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dallas subsequently stripped play-calling duties from the 34-year-old Parker and gave them to Pettine, who turned 60 a few weeks before deciding to come out of retirement. Jones had already said no more coaching changes were coming . He said it again going into a long weekend and a 10-day gap between games. “I wouldn’t anticipate that,” Jones said. “We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive in my mind without coaching changes at this time.” What's working Prescott has accounted for 20 touchdowns (17 passing, three rushing) with two interceptions — one of them meaningless on the final play against the Eagles — in the past six games. The Cowboys are 3-3. What needs help Yes, the Dallas defense is bad. The Cowboys have given up at least one touchdown of 50 or more yards in five consecutive games. Breakdowns on special teams have been crippling, too. The first time it felt like Dallas was in trouble against Philadelphia was when the Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown. Then right after the Cowboys restored a 14-point lead, they gave up a 55-yard kickoff return. Stock up WR KaVontae Turpin probably deserves some credit for an offense that scored on 12 of 13 drives with 11 touchdowns over six quarters from the start of a 51-30 victory over Tennessee to halftime against Philadelphia. Turpin had a 22-yard scoring run against the Titans and a 31-yard TD catch on a screen against the Eagles. His return from a rib injury has made an already potent offense seem more explosive. Stock down The Cowboys have let three backup quarterbacks beat them at home this season. Undrafted Tampa Bay rookie Jalon Daniels had a 110.2 passer rating against Dallas compared to an average of 57.0 in his other two starts. Arizona's Gardner Minshew had a 137.3 rating after replacing an ineffective Jacoby Brissett, then an 83.5 rating in his only start the next week, when he tore a ligament in his elbow. Milton was at 121.8 against the Cowboys after the ratings in his first two career starts for the Eagles were 66.9 and 73.7. Injuries Schottenheimer said DT Quinnen Williams had back spasms. ... CB Joey Porter Jr. exited in the first half appearing to favor his right arm or shoulder but returned to the game on the same series. Key number 129 — The point total for the Cowboys over a three-game span, three shy of the franchise record from 1968 when Dallas won all three at the start of a 12-2 regular season. These Cowboys went 1-2 in those games. Next steps Even if they win three of the next four games against playoff-caliber opponents, the Cowboys would be 8-8 going into the finale. The NFC East-leading New York Giants would have to go 2-4 in their next six for Dallas to have a chance to catch them. ___ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

title: Joe Milton: Eagles don't quit, so happy to be on this team
summary: Six weeks ago, Joe Milton was on the Cowboys' practice squad.
content: Six weeks ago, Joe Milton was on the Cowboys' practice squad. On Thanksgiving, Milton led the Eagles to a win over the Cowboys in one of the most memorable Thanksgiving performances in NFL history. Milton was outstanding in leading the Eagles from a 21-point deficit to a 39-38 win, completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards, with three passing touchdowns and a 15-yard rushing touchdown. "A lot of emotions, but just mainly so happy for this team," Milton said. "This team never let up. These guys never dropped their heads. Everybody just kept saying, 'We're good. Keep doing what we're doing.' As a quarterback, that's what you want to hear, especially when you're the new guy on the team and you've got a whole bunch of guys that you're not so familiar with. These guys don't quit. That's one thing I love about this team." Milton said he still loves his former teammates on the Cowboys. When a reporter told Milton that it looked like at one point he was gloating toward the Cowboys' sideline, Milton said he didn't remember that but has nothing but respect for the people in Dallas, even as he was celebrating a victory over them. "If I did, then I'm sorry, but I was just in the moment. There's no other explanation for that," Milton said. "It was just great coming back here and playing in this stadium, in Jerry World, and seeing the guys I worked hard with in camp and OTAs. But it's about the Eagles."

title: “What a Joke”: Brittany Mahomes Rips NFL Referees After Controversial Rashee Rice Decision Costs Chiefs Against Bills
summary: That’s not how the Kansas City Chiefs fans expected their Thanksgiving to end. They might have still gotten over their 13-10 defeat to the Buffalo Bills.
content: Copyright: xImagexPressxAgencyx originalFilename: collin-losangel230711_npmhp.jpg ©IMAGO/NurPhoto That’s not how the Kansas City Chiefs fans expected their Thanksgiving to end. They might have still gotten over their 13-10 defeat to the Buffalo Bills. But the fact that a crucial play by Rashee Rice was controversially overturned is what left the Chiefs fans upset at the referees. When it comes to Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany, she immediately took to social media to rip the officials. “HAHAHAHAHAHA,” wrote Brittany on her Instagram story . “WHAT A JOKE. Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? With the game tied at 10-10, Kansas City faced a third-and-10 deep in its own territory when the wide receiver made the difficult grab. But Rice went crashing to the ground in the process. It led officials, Alex Kemp and co., to take another look. The review did not go Kansas City’s way, as the referees overturned the completion after determining that Rice failed to retain possession as he hit the ground. The NFL's officiating is under fire after a pivotal call derailed Kansas City's playoff hopes. Stay ahead of the controversy with our NFL newsletter for instant analysis and breaking updates. That’s what turned the tables against the Chiefs. Forced to punt after the incompletion, the Chiefs gave the Bills another opportunity to move the ball, eventually leading to the game-winning field goal. Kansas City refused to go down without a fight, refusing to give up. However, Tyler Bass had the final say, as he pulled off a 57-yard field goal to give Buffalo the victory. One controversial ruling and the internet went on fire to rip the referees. While Brittany voiced her own protest, she made others’ opinions on this matter feel heard. Brittany also shared a post from a fan who had shared the clip of Rice’s play. “This was ABSOLUTELY a catch by Rashee Rice, highway robbery on a fantastic catch,” read the comment, which Mahomes’ wife, too, supported and shared on her Instagram story. Another reshared post was from a page called Jukedly. “THIS IS ONE OF THE WORST CALLS OF ALL TIME: #CHIEFS WR RASHEE RICE MADE A RIDICULOUS ONE-HANDED CATCH ON THIRD DOWN, AND THE REFS RULED IT A CATCH ON THE FIELD,” the post read. “THEY THEN OVERTURNED THE CALL IN BUFFALO’S FAVOR, RULING IT AN INCOMPLETE PASS. AWFUL.” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid also is not convinced by the ruling. “That wasn’t clear and obvious,” he said as reported by The Kansas City Star’s sports columnist, Sam McDowell. As the debate continues about the fairness of the call, Buffalo has made history as the first team this season to secure 10 victories. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are now trailing the Denver Broncos in the AFC West. title: Kickers made the difference as Harrison Butker missed, Tyler Bass won the game
summary: The Thanksgiving night game between the Bills and Chiefs was billed as the battle of two great quarterbacks, Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes.
content: The Thanksgiving night game between the Bills and Chiefs was billed as the battle of two great quarterbacks, Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. What proved to matter even more was the contrast of two kickers, as Buffalo's Tyler Bass was great and Kansas City's Harrison Butker was not. On a rainy day in Buffalo, the fourth quarter featured Bass making a 54-yard field goal to tie the game 10-10, Butker missing a 46-yard field goal that would have given the lead back to the Chiefs, and then Bass making a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game, 13-10. Bass has been excellent this season. He's now 26-for-27 on field goals in 2026, with his only miss coming from 54 yards in last week's win over the Dolphins. Butker has been terrible this season. He's now 15-for-23 on field goals in 2026, and his eight misses are the most for any kicker in the league. He also hasn't made a single kick longer than 50 yards this season; 31 other NFL kickers have made at least one from beyond 50. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said after the loss that he wasn't ready to say whether Butker will remain the kicker in Kansas City. "I'll go back and go through all of it again," Reid said immediately after the game. "Not gonna make any decisions right this minute." It's hard to see how the Chiefs can stick with Butker down the stretch. A kicker's job is to make his kicks, and Butker simply isn't performing.

title: Latest injury update on Bears TE Colston Loveland
summary: Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland suffered a knee injury against the Detroit Lions. We're tracking the latest updates.
content: The Chicago Bears mounted an impressive 39-35 comeback win over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, improving to 9-2 with their sixth straight win. But they played most of it without tight end Colston Loveland, who suffered an injury early in the game. Loveland suffered a knee injury on Chicago's second offensive possession of the game, where he was blocking for running back D'Andre Swift on a run play. Loveland was checked out at the blue medical tent before being carted to the locker room with a towel over his head. He was later ruled out for the game. It wasn't an encouraging sign for one of the Bears ' most important players, especially given how injuries have already impacted the team. There's concern about Loveland's status moving forward. But what's the latest on his injury? Colston Loveland injury update The Bears suffered another blow at the tight end position with Colston Loveland suffering a knee injury in the first quarter. Loveland, who had committed a brutal fumble on the first possession, was blocking on a run play when he was shoved backward by Lions linebacker Trevor Nowaske and over running back D'Andre Swift. After a brief stint in the medical tent, Loveland was carted to the locker room with a white towel over his face. How much time will Colston Loveland miss? It's currently unknown how much time Colston Loveland will miss after his knee injury. After the game, head coach Ben Johnson said he wasn’t sure about Loveland’s status and that the team planned to find out more Friday. That MRI will be crucial to determining the severity of the injury, and the hope is it's a knee sprain rather than something more severe. Who will play in Colston Loveland's absence? The Bears have been dealt brutal injury blows this season, but no position has been hit worse than tight end, which was the team's strength coming into the 2026 season. Before Loveland's injury, Chicago lost Cole Kmet for the season to a knee injury, which thrust rookie Sam Roush into a larger role. Regardless of how much time Loveland will miss, the Bears will be leaning on their third-round rookie to lead the charge at tight end and Stephen Carlson, who has been a practice squad mainstay. summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin did not hold back Thursday night. It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way — I’ve presided…
content: Jan 4, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin and quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) celebrate after defeating the Baltimore Ravens at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin did not hold back Thursday night. Speaking with Mike Tirico at halftime of NBC’s Chiefs-Bills Thanksgiving game, Tomlin described the ongoing drama in Pittsburgh as “a dumpster fire.” “I’m upset about it. It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way — I’ve presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset,” Tomlin said. The comments came one day after the Steelers released Aaron Rodgers. The quarterback had been benched for Friday’s game against Denver and then appeared on The Pat McAfee Show , where he accused current coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring in meetings, missing walkthroughs and film work, and breaking a halftime huddle with “1-2-3 Packers.” McCarthy later confirmed the huddle slip and said Rodgers had issued an ultimatum outside his job description; the team waived him. Tomlin, who coached Rodgers in 2025 before stepping down after 19 seasons, struck a note of sadness rather than taking sides. He called the public airing of internal issues “counterculture to professional football” and expressed concern that it could mark the end of a legendary career. He also said Rodgers had been “beloved” in the locker room the previous year and had worked to understand Steelers culture and engage with teammates. title: Mike Tomlin Calls Steelers Mess A ‘Dumpster Fire’ After Rodgers Exit
summary: Mike Tomlin labels the Steelers a 'dumpster fire' after Aaron Rodgers' public rant. See the coach's blunt take on the fallout and what it means for the locker room.
content: Nov 9, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin and quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) walk off the field after the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin did not mince words on Thursday , calling the current situation in Pittsburgh a “dumpster fire.” The comment came after Aaron Rodgers aired out dirty laundry on “The Pat McAfee Show,” leading to his swift release on Wednesday. Tomlin, now working as an analyst for NBC, expressed deep sadness over the public nature of the breakup. He noted that the team he led for 19 years has hit a low point that will be hard to fix. Tomlin’s Blunt Assessment of the Chaos Tomlin spoke to Mike Tirico during NBC’s halftime broadcast of the Chiefs-Bills game on Thursday. He admitted he felt a “range of emotions watching that course of events yesterday.” His primary feeling was sadness for a legendary career that might be ending. He also lamented the culture clash, stating that airing grievances in public runs counter to the culture of professional football. Tomlin was clear that he does not say “dumpster fire” in a judgmental way, but rather as a factual description of the mess. He has seen similar situations before. “I’ve presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years,” Tomlin said, according to ESPN . Despite his experience, he emphasized that this specific moment is upsetting for him and for Steeler Nation. The former coach highlighted the shock of seeing Rodgers, who was beloved by the locker room, sever ties on live television. Tomlin praised the quarterback’s work ethic and his genuine embrace of the Steelers culture during their single season together in 2025. Leadership Challenges and the Path Forward The fallout has left head coach Mike McCarthy in a tough spot. Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep during meetings and of lacking effort on the defense. While owner Art Rooney II stated he has “100 percent confidence” in his coach, Tomlin sees a different reality. He told NBC that the situation created challenges, and those challenges are “probably an understatement if all of those things are true,” per the New York Post. The team’s future now hinges on relationships within the building. McCarthy attempted damage control by holding a “very direct” meeting with team leaders . He told reporters via Steelers Now’s Alan Saunders that he appreciated the chance to talk through what was on their minds. McCarthy claimed he is proud of his leadership despite the noise. However, Tomlin warned that overcoming this crisis depends entirely on how the players feel about their coach. If the team does not buy in, the season could spiral further. Other legends weighed in on the drama as well. Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe ripped Rodgers on the Night Cap podcast, calling him arrogant and aloof. Sharpe said Rodgers “lacked leadership” and noted that he is a four-time MVP who has only appeared in one Super Bowl. Meanwhile, the Steelers have turned to Mason Rudolph to start for the final seven games. The team faces the Denver Broncos on Friday with a new quarterback under center. The End of an Era for Rodgers Rodgers cleared waivers on Thursday after the 4 p.m. ET deadline passed with no claims and is now a free agent. Tomlin suggested there is still a possibility for the 42-year-old to play again. ‘It’s a 32-team league,’ he said, noting that all it takes is ‘one suitor’ or one overtime win to change a season. The incident marks a dark chapter for a franchise that values stability. Tomlin’s “dumpster fire” comment captures the severity of the breakdown between a star player and his coach. The Steelers must now decide if they can move past the public accusations and focus on winning the remaining games. The team’s identity is currently in flux as they navigate this unprecedented turmoil.

title: The Morning After...the Bears' comeback win vs. Lions on Thanksgiving
summary: The Chicago Bears defeated the Detroit Lions, 39-35, on Thanksgiving. Our staff shares their thoughts on the team's thrilling comeback win.
content: The Chicago Bears defeated the Detroit Lions , 39-35, on Thanksgiving, winning their sixth straight game, improving to 9-2 and taking hold of first place in the NFC North. The Bears trailed for all but three seconds against the Lions, but they managed to do what they did best last season and mount a fourth-quarter comeback that kicked off a thrilling Thanksgiving slate. Chicago's offense got off to a rough start before kicking into high gear with Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift and Rome Odunze leading the charge. Meanwhile, despite allowing 200-plus rushing yards to Jahmyr Gibbs, they were able to contain Detroit's offense in key moments that helped lead to that impressive comeback. There's plenty to discuss from this game, including Chicago's remarkable fourth-quarter comeback with shades of 2025, Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze's heroics and a defining win in the Ben Johnson era. Our Bears Wire staff is sharing their thoughts on Chicago's Week 12 win victory vs. Detroit. Alyssa Barbieri The Bears delivered a 2025 throwback in their Thanksgiving win over the Lions. After not trailing for a single second since Caleb Williams returned to the starting lineup, they found themselves trailing for most of the game against Detroit. But it's not who's leading for a majority of the time that counts; it's who's leading when the clock strikes zero. And Chicago was able to steal the lead with three seconds remaining to win their sixth straight game, their first against the NFC North, and take sole possession of first place in the NFC North at 9-2. I'll admit, I reverted to my "the sky is falling" mentality as the Bears shot themselves in the foot throughout the first three quarters of the game. Old habits die hard. But, every time, I'm more than happy to admit that I was wrong and Ben Johnson has altered the DNA of this team. Because this is the kind of game that shows you the talent and resilience of this Bears team, as well as why they're a legitimate Super Bowl contender. Even as they're committing a league-high number of turnovers, allowing 200-plus rushing yards to Jahmyr Gibbs and trailing by 11 points in the final eight minutes, Chicago managed to pull off one of their infamous fourth-quarter comebacks as Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze went nuclear for a pair of touchdowns, including the game-winner in the final three seconds. This Bears team has come a long way since two Thanksgivings ago during the meltdown that marked the end of the Matt Eberflus era. Chicago has managed to win in every way possible -- getting an early lead and never relinquishing it or trailing for all but three seconds and getting arguably the biggest win of the Ben Johnson era. When all is said and done, we could very well look back on this game as a defining moment and one that impacts NFC North and NFC playoff seeding as the Bears look to make a run. But, for now, it's a reminder that this Chicago team is never out of a game and, just when you count them out, they relish mounting a comeback that leaves you in awe. Brendan Sugrue Did you miss the heart-racing moments and insane comebacks from 2025? Apparently things were going too well, and the Bears needed to bring back the dramatics to win a football game. In all seriousness, though, that was such a galvanizing victory for every member of the Bears. Outside of last year’s comeback against the Green Bay Packers, it’s their most important regular season win. But this was ugly at many points. The Bears were dreadful for much of the game, particularly on defense. The Lions came ready to play and dominated the line of scrimmage to allow players like Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Jameson Williams to produce chunk plays. They allowed 549 yards, something they haven’t done since 1954, and still pulled out the victory. That’s what happens when you have an elite quarterback on the other side of the ball. Johnson and Williams exorcised some demons Thursday. Johnson got the monkey off his back by defeating his old team in their building, while Williams got his first win over Detroit in his career, as he was in a similar situation from the Thanksgiving gaffe two years ago. Instead of missing Rome Odunze with time expiring, Williams found him in the end zone for their biggest touchdown connection yet. It’s poetic. Even though the Bears were 8-2 coming into this week, Thursday was a must-win game. They needed to climb back in the division and prove they are still capable of beating anyone. And even if things look dire early, you can never count out this group. If you maintained the belief that this is a Super Bowl-caliber team, this game reaffirmed your faith. If you started to have doubts, welcome back. The Bears will be playing in the NFC Championship game at a minimum this year. We just might want to load up on anxiety meds between now and then. Mike Pendleton Coming in this game had to be a signature moment in the young coaching career of Ben Johnson, and in the end it would be not only for him but for quarterback Caleb Williams as well. There is still plenty of cause for concern with the inconsistency on offense and for the first time since Jeffrey Simmons arrived, the defense looked beyond vulnerable. The 2025 version of this team amazed everyone with their ability to have comeback wins in the fourth quarter. Those lessons learned last year helped pave the way for the final minutes of the game, both offense and defense. Linebacker TJ Edwards has always been a center-piece of the defense, albeit mostly overlooked and he had the most important play of the game with his tackle on Jahmyr Gibbs. Chicago has a lot to clean up with Jacksonville up next, but the thrill of victory is alive and well as they sit in first place. Vinnie Parise The Chicago Bears had one of their most epic wins of the Ben Johnson era on Sunday. They found a way to win a football game against and elite division rival, despite being down for most of it. Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for the game winning score with 6 seconds left to make it a Thanksgiving to remember. The Bears are now 9-2. It wasn’t the easiest path to get there, but they now control their own destiny when it comes to winning the NFC North, and securing a home playoff game to kick off the postseason. This win is one that they can learn a lot from. The Bears had two big wins in crunch time last year against the Green Bay Packers, but this feels like Ben Johnson’s signature win. Against his old team, and attempting to win a division where everyone is great, his offense found a way to get it done in the final seconds. This was an incredible way to get it done. Everyone involved should be proud, and now it’s time to prepare for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Ariana Pensy Throughout his head coaching career so far, head coach Ben Johnson has struggled to win division games. Chicago was 0-2 in the NFC North before this game and only had two regular-season wins against the division last season. They were swept by Detroit last season and quarterback Caleb Williams had not defeated the Lions yet in his NFL career after their Thanksgiving blunder in 2024. Getting this win was important for many reasons, but getting their first win against Detroit since 2023 and taking control of the NFC North were certainly top on the list. With the score 19-10 at halftime, this did not seem like the type of game that would end in a shootout. The Bears’ offense struggled throughout that first half and their safety debacle was ugly to see. Honestly, at that point, it seems like Chicago was on their way to a third division loss this season. But their offense got going in the second half, scoring a touchdown on four of their six drives. They also held Detroit to 16 points in the second half and generated a turnover, which is a victory given how Jahmyr Gibbs went off against them. Chicago’s defense against Gibbs was probably the ugliest part of this game. He had over 200 rushing yards and averaged nearly 10 yards per carry; Gibbs also had a total of three touchdowns. No one in the NFL is playing on Gibbs’ level right now, so the Bears’ defense probably will not be exploited this badly going forward. Still, it was shocking to see this team give up that many yards on the ground. But winning teams overcome adversity and that is precisely what Chicago did in this game. Odunze’s game-winning touchdown has to be the best catch in his NFL career so far. The Bears also had a turnover of their own early in the game by tight end Colston Loveland, who was not able to return due to a knee injury. This is a Super Bowl-caliber team and possibly the best overall team the Bears have had since 1985. Randy Holt The Bears allowed over 200 yards rushing to Jahmyr Gibbs and 300 yards passing to Jared Goff. They fumbled twice in the first half, one of which was lost and one of which led to a safety and subsequent touchdown for the Lions ahead of the end of the first half. Caleb Williams was sacked four times. And not only did they trail for the first time in five games, but they were behind for all but three seconds of a 60-minute game. All of those things seem to matter just a little bit less, however, when Caleb Williams is your quarterback and Ben Johnson is your head coach. Obviously, there were a number of different developments on Thursday that were less than ideal. The defense could not match the speed of Detroit. Colston Loveland may have sustained a long-term injury. But the Bears proved that the ability to work back from adversity compounded with a deficit on the scoreboard is still very much woven into the fabric of this team, even if we haven’t seen it this year in the way that we did so frequently in 2025. Williams was, of course, at the heart of it all. Following a 70-yard touchdown run by Gibbs, he led the Bears on a three-play scoring drive to narrow the margin to three. And while the defense struggled all afternoon, all they needed was to give their offense a chance. A late interception and a massive stop of Gibbs by T.J. Edwards on fourth down did just that, with Williams seizing the moment in a way to which we’ve become so accustomed over the past two years. Let’s not forget Rome Odunze’s role in all of it, either. There was always a world in which this was the worst we saw out of the Bears on defense; Detroit at home with their speed is a tough ask of any unit. And the loss of Loveland shouldn’t be overlooked in all of this. After a couple of more muted performances on offense, though, they got both Caleb Williams (345 yards) and the run game (6.1 YPC) back in a direction that can match anyone. Toss in the first division win of the year, and it’s hard to find a more momentous one in the win column than the one the Bears put up on Thursday. title: ‘Who needs Aaron Rodgers?’ – Steelers fans react to Mason Rudolph’s performance vs Broncos
summary: Mason Rudolph led the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the Denver Broncos in his first start since Aaron Rodgers was released. It has been quite the week for the Steelers, with Rudolph handed a matter of days to prepare himself to start in Rodgers’ place.
content: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Mason Rudolph led the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the Denver Broncos in his first start since Aaron Rodgers was released. It has been quite the week for the Steelers, with Rudolph handed a matter of days to prepare himself to start in Rodgers’ place. Despite the short notice, the 31-year-old looked like he had been starting all season long for the Steelers. In what was a huge opportunity for the Steelers to silence some of the outside noise, it was clear that the new starting quarterback in Pittsburgh impressed the fans. So much so that a lot of Steeler Nation were left suggesting Rodgers may have actually been the problem all along. Pittsburgh Steelers fans react to Mason Rudolph’s performance in win over Broncos After Rodgers was initially benched by Mike McCarthy, a lot of people believed it wasn’t down to his performance. As it surfaced that there had been a major disagreement behind the scenes, Rudolph was left to focus on his preparation amid the outside noise. ‘Maybe Mason Rudolph just throws a better ball than Aaron Rodgers,’ said one Steelers fan on X. ‘Boy, Rodgers is looking bad right now,’ added another. Rudolph ended the game with 142 passing yards and a single touchdown. Importantly, the quarterback did not turn the ball over, unlike Bo Nix, who threw two interceptions in what was just an awful game for the Broncos QB. Following the comments on McCarthy’s bad habits inside the Steelers’ building, one fan said: ‘Are we sure Aaron Rodgers wasn’t the one sleeping during the meetings?’ ‘Rodgers was the problem wow,’ another said. Interestingly, the change at quarterback seemed to get the best out of DK Metcalf, who scored a touchdown on Patrick Sutain II inside the opening quarter. However, Metcalf sent a message of support to Rodgers through his celebration. ‘Who needs Aaron Rodgers?’ said one fan. ‘Rodgers must feel like a clown today,’ added another. title: NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Giants matchup
summary: Who do the NFL experts have winning on Sunday between the Indianapolis Colts and the Giants? Let's take a look.
content: The Indianapolis Colts return home in Week 12 for a matchup with the New York Giants . After moving on from Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson will make his first start since the 2024 season. title: Is there an NFL game today? Which teams play on Black Friday?
summary: In case three NFL games on Thanksgiving weren't enough, the league is hosting its fourth-ever Black Friday game.
content: Black Friday isn't just a day for shopping around for the best deals. It's now also a day for football . In case three NFL games on Thanksgiving weren't enough, the league is hosting its fourth-ever Black Friday game. The NFL held its first Black Friday game in 2023. While Thanksgiving is most commonly associated with football, the NFL turned it into a full weekend experience as the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers face off a day after America consumed copious amounts of turkey. Here's what you need to know about the NFL Black Friday game, including how to tune in. Which NFL teams play on Black Friday? The Denver Broncos will travel to Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to face the Steelers on Black Friday. Both the Steelers and Broncos made the playoffs in 2025 but suffered tough losses that kept them shy of a Super Bowl appearance. This Week 12 game between the two teams could play a significant part in determining the AFC playoff picture in 2026. What time does the Broncos vs. Steelers game start? 3 p.m. ET. Kickoff for the NFL's Black Friday game is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET. It is the lone game of the day and fits in just before the typical late slate of games football fans enjoy on Sundays. Because Amazon Prime Video is not carrying any of the Thursday games, which it typically does during the regular season, the streaming-only network is carrying the NFL's Black Friday game. Local viewers in Denver and Pittsburgh can catch the game on cable. Al Michaels will be on the call with analyst Kirk Herbstreit and sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung. How to watch the Broncos vs. Steelers on Black Friday TV channel: ABC (for in-market viewers). Streaming: Amazon Prime Video. Stream the NFL's Black Friday game on Amazon ABC will also simulcast the game locally. The Broncos-Steelers game airs on KMGH-TV (channel 7) in the Denver area and WTAE-TV (channel 4) in Pittsburgh. title: NFL Under Fire After Refs’ Controversial Call Wipes Out Eagles TD Following Javonte Williams Fumble During Cowboys Clash
summary: An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted.
content: LANDOVER, MD – DECEMBER 25: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams 33 reads his blockers during game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Washington Commanders on December 25, 2025 at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD. Photo by Charles Brock/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA DEC 25 Cowboys at Commanders EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon251225004 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted. The officials’ interpretation of forward progress is disputed; some analysts argue Williams did fumble before being ruled down. Nevertheless, the ruling has now prompted fans and analysts to question how the rule was applied and whether the league enforces it consistently across games. “Whistle halts Riq Woolen return after Javonte Williams fumble. Nick Sirianni protested the early stoppage,” Wire Report NFL posted on X . Williams was driving toward the end zone when the ball came loose just short of the goal line in the second quarter. Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen scooped it up and took off for a 97-yard return that looked like a touchdown. Before he got there, the whistle blew. The officials ruled that Williams’ forward progress had already been stopped, which meant the play was dead before Woolen reached the end zone, preventing a TD rather than erasing one. When a touchdown gets erased in a rivalry game, the entire playoff picture shifts. Stay ahead of every controversial call and its impact with EssentiallySports NFL coverage. That ruling carries a harsh consequence, because forward progress calls can’t be challenged. Nick Sirianni had nothing to throw a flag over and no review to ask for, so the Eagles simply had to line up again. Dallas then scored its own touchdown to build the halftime cushion. By the start of the fourth quarter, the Cowboys led 31-17, with Philadelphia having added ten points in the second quarter and seven in the third. The officials’ call on it is now drawing heavy criticism. One fan, whose comment was originally in Spanish, summed up how it looked from the stands: “To me, this was a fumble by Javonte Williams and a potential defensive TD for the Eagles that would have made it 21-17 at halftime. The refs blew the whistle (too early, in my opinion), and that killed the play. Anyway… on to the next one.” Media voices were just as direct. Former ESPN writer Ed Werder pointed to how plays like this are usually handled: “That was a quick whistle on the potential Javonte Williams fumble and Eagles recovery. They usually allow that to play out through the return. Riq Woolen was stopped from a 98-yard return by whistle. Nick Sirianni had a legit argument and made it.” Eagles reporter Brandon Lee Gowton was far less diplomatic, as he said on X, “Absolute horseshit ruling on that Javonte Williams fumble creates a 14-point swing in the Cowboys’ favor. Abysmal officiating.” Interestingly, the frustration wasn’t limited to Philadelphia’s side. Cowboys beat reporter Joseph Hoyt saw it the same way. “They’re going to say his forward progress is stopped, but Javonte Williams did fumble that, it was a clear recovery, and Tariq Woolen took it back for a TD. Cowboys catch a HUGE break,” Hoyt wrote on X. Fan comments piled up too. One take captured the mood of the Eagles faithful. “Eagles fans feel robbed 😤 Philly appeared to rip the ball from Javonte Williams near the goal line, but officials ruled his forward progress was stopped, and the call wasn’t reviewable. #FlyEaglesFly” And one fan directed his anger straight at the league’s officiating account. :@NFLOfficiating enough of this garbage of a product you have out there. Fine them, fire them, do something!”, a fan wrote. A call that can’t be reviewed leaves nothing but the debate, and this one will be argued for a long time. title: Pat McAfee Comes to Brandon Aubrey’s Defense & Blames Cowboys Snapper for Missed Field Goal
summary: The Dallas Cowboys’ Thanksgiving game did not go as planned, despite making significant headway in the first two quarters of the game. But the Philadelphia Eagles made a late-game comeback, scoring 22 points in the final quarter itself.
content: November 15, 2025, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA: November 15, 2025: Pat McAfee on ESPN College Game Day during the University of Pittsburgh Panthers vs. Notre Dame Fighting Irish at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh PA. Brook Ward / Apparent Media Group Pittsburgh USA – ZUMAa234 20251115_zsa_a234_326 Copyright: xAMGx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire The Dallas Cowboys’ Thanksgiving game did not go as planned, despite making significant headway in the first two quarters of the game. But the Philadelphia Eagles made a late-game comeback, scoring 22 points in the final quarter itself. What sealed their narrow 39-38 win over the Cowboys was a missed field goal opportunity by Brandon Aubrey, earning the Cowboys kicker a fair amount of criticism. But NFL analyst Pat McAfee pushed back against the Brandon Aubrey slander with an X post uploaded on November 26 , pointing out the real reason Aubrey missed. “Just a reminder.. In modern football, [with] long snapping being a full time job, the snapper is 90% responsible for the laces,” McAfee wrote. The opportunity for the field goal came late in the fourth quarter with three minutes and 27 seconds left on the clock. On fourth-and-5 play at Philadelphia’s 22-yard line, holder Bryan Anger placed the ball but failed to turn the laces around in time before Aubrey kicked the ball. With the Cowboys kicker making contact with the side of the ball with the laces out, the 40-yard attempt flew wide left rather than straight through the uprights. When a kicker takes heat, the details matter. Subscribe to stay across the Cowboys' roster drama and the technical breakdowns reshaping playoff narratives. The miss proved to be disastrous for the Cowboys and prevented them from establishing an 11-point lead that would have sealed their win. But the Eagles soon scored a touchdown and a field goal that gave them a single-point lead with two seconds left on the clock. But while most critics blamed Aubrey for costing the Cowboys their sixth win of the season, McAfee pointed out that there was a reason why the NFL had stepped away from the tradition of using backup centers or punters as long snappers. He reasoned that the entire responsibility of a long snapper was to perfectly snap the ball to the punter or the holder, who spotted it on the ground just before the kicker struck it. So, the responsibility of making sure that the laces were not facing the kicker fell on the snapper, rather than the holder or the kicker. In the NFL, a long snapper controls where the laces land by repeating the exact same snap tempo, grip, and distance every time, which allows the ball to complete a certain number of rotations before reaching the holder. In this case, McAfee assigned the blame to the Cowboys’ long snapper Trent Sieg. He believed that Sieg was the one who should have been held accountable for his role, which was to make sure the ball landed with the laces facing away from Aubrey when he made the field goal attempt. During the postgame conference, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer also addressed the missed opportunity. Rather than blaming Aubrey, the head coach stated that he was going to reserve his judgment until he watched the film and assessed the special team’s overall execution. title: Patriots vs. Chargers weather forecast: It won’t matter, and that’s good for New England
summary: Up-to-date weather forecast for Sunday’s game between the Patriots and Chargers.
content: SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA, is an indoor arena and therefore unbothered by the elements. This means that any weather forecast for Sunday’s game between the New England Patriots and their hosts, the Los Angeles Chargers, will be irrelevant and have no bearing on the outcome of the Week 12 contest. For a 5-5 Patriots team currently outside of the playoff picture but well within striking range — particularly considering some recent developments elsewhere in the AFC — that should be a positive. Why? Because a controlled environment without any meteorological challenges means one less factor of uncertainty surrounding backup quarterback Tommy DeVito, who is set to start his first game in place of the injured Drake Maye. In addition, no weather impact also should help the Patriots in the kicking game; Andy Borregales has made just 11 of 14 field goal tries and also missed one of his 25 extra points this season. With wind not a significant factor, however, he will not have to worry about this part of the operation being an issue. In what might end up as a close game, any help he and the Patriots as a whole can get in that regard is welcome. As for the conditions outside the stadium, the temperature at kickoff is projected as mostly sunny with a high of around 74°F by the National Weather Service . No precipitation is in the forecast. Kickoff between the Patriots and Chargers at SoFi Stadium on Sunday was flexed from primetime to 4:05 p.m. ET .

title: Joe Milton, Eagles pull off stunning upset vs. Cowboys | How it happened
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are facing the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving at AT&T Stadium in Week 12 NFL action. Follow along for live updates.
content: Happy Thanksgiving, Philadelphia Eagles fans. Joe Milton and the Eagles pulled off an unbelievable upset win on Thanksgiving, beating the Dallas Cowboys, 39-38, at AT&T STadium. The Eagles trailed by 21 points in the third quarter. It didn’t matter. Nick Sirianni’s team rattled off 22 fourth-quarter points and upended the Cowboys in stunning fashion. Here’s how it happened. FOURTH QUARTER 0:02 — Eagles 39, Cowboys 38 Unbelievable. Jake Elliott drilled a 60-yard field goal to win it. JAKE ELLIOTT FROM 60 YARDS OUT EAGLES COMEBACK IS COMPLETE PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LJoGRn56xr — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 2:10 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 36 Joe Milton did it again. Unbelievable. The cannon-armed QB engineered a four-play, 70-yard touchdown drive, ending in a 24-yard strike to Makai Lemon in the back of the end zone. However, the Eagles’ two-point conversion attempt to tie the game fell incomplete. So, the Eagles will need another defensive stop and a field goal to pull the upset. MILTON TO LEMON OH MY PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LMyTJqf8v5 — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 7:05 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 30 Joe Milton couldn’t keep his ridiculous play going, throwing a bad interception into triple coverage on third-and-16. The Eagles’ defense has to come up with a stop to get the ball back for Milton and the offense to pull off the upset. 9:09 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 30 And just like that, the Eagles are back in it. Joe Milton is having a day. After a 55-yard kickoff return by Britain Covey, the Eagles needed only three plays to find the end zone. Two completions to DeVonta Smith preceded Milton’s 15-yard touchdown scramble to cut the Cowboys’ lead. Nick Sirianni decided to go for the two-point conversion, and the Eagles didn’t get it. But this is yet again a game. JM3 TAKING OFF pic.twitter.com/uOmx34nE6S — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 27, 2026 10:11 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 24 Just like that, the Cowboys answer. Quinyon Mitchell got put on skates by Ceedee Lamb, who ripped off a 39-yard catch-and-run into Eagles’ territory. A few plays later, Dak Prescott went airborne for an acrobatic, 14-yard touchdown scramble to make it a two-score game again. INSANE EFFORT BY @dak 🤯 📺: #PHIvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/J9HR0OTmZi — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 27, 2026 13:46 — Cowboys 31, Eagles 24 Well, well, well. We have a game. After a huge defensive stop on third-and-short, defensive tackle Ty Robinson blocked the Cowboys’ punt, and Kenny Moore returned it for a touchdown. Just like that, the Eagles are back in it. EAGLES BLOCKED PUNT TD PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1mrM5lDeTK — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 THIRD QUARTER 0:15 — Cowboys 31, Eagles 17 This Joe Milton-DeVonta Smith connection has been fun to watch. For the second time, Milton uncorked a bomb downfield for Smith. The Eagles’ WR1 was wide open and hauled in a 45-yard touchdown for his second of the day. The Eagles are going to go into the fourth quarter down 14. The defense needs to step up if they want to pull this off. Went back for seconds 😏 pic.twitter.com/6bGjh1x6wK — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 27, 2026 3:35 — Cowboys 31, Eagles 10 The Cowboys have made this a 21-point game thanks to a 59-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey. The Eagles are going to need a touchdown on this next drive and a miracle from Joe Milton to make this thing close. SECOND QUARTER 0:04 — Cowboys 28, Eagles 10 The Eagles might have gotten jobbed there. What looked like a clear fumble by Javonte Williams and a recovery by Riq Woolen was waved off due to, in the referees’ eyes, Williams’ forward progress being stopped. Just a really bad call. Williams was still fighting for the end zone. Anyway, the Cowboys took advantage of their extra chance. A dump-off pass to Williams got him into the end zone, and Dallas takes a three-score lead into halftime. THE REFS JUST BLEW THE PLAY DIED RIQ WOOLEN PICKED THE FUMBLE UP BUT FORWARD PROGRESSED WAS CALLED NO NO NO NO pic.twitter.com/4Ps1TNllV4 — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) November 26, 2026 4:06 — Cowboys 21, Eagles 10 That was fun! Joe Milton earned his “Mr. Rocket” nickname there, unleashing a 50-yard missile downfield toward DeVonta Smith. And the “Slim Reaper” did his thing, making a leaping touchdown grab. The Eagles probably aren’t going to win this game. But that was a hell of a play — giving Birds fans something to be thankful for while housing Thanksgiving seconds. MR. ROCKET ➡️ SMITTY pic.twitter.com/lnUam2a5jU — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 26, 2026 5:09 — Cowboys 21, Eagles 3 Yeah, this has the makings of a blowout. The Cowboys just rattled off six-play, 60-yard touchdown drive, punctuated by a 12-yard rushing score by Javonte Williams. The Eagles’ defense is getting worked. Plain and simple. Javonte Williams 2 tuddies! PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kEk9TAiXuz — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 8:09 — Cowboys 14, Eagles 3 Saquon Barkley is questionable to return with a stinger. Dallas Goedert is questionable with a shoulder injury. Guys are dropping like flies. But at least Joe Milton is balling. Milton had a couple of dimes on a drive that finished with a 48-yard field goal by Jake Elliott. Milton found DeVonta Smith, who went up for a 24-yard catch. And he escaped third-down pressure to hit Makai Lemon for a 20-yard gain. The Eagles are going to need touchdowns, not field goals, in order to come back and win this one. But a positive drive. Milton scrambles and finds Makai Lemon to convert on 3rd and long 🔥 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5VDZMI6ZOn — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 DeVonta Smith gets UP to make this catch 😳 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SmyS6ylWf9 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 FIRST QUARTER 0:36 — Cowboys 14, Eagles 0 This is getting ugly quick. The Cowboys took advantage of the fourth-down stop with a 31-yard touchdown by Kavontae Turpin. The speedster turned on the jets. Too easy. The Eagles’ defense should have been off the field before the Turpin score. But they allowed another long conversion, this time on third-and-16. The Eagles’ defense was going to have to play its “A” game in order for Nick Sirianni’s team to be in this game. That’s not happening so far. KAVONTAE TURPIN IS TOO FAST PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0MqBAQPtHh — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 3:14 — Cowboys 7, Eagles 0 That was some brutal stuff from Sean Mannion and the Eagles’ offense. They had a nice drive going, marching 58 yards on 10 plays down to the Cowboys’ 36-yard line. The Eagles went for it, which was smart. But the play-call wasn’t. The Eagles lined up under center with Saquon Barkley as the fullback and Will Shipley as the running back in a split formation. Instead of QB sneaking with Joe Milton, the Eagles handed it off to Barkley, and he was stuffed. Ugly stuff. Quinnen Williams and the Cowboys' defense is up to the task on 4th down 😤 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rQypBXtAtk — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 8:50 — Cowboys 7, Eagles 0 Welp, that couldn’t have started any worse for the Eagles. The Cowboys went on an 11-play, 77-yard touchdown march on the game’s opening series. Cooper DeJean went off with what appeared to be a concussion. Dak Prescott converted a third-and-18, finding a wide-open Ceedee Lamb. And Javonte Williams punched in a goal-to-go score. Let’s see if Joe Milton and the Eagles can answer. Dak to CeeDee for a big 3rd down conversion 👏 📺: #PHIvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/B4AEcF3gaz — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 26, 2026 Read the original article on NJ.com . title: Pittsburgh Steelers ease to victory against Denver Broncos
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers earned a comfortable 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos. The game was the Steelers' first since veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers was released on Wednesday and they took a dominant 14-0 lead in the first quarter.
content: FILE PHOTO - A view of the NFL logo on the pitch before the 2026 NFL Game between Atalanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at the Santiago Bernabeu. (is associated with: «Pittsburgh Steelers ease to victory against Denver Broncos») Nathalia Araújo/dpa The Pittsburgh Steelers earned a comfortable 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos. The game was the Steelers' first since veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers was released on Wednesday and they took a dominant 14-0 lead in the first quarter. TJ Watt pounced on a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone before Mason Rudolph found DK Metcalf, with Chris Boswell making the extra point both times. Denver earned their first points with a safety and Wil Lutz's field-goal, but Pittsburgh responded when Jalen Ramsey intercepted Nix's throw before charging into the end zone to take a 24-5 lead at the break. Boswell extended the Steelers' advantage with a fourth-quarter field-goal to wrap up their seventh win of the season.

title: Rams Legend Weighs in on Aaron Rodgers/Steelers Fiasco
summary: This Rams legend chimed in on the much debated Aaron Rodgers/Steelers issue. The post Rams Legend Weighs in on Aaron Rodgers/Steelers Fiasco appeared first on HEAVY.
content: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams talks with Aaron Rodgers #8 of the New York Jets. Getty Aaron Rodgers versus Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers engulfed the NFL’s Thanksgiving week. Their fallout even occurred on the eve of the Los Angeles Rams’ pre-Turkey Day win over Rodgers’ former team, the Green Bay Packers. Still, Rodgers’ release following his explosive interview on The Pat McAfee Show sparked a bevy of reactions including from former NFL players. Now one Rams legend chimed in with a deep “motives” take on Black Friday. Which Rams Legend Dove Into Aaron Rodgers/Steelers Debacle Former Rams quarterback Jim Everett delivered a deep take on the matter. Except the Rams star from the late 1980s, early 1990s shined a light on Rodgers using new media to his advantage here. “You’ve heard a lot of voices say Aaron Rodgers should have kept it in house. Stay quiet. Be a team guy,” Everett began in his post on the social media website X , formerly Twitter. “Most of those voices get paid by the NFL system.” Everett then explained how “teams, networks, sponsors” all form “the status quo works for them.” Then Everett shared what speaking out really does in this situation. “Speak up and you risk the next job. Stay quiet and the system keeps rolling, even if it rolls right over you,” Everett added. ‘Independent’ Aspect That Comes Into Play for Aaron Rodgers Here But then the LA media personality Everett shined a light on how independent media hands Rodgers leverage to air out the dirty laundry involving his now former team. “People outside that money circle see it differently, more independent thought than automatic loyalty,” Everett added. “This is why this one is different.” Everett concluded with “Watch who is defending silence and who is attacking the guy who spoke. Their motives speak the loudest.” Rodgers represents the latter in this case. Deeper Meaning Behind Platform Aaron Rodgers Has One counterargument is Rodgers having 22 NFL seasons under his watch allows him to speak freely. Everett himself acknowledged that Rodgers has that leverage. However, the rise of “new media” has benefitted athletes like Rodgers to become more outspoken. He’s built a strong relationship and widely publicized one with the former NFL punter for the Indianapolis Colts McAfee. It just so happens a past Packers teammate of Rodgers AJ Hawk is a contributor to the show too. Hawk and Rodgers won the 2010 season Super Bowl together, which became Rodgers’ lone title. McAfee’s show guests are former or current NFL players, allowing those athletes including Rodgers to feel comfortable in that realm. However, multiple reports revealed Rodgers is paid to appear on McAfee, which in turn hands him the power to dictate what questions the panel can ask him plus allow Rodgers to hold nothing back with his words on the platform. Still, Rodgers’ rant sparked his demise from the Steelers. He accused McCarthy of “snoring” during team meetings and not diving deep into the game plan. Rodgers’ final straw was McCarthy and Pittsburgh denying him the power to call his own plays. The Rams struggled against Rodgers, owning a 2-6 record all-time against him. But LA defeated a New York Jets team led by him in 2024. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Rams Legend Weighs in on Aaron Rodgers/Steelers Fiasco appeared first on HEAVY .

title: Recent opponents reportedly spill truth about Patriots 'soft' defense
summary: The Patriots' defense was reportedly called "soft" by recent opponents.
content: The perception from some of the New England Patriots' recent opponents is that the defensive unit is "soft." That's a major turnaround for a unit that was considered one of the best in the NFL last season. With that said, the Patriots have given up 99 points in total over the last three games. That includes 35 points against the Detroit Lions and 45 points against the Green Bay Packers. There really is no sugar-coating the fact that it has looked like a disaster at times against top-tier offensive teams. Even worse, those other teams are starting to talk about it. "I've had conversations with people that have played the Patriots of late, and that is a word that has come up about their defense is soft," Perry said on Zolak & Bertrand . "And softer than what they were anticipating I think, too, because you have some big names, especially up front there like in the interior and the way they were moved in that Lions game I think surprised a lot of people." The defensive front has struggled to stop the run and get home consistently enough to impact opposing quarterbacks. However, one of the more disappointing problems for the Patriots has been their defensive backfield. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez hasn't played up to his potential, and Carlton Davis Davis hasn't been available due to injury. Kevin Byard has also struggled at safety. There is also the fact that defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr hasn't been as effective as a play-caller as he was a year ago. Overall, it has been a frustrating season for a defensive unit that came into the year with high expectations. The good news is that there is still time left to turn things around with the hardest stretch of football still ahead. Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook . title: Which remaining opponent scares Washington fans most? Here is how Hogs Haven voted in Week 12 - survey results
summary: Consecutive prime-time victories over Giants & Bengals have erased gloom of the 1-3 start; with Dallas stumbling on Thanksgiving, Washington is squarely in the NFC East hunt
content: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Climbing out of an early hole Not so long ago, for many Commanders fans, the 2026 season felt like it might slip away before Halloween. Washington stumbled out of the gate to a 1-3 start, absorbing frustrating losses to the Eagles, Cowboys, and Colts while fans questioned whether the players and coaching staff could stabilize the ship. Fast forward to the end of November, and the view from Northwest Stadium looks markedly different. Over the past four games, the Commanders have gone 3-1 — taking down two division leaders in the New York Giants (24-21) and Cincinnati Bengals (22-20), getting a useful divisional win against the Eagles, and dropping only a tight 20-13 decision to a strong 7-4 Los Angeles Rams team. Currently standing at 4-5-1, Washington is far from a finished product, and nobody is booking Super Bowl flights just yet. Still, the trajectory has shifted, and the schedule ahead opens up considerably compared to the front-loaded gauntlet the burgundy & gold has had to take on and survive. This week’s Reacts survey: Confidence roars back In our Week 12 Hogs Haven Reacts survey, we opened with our standard barometer question: Are you confident about the direction of the team? The numbers reflect a dramatic mood swing across the community: 80% voted “Yes,” while just 20% voted “No.” That 34-point leap from last week’s 46% mark represents the highest confidence rating since Week 2 (83%) and a sharp reversal from the 14% nadir recorded two weeks ago. Reading through the comments section of the survey article and Feed post surveys, the drivers behind that optimism are clear. First-year defensive coordinator Daronte Jones earned widespread praise for orchestrating Monday night’s shutdown of Joe Burrow and Cincinnati. Despite missing key front-seven pieces like Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne (both on injured reserve and out for the balance of the regular season), Washington held the Bengals to 31 rushing yards on 14 carries and limited Ja’Marr Chase to 31 receiving yards. Commenters like MikeDHTTC and WashNDUNC pointed directly to Jones’ two-high safety looks and late-game pressure — culminating in Nick Cross’s third-down sack on Cincinnati’s final drive — as evidence that the defense has, at last, found its identity. On offense, fans have rallied around Jayden Daniels’s late-game poise and the emergence of young playmakers. Daniels engineered a 64-yard drive in 34 seconds, without timeouts, to set up rookie kicker Drew Stevens’ walk-off field goal on Monday night, leaning on rookie receiver Antonio Williams (nine catches, 122 yards) and tight end Chig Okonkwo (66 yards) in the latter portions of the game. As Rook6980 noted, seeing a young core — including Williams, Sonny Styles, Trey Amos, and Josh Conerly Jr. — produce alongside Daniels gives the fanbase tangible proof of a sustainable foundation. Even among the 20% who voted “No”, the skepticism wasn’t rooted in despair; rather, they want to see offensive coordinator David Blough string together cleaner first halves against inferior opponents before fully buying in to the idea that the team is on-track. Which remaining opponent poses the toughest test? Our second question asked readers which of Washington’s remaining opponents will be the toughest to beat. The results broke down heavily toward one NFC North contender: Visit our partners at FanDuel The Vikings loom large In reviewing the comments, I found the logic behind the 56% vote for Minnesota was virtually unanimous: Brian Flores’ defense. Readers like evarigan , OMG-WTF , and Redskins75 cited the Vikings’ league-best scoring defense (allowing just 16.1 points per game) and aggressive blitz packages as a nightmare matchup on the road at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 16. Respondents also pointed out the intriguing chess match between Flores and his former pupil, Daronte Jones, alongside the storyline of facing former Washington quarterback Kirk Cousins. Are the Jaguars being overlooked? Because the Jaguars play in the AFC South, many NFC-focused fans may simply be less familiar with Liam Coen’s squad — and may have been swayed by Jacksonville’s surprising 23-18 loss to the Giants last week. When you stack Minnesota’s full body of work against that of the Jacksonville Jaguars, an interesting pattern emerges. Statistically, the 7-3 Jaguars could actually be the more complete team: While Minnesota has been “winning ugly” behind an elite defense and a 28th-ranked scoring offense, Jacksonville boasts a top-six scoring attack to go with a top-three scoring defense. Commenters evarigan and Alex Rowsey nailed that distinction, noting that traveling to Jacksonville in Week 17 to take on that balanced AFC juggernaut could ultimately prove even more daunting than the trip to Minneapolis. A note about the Simple Rating System: You may not be aware of the SRS, so I thought I’d include an explanatory note here about what it is and where it comes from: Simple Rating System (SRS) is a statistical metric created and maintained by Pro-Football-Reference (Sports Reference) that evaluates a team’s overall quality using only two inputs: point differential and strength of schedule. An SRS rating of 0.0 represents a league-average team. A team’s score tells you how many points better or worse than an average team they are on a neutral field. For example, an SRS of +9.89 means a team is roughly 10 points better than an average NFL squad, whereas a +4.31 rating puts a team about four points above average. How it works The formula is straightforward: SRS = Average Margin of Victory + Strength of Schedule Because strength of schedule depends on the quality of opponents—whose own ratings depend on their opponents—Pro-Football-Reference solves a system of linear equations across all 32 teams simultaneously so that every team’s rating accounts for the exact point differentials of every opponent they have played. For an explanation of EPA per play in the NFL, CLICK HERE The NFC East picture after Thanksgiving The Cowboys in Week 18 Interestingly, 13% of voters pegged the Dallas Cowboys as the toughest hurdle left on the slate, with WashingtonFMJ_Bulletskins and IronMike66 predicting the Week 18 finale will decide the division. Notably, our survey closed before Thursday’s Thanksgiving action, when Dallas blew a 21-point lead and fell 39-38 to the Eagles on a late Jake Elliott field goal. I’m not sure how much that outcome might have changed a few votes in the survey. That Dallas stumble leaves the NFC East standings tightly bunched heading into Sunday: Because Washington’s record includes a tie, and the Commanders have played one fewer game than Dallas, a victory in Arizona on Sunday pulls the Commanders even with the Cowboys at five wins and keeps Washington ahead of Dallas in the division race. Over the final seven games, the math is straightforward: Washington needs to outpace Dallas by at least one win and make up two wins on the Giants in order to finish with at least the same number of wins as both divisional rivals, claiming the NFC East crown. What’s right in front of us: Commanders at Cardinals Before worrying about Minnesota, Jacksonville, or Dallas, Washington has to handle business in the desert against the 3-8 Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Under head coach Mike LaFleur, Arizona has struggled on both sides of the ball, ranking 29th in scoring offense (17.4 points per game) and 31st in scoring defense (29.4 points per game) while dropping three straight. Even so, tight end Trey McBride (63 receiving yards per game) remains a focal point that will test Washington’s linebackers and safeties. The Cardinals have beaten both the Rams and the Cowboys this season, and can’t be taken lightly by the Commanders if Washington hopes to finish the season with a winning record and compete for the division title. For those tracking the action with our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook, oddsmakers do expect the Commanders to keep their momentum rolling: Spread: Washington Commanders -7.5 (-105) / Arizona Cardinals +7.5 (-115) Moneyline: Commanders -375 / Cardinals +300 Over/Under: 41.5 points (-110/-110) Kickoff at State Farm Stadium is set for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday — which means a 4:25 a.m. Monday wake-up call for those of us watching from Bangkok. If Washington avoids the slow start that plagued them early against Cincinnati and takes care of a vulnerable Cardinals squad, that 80% confidence number should have plenty of staying power heading into December! title: Rodgers gear slashed to $3 as Steelers fans embrace Mason Rudolph era
summary: Garments featuring Rodgers have been marked down to $3 each or $12 for a dozen.
content: WPXI The Pittsburgh Steelers have cut ties with quarterback Aaron Rodgers following an interview on “The Pat McAfee Show,” prompting Strip District businesses and fans to move forward ahead of a Black Friday matchup. Backup Mason Rudolph has taken over the starting quarterback role as Pittsburgh enters the game with a 6-4 record. The roster change quickly reached Penn Avenue in the Strip District, where merchants began clearing out team apparel. At sports merchandise shop Yinzers in the Burgh, the phrase “Mr. Rodger’s Neighborhood” is no longer displayed, replaced by steep discounts on items featuring the former quarterback. Garments featuring Rodgers have been marked down to $3 each or $12 for a dozen. A store employee commented on the inventory clearance, saying, “We are selling a lot of them – mostly to his family, but that’s okay.” The retailer also intends to produce a Christmas Rudolph shirt. Supporters in the district shared contrasting views on the quarterback change. One fan reflected on the departure, saying, “To me, it was almost tragic, you know, the way it happened and how really bad it is on the organization.” Another supporter welcomed the spectacle, adding, “I don’t want to miss a chance to watch a dumpster fire on fire float down the Allegheny River.” Other supporters expressed confidence in Rudolph and the team’s playoff hopes. “We’re 6-4. We’re not out of it, by a long shot,” one supporter said. Another supporter pointed to Pittsburgh’s strengths, saying, “We play really well at home and have a really good defense, so we’re hoping to rally around him today.” Download the FREE WPXI News app for breaking news alerts.
