title: Skip Bayless highlights the Cowboys ‘problem’ after giving up largest NFL lead in Thanksgiving history
summary: The Dallas Cowboys’ Thanksgiving ended in disappointment as they somehow managed to blow a 21-point lead against a struggling Philadelphia Eagles team. The Eagles are without star quarterback Jalen Hurts and went into Thursday’s game with a 3-7 record.
content: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys’ Thanksgiving ended in disappointment as they somehow managed to blow a 21-point lead against a struggling Philadelphia Eagles team. The Eagles are without star quarterback Jalen Hurts and went into Thursday’s game with a 3-7 record. Yet Philadelphia, who were 31-10 down in the third quarter, somehow managed to come back to win 39-38, handing the Cowboys the unfortunate record of giving away the largest lead on Thanksgiving in NFL history. Skip Bayless thinks the Dallas Cowboys don’t fear losing This collapse has obviously not gone down well with fans of the Dallas outfit, with Skip Bayless among them. Highlighting the problem with the current Cowboys team, he suggested that they do not ‘fear losing’ while also listing several other issues. He wrote: “The problem with this Cowboy team is that it doesn’t fear losing. No accountability. No urgency. No strong leadership. Weak head coach. Great granddaddy owner. No killer instinct.” Jerry Jones has also been questioned by Cowboys fans on the back of the defeat to the Eagles but it remains to be seen if they will make any changes once 2026/27 is over. They are now 5-7 for the season and there is a real chance they will miss out on the playoffs for a third year in a row – something that has not happened to them since the early 2000s. Coach Brian Schottenheimer oversaw the 2025 campaign as well and another year without a postseason probably won’t help his long-term future. He has since commented on the Cowboys’ collapse, saying: “We’ll go back to the drawing board, go back to the process, and trust the process. This was a short week. Again, there’s things that we’re going to draw from this in a positive way. The five sacks were positive, but we’ve got to get him down more. I thought, offensively, we moved the ball up and down the field in the first half, but not good enough in the second half; but the process doesn’t change.” Dallas will return to action on December 7 against the Seattle Seahawks before taking on the Los Angeles Rams and the Jacksonville Jaguars, all of whom currently have positive records. title: Steelers-Broncos Game Makes NFL History
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Friday at Acrisure Stadium was a Scorigami. It was the […]
content: Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson celebrating with teammates during a game against the Denver Broncos on Nov. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers’ 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Friday at Acrisure Stadium was a Scorigami. It was the first time in NFL history that a game ended with that score. That is the 1102nd unique score in NFL history, and the seventh of the 2026 season. It’s the second time this year that the Steelers have had a Scorigami, the first occurring in the team’s 38-18 loss to the Cincinanti Bengals in Week 10. DEN 5 – PIT 27 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1102nd unique score in NFL history, and the 7th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/HHAt6TjtjB — Scorigami (@ScorigamiGuy) November 27, 2026 Denver mustered only 205 yards of offense. The five points scored by Denver were the fewest since Sean Payton became the team’s head coach in 2023. The Steelers had two defensive touchdowns in the first half. Mason Rudolph completed a 65-yarder to Germie Bernard and a 22-yard touchdown to DK Metcalf. The halftime score of 24-5 was also a first in NFL history. The Steelers are the only team in the NFL with two defensive touchdowns in a game this year. title: Steelers’ David Bakhtiari shares a wild ‘Hail Mary’ take on Aaron Rodgers’ situation
summary: As the NFL world digests the stunning divorce between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers, one of the quarterback’s longtime protectors summed it up with a dramatic football metaphor. Following Pittsburgh’s official decision to release Rodgers, former Green Bay Packers All-Pro left tackle David Bakhtiari took to X to share a succinct reaction […] The post Steelers’ David Bakhtiari shares a wild ‘Hail Mary’ take on Aaron Rodgers’ situation appeared first on ClutchPoints.
content: Mark Hoffman-USA TODAY Sports Steelers’ David Bakhtiari shares a wild ‘Hail Mary’ take on Aaron Rodgers’ situation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the NFL world digests the stunning divorce between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of the quarterback’s longtime protectors summed it up with a dramatic football metaphor. Following Pittsburgh’s official decision to release Rodgers, former Green Bay Packers All-Pro left tackle David Bakhtiari took to X to share a succinct reaction . We just witnessed Aaron Rodgers last Hail Mary. pic.twitter.com/6JnaXWJT5J Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — David Bakhtiari (@DavidBakhtiari) November 25, 2026 “We just witnessed Aaron Rodgers last Hail Mary,” Bakhtiari wrote. Bakhtiari protected Rodgers’ blind side for a decade in Green Bay. He has frequently roasted his former teammate on social media, too. He captured the finality surrounding the 42-year-old’s confirmed farewell campaign. Rodgers’ abrupt exit followed a tumultuous 48-hour spiral. He alleged McCarthy slept through meetings and lost the locker room . That prompted team president Art Rooney II to back his coach and label the quarterback’s ultimatum as insubordination. With Rodgers now a free agent just days before his 43rd birthday, Pittsburgh turns its offense over to Mason Rudolph. That’s ahead of Friday’s Week 12 Black Friday clash against the Denver Broncos. Whether another contender gambles on Rodgers down the stretch remains uncertain. In Bakhtiari’s eyes, though, the legendary passer’s final desperate heave has already hit the turf. Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers on a one-year, $22 million guaranteed contract for what should have been his final NFL campaign. The veteran quarterback authored a turbulent, dramatic chapter that abruptly ended in his release ahead of Week 12. Through 10 starts, the four-time MVP guided Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record. He completed 220 of 361 passes (60.9%) for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions. However, he also operated behind an injury-plagued offensive line. As such, Rodgers took 31 sacks and led the NFL in sack yardage lost. He has posted a career-low 86.6 passer rating alongside a 45.6 QBR. title: ‘He’s a Strange Guy,’ ‘The One Thing You Don’t Do’ — Steelers Legend Terry Bradshaw Doesn’t Mince Words About Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Drama
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw picked a side in the Aaron Rodgers saga, and it was Mike McCarthy’s. Bradshaw minced no words on FOX’s Thanksgiving pregame show on Thursday.
content: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers and Terry Bradshaw Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw picked a side in the Aaron Rodgers saga, and it was Mike McCarthy’s. Bradshaw minced no words on FOX’s Thanksgiving pregame show on Thursday. He stood with McCarthy, the head coach, and the Rooney family a day after the Steelers released Rodgers, who had leveled a string of accusations at McCarthy on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Terry Bradshaw Faults the Way Aaron Rodgers Left Pittsburgh Bradshaw began with the Rooneys and McCarthy, and he was open about his own ties: “Growing up in that family, the Rooney family especially, I would say this: they’re a classy, classy bunch, classy organization. Mike McCarthy and I have been friends for years. Classy man. I don’t know all the details. … I’m sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. … Am I surprised? Absolutely not. To my opinion, he’s a strange guy anyway.” Notably, the heart of his criticism was how Rodgers went about leaving: “And the one thing you don’t do—all of us athletes up here, including you, none of us turn on our teammates. We don’t turn on our coaching staff. We don’t turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out. Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that.” He also turned to something he remembered Rodgers saying about life after Pittsburgh: “And one thing I’m reminded of. He said, when my—when I’m through playing here in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear and you’ll never hear or see from me again. And I hope this is one time he’s telling the truth.” Bradshaw was reacting to a whirlwind few days in Pittsburgh. The Steelers benched Rodgers for Mason Rudolph on Tuesday night, ahead of Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. On Wednesday, Rodgers went on McAfee’s show and accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and skipping others, along with team events. Rodgers was indeed blunt about where he stood on the benching and the play-calling: “If you try and bench me or don’t change the play-calling, then you should just release me, because I feel like, at this point, I’m doing what’s right for the organization.” RUN YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Ultimate GM Simulator McCarthy, who made the call to bench Rodgers, met reporters later Wednesday and kept the details to himself, though he called what Rodgers had made an “ultimatum.” Incidentally, the Steelers cut Rodgers the same day. Meanwhile, team president Art Rooney II made the organization’s position clear on Thursday in an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac: “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney also pointed to the teammates Rodgers left behind: “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload. … He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure.” When asked whether he regretted signing Rodgers, Rooney said: “I’m disappointed the way it came out. … But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” Rodgers and McCarthy go back a long way. They spent 13 years together in Green Bay, including a Super Bowl XLV win over Pittsburgh, and the Steelers turned to McCarthy after 19 seasons under Mike Tomlin. Rodgers returned this past spring for a second season in Pittsburgh on a one-year contract with $22 million guaranteed. The 42-year-old QB cleared waivers Thursday and is now a free agent. He is 29th in PFN’s QB Impact Rankings with a grade of 67.2. Rodgers has said 2026 will be his final NFL season, though he has not said whether he intends to sign with another team for the remainder of it. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Stunner! Eagles rally from 21 down to beat Cowboys 39-38. 4 takeaways
summary: The Eagles rallied from 21 points down late in the third quarter to beat the Dallas Cowboys 39-38
content: ARLINGTON, Texas − It took 10 games, but finally, the Eagles ' offense had by far the output of the season, with quarterback Joe Milton throwing two long touchdown passes to DeVonta Smith, one for 50 yards and the other for 45. The Eagles also blocked a punt and recovered the ball for a touchdown. They needed all of it, including a 60-yard field goal by Jake Elliott with 2 seconds left as they rallied from 21 points down late in the third quarter to stun the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 on Nov. 26. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Eagles had scored their most points in any game this season, by far, as embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and the offense finally showed its potential. And that was with running back Saquon Barkley and tight end Dallas Goedert leaving in the first quarter with injuries. The Eagles fell behind 21-3 midway through the second quarter, and 31-10 with 3:35 left late in the third quarter. That's when the Eagles finally got the offense going, or at least figured out that their best play was simply to throw the ball deep to Smith. The Eagles' star wide receiver finished with a career-high 200 yards receiving on 11 catches, to go along with two touchdowns. Milton, making only his third career start, went 21-for-31 for 331 yards with 3 TDs and an interception. Milton and Smith's first connection came with 4:06 left in the first half with the Eagles at midfield. Milton rolled to his left, motioned to Smith to keep going, and then fired the ball across the field and all the way into the end zone for a 50-yard touchdown. NextGen stats measured Milton's throw at 64.4 air yards. The two hooked up again for a 45-yarder with 15 seconds left in the third quarter. That pulled the Eagles to within 31-17. They were down by just seven points when Ty Robinson blocked Bryan Anger's punt as Kenny Moore scooped it up and ran it back three yards for a touchdown. The Eagles were within a touchdown for the first time since they fell behind 7-0 on the Cowboys' opening drive. But the Cowboys came right back on Prescott's 19-yard run. Milton answered with a 15-yard TD of his own to make it 38-30 with 9:09 left after the Eagles went for the two-point conversion and failed. But the Eagles got a break when Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal with 3:23 left. The Eagles went right to work as Milton hit Makai Lemon from 24 yards out. Again, the two-point conversion failed. But the Eagles had one more chance after they stopped the Cowboys on fourth down on Ty Robinson's sack with 50 seconds left. Then the Eagles barely got close enough for Elliott's 60-yard field goal, the second longest of his career. Here are three more takeaways: Joe Milton has a memorable game It was just Milton's third career start. But the Eagles' quarterback, a member of the Cowboys practice squad before the Eagles signed him on Oct. 16, made things happen with his arm (two long TDs) and his legs (a 15-yard TD run). In all, Milton was 21 of 31 for 331 yards and 3 touchdowns. Was it a fumble that could've turned game around? It appeared that Cowboys running back Javonte Williams fumbled the ball at the goal line late in the first half. On 1st-and-goal from the 1, Williams was stopped by Eagles defensive tackle Ty Robinson and the ball came out. Riq Woolen recovered the ball and was running towards the Cowboys end zone. But the play was blown dead as the officials said Williams' forward progress was stopped. Had it been ruled a fumble, and an Eagles touchdown, the Eagles would have cut the Cowboys' lead to 21-17. Instead, the Cowboys kept possession and scored with 4 seconds left in the half for a 28-10 lead. Rough game for Quinyon Mitchell Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell had his hands full against Cowboys receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. And that was before Cooper DeJean left early in the game with a concussion. Mitchell was called for three defensive penalties in the first half alone − two defensive pass interference calls and an illegal contact call. The second pass interference call was on Prescott's pass to CeeDee Lamb into the end zone, thus giving the Cowboys a first down at the Eagles' 1 yard line with less than a minute left in the first half. The Cowboys scored with 4 seconds left in the first half for a 28-10 lead. It wasn't just Mitchell, who was selected to the Pro Bowl in each of the last two seasons. Riq Woolen also had a tough time covering the Cowboys receivers. Woolen was beaten for a 36-yard completion to Pickens in the first quarter that set up the Cowboys' second touchdown. Prescott went 9-for-14 for 159 yards and 2 touchdowns in the first half. Contact Martin Frank at mfrank@delawareonline.com. Follow on X @Mfranknfl. title: Terry Bradshaw calls Aaron Rodgers 'strange' and hopes he goes away
summary: Terry Bradshaw didn't hold back on Fox, calling Aaron Rodgers a "strange" guy and saying he hopes he keeps his promise to disappear.
content: Terry Bradshaw called the Pittsburgh Steelers a classy organization Thursday evening. The Steelers Hall of Famer had much harsher words for Aaron Rodgers. "Am I surprised? Absolutely not. In my opinion, he's a strange guy anyway," the NFL analyst said during Fox's Thanksgiving pregame show. Bradshaw, who won four Super Bowls as the Steelers' quarterback from 1970 to 1983, also brought up Rodgers' vow to disappear once he is done playing. "And I hope this is one time he is telling the truth," Bradshaw said. Rodgers gave Bradshaw plenty of reason for the spicy comments. A day earlier, after the Steelers benched him for Mason Rudolph, Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show," accused coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through team meetings and said he wasn't coming back. The Steelers waived him that afternoon. Bradshaw said he has been friends with McCarthy for years and didn't know all the details, but he knew enough. "None of us turn on our teammates," Bradshaw said to the panel of former players with whom he co-hosts. "We don't turn on our coaching. We don't turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out. "Aaron Rodgers didn't do that." Bradshaw had never wanted Rodgers in Pittsburgh. In May 2025, while the Steelers were courting Rodgers, Bradshaw told 103.7 The Buzz in Arkansas that the quarterback should stay in California and "chew on bark." Rodgers, 43, laughed it off at the time. Now, the Steelers continue their season with Rudolph at quarterback , starting with the Black Friday game against the Broncos . Rodgers' future is up in the air. He's already said on McAfee's show that he's not going to be calling teams searching for new opportunities. "When this is done, it's Keyser Soze," Rodgers said. "And you won't see me." This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Terry Bradshaw calls Aaron Rodgers 'strange' and hopes he goes away

title: Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 12
summary: Who has the edge when the Tennessee Titans travel to the Jacksonville Jaguars in NFL Week 12? See our scouting report.
content: Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh hopes he hasn’t lost his fastball. But the former San Francisco 49ers and New York Jets defensive coordinator, who has built a respected zone coverage scheme, acknowledged NFL coaches might be familiar with it now. “That's a valid question,” Saleh said the day after the Titans ' 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Nov. 22 . “I think San Francisco is still doing a hell of a job (with the defense). I think Houston in spots is still playing some good football. At the end of the day … When you watch defensively, we (NFL teams) are all kind of running the same stuff. “It's just executing at the level that it needs to be executed to be your best.” More: Mike Vrabel: Amy Adams Strunk drove Titans' decision to trade A.J. Brown More: Titans must do more than just talk about how 'disgusting' the Cowboys loss was | Estes The Titans (1-9) have little time to fix big defensive issues before playing the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) at EverBank Stadium on Nov. 29 (FOX, noon CT) in their second meeting in three weeks. While quarterback Cam Ward and the offense have improved, Tennessee's defense has gone the other way, allowing more than 40 points in three straight games and over 450 yards of offense in four consecutive games. Saleh’s defense dropped to last in yards allowed per game (399.8) and has the league’s second-worst defensive grade overall this season overall, according to Pro Football Focus. Jacksonville struggled in a 23-18 loss to the New York Giants in Week 11. But the Jaguars racked up 459 yards of offense in a 40-23 victory over the Titans in Nashville on Nov. 15. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards passing and three touchdowns. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Jaguars. One Jacksonville Jaguars stat to know: 1 One touchdown for the Jaguars in six trips to the red zone against the Giants. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Jacksonville Jaguars The Titans aren't going to sneak up on a Jacksonville team trailing Buffalo (9-1) by two games for the AFC No. 1 playoff seed. But Ward and Tennessee’s offense might be able to keep up if Saleh can figure out how to expose the Jaguars’ recent protection issues. Jacksonville gave up three sacks against the Giants, which contributed to Lawrence's first game with multiple interceptions (2) since Week 12 of last season. The Titans have struggled pressuring quarterbacks, though. They didn’t turn any of their 13 pressures into sacks against Dallas and posted their third game without a sack this season. Ward's looking more capable getting his team to the 30-point mark each week. He took a small step back against Dallas but still posted a season-high 117.1 quarterback rating and has thrown for 783 yards, six touchdowns and one interceptions over the past three games. Where Jacksonville Jaguars have edge vs. Tennessee Titans Every quarterback in the league wants to face Tennessee’s secondary right now. The Titans are allowing an NFL-worst 272.7 yards passing per game. They’re digging through the depth chart too, with safety Tony Adams (illness) unavailable last week against Dallas and cornerback Cor’Dale Flott (neck) not finishing the game. Cornerback Micah Robinson and safeties Terrell Burgess and Isaiah Oliver will be in another tough spot if the injuries don't clear up. Flott and cornerback Joshua Williams combined to allow 13 catches on 15 targets for a combined 156 yards receiving and a touchdown against the Cowboys. Matchup to watch RB Tony Pollard/Titans offensive line against Jacksonville’s run defense. Pollard has rushed for 100 yards or more in three of the last four games, with Jacksonville being the exception. He ran for just 33 yards on nine carries in the teams’ first meeting. title: ‘Tom Brady Is Disgusted With Aaron Rodgers’ — NFL World Reacts As Legendary QB Makes Feelings Clear on Steelers-Mike McCarthy Controversy
summary: During Thursday’s Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys broadcast on FOX, Tom Brady addressed the messy split between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He kept his tone calm and measured, but his message landed hard with many viewers.
content: ‘Tom Brady Is Disgusted With Aaron Rodgers’ — NFL World Reacts As Legendary QB Makes Feelings Clear on Steelers-Mike McCarthy Controversy During Thursday’s Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys broadcast on FOX, Tom Brady addressed the messy split between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He kept his tone calm and measured, but his message landed hard with many viewers. The NFL legend and FOX analyst built his comments around what he called the sanctity of the locker room, and he said private matters should not be made public. Many fans and analysts heard that as a pointed rebuke of Rodgers. Reactions online came quickly, and several people said Brady had all but called Rodgers a bad teammate. Tom Brady Defends Sacred NFL Locker Room After Steelers Cut Aaron Rodgers The Steelers cut Rodgers, their starting quarterback and a four-time NFL MVP, after he went on Pat McAfee’s show on Wednesday and “basically burned the house down,” as Brady put it, criticizing Mike McCarthy and the whole organization. “It was a weird situation,” Brady said. He noted that the Steelers have a game on Friday and said they all now have to deal with the aftermath. For Brady, that was the core of the problem. The damage, in his view, does not stay with one player. It spills onto everyone else in the room. Brady then made the point he clearly wanted viewers to hear. He said an NFL locker room is “a very sacred place,” adding that “we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players.” “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room, you’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together,” he said, adding that the locker room should not be the place for “private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” BUILD YOUR TEAM’S DRAFT: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Brady did not dismiss what Rodgers has done on the field. He called Rodgers a Hall of Famer and said he is “a tremendous player.” He also said his criticism had “nothing to do with his play style.” Then came one of the more striking lines of the segment. “If that’s the last pass he throws, that’s a really sad way to end,” Brady said. From there, Brady drew on his own career. He said he was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years. “What made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish,” he said. A moment later, he added: “And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you wanna promote.” PICK THE PLAYOFF FIELD: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Brady said again that he was fortunate to be in a great locker room. “I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches,” he said. He then closed with a line that summed up his view of the whole situation: “nobody wins when the family feuds.” Fans and Analysts React to Brady Burying Rodgers With Polite Criticism Brady never directly called Rodgers selfish or a bad teammate. Still, people read between the lines. Robin Lundberg, a WNBA analyst, put it bluntly in a post on X: “Tom Brady is disgusted with Aaron Rodgers.” Many fans read the comments the same way. They saw Brady choosing his words carefully while still making his feelings plain. One fan wrote that Brady “is doing everything he can right now to not call Rodgers a selfish loser. Basically said it as politely as possible.” Sports announcer Chase Snyder made a similar point about how far Brady went without saying the words outright, noting that “Tom Brady just said Aaron Rodgers is a bad teammate in every way he possibly could without directly saying he’s a bad teammate.” Jarrett Bailey, an NFL analyst, focused on the contrast between Brady’s tone and the weight of what he said. “Tom Brady just very politely and professionally buried Aaron Rodgers,” Bailey wrote. Not everyone thought Brady went quite that far. One fan called it “a light scolding for Aaron Rodgers from Tom Brady there.” Some fans also praised the way Brady handled such a touchy subject on live TV. “Brady, in a very professional way took care of the Rodgers situation. Well done,” one fan wrote. Taken together, the reaction showed how sharply Brady’s words cut, even in a mild tone. He praised Rodgers as a player and called a possible end to his career sad. But he also made clear that, in his view, airing a team’s private business in public crosses a line. As Brady pointed out, the Steelers now have to play on Friday while dealing with the fallout, and for many viewers his core message was easy to hear. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Why even Trent Williams envies the high point of new 49ers starter Vederian Lowe's career
summary: Vederian Lowe has big shoes to fill with Colton McKivitz out. But the San Francisco 49ers' newest starter has one feat to his credit that even future Hall of Famer Trent Williams wishes he'd done.
content: San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle Vederian Lowe (76) blocks during an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Scot Tucker) (Scot Tucker/AP) Vederian Lowe has picked Trent Williams ' brain and studied the generational left tackle's film since signing with the San Francisco 49ers in March, but the onetime sixth-round pick and part-time NFL starter understands there are limits to what he can replicate. "A lot of the things that he does, I can't do," Lowe said. "Because Trent is one of one." However, there is something Lowe has done that Williams has spent his illustrious 16-season career wishing he could do. On Nov. 17, 2024, Lowe, then with the Patriots, realized every 300-pound man's dream when he caught a 4-yard touchdown from quarterback Drake Maye in a loss to the Chargers. Asked where his lone catch ranks among his career highlights, Lowe smiled and invoked Williams, who is catch-less and has long lobbied head coach Kyle Shanahan for a goal-line pass. "That (catch) might be number one because they don't come by - I was talking to Trent and even Trent doesn't have one," Lowe said. "So I'm like, ‘OK.' That's up there for sure." The lofty ranking Lowe has assigned his reception speaks to the rarity of such a snag. But it also speaks to the modest number of highlights he's collected in a five-season career that has included 25 starts, just four since Jan. 5, 2025. But that could be changing. Last Sunday, in a 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City, Lowe was unexpectedly thrust into the role of a key starter on a Super Bowl contender when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a broken and dislocated ankle in the second quarter . McKivitz's season is over. Lowe's chance to show why the 49ers signed him to a two-year contract with a maximum value of $12 million to serve as their swing tackle is just beginning. "That's why we brought him here," Shanahan said. "Anytime you have a swing tackle - that means you better be capable of starting. He's started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter. And that's why we targeted him." Lowe is assuming some sizable cleats. McKivitz, 30, was earning every bit of the three-year, $45 million extension he signed last year by not allowing a sack in 327 pass-blocking snaps this season before his injury. The very early returns, however, are promising. On Lowe's first snap after replacing McKivitz, he pancaked defensive tackle Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins on a 10-yard run by Christian McCaffrey . It was the start of a 38-snap performance in which Lowe committed a false start, but he didn't allow a QB pressure on 19 pass-blocking snaps against Minnesota's chaotic, blitz-heavy defense, a unit which leads the NFL in sacks. Lowe did so despite logging most of his snaps at left tackle throughout his career. His only four starts at right tackle were in 2023 with the Patriots and he'd spent most of his practice time on the left side since joining the 49ers. "Swinging from both sides," Lowe said, "it's not an easy task at all." Center Jake Brendel wasn't surprised Lowe managed to make it look seamless. Brendel, 34, was struck by the questions Lowe was asking about the 49ers' intricate blocking schemes not long after his arrival. Lowe peppered Brendel with queries about "chokes," "blunts" and "seals," all backside blocks from tight ends or other players lined up outside the 49ers' offensive tackles. "He asked me questions that guys don't ask me until year three or four in the system," Brendel said. "So the guy knows football … A lot of backup tackles kind of just float around and then they go in and they're like, ‘All right, I'll get it done physically, but I'm not expecting to be at the level of a starter.' This guy's definitely starting (material)." The Patriots weren't convinced about Lowe's first-string ability. After Lowe made a season-high 13 starts in 2024, New England drafted left tackle Will Campbell with the No. 4 pick to replace him last year. Lowe made four starts as a fill-in in 2025 after making 21 starts the previous two seasons. After his step down in status, he joined the 49ers knowing he'd have no shot to unseat Williams or McKivitz. Now, however, he's a starter on a 9-1 team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. Lowe has a chance to help his new team earn a ring while showing he's more than a well-compensated backup. If last Sunday's performance was any indication, it's an opportunity he's ready to seize, much like that pass he caught in 2024, a moment even Williams can only hope to replicate. "The opportunity doesn't come by too often," Lowe said, "and I was not dropping that." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: Wu-Tang Clan takes over Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving halftime show
summary: The legendary rap collective tore through decades of classics during the Lions-Bears game, with Eminem curating the performance and Chad
content: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: The Wu-Tang Clan performs the halftime show during the game between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Photo by: Gregory Shamus / Getty Images The legendary rap collective tore through decades of classics during the Lions-Bears game, with Eminem curating the performance and Chad Smith joining on drums. Thanksgiving came with a side of Shaolin at Ford Field. Wu-Tang Clan took over the Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving Day halftime show on Thursday, delivering a rapid-fire run through the songs that helped establish the Staten Island collective as one of hip-hop’s most influential groups. The group hit the field during the Lions’ matchup against the Chicago Bears dressed in Detroit blue and backed by Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith. The group opened with “Triumph” before moving through a medley that reportedly included “Da Mystery of Chessboxin’,” “Protect Ya Neck,” “Method Man,” “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” “Ice Cream,” “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” Young Dirty Bastard stepped in to represent his late father, founding Wu-Tang member Ol’ Dirty Bastard, during “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” Before the show, he shared a backstage photo with Eminem, who helped bring the performance together. Eminem did not join Wu-Tang onstage, but his fingerprints were all over the production. According to Complex , the Detroit rapper and his longtime manager, Paul Rosenberg, served as executive producers and selected the group to headline the show. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Detroit Lions (@detroitlionsnfl) The performance marked the second year of their multiyear partnership with the Lions. In 2025, Eminem made a surprise appearance alongside Jack White during the team’s Thanksgiving game, performing “‘Till I Collapse” before the Detroit rock star closed the set with “Seven Nation Army.” When Wu-Tang’s appearance was announced earlier this month, Lions President and CEO Rich Haddad described the holiday game as one of sports’ greatest traditions and the group as one of music’s greatest acts. “We are thrilled to have Wu-Tang headlining our Thanksgiving halftime show and grateful to Marshall and Paul for their partnership,” Haddad said in the NFL’s announcement . The booking arrived during an already celebratory period for the group. Less than two weeks before the Thanksgiving performance, Wu-Tang Clan received the Early Influence Award at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony. Chris Rock inducted the group, praising its members for building a global hip-hop force without relying on the traditional industry machine. Wu-Tang then performed another crowd-pleasing medley featuring “C.R.E.A.M.,” “Method Man” and “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” The latest honor follows the group’s “Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber” tour, which was announced as its final North American run. RZA previously described the tour as a chance for the members to come together once more and spread Wu-Tang’s music and culture around the world. Thursday’s halftime show proved that whether the stage is an arena, an awards ceremony or the middle of a football field, the Clan still knows how to command a crowd. title: ‘Zero Sense Outside Chicago Connection,’ ‘Dumbest Take’ — Fans Torch Colin Cowherd Over ‘Insane’ Caleb Williams-Michael Jordan Comparison
summary: Colin Cowherd posted about Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams on Thanksgiving, and fans quickly pushed back on his assessment of the young quarterback. The 39-35 victory over the Detroit Lions snapped Detroit’s six-game winning streak, gave Chicago its first NFC North win of the season, and left the Bears alone atop the division.
content: Fans question Colin Cowherd's Caleb Williams-Michael Jordan comparison after the Bears quarterback rallies Chicago past the Detroit Lions. Colin Cowherd posted about Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams on Thanksgiving, and fans quickly pushed back on his assessment of the young quarterback. The 39-35 victory over the Detroit Lions snapped Detroit’s six-game winning streak, gave Chicago its first NFC North win of the season, and left the Bears alone atop the division. Williams, the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, led the comeback with a touchdown in the final seconds. Fans Dismiss Colin Cowherd’s Michael Jordan Comparison for Caleb Williams Cowherd, host of “The Herd” on FS1, offered little explanation when he posted Thursday : “Caleb is a young MJ.” One fan responded , “This is an insane tweet (expletive).” Another wrote , “Please stop this.” Chicago trailed by 11 midway through the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs broke free for a 70-yard touchdown, his third score of the game. Williams answered with a 41-yard touchdown pass to Rome Odunze and ran in the two-point conversion to cut Detroit’s lead to 35-32. With three seconds left, he found Odunze again, this time for a 6-yard touchdown that put the Bears ahead for good. Cowherd had praised Williams before Thursday, including after the quarterback suffered a right hamstring injury in Week 2. On September 21, while his availability remained uncertain, Cowherd said : “When you’re as generationally gifted as Caleb, or LeBron, or Wemby, or Mahomes and Josh Allen, you’re not carrying a team, you’re carrying a league.” Not everyone agreed with his latest assessment. One fan remarked : “This makes zero sense outside of the Chicago connection.” Another added , “This is the dumbest take I’ve ever seen in my life. Just because they’re both in Chicago? Incredibly lazy comparison.” Williams completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and 2 touchdowns against Detroit. Through Thanksgiving, he had 12 passing touchdowns and 6 interceptions in 8 appearances. A reply to Cowherd read: “10 TDs 7 INTs on the season. Basically a league average QB with high upside.” Another fan commented : “Michael Jordan was averaging 37.1 points a game in his 3rd year. Caleb Williams has 12 passing touchdowns in 11 games.” The Chicago Bulls legend’s 37.1-point average came during his third NBA season. Williams, meanwhile, had appeared in only 8 of Chicago’s 11 games at the time of the comparison. SEE ALSO: ‘Here We Go Again,’ ‘The Suffering Never Ends’ – Timberwolves Fans Brace for Worst After LaMelo Ball Goes Down With Ankle Injury vs. Thunder Williams’ development has given Chicago plenty to build on since his rookie season, when the Bears went 5-12. In 2025, he led the team to an 11-6 record, the NFC North title and its first playoff victory since 2010. He also set a Bears single-season passing record with 3,942 yards and earned the team’s 2025 Offensive Player of the Year honor. The quarterback helped produce seven wins in games Chicago trailed in the final two minutes that season, including six in the regular season and one in the playoffs. Thursday’s comeback added another late victory to his résumé, as the Bears improved to 9-2 and extended their winning streak to six games. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Andy Reid disagrees with overturned Rashee Rice catch after Chiefs' loss to Bills: 'That was not clear and obvious'
summary: We may never know what a catch is in the NFL.
content: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice appeared to have a much-needed first down against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. The NFL's replay center disagreed. With the game tied 10-10 and two minutes left in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs got the ball deep in their own territory. A pair of incompletions left them facing third-and-10, at which point Patrick Mahomes appeared to connect with wide receiver Rashee Rice for 11 yards and the first down. However, the play was surprisingly overturned on replay, with the official only saying, "After review, the ball hit the ground, it's an incomplete pass." This was ruled a catch for Rashee Rice on the field and was overturned to incomplete after review: pic.twitter.com/mh6QNXsnPJ — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 The call was popular at Buffalo's Highmark Stadium, but not so much on social media. The video replay indeed showed the ball hit the ground while pinned between Rice's right hand and shoulder, but that alone doesn't make the play an incomplete pass. The ball must also come loose while hitting the ground before Rice establishes possession, and that was very much up for debate. Additionally, the NFL maintains a "clear and obvious" standard for overturning plays. So the replay officials in New York City not only believed Rice hadn't completed the catch, they also decided it was clear to anyone watching. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid very much didn't seem to think that was the case after his team’s 13-10 defeat , via Kansas City's KSHB 41 : "Not [a call] that I agreed with, but yeah. This came from New York, so it's not from these guys. Our guys called it a completion, the guys who were working the game. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball and his elbow hit and then the ball hit, but he had control. "Normally, in those kind of situations, it's gotta be clear and obvious. To me, that was not clear and obvious." Rashee Rice appeared to have a first down for the Chiefs. The NFL's replay center disagreed. AP Photo/Matt Rourke Mahomes' wife Brittany, meanwhile, used the occasion to dispute the idea the Chiefs have benefited from calls during their recent run, writing the following on her Instagram story : "HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE "Guess we can't even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s*** anymore from anyone" She also posted a collection of social media posts criticizing the call to her story. NFL vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth spoke to a pool reporter, pointing to Rice's hand moving up the ball as evidence that he lost control. The pool report with NFL VP of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth on the overturned ruling of a catch by Rashee Rice. “As the receiver is going to the ground, he had the ball in his right hand and when he contacted the ground, his hand slid up the ball and we deemed that a loss of… pic.twitter.com/Cl094uWVk0 — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) November 27, 2026 To be clear, this play did not singlehandedly cost the Chiefs the game, though it's undeniably frustrating. Had the Rice catch stood, they still would have needed to travel half the field to reach field-goal range, on a day in which struggling kicker Harrison Butker made one field goal from 26 yards and missed another from 46. Facing fourth-and-10, Kansas City was instead forced to punt out of its own end zone. The teams immediately exchanged three-and-outs and appeared headed to overtime, only for field position to bite the Chiefs again when a disastrous punt sequence put the Bills in field-goal position for the final play.

title: The Anaheim Ducks Are Getting One Of The NHL’s Most Exciting Young Forwards Back
summary: Cutter Gauthier’s historic November has received plenty of attention, but the Anaheim Ducks have another 22-year-old or younger forward producing […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cutter Gauthier’s historic November has received plenty of attention, but the Anaheim Ducks have another 22-year-old or younger forward producing at better than a point-per-game pace this season. Beckett Sennecke is expected to return to the Ducks’ lineup Friday against the Los Angeles Kings after missing three games with an upper-body injury. Head coach Joel Quenneville confirmed Thursday that Sennecke is ready to return, according to Zach Cavanagh of The Sporting Tribune. The 20-year-old has scored 12 goals and registered 14 assists through 22 games this season after finishing third in Calder Trophy voting with 23 goals and 60 points in 82 games last season. He’s nearly doubled his goal-scoring rate and is on pace for 99 points over a full 84-game schedule. Less than three years ago, Sennecke was playing junior hockey with the Oshawa Generals. He’s now producing at a rate that would’ve put him among the NHL’s leading scorers in most seasons. Sennecke has some ridiculous puck skills, and 10 of his 12 goals this season have come from high-danger areas. According to NHL EDGE, that ties him with Auston Matthews for second in the league, just one behind Artturi Lehkonen. He’s also been on the ice for 22 power-play goals, one fewer than Gauthier. The Ducks lead the NHL with a 33.7% power play, and Sennecke was back practicing with the first unit Thursday. With Leo Carlsson sidelined by an upper-body injury, NHL.com has Sennecke projected to play alongside Gauthier and Roger McQueen on Friday. That’s three forwards selected inside the top 10 of their respective drafts, none of whom are older than 22. McQueen, the 10th overall pick in 2025, scored against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday and could benefit from playing between two of the league’s most productive young wingers. There aren’t many better linemates for a young center trying to establish himself offensively in the NHL right now. The Ducks lost consecutive 3-2 games against the Utah Mammoth and Seattle Kraken in Sennecke’s absence before beating San Jose 7-0 on Wednesday. They enter Friday’s game with a 12-13-1 record despite the offensive production they’ve been getting from their young forwards. Anaheim has two games against Los Angeles this weekend, and with Carlsson still out, Quenneville could give us our first extended look at what Gauthier, McQueen and Sennecke can do together. title: Calgary Flames Have a $52.5 Million Goaltender, but Their Backup Is Making Things Interesting
summary: When the Calgary Flames signed Dustin Wolf to a seven-year, $52.5 million contract extension in September 2025, there wasn’t much […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the Calgary Flames signed Dustin Wolf to a seven-year, $52.5 million contract extension in September 2025, there wasn’t much reason to question who would be starting the majority of their games for the foreseeable future. Wolf had just posted a .910 save percentage through 53 games as a rookie and finished second in Calder Trophy voting. Less than two months into the first season of that contract, the Flames are getting considerably better goaltending from Devin Cooley, who’s carrying a cap hit of just $1.35 million. Cooley has a .909 save percentage and a 2.81 goals-against average through 11 appearances this season, compared to Wolf’s .878 save percentage and 3.42 goals-against average through 15 appearances. According to MoneyPuck data via Puckpedia, Cooley has saved 3.45 goals above expected this season, while Wolf has allowed 6.58 more goals than expected. Cooley has also been considerably better relative to the quality of shots he’s faced. Cooley Has Been Overlooked Since Last Season Cooley went undrafted and didn’t make his NHL debut until he was 26 with the San Jose Sharks. He signed with the Flames in July 2024, led the Calgary Wranglers with 21 wins and earned an American Hockey League (AHL) All-Star selection the following season before establishing himself as an NHL backup in 2025-26. He posted a .909 save percentage through 31 appearances last season, saving 17.26 goals above expected. According to NHL EDGE , his .850 high-danger save percentage was tied for second in the league behind only Ilya Sorokin. The Flames signed Cooley to a two-year, $2.7 million contract extension last December. Huska had already started leaning on Cooley more heavily before he suffered a lower-body injury against the Edmonton Oilers on Oct. 28. Cooley had won four consecutive starts against the Carolina Hurricanes, Minnesota Wild, Detroit Red Wings and Toronto Maple Leafs, stopping 127 of 133 shots for a .955 save percentage. He was also named the NHL’s Second Star of the Week on Oct. 26. He’s posted a .902 save percentage through four starts since returning from injury, including an impressive 29-save performance in Monday’s 2-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators . Wolf has also improved recently, going 3-1-1 with an .896 save percentage over his past five starts. Flames Don’t Need Wolf To Play 60 Games There’s a reason the Flames committed so much money to Wolf. Before his outstanding NHL rookie season, he was twice named the AHL’s Goaltender of the Year and won the league’s most valuable player award in 2022-23. He’s still only 25, and the Flames are assembling the defensive core that could be playing in front of him for much of his contract. Between Simon Nemec, Zayne Parekh and Carson Carels , the organization has invested heavily in its future on the blue line. However, Cooley has saved 20.71 goals above expected since the beginning of last season, compared to Wolf’s minus-7.93, per Moneypuck, despite making 30 fewer appearances. Both goaltenders are under contract through at least 2027-28, and there’s enough evidence to justify splitting the starts more evenly. Wolf doesn’t need to lose his job as Calgary’s franchise goaltender for Cooley to be rewarded for how well he’s played. content: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 12: Kaiden Guhle #21 of the Montréal Canadiens looks on during the third period against the Boston Bruins at TD Garden on November 12, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. The Canadiens defeat the Bruins 5-2. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty MONTREAL, CANADA - NOVEMBER 14: Artturi Lehkonen #62 of the Colorado Avalanche and Kaiden Guhle #21 of the Montréal Canadiens battle for the puck along the boards during the first period at the Bell Centre on November 14, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images) Getty ELMONT, NEW YORK - APRIL 12: David Reinbacher #64 of the Montréal Canadiens skates in his first NHL game against the New York Islanders at UBS Arena on April 12, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Getty The Montreal Canadiens have provided a clearer understanding of Kaiden Guhle’s injury after the defenseman’s early exit in Colorado. Guhle is day-to-day with an upper-body injury, TSN’s Kenzie Lalonde reported Friday, relaying the team’s announcement. “Canadiens announce that Kaiden Guhle is day-to-day (upper body),” Lalonde wrote. Canadiens announce that Kaiden Guhle is day-to-day (upper body) . #Habs — Kenzie Lalonde (@KenzieTSN) November 27, 2026 The designation leaves his availability unresolved ahead of Saturday’s game against the Vegas Golden Knights. It also gives Montreal its first reported clarification of the injury since Guhle left Wednesday’s contest. Canadiens Clarify Kaiden Guhle’s Injury After Colorado Exit Getty MONTREAL, CANADA – NOVEMBER 14: Artturi Lehkonen #62 of the Colorado Avalanche and Kaiden Guhle #21 of the Montréal Canadiens battle for the puck along the boards during the first period at the Bell Centre on November 14, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images) Guhle, a defenseman averaging more than 22 minutes per game, had his night end during the second period against the Colorado Avalanche. Sportsnet reported that Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog hit Guhle from behind near the boards. The two later became tangled in front of the net on the same shift and fell to the ice. Guhle didn’t return after that sequence. Montreal subsequently announced that he would miss the remainder of the game. He finished with 10:53 of ice time, two shots on goal and a minus-1 rating. Coach Martin St. Louis had no update after the game, according to Sportsnet. Friday’s announcement supplies an injury category and a day-to-day designation. Lalonde’s report didn’t include a firm return date or confirm whether Guhle would face Vegas. However, a return Saturday would allow the Canadiens to avoid an absence going beyond the Colorado game. If Guhle can’t play, St. Louis will have to redistribute his workload. The 24-year-old had two goals and four assists, Sportsnet noted. Guhle’s Status Could Create Opportunity for David Reinbacher Getty ELMONT, NEW YORK – APRIL 12: David Reinbacher #64 of the Montréal Canadiens skates in his first NHL game against the New York Islanders at UBS Arena on April 12, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) David Reinbacher is one potential option if Guhle needs more time. RotoWire identified Reinbacher as a likely replacement for Saturday if Guhle cannot dress. NHL.com projected Guhle alongside Noah Dobson before Wednesday’s game, with Reinbacher listed as a scratch. Inserting another defenseman would address the open roster spot. Montreal would still need to define its pairings and decide how to divide Guhle’s usual minutes. The Canadiens made a commitment to Guhle when they signed him to a six-year, $33.3 million extension in July 2024. PuckPedia lists his annual cap hit at $5.55 million, with the contract running through 2030-31. Montreal selected Guhle 16th overall in the 2020 draft, via its contract announcement . His current deal reflects the club’s long-term investment in a player who has taken on a heavy nightly assignment. He also underwent minor adductor surgery last summer, the Canadiens announced in September . As of the current timeframe, Montreal’s next decision will be about his availability against Vegas and the defensive alterations required if he sits. title: Flyers beat Canucks 5-2 after leading scorer Matvei Michkov is benched for 'internal team matter'
summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Travis Konecny, Porter Martone and Tyson Foerster scored on the power play and the Flyers beat the Vancouver Canucks 5-2 Friday with Philadelphia leading scorer Matvei Michkov benched.Michkov was scratched for an “internal team matter,” according to a statement by Dan Hilferty, the Flyers' team governor, about two hours before gametime.
content: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Travis Konecny, Porter Martone and Tyson Foerster scored on the power play and the Flyers beat the Vancouver Canucks 5-2 Friday with Philadelphia leading scorer Matvei Michkov benched. Michkov was scratched for an “internal team matter,” according to a statement by Dan Hilferty, the Flyers' team governor, about two hours before gametime. The 21-year-old Russian leads Philadelphia with a team-best 11 goals and 20 points. Flyers coach Rick Tocchet said before the game that that he wanted to get through the contest and would address the Michkov issue later. Noah Cates also scored and Sean Couturier added an empty-net goal for Philadelphia, which has won four of its last five game. Dan Vladar made 18 saves. Jake DeBrusk and Filip Hronek scored for Vancouver, which has lost four of its last five games and has a league-worst record of 6-21-1. Leevi Merilainen made 24 saves. The Flyers power play, which has been among the worst in the NHL in recent years, converted three of five chances against the Canucks. Foerster opened the scoring in the first period, scoring with a wrist just under five minutes in. Early in the second, Cates grabbed a loose puck and slid it through Merilainen’s pads. Martone added his fourth of the season at 10:37. Vancouver rallied by scoring the next two goals. Hronek scored at 12:05 of the second and DeBrusk’s shot at the 2:22 mark of the third that made it a 3-2 game. But, 3 1/2 minutes later Konecny picked up a loose puck to the side of Merilainen and punched home his fifth of the season to restore a two-goal edge. Up next Canucks: At Boston on Sunday. Flyers: Host the New York Islanders on Saturday. ___ See AP’s full NHL coverage here

title: Gabe Perreault Expected To Be Out For 4-6 Weeks Due To Lower-Body Injury
summary: Gabe Perreault will miss four to six weeks due to a lower-body injury that has landed him on injured reserve.
content: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Gabe Perreault will miss four to six weeks due to a lower-body injury that has landed him on injured reserve. Perreault played during the New York Rangers’ Wednesday night game against the Buffalo Sabres, and it’s unclear when or how he sustained this apparent lower-body injury. The Rangers recalled Juuso Pärssinen from the Hartford Wolf Pack of the American Hockey League upon placing Perreault on injured reserve. Along with Perreault, Oliver Bjorkstrand and Alberts Šmits are also on injured reserve, while Igor Shesterkin and Joe Veleno have been placed on long-term injured reserve. According to Mollie Walker of The New York Post , Mike Sullivan said he's never experienced an injury list to this extent before in his entire coaching career. “We talk a lot about complementary skill sets,” Sullivan said. “What line needs what in order to try to help it and make it work. I think the guys have done a great job, just as far as the next-man-up mindset, and it’s going to provide opportunities for others. I know it’s a cliche, but it’s the truth. The expectations don’t change. Pavel Dorofeyev, who has missed the past three games due to a lower-body injury, shed his non-contact jersey during Thursday’s practice, as Sullivan “wouldn’t rule him out” for Friday night's game against the Chicago Blackhawks.

title: This Mammoth rookie just made history in Nashville
summary: The Utah Mammoth pulled off an all-important shootout victory against the Nashville Predators Friday afternoon.
content: Utah Mammoth forward Lawson Crouse (67) celebrates his goal with teammates during the third period of an NHL hockey game against the Nashville Predators, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (AP Photo/Camden Hall) | Camden Hall For the first time ever, the Utah Mammoth have won a game in a shootout under that moniker. The franchise’s last shootout win came when it was known as the Utah Hockey Club on Feb. 9, 2025, against the Washington Capitals. On Friday afternoon, the Mammoth got it done in Nashville with a final score of 6-5 over the Predators. It’s an all-important win for the Mammoth, who came into the game trailing the Predators by two points in the standings. They allowed their opponents a point in this one, but trimming that gap is a positive result for Utah regardless — and not letting it get even wider was perhaps even more important. “I thought it was a gritty win by the boys,” said Anders Lee, who busted a 14-game goal drought by scoring twice on Friday. “Sometimes, that’s how you’ve got to win a game, and we found a way tonight.” The Mammoth now move on to Dallas, where they’ll take on another close divisional opponent in the Stars. The Stars lost to the St. Louis Blues Friday afternoon, putting them on a two-game losing skid. Utah has won four of its last five games — a good bounce back from the franchise-high six-game losing streak that preceded it. For head coach André Tourigny, though, that shouldn’t be seen as an impressive feat. “We don’t want that to be an achievement,” he said of winning four of five games. “We want that to be a blueprint.” Leezy back for seconds! Tied up, 5-5. pic.twitter.com/zomNgO4t4X — Utah Mammoth (@utahmammoth) November 27, 2026 Mammoth rookie makes history For the first time ever, a Utah-drafted player has suited up for the Mammoth in a regular-season NHL game. It’s not Tij Iginla, the first player the team ever selected in the draft. It’s not Cole Beaudoin, Caleb Desnoyers or Ethan Belchetz, the Mammoth’s other first-round picks. It’s Gregor Biber. Biber is a 6-foot-3 defenseman from Austria, whom the team drafted in the fourth round of its inaugural draft in 2024. He was the first player selected in that round of the draft, and fittingly, he’s the first one to play in an NHL game. A debut to remember! pic.twitter.com/5luYjgbe6o — Utah Mammoth (@utahmammoth) November 27, 2026 Whether it’s his first game or his 1,000th, a lot is expected of an NHL defenseman. Not only is he tasked with keeping the puck out of his net against some of the best hockey players in the world, but he’s also responsible for making plays to transition the puck into the offensive zone. Biber did that and more in his debut. He only played 9:33 on Friday, but he defended well in that span. In fact, he was the only defenseman on either team who wasn’t on the ice for a goal against. On the contrary, he was on the ice for teammate Lawson Crouse’s goal, giving him a +1 rating. He also managed two shots on net, and both were really good looks. “I think he was pretty good, actually,” Tourigny said of the 20-year-old after the game. “He moved the puck well, he closed quickly. For a guy who was in his first game and not a lot of practice because of the schedule lately, I think he did pretty good.” That shouldn’t necessarily come as a surprise, as he has been more than solid with the AHL’s Tucson Roadrunners in 14 games to open this season. In a recent interview with the Deseret News, Roadrunners head coach Steve Potvin mentioned a number of things that have impressed him about his young defensemen, including Biber. “They play such a responsible game in how they manage the ice. It’s pretty impressive,” he said. “(Biber) and (Tomas) Lavoie and (Artem) Duda, like, they really cover a lot of ice, and how they route and push the play to the perimeter all the time and make it hard on the opponent, it doesn’t feel like you’re coaching rookies.” Another achievement Biber could potentially capture is to become the first Utah-drafted player to score a point in the NHL — for any team. Beaudoin, who was traded to the New York Rangers in the deal that brought Vincent Trocheck to the Mammoth, has played four games with the Blueshirts but has yet to record a point. Whether Biber plays again on Saturday remains to be revealed. In the past, Utah’s coaching staff has sometimes managed back-to-back games by using every available roster player in one game or the other. Nick DeSimone sat out in Nashville, but he could potentially play in Dallas. An advantageous exploitation MacKenzie Weegar tallied three assists in Nashville on Friday, matching his career high and becoming the third Mammoth defenseman to accomplish that feat this season. It was also his first multi-point game of the year. That didn’t happen by chance. Weegar played three seasons under current Predators head coach Andrew Brunette when they were both with the Florida Panthers. Brunette was primarily responsible for the team’s offense, so Weegar spent plenty of time defending against Brunette’s system in practice. With all that repetition comes an understanding of the loopholes. “I kind of knew their systems and I knew they pressure hard,” Weegar said. “The puck moves faster than the players on the other side. I tried to get it up to the forwards as fast as I could and get pucks to the net, find ways to create in the offensive zone. “It’s good to know the coach on the other side sometimes.” In the 11 games he’s played against the Predators since Brunette took over as the team’s bench boss, this was by far Weegar’s best offensive performance. He now has five points in those games. Nashville Predators center Shane Wright (15) handles the puck against the Utah Mammoth during the second period of an NHL hockey game Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (AP Photo/Camden Hall) | Camden Hall

title: MN Wild Have Aggressive Plans at NHL Trade Deadline
summary: What do the Minnesota Wild have planned at the trade deadline, after losing out on Dylan Larkin? More Aggressiveness.
content: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Thanksgiving came and went with the Minnesota Wild sitting first in both the Central Division and the Western Conference. At 18-4-5 with 41 points, they’re nine points ahead of Dallas, even after Wednesday’s 4-3 loss to the Utah Mammoth snapped their franchise-record 15-game point streak. Most of that run came while Minnesota was still chasing a center. The Wild were one of the three teams on the list of preferred destinations Dylan Larkin gave Detroit in June. For the next 5.5 months, they were the team chasing Larkin the hardest and the team he reportedly wanted to play most for. Unfortunately, all that effort was for not. Earlier this week, their chase for Larkin officially ended when the Red Wings traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens for Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, the rights to Michael Hage and four draft picks , including first-rounders in 2027 and 2029. Minnesota Wild tabbed as aggressive deadline buyers So, what are the Wild going to do now? Well, if you thought president of hockey operations, Bill Guerin, was going to spend the next couple months before the March 1 NHL trade deadline depressed over what could have been with Larkin on roster, you don’t know Billy G. Instead, according to Michael Russo (The Athletic) Minnesota will be an “aggressive buyer” leading up to the deadline. He expects the Wild to continue shopping for a top-six forward, either at center or on the wing. The goal: Add talent to the lines behind the Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy, Joel Eriksson Ek line, which has been producing most of this team’s points through 27 games. The Wild went hard after Dylan Larkin, and there’s no doubt that they will continue to pursue a top center, a top-six winger or both. Thank goodness for the prolific top line, because right now, they’re basically deploying two third lines after it. The issue will be cap space. Minnesota is projected to have $4.4 million available at the deadline, per PuckPedia. Michael Russo – The Athletic Related: Minnesota Wild Already a Playoff Lock? The above excerpt is from a piece posted at The Athletic Friday morning, which ranked every NHL team by playoff confidence tiers, with a trade deadline aggressiveness label attached. Along with their “Aggressive buyer” label, the Wild got a 5 out of 5 on playoff confidence (“It’s a lock”). How dominant has Minnesota’s first line been? After today’s matinee against the Colorado Avalanche. the Wild will have played 1/3 of their regular season schedule. How good is the MN Wild’s top line? To this point, Kaprizov has 49 points (19 goals, 30 assists), which is on pace for over 150 points on the season. Boldy, meanwhile, has 32 points and Eriksson Ek has 26. Combined, those three have 43 goals and 107 points. That’s nearly half of the Wild’s 98 total goals this season. At 5-on-5, MoneyPuck has that line on the ice for 26 goals for and three against in 296.1 minutes together. Russo had it at 26-2, best in the NHL, before Utah scored a 5-on-5 goal against it in the second period on Wednesday. Wild NHL rankings Points (1) Wins (T-1) RW (T-1) GF/game (5) GA/game (1) PP (6) SV% (1, by 11 percentage points) Blocked shots (1) Takeaways (T-3) Scoring first (1, 15 straight games) Leading games (1) Top line 5v5 GF-GA 26-2 (best in NHL) — Michael Russo (@RussoHockey) November 24, 2026 Yakov Trenin, Danila Yurov and Maxim Shabanov, the line with the next-most 5-on-5 time, are 5-3 in 157.7 minutes together. Blake Coleman, Michael McCarron and Bobby Brink are 6-3 in 132.9 minutes. That’s 11 goals for in 290.6 minutes between those two lines, compared with 26 for the top line in about the same ice time. McCarron, who centers Coleman and Brink, has four goals and 10 points in 26 games. Trenin has five assists, no goals and a 37.0% faceoff rate in 26 games. The Wild’s cap math after missing on Dylan Larkin The $4.4 million Russo cited comes from PuckPedia ‘s projection of Minnesota’s cap space at the trade deadline , 2 p.m. CT on Monday, March 1, 2027. Minnesota’s current cap space is $1.3 million, against a $104 million cap. Larkin’s cap hit is $8.7 million on an eight-year, $69.6 million contract that runs through 2030-31. Quinn Hughes ($7.85 million) and Olli Maatta ($3.5 million) are both on injured reserve , not long-term injured reserve, and PuckPedia shows the Wild’s LTIR pool at $0. The Wild are also still carrying about $1.67 million in buyout charges for Zach Parise and Ryan Suter this season. In a Nov. 24 mailbag , Russo and Joe Smith went through the Wild’s Plan B options, with Pavel Zacha and Ryan O’Reilly among the more realistic names and Auston Matthews, Evgeni Malkin and Sidney Crosby discussed as longer shots. Smith wrote that the Wild “aren’t paying a Larkin price” and “only have so many trade chips left.” PuckPedia shows Minnesota with its 2027 first-round pick, but without its 2027 second- or third-round pick. Related: Confirmed: Red Wings Conspiring Against Larkin, Not Negotiating in Good Faith with Wild On Nov. 24, Russo said on X that PuckPedia projected about $7.7 million in deadline space if the Wild were without Calvin Pickard and Viking Gustafsson Nyberg was sent down, adding, “Obviously will change.” Pickard has since cleared waivers and gone to Iowa, while Gustafsson Nyberg ($975,000) is still on PuckPedia’s NHL roster and hasn’t played an NHL game this season. title: Penguins: Overreaction trade Pittsburgh must make amid brutal start to NHL season
summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins defied expectations during the 2025-26 NHL campaign, returning to the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the first time since 2022. Additionally, after falling into a 0-3 hole against the divisional rival Philadelphia Flyers, the Penguins battled back and came within a goal of forcing what would have been a decisive Game 7. […] The post Penguins: Overreaction trade Pittsburgh must make amid brutal start to NHL season appeared first on ClutchPoints.
content: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Penguins: Overreaction trade Pittsburgh must make amid brutal start to NHL season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Penguins defied expectations during the 2025-26 NHL campaign, returning to the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the first time since 2022. Additionally, after falling into a 0-3 hole against the divisional rival Philadelphia Flyers, the Penguins battled back and came within a goal of forcing what would have been a decisive Game 7. Understandably, expectations for this season were that they would be able to build off the momentum of last season despite their core of Sidney Crosby , Evgeni Malkin , Kris Letang, Erik Karlsson, and Bryan Rust all being a year older. Instead, the exact opposite has happened, and many are wondering if Father Time has finally caught up to the Penguins for good. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) As of Nov. 27, the Penguins are 7-15-2, good for last place in the Metropolitan Division. Crosby’s offensive output currently has him on pace for just 52 points, which would be his lowest output since scoring 47 points (albeit in just 41 games) in 2019-20. And rumors surrounding Malkin, who agreed to come back for at least one more season, continue to grow louder as the Penguins sink further in the standings. That being said, it’s time for Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas to do the difficult thing that was once thought inevitable: begin the rebuilding process by trading Malkin and giving him one more chance to win the Stanley Cup before his Hall of Fame career comes to an end. Because, barring a miracle, that’s simply not going to happen in Pittsburgh; their run is over. Penguins need to do the difficult thing and trade Evgeni Malkin © Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Simply put, the Penguins’ run of any kind of reasonable hopes of success in the Stanley Cup Playoffs has run its course. And fans in Pittsburgh can count themselves thankful that they got to see one of the more impressive runs that any team could hope for, and one that several other fan bases around the NHL, many of which are decades older than the Penguins, would do anything to experience. The Penguins qualified for the postseason every year from 2007 through 2022, advanced to the Eastern Conference Final four times, and won the Stanley Cup three times, including becoming the first team since the 1997 and 1998 Detroit Red Wings to win consecutive titles (2016, 2017). Malkin played a major role in that run of success, winning the Conn Smythe Trophy as postseason MVP in 2009 and capturing multiple personal accolades along the way. His status as a future NHL Hall of Famer is guaranteed, and his No. 71 jersey number will be retired by the Penguins not long after he decides to hang up the skates for good. However, there’s no point in prolonging what’s coming for the Penguins. Their core is aging, and Crosby finally appears to be slowing down based on his significantly reduced production so far this season. They have little realistic chance of climbing back into the playoff picture in the Eastern Conference and are facing a difficult rebuilding process. The right thing for the Penguins would be to do right by Malkin and trade him to a contending team, giving him one last chance at a Stanley Cup while allowing Pittsburgh to recoup assets that could help kick-start the rebuilding process. He’s already been linked to the Minnesota Wild , who are still looking for a 2C after missing out on Dylan Larkin. It’s been an enviable run for Malkin in Pittsburgh, but it has run its course. Malkin, who was selected with the No. 2 overall pick by the Penguins in the 2004 NHL Draft, has appeared in 1,289 career NHL games and has scored 540 goals with 887 assists. He’s also contributed 69 goals with 114 assists in 183 career postseason games. title: Red Wings Blank Blue Jackets for Second Straight Victory
summary: Many people had the day off work on Black Friday, and thanks to the Detroit Red Wings, that group included […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Many people had the day off work on Black Friday, and thanks to the Detroit Red Wings, that group included the person in charge of firing the cannon at Nationwide Arena when the Columbus Blue Jackets score a goal. JOHN GIBSON SAID "NO GOALS" 😮‍💨 He records his 29th career @pepsi shutout! pic.twitter.com/C8UsX4pTAi — NHL (@NHL) November 27, 2026 Detroit goalie John Gibson turned aside all 18 shots he faced as the Red Wings blanked the Blue Jackets 2-0 on Friday. It was Gibson’s first shutout of the season and 29th of his NHL career. The Red Wings now have three shutouts in 25 games this season. JT Compher’s first-period goal proved to be the game winner. Compher slipped into an open seam in the high slot and whipped a Ben Chiarot feed past Blue Jackets goalie Jet Greaves. Compher scored for the second consecutive game and the third time in the past six games. THE CAT LETS IT RIP! 🚀 Alex DeBrincat gives the @DetroitRedWings a 2-0 lead! pic.twitter.com/t5A35IUNfe — NHL (@NHL) November 27, 2026 Alex DeBrincat made it 2-0 in the third period, beating Greaves with a one-timer from a sharp angle. Detroit won consecutive games for the first time since October 26 and 29. Takeaways Defenseman Andreas Englund took a first-period high-sticking penalty, just his second minor penalty of the season. Detroit won at Columbus for the first time since January 2, 2025. All five of Gibson’s shutouts with the Red Wings have come on the road. Detroit, Edmonton and Colorado are tied for second in the NHL in shutouts, each with three shutouts this season. Dallas leads the league with five shutouts. Defenseman Jacob Bernard-Docker and forward Carter Mazur were healthy scratches for Detroit. Red Wings defenseman William Wallinder (undisclosed) and goalie Sam Montembeault (IR) missed the game through injury . Key Stat With his goal on Friday, DeBrincat has nine goals in his past 11 games facing the Blue Jackets. He has points in each of his past 12 games against Columbus. Key Moment Detroit killed off both Columbus power-play opportunities and has allowed just one power-play goal over the past seven games (10-for-11). That’s a 90.9% success rate. Up Next The Red Wings are back in action on Saturday, playing host to the Nashville Predators at Little Caesars Arena at 7 p.m. ET. title: Red Wings Still Playing Hardball With Rochette
summary: Erstwhile Grand Rapids Griffins forward Theo Rochette is back in Switzerland, but as far as the Detroit Red Wings are […]
content: Erstwhile Grand Rapids Griffins forward Theo Rochette is back in Switzerland, but as far as the Detroit Red Wings are concerned, he still belongs to them. The Canadian-born Swiss international signed a one-year free-agent contract with the Red Wings last summer. At the time, he was gung-ho to give an NHL shot a go. “That’s what I’ve always wanted,” Rochette said. “And at the end of the day, my dream is to play in the NHL , so I don’t want to have any regret not trying.” However, after playing just nine AHL games with the Griffins, Rochette left the team. Vor den Augen von Nati-Star Théo Rochette, der im Waadtland als Rückkehrer gehandelt wird, siegt Lausanne gegen Rapperswil nur hauchdünn. https://t.co/kxcoVV2h25 — Blick Sport (@Blick_Sport) November 24, 2026 Lausanne HC, his Swiss club last season, has confirmed that Rochette is back in Switzerland. However, the Detroit brass is holding firm. They’ve not indicated that they are willing to release Rochette from the NHL pact he signed with the Red Wings. “They’ve explained their decision, but I don’t want to go into detail,” Lausanne HC John Fust said, according to reporting by Swiss Hockey News . Fust did confirm that Rochette had been back in Switzerland for several days. Rochette was in attendance earlier this week when Lausanne HC played Rapperswil in a Swiss National League game. Fust also added that the negotiations between his club and the Red Wings organization are ongoing. Red Wings Prospect Has Contract With Swiss Club Rochette, who played for Switzerland’s silver medal-winning squad at the 2026 IIHF World Championship, has a contract with Lausanne HC that runs through the 2030-31 season. However, like most European contracts, it includes an out clause permitting him to pursue NHL jobs. Sous les yeux de Théo Rochette, le LHC a souffert contre Rapperswil https://t.co/FaOKdl1O0D Source : 24 Heures pic.twitter.com/o9cmpdcHiE — Lausannehc-Partisans (@LhcPartisans) November 25, 2026 Rochette would need to gain his release from the Red Wings before the January 31, 2027, Swiss National League trade deadline. Otherwise, he will be ineligible to play for Lausanne HC this season. Rochette had 1-4-5 totals in five AHL games with the Griffins. His most recent appearance for Grand Rapids was in an October 24 game at Van Andel Arena against the Cleveland Monsters. Last season, Rochette led Lausanne HC with 22 goals.
