title: REPORT: Ottawa Senators 'Likely' Inquired About Collin Graf
summary: The Ottawa Senators are clearly open for business, as GM Steve Staios has been making the rounds, including a trip to Nashville to watch the Predators take on the Penguins. Now, there's a report that he could have inquired about a San Jose Sharks forward.
content: The Ottawa Senators are clearly open for business, as GM Steve Staios has been making the rounds, including a trip to Nashville to watch the Predators take on the Penguins. Now, there's a report that he could have inquired about a San Jose Sharks forward. On Wednesday, Senators columnist Bruce Garrioch shared the following : "A league executive told the Ottawa Citizen on Tuesday that the Senators have likely kicked the tires on 24-year-old winger Collin Graf of the San Jose Sharks." Now, it's important to note that there wasn't much detail beyond that. It doesn't sound like a legitimate trade offer has been made, at least not one that's been reported publicly. Graf's name entered the rumor mill last week when he was a healthy scratch for two consecutive games, but considering the fact that the Sharks signed him to a three-year contract extension in July, it doesn't seem likely that they'd be in a hurry to move on from the 24-year-old. At this stage, it simply seems like Staios inquired about Graf, as he likely has done with many players from many different teams. With that being said, the Senators and Sharks have been known to make trades, as both William Eklund and Fabian Zetterlund were sent to Canada's capital in recent years.

title: Sam Bennett scores 200th career goal with 24 seconds left as Panthers beat Capitals 3-2
summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Sam Bennett scored with 24 seconds remaining, the 200th goal of his career, and the Florida Panthers rallied past the Washington Capitals 3-2 on Friday.Bennett redirected a shot by Matthew Tkachuk past Washington goaltender Logan Thompson for his 12th of the season.
content: WASHINGTON (AP) — Sam Bennett scored with 24 seconds remaining, the 200th goal of his career, and the Florida Panthers rallied past the Washington Capitals 3-2 on Friday. Bennett redirected a shot by Matthew Tkachuk past Washington goaltender Logan Thompson for his 12th of the season. He has five goals in his past three games, including a hat trick against Buffalo on Nov. 21. Aaron Ekblad and Eetu Loustarinen also scored for the Panthers, who have won three straight. Brady Tkachuk and Matthew Tkachuk each had two assists. Rookie defenseman Cole Hutson scored twice for the Capitals, opening the scoring in the first period on the power play and going coast-to-coast to give Washington a 2-1 lead with 6:54 to go. His 18 points are third among rookies behind Chicago's Roman Kantserov (20) and Vegas's Trevor Connelly (19). Jacob Markstrom made 24 saves for the Panthers, while Thompson had 28 for Washington. Ryan Leonard, Justin Sourdif, Ivan Miroshnichenko and Pierre-Luc Dubois each had one assist for the Capitals. Loustarinen tied it with 4:18 remaining in regulation, scoring on a set play one-timer. Brad Marchand and Anton Lundell had the assists. Marchand has four points in two games since returning from an injured left knee. Washington has lost six of seven, all in regulation. Up next Panthers: Host Tampa Bay on Saturday. Capitals: Host St. Louis on Saturday. ___ See AP’s full NHL coverage here

title: 2 Up, 2 Down: More Frustration As Sunderland Drop Europa League Points
summary: Sunderland and Jagiellonia played out a scrappy draw as our Europa League campaign misfired again. Our writers react.
content: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 26: Sunderland's Chris Rigg crosses the ball despite the attentions of Jagiellonia Bialystok's Jeremy Agbonifo during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Sunderland AFC and Jagiellonia Bialystok at Stadium of Light on November 26, 2026 in Sunderland, United Kingdom. (Photo by Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images David Elliott says…. Well in, Timur! Tutierov deserves credit for his endeavour and willingness to fight for the cause. He also has that handy knack of being in the right place at the right time, which is invaluable for a front player. Robin Roefs stands out Roefs was excellent. I never bought in to the narrative that he has dropped off but rather he was left seriously exposed. He certainly saved our blushes. Shapeless Sunderland Our shape and press were not working. Somehow we’re allowing teams to play out from the back and then suddenly find acres of space to drive at our defence. The press is disjointed and confused; I can’t see the triggers that mean everyone pushes up and shuts down their options. A low-key atmosphere This one will be very unpopular, yet it saddens me to hear fans booing and singing the name of a player who has left us, and leaving the stadium early. The attendance was disappointing — I’m fully aware that AC Milan and Christmas are coming, but this is Europe and we don’t know when this will come round again. Jon Guy says… A decent point? It’s a stretch but we got another point. Arguably the easiest game of the eight and we made hard work of it, and I’m really polishing a turd here to say it was anything but disappointing. Thank God for Robin Roefs What player we have in our number one. If it wasn’t for him we’d be talking about a crushing defeat. Some great saves from our goalkeeper who has to be up there with the best in the league. Where’s the energy gone? It could be six down but the first is once again we simply don’t look like we have any energy and for a team with a coach who is meant to be a tactical genius, we didn’t look like we had a tangible game plan. It was a really poor effort and there was no intensity at all. Given this is a team which played last season with a really good press, this is a worry. As fans we want the players to put a shift in, but how many can say they came off the pitch physically spent? Another defensive nightmare The basic fundamental mistakes just keep on happening. What’s happened to the defence this season? We look so brittle at the back, and the players look so frightened. If the team has lost confidence in the back line, it’ll change the team’s whole approach. It’s becoming a major issue. Mark Ryan says… Robin Roefs keeps it respectable Great bit of shot stopping and hopefully he can bring this form into the Premier League as he was given far more efforts than anyone was expecting. General disappointment All the excitement, fanfare, buzz and league pain for the Europa League. It felt like the EFL Trophy as the standard of football was at best uninspiring , but in the main it was below that standard. Really, what’s the point? I wasn’t entertained and neither were the thousands that booed at the end. Soft-touch Sunderland? At times we were carved open like the turkeys we were. A reminder that Jagiellonia are ninth in Poland. They may have had most first-team players playing but various gifts from Reinildo et al, the result could and probably should’ve been worse. What have we done to Chris Rigg? Missing for most of the first half and only showed flashes of what he can produce. His movement was often non-existent; maybe one progressive pass and a shot. He wasn’t the worst performer but watching at times, he struggled to get into the game. Tom Albrighton says… I Know It’s Over The best part of that dirge was the referee putting us out of our misery five seconds early. The Sound of Silence A very quiet crowd was reflective of one of most abject Sunderland performances in years. An affront to anyone who endured the cold to watch a game with zero intensity and zero creativity. The silence at full time was particularly deafening. Automatic Stop I don’t know why we do it but once again we were subject to an evening where the default setting of the entire team was to put their foot on the ball, kill it and then go sideways and repeat ad infinitum. It hasn’t worked this season and it isn’t going to work this season, so stop doing it. We’d knock a crab sick with how much we go sideways. Over and Over The repetition of our slow play is becoming something of a bone of contention. Both wingers were absolutely hopeless but never helped by the fact the service they received was as equally as poor and their support was non-existent. I’d love to know what the coaches are seeing and thinking when it’s pretty clear to everyone that playing in such a way saps any and all creativity from them.

title: €50m Uruguay Star Wants Manchester United Move
summary: Manchester United Tracking Maxi Araújo as January Left-Back Question GrowsManchester United have spent months tracking Maxi Araújo, and according to Sport Witness, their interest remains active afte...
content: €50m Uruguay Star Wants Manchester United Move Manchester United Tracking Maxi Araújo as January Left-Back Question Grows Manchester United have spent months tracking Maxi Araújo, and according to Sport Witness , their interest remains active after seeing him first-hand in the 2-2 draw with Sporting. The key detail is simple enough. The player wants the move, United like the player, and the only real obstacle looks like the fee. Sport Witness report that a source close to the situation says the Uruguay international is “very open to joining the Premier League side”. That matters. In transfer talks, willingness from the player often does a lot of the heavy lifting. It does not close a deal, but it changes the temperature. Maxi Araújo Interest Looks Genuine This is not one of those stories built on one scout in the stands and a lot of noise. United have “closely followed Maxi Araújo for months”, and they used the Lisbon trip to take another proper look. Sport Witness add there is “mutual appreciation”, which usually means the groundwork has already been done quietly. Araújo also gave them something tangible on the pitch. He played the full 90 minutes against United and assisted Luis Suárez for Sporting’s opener in the 33rd minute. Over the season, he has made 15 appearances and was making his 14th start. Availability matters, and so does output. Photo IMAGO January Transfer Fee Remains Central Issue The numbers are clear. Araújo signed a new Sporting deal until 2030 in August, and that contract includes an €80m release clause. He is also on what Sport Witness describe as a “top salary at Sporting”. So nobody should expect a bargain. That said, the report adds that “€50-60m should be enough to take the player in January”. In modern terms, that is the real valuation point, not the clause. The problem for United is straightforward. The same source believes they are “unlikely to invest that amount of money on a fullback in January”. That sounds believable. Manchester United Left-Back Need Is Obvious United’s need at left-back is hardly a secret. Luke Shaw has again missed time with injury, while Harry Amass remains more of a developing option than a guaranteed solution. In Shaw’s absence, United have patched the role with Diogo Dalot and Lisandro Martínez. It works in spells, but it is still patchwork. That is why the final line in the report stands out most: “What is certain is that Maxi Araújo’s camp are open to Manchester United.” The player is interested, United are convinced enough to keep watching, and the position needs addressing. The only question is whether the club view Araújo as a necessity now, or a luxury they can delay until summer. Our View This is the sort of report that makes sense straight away. The left-back situation has dragged on too long and it keeps forcing compromises elsewhere. If a specialist is available, and if he already looks comfortable at a high level, then United should be asking harder questions about why this keeps getting postponed. Araújo sounds like a serious option, not a random name thrown into the market. “Mutual appreciation” is usually code for proper contact, proper checks, proper intent. If that is where this is heading, then dithering would be irritating. The club already know what happens when injuries hit and square pegs get shoved into full-back roles for months. The fee is the sticking point, obviously. €50-60m is a lot for a January full-back. Nobody sensible ignores that. But context matters. Paying big for the right player is one thing, paying smaller fees for temporary fixes and then still needing the proper signing later is worse business. If Pochettino wants him, that should carry weight. Managers need tools that fit what they want to do, and United have lacked balance on that side for too long. There is no guarantee Araújo becomes a star, but the logic is clean. The player is keen, the need is there, and the evidence has already been gathered up close. At some point, the club have to stop admiring problems and start solving them.

title: Ao Tanaka on new deal, support from the stands and never-quite-satisfied attitude
summary: Ao Tanaka became the second player of the week to sign a new contract with Leeds United, following in the footsteps of his team-mate, Dominic Calvert-Lewin.The Japanese international has been a consis...
content: Ao Tanaka on new deal, support from the stands and never-quite-satisfied attitude Ao Tanaka became the second player of the week to sign a new contract with Leeds United, following in the footsteps of his team-mate, Dominic Calvert-Lewin. The Japanese international has been a consistently high-performer at the heart of Daniel Farke’s midfield since his arrival in the summer of 2024, and has now extended his stay at Elland Road until the summer of 2029. “I am so happy to accept my contract,” he began. “I feel so comfortable to play for Leeds United. My team-mates, fans, everyone helped me on the pitch, so I enjoy playing football with Leeds United. I am so happy.” Tanaka’s opening words above were to LUTV after signing his new terms, and his beaming smile matched the vocabulary, showing his happiness. The connection between the midfielder and the fans has been key, and he admits he hears the support in matches. “In the game, I get a lot of power in this song [when he hears his chant from the stands], and yeah, I don’t know if this is normal or not, because I just play only for Leeds United in England. But in the home games especially, I feel like ‘okay, I have to score, I have to play well’. It gives me power.” Now in his second year at the top-table of English football, LUTV asked Ao what he had learned about Premier League football, and how he is continuing to improve his game. Tanaka explained: “Especially physicality and intensity is a different level than before. It is not easy to adapt to the club, the league, the football, but this is a massive challenge for me, and then I could improve my quality as a footballer. “Every team has high-quality players. Last season, I felt like it is difficult to get a point every game because every team is so good. I feel I have to learn a lot of things every game. If I am starting or the game winner, it doesn't matter. I need to learn a lot of things and then now I can understand everything in the plan, but I think I learn a lot of things in the plan. It is not easy but I enjoy playing football in the Premier League.” You can watch Ao’s full signing interview on LUTV, as well as reading an extended interview with him in this weekend’s matchday programme against Coventry City!

title: Ao Tanaka extends his stay at Elland Road
summary: Leeds United are thrilled to announce Ao Tanaka has signed a new contract with the club.The Japanese international will remain at Elland Road until 2029, joining fellow teammate Dominic Calvert-Lewin ...
content: Ao Tanaka extends his stay at Elland Road Leeds United are thrilled to announce Ao Tanaka has signed a new contract with the club. The Japanese international will remain at Elland Road until 2029, joining fellow teammate Dominic Calvert-Lewin in committing his future to the Whites. Ao joined in 2024 from Fortuna Düsseldorf and played an integral part in our title-winning campaign, making his debut on home soil in a win against Hull City. His first goal for the club came in the reverse fixture with the Tigers. That strike earned Tanaka individual recognition by winning the Goal of the Season accolade, the first of two awards in his debut season. After 43 appearances in the Sky Bet Championship, the midfielder was also voted by his peers as Players’ Player of the Season for his role in firing the Whites to the second-tier title. Following promotion, Ao made his Premier League debut in the Elland Road opener against Everton and would go on to feature 33 times across all competitions, netting four times, helping the Whites secure a 14th-place finish. His two goals in the league came against Chelsea and Liverpool, helping kickstart a strong run of form across December and into the New Year. Tanaka was also on target twice in a memorable Emirates FA Cup run, with Leeds reaching the last four of the competition. In the summer, the Japan international added to his 38 caps with three outings at the FIFA World Cup as the Samurai Blue reached the last 32 in the tournament. He has since added further appearances to his tally in the October and November breaks, to reach 47 in total. So far this campaign, Ao has featured 12 times in all competitions in the heart of midfield. He grabbed an assist at Brighton & Hove Albion and saw a fierce strike deflect into the back of the net in the 4-1 dismantling of Newcastle United. Everyone at Leeds United is delighted to see Ao extend his time at Elland Road, where he will continue to add energy and fight to the heart of our midfield.

title: Arsenal ready to go all out for Nico Paz as Mikel Arteta identifies £100m-rated Argentine as his next creative superstar
summary: Arsenal have emerged as serious contenders to sign Argentine sensation Nico Paz as Mikel Arteta looks to future-proof his midfield options at the Emirates Stadium. The 22-year-old has enjoyed a meteoric rise in Serie A, establishing himself as one of Europe's most coveted young playmakers under the guidance of Cesc Fabregas.
content: Como 1907 v AEK Athens - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal have emerged as serious contenders to sign Argentine sensation Nico Paz as Mikel Arteta looks to future-proof his midfield options at the Emirates Stadium. The 22-year-old has enjoyed a meteoric rise in Serie A, establishing himself as one of Europe's most coveted young playmakers under the guidance of Cesc Fabregas. Arteta eyes Argentine playmaker for long-term project Arsenal are reportedly intensifying their efforts to secure the services of Como star Paz, with the Gunners identifying the attacking midfielder as a priority target for the 2027 summer transfer window. According to ESPN Argentina , the North London club has maintained consistent contact with the player's representatives and has been conducting extensive scouting missions to monitor his development in Italy. Arteta is said to be a huge admirer of the 22-year-old’s versatility and technical proficiency, viewing him as a player who can elevate the club's creative output alongside captain Martin Odegaard. The Argentine international has become the focal point of a Como side that has surprised many in Serie A, showing a remarkable ability to dictate play and find the back of the net. While Arsenal were initially linked with a move for Paz during the previous summer, the youngster opted to remain at Como to ensure regular playing time and continue his progression under Fabregas. That decision has paid dividends, as his current form has seen his market value skyrocket, with reports suggesting that his current club could demand a fee in the region of €100m from any potential suitors outside of his former employers in Madrid. Real Madrid buy-back clause creates transfer hurdle Securing Paz will not be a straightforward task for the Gunners due to the complex contractual agreements currently in place. Real Madrid still hold a significant degree of control over their former academy product, retaining a buy-back option that is reportedly set at €80m for the summer of 2027. Despite this leverage held by the Spanish giants, the midfielder is believed to be reluctant to return to the Santiago Bernabeu, where he would face immense competition for a starting role. This hesitancy to move back to the Spanish capital has provided Arsenal with a glimmer of hope that a deal can be struck with Como directly. The financial logistics are further complicated by the fact that Como recently paid £50m to restructure the initial buy-back arrangement they had with Madrid. For Arsenal to jump to the front of the queue, they will likely need to present a massive financial package that exceeds the fixed price available to Real madrid. Manchester United rivalry intensifies for Paz signature 브루노 페르난데스 (Bruno Fernandes) Arsenal are not alone in their pursuit, as rivals Manchester United have also identified Paz as a potential replacement for Bruno Fernandes . The Red Devils are currently facing uncertainty regarding the future of their captain, whose contract is nearing its conclusion, and they view the Argentine as the ideal long-term successor at Old Trafford. For Paz, the decision will likely hinge on the sporting project and the guarantee of Champions League football. "Arsenal have been in contact with Nico Paz’s entourage for some time and have been scouting him closely. There will be a battle for his signature, with Manchester United also showing interest. Champions League qualification will be key for the player," the report from ESPN Argentina detailed. With Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain also lurking in the background, the race for the 22-year-old is shaping up to be one of the biggest transfer sagas of the coming year.

title: Arsenal ready to make a serious move to sign Real Madrid-linked Serie A playmaker
summary: Earlier in the day, it was reported that Manchester United are among the clubs interested in the services of Nico Paz.The Argentine international has been identified as a potential long-term replaceme...
content: Arsenal ready to make a serious move to sign Real Madrid-linked Serie A playmaker Earlier in the day, it was reported that Manchester United are among the clubs interested in the services of Nico Paz . The Argentine international has been identified as a potential long-term replacement for Bruno Fernandes, whose contract at Old Trafford expires at the end of the season. This makes things interesting for Real Madrid, as the club hold an €80 million buyback clause for the Como playmaker. Arsenal ready to make a serious move Arsenal are serious about signing Nico Paz. (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images) However, Man United are not the only club interested in Paz, as Arsenal, too, are keen on getting their hands on the former Real Madrid academy prospect. According to ESPN (h/t Eduardo Hagn ), Arsenal are prepared to seriously pursue Paz in the summer of 2027, as they look to add more creative firepower to the team. Arsenal have already been in contact with Paz’s representatives for some time. The club have also been scouting the playmaker quite closely. Arsenal want to convince Paz to move to the Premier League, rather than entertaining the prospect of a Real Madrid return, where his first-team chances could be limited. A red alert for Real Madrid Nico Paz set for a big move in the summer of 2027. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) While Manchester United may have lost their appeal as a club in recent years, Arsenal’s interest in the player should raise alarm bells at Real Madrid. Thanks to the success Arsenal have had in recent years, the Gunners are in an excellent position to convince Paz to completely give up on his Real Madrid dream and play more regularly at the Emirates. It has been reported in the past that while Paz is open to the idea of returning to Real Madrid, he wants the club to assure him of a guaranteed place in the starting eleven. Real Madrid, therefore, must soon come to a decision as far as the Argentine’s future is concerned. They can either activate the buyout clause and try to sell him for a higher fee, or they could try to accommodate the player in their current lineup. Given Real Madrid’s squad build, though, accommodating Paz in a team that already has Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler could be next to impossible. Arsenal, therefore, certainly have a case to make.

title: Arteta gives latest update on Raya ahead of Man City match
summary: Mikel Arteta has refused to rule David Raya out of Arsenal’s Premier League clash with Manchester City, with the goalkeeper back in training ahead of Sunday’s game.Raya remains a doubt for the mee...
content: Arteta gives latest update on Raya ahead of Man City match Mikel Arteta has refused to rule David Raya out of Arsenal’s Premier League clash with Manchester City, with the goalkeeper back in training ahead of Sunday’s game. Raya remains a doubt for the meeting at the Emirates after missing the midweek draw with Borussia Dortmund following the injury he sustained against Newcastle. But Arteta says a decision on his availability has not yet been made. “I don’t know,” the Arsenal boss said when asked whether Raya will be available. “We still have a few hours for the game, so we’re just trying to get everybody back.” Asked whether the goalkeeper has been able to train, Arteta confirmed: “Yeah, they’re all training.” But when pressed on whether Raya had been able to fully test himself by diving during the session, Arteta added: “That I’m not sure.” Stay up to date with all the latest Arsenal news by joining our Arsenal WhatsApp channel .

title: Auxerre full-back Lamine Sy to be out for ‘between six weeks and six months’ due to injury
summary: AJ Auxerre’s Lamine Sy (24) will be out for an extended period, his manager Will Still announced at a press conference two days ahead of the home match against Olympique de Marseille on matchday 12 ...
content: Auxerre full-back Lamine Sy to be out for ‘between six weeks and six months’ due to injury AJ Auxerre’s Lamine Sy (24) will be out for an extended period, his manager Will Still announced at a press conference two days ahead of the home match against Olympique de Marseille on matchday 12 of Ligue 1. “Lamine has torn his meniscus and will be out of action for quite some time,” said the 34-year-old manager. Whilst the exact length of his absence is yet to be confirmed, Still indicated that his player would not return to action for at least six weeks in the “best-case scenario”. In the “worst-case scenario”, his absence could last up to six months. An undisputed first-team regular for AJA, Sy has started nine of the 11 matches (scoring one goal) in which he has featured since the start of the 2026-27 season. Called up to the Senegal national team for the first time in his career during the September international break, he made his debut in the Lions of Teranga’s 1-1 draw with Mozambique, before featuring in the matches against Ethiopia (1-0 win) and the Comoros (1-0 win). title: Azaz feeds off emotions - Eckert
summary: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert speaks to BBC Radio Solent after win over Middlesbrough.
content: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert spoke to BBC Radio Solent following their 2-0 win over Middlesbrough. "We've had some special games here. The boys have done very well. We had so much support and that gives you energy and additional emotions that you need to manage before and during the game. We deserved it," he said. "We've had a couple of games when we've gone [ahead] and probably haven't managed those games the way we can. It's something we've worked on and addressed. We've made a good step forward today. "Night games at St Mary's are just special, especially if it [starts] the weekend. We need to make sure we improve our performances on the road. That will be the next step for us and we can show that against Wolves [away] on Saturday week. "If you take the emotions away from Finn [Azaz], he's half the player he is. He feeds off that. It is what it is. I don't want to start complaining about anything tonight." Latest Southampton news and analysis

title: Barcelona close to reaching a contract renewal agreement with academy gem after first-team breakthrough – report
summary: According to The Athletic, Barcelona are nearing an agreement to extend Brian Farinas’ contract, with the versatile right-back emerging as another young talent the club wants to secure for the long ...
content: Barcelona close to reaching a contract renewal agreement with academy gem after first-team breakthrough – report According to The Athletic , Barcelona are nearing an agreement to extend Brian Farinas’ contract, with the versatile right-back emerging as another young talent the club wants to secure for the long term. Notably, the proposed renewal would take his deal from 2028 to 2031, strengthening Barça’s protection against interest from other clubs. Barcelona want to reward Farinas after first-team breakthrough As stated before, Barcelona sporting director Deco has held several meetings with Farinas’ representatives , with negotiations now approaching their final stages. The club’s intention is to recognise the 20-year-old’s progress and bring his contract in line with his growing status under Hansi Flick. Farinas’ current agreement runs until 2028 and reportedly contains a €15 million release clause. Barcelona are understood to want to improve his financial terms and increase the clause, which they consider insufficient to protect a player beginning to attract attention. Barcelona are close to securing Brian Farinas’ future. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) It has previously been reported that Barcelona had reached a verbal agreement to extend his contract until June 2031, although the club has yet to make an official announcement . First-team opportunity accelerated negotiations Barcelona’s renewal plans for Farinas began in August, when he was promoted into the first-team setup and given a senior squad number. However, discussions gained momentum after his first-team debut against Alaves in late October. Originally a midfielder, Farinas had to wait for his opportunity, with injuries to Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia and Xavi Espart opening the door for him to play as a right-back. He responded by playing the full match against Alaves and subsequently featuring against Atletico Madrid and Aston Villa. Brian Farinas will renew his contract until 2030. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His ability to operate in more than one position has also strengthened his value to Flick, who has used him primarily as a right-back despite his background as a midfielder. Barcelona continue securing their core players Farinas’ proposed renewal forms part of Barcelona’s strategy to secure players who have become core members of the first-team picture. Raphinha recently committed his future to the club until 2030, while Xavi Espart signed a two-year extension last week that also keeps him under contract until 2030. Gerard Martin is another player whose renewal is reportedly close. For Barcelona, extending Farinas’ deal would provide greater contractual security at a time when his first-team opportunities are increasing. A longer agreement and improved release clause would also give the club more control over his future as he continues to develop.

title: Barcelona’s unlikely goal machine is starting to make his case
summary: Gabriel Jesus has made an encouraging start to life at Barcelona, scoring five goals in just 376 minutes despite struggling to secure regular playing time. The Brazilian striker arrived at Spotify Ca...
content: Barcelona’s unlikely goal machine is starting to make his case Gabriel Jesus has made an encouraging start to life at Barcelona, scoring five goals in just 376 minutes despite struggling to secure regular playing time. The Brazilian striker arrived at Spotify Camp Nou to take over Robert Lewandowski’s place, but has found opportunities limited by Raphinha’s remarkable form in the centre forward position. While expectations were modest compared with those surrounding Lewandowski, Jesus is beginning to show why Barcelona brought him to the club. His goalscoring return has been particularly impressive considering he has made only 11 appearances and had not completed a full match before the Champions League fixture against Sabah in Baku. Gabriel Jesus scores whenever Flick starts him One of the most striking aspects of Jesus’ Barcelona career so far is his record when selected from the beginning. The striker has scored in all three matches in which Hansi Flick has started him, finding the net against Getafe, Real Betis and Sabah. Gabriel Jesus has scored five goals in very limited time for Barcelona. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His goal in Baku came from close range , with Jesus reacting quickly to a loose ball inside the penalty area. It was not a spectacular finish, but it still showed the instinctive positioning that has become a feature of his performances. As such, the Brazilian has scored five goals in 376 minutes, which translates to a goal every 76 minutes. Barcelona have discovered a natural finisher Jesus, who signed from Arsenal, has already shown different ways of scoring during his short Barcelona spell, having demonstrated quality in the air, the ability to finish with either foot, a powerful strike and composure when opportunities arrive inside the box. His greatest strength, however, may be his anticipation. Jesus regularly positions himself to react before defenders, allowing him to convert chances that might otherwise disappear. Gabriel Jesus has scored the same amount og goals as Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Mind you, his five goals also match the totals of Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi, despite both players having enjoyed considerably more playing time. Raphinha’s form limits his opportunities Meanwhile, it is clear that Raphinha’s extraordinary run of 19 goals in 16 matches has made it difficult for Jesus to establish himself as Barcelona’s first choice in attack. The Brazilian winger has excelled as a centre forward, a development that even surprised Raphinha himself. Jesus still needs to improve his understanding with teammates including Fermin Lopez, Pedri, Lamine Yamal and Gordon as he adapts to Barcelona’s style, but that will improve as the season moves on. For now, however, his numbers provide a compelling argument for greater involvement. Five goals from limited opportunities suggest that Barcelona have a striker capable of making an immediate impact whenever Flick turns to him.

title: The Bayern Insider: Crucial Musiala meeting held as Olise concern emerges behind the scenes
summary: Welcome to today’s exclusive & comprehensive round-up of all things Bayern Munich from Bayern insider Christian Falk. Featuring updates on Jamal Musiala, Michael Olise, Joshua Kimmich, and Donyell M...
content: The Bayern Insider: Crucial Musiala meeting held as Olise concern emerges behind the scenes Welcome to today’s exclusive & comprehensive round-up of all things Bayern Munich from Bayern insider Christian Falk. Featuring updates on Jamal Musiala, Michael Olise, Joshua Kimmich, and Donyell Malen. Today’s top stories What is the latest on the Jamal Musiala situation? Could Nicolò Tresoldi be signed in the January transfer window? Is Derry Scherhant a potential option to cover Luis Diaz? And plenty more on Max Eberl, Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, Jonathan Tah & Min-jae Kim For everyone following our work here on CF Bayern Insider, you’ll know how close you are to the inner workings of this football club, because it was again our exclusive that delved into the Jamal Musiala story. We had a photo of the secret meeting at Säbener Straße on Tuesday, and we knew what happened there. Before, we heard about Uli Hoeneß talking about a need to potentially discuss the salary; CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen spoke along similar lines… and then there was Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who spoke in an interview after the match against FC Köln. It’s an interesting situation, as he wasn’t in the mixed zone like the other Bayern bosses. The cameras were coming up to him in the stands. It wasn’t really spontaneous. It was absolutely planned and the message was really direct, certainly more direct than the messages we’ve seen before from the other bosses. He was saying that Bayern don’t know if they can sell Jamal Musiala and they weren’t sure if anyone follows this player anymore, as he doesn’t have a market value anymore. The club believes that it has to talk with Musiala’s side now, because for 12 days they’ve talked about the footballer but not directly with his entourage. With this in mind, we knew there had to be a meeting taking place, and we were there! Want more CF Bayern Insider coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust In the end, Vincent Kompany, Christoph Freund, and Max Eberl – this side of Bayern Munich – have always been in talks with the Musiala side, and they know how he’s feeling, how the treatment is going, if he’s improving, whether he’ll be on the pitch, and so on. But not all of the bosses are so clearly informed. This is why it was so important that this meeting Säbener Straße took place and the bosses were at the table. Jan-Christian Dreesen, Herbert Hainer – on one hand the CEO, on the other the president – and Eberl were there in talks with Jamal Musiala’s team. They told him that not everyone is thinking about the situation like some people are speaking about it. They want the best for the playmaker. They also don’t want to talk about the salary right now. Bayern also released a press release to confirm talks and that they were aware of the medication and what will happen in the future, and they don’t want to put pressure on him. On the other hand, we know that they didn’t write in this message: if in the next month there is no development, and we’re not talking about January and February… we’re talking about the next six months, then Bayern Munich will have to talk about the salary. But this is not what we want; this is not what we expect. Everyone is hoping that Jamal Musiala can be the best possible version of himself. This is what the Musiala side said at this meeting – they believe he can be the Musiala he was before they found the right medication. You can get the best performance. There have been a lot of rumours and speculation around this saga, including about the player’s signing fee. I’m afraid to say a lot of misinformation has been spread – so this is exactly why we’re here to say what is TRUE and NOT TRUE. There is a fear of Joshua Kimmich… (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Key figures in the club know the comments about Musiala were a bit too much. They did want to start a conversation about the topic, but the intention wasn’t to pass judgement on the Germany international, nor to put so much pressure on a footballer who is, ultimately, unwell. This is why it’s so important that Joshua Kimmich, who is the secret captain of this team, spoke on behalf of the dressing room. There is a fear of Kimmich, and this has something to do with Michael Olise, as the Frenchman is very, very close with Musiala. Bear in mind, he’s seeing what’s playing out in public. On that point, it can’t be emphasised enough that if you want to encourage Olise to sign a new contract with FC Bayern, you need to be able to rely on the argument of the Bayern family – not just the numbers in the contract. From Olise’s point of view, you could forgive him for thinking, Well, what do the numbers matter anyway if decision-makers will end up wanting to have a discussion if my performance levels dip? This is a really important point now. Michael Olise is thinking about his future, and Jo Kimmich is aware of this. He wants the best possible team, as he wants to win the Champions League with Bayern Munich. It’s a lot harder to do that without players like Michael Olise in the first XI. This is why the 31-year-old has joined in on the discussion with the bosses. For the record, I think this is really brave, and I’m glad he showed up for the team. Was there a gentlemen’s agreement between Bayern & Musiala? ❌It is NOT TRUE: Bayern had a gentlemen’s agreement (from the summer) with Jamal Musiala’s side that they could alter the contract. It’s true that there was a meeting at Uli Hoeneß’s residence in Tegernsee. I’ve been sat there a few times myself – quite often, I can say! I know a meeting took place, but there was absolutely no agreement with regard to what would or wouldn’t happen with the contract. They made a strategy, at this point, in terms of what would happen if this topic became public and how they could handle the situation with the medication. It was all about how Bayern could help Musiala in these special circumstances. Of course, everyone will be more than aware of the fact that when two people are talking, sometimes not everyone hears the same thing. So, perhaps there was a little wish from the Bayern side that there could be something implemented so that there could be a later discussion about the financial side of things. But no, this just wasn’t a topic. Max Eberl in trouble with the supervisory board again? (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) It’s true that the supervisory board is a big thing at Bayern Munich. We know Karl-Heinz Rummenigge isn’t the biggest fan of director of sport Max Eberl. He didn’t want the former RB Leipzig chief to get a contract extension. We know that at the meeting to decide Eberl’s future, he abstained from the vote. Yes, you can say Eberl played a key role in making this contract for Jamal Musiala, but the supervisory board also had to approve it! Rummenigge’s comments was a criticism of Musiala, but it was also a criticism of the 53-year-old’s work. I think everyone can see one plus one equals two in this case. But in the end, everyone from the other side, including Christoph Freund, Max Eberl and, especially, Vincent Kompany are totally clear that they did the right thing. At the end of the day, the supervisory board agreed to the contract. There is some truth in Rummenigge being irritated by the nature of the contract, but it’s not a feeling shared by the whole group. Nicolò Tresoldi has caught the eye at Bayern ✅It is TRUE: Nicolò Tresoldi is on the list at Bayern Munich. They are in talks with the player’s side. He’s an interesting player! I know that he was very high on the list of the chief scout, Nils Schmadtke. The 37-year-old has to leave in January, so he won’t be in charge later. Regardless, the deal won’t happen in January because I heard that Brugge won’t sell him midway through the season. The board and the supervisory board at Bayern Munich want to see what will happen in the next month or so. For such a deal, you have to work a bit longer to get Tresoldi out of his contract. My thinking is that this isn’t a deal they can sort in January. But to be honest, he is on the list for the future and they’re keeping a close eye on his performances. Nicolò Tresoldi could play for the German national team. He hasn’t decided yet. He can also play for Italy, but he’s currently playing with the Germany U21s. He’s very, very interesting for Bayern Munich, but not a topic for January. Could Donyell Malen be a target for January? (Photo by Luca Amedeo Bizzarri/Getty Images) ❌It is NOT TRUE: Bayern are considering Donyell Malen as a January signing. He’s doing very well at Roma at the moment. Also, for such a striker, you need a strategy and a long-term plan. He’s not one you bring in now for just a few months and then relegate to the bench as soon as Harry Kane is back. I know why these rumours are out there. As everyone is thinking Bayern Munich need a striker, the agents are hoping to make a good deal. But I’m afraid to say that Malen is simply not a topic at this stage. Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting There is truth in the links to Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting. The 37-year-old has the option of a potential temporary return to FC Bayern in mind. There could be such a deal. When you look at the past of Bayern Munich, this is a plan they’re prepared to execute in certain circumstances. Remember players like Claudio Pizarro, who may be a little bit older, and you bring them in, taking advantage of the fact that they already know the club and the playing style. This would be an idea for a few months and you don’t have to give him a long-term contract. He wouldn’t have the same salary as he had a few years before when he last played for Bayern Munich. This could happen, but it would be a transfer at the end of the window in January. The club’s decision-makers will look at the squad, and if they think they need one more player, Choupo-Moting could be the option. Derry Scherhant: The Luis Diaz backup? (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images) ✅It is TRUE: Derry Scherhant has been scouted by Bayern Munich as a potential backup option for Luis Diaz. He’s a perfect player for FC Bayern; he’s already a German national player. Jurgen Klopp gave him international status. This is the kind of player who would work at Bayern. He’s young, of course, and the playing time wouldn’t be massive in Munich. The player is considering his next step. However, Bayern know he could be a big topic in the summer. We’ve already talked about several options on the list. JJ Gabriel has gone to Real Madrid, so they’ve already lost him. Everyone’s seen the match Rio Ngumoha had for Liverpool against Manchester United. Liverpool fans will be very happy, but you have to think the Reds will push to give him a new contract. I’m thinking it’ll be difficult to sign this player for Bayern now. It would be a shame, given there was a genuine chance to sign the teenager in the summer. There were talks with the brother, and FC Bayern were prepared to pay €70m [£58.5m], but Liverpool said no. At the time, I thought, perhaps, there would be an opportunity to sign him the following summer with a year left on his contract. At the moment, I don’t have much faith in this happening! Talks with Jonathan Tah and Min-jae Kim It’s an interesting situation! Min-jae Kim was set for talks in the Autumn. In the German calendar, this runs until 21st December. I heard there should have already been talks with the South Korean international. However, because of the Jamal Musiala situation, Bayern are prioritising this before moving on to Kim’s talks. They’ll have to find a new appointment. I’m not sure if they’ll make it this year! On the Jonathan Tah talks: his agents were at Säbener Straße and were talking about the centre-back’s situation. They wanted to make clear that the German international is the boss in the defence and that he’s the man beside Dayot Upamecano. They also wanted to make clear that he’s the number one there. Against Lille, he was on the bench. However, it should be noted that Upamecano prefers to play with Tah. So, I think if there are offers for Kim, Bayern Munich will decide that he can leave. Also, the former Napoli star is feeling well at the moment, and he has time to decide on his future.

title: Which Bayern Munich player needs to step up most vs. Hamburger SV?
summary: FC Bayern needs a hero.
content: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich cannot afford to let the loss to LOSC Lille turn into a slump, and Saturday’s trip to Hamburger SV offers an immediate chance to respond. With injuries continuing to test Vincent Kompany’s squad, the players available need to carry more weight. The question is: Which Bayern Munich player needs to step up most against HSV? Michael Olise would be an obvious pick if fit, but Bayern need contributions across the pitch. Joshua Kimmich has to set the tone, control the midfield, and keep Bayern steady when Hamburger SV pushes forward. Luis Díaz must bring the directness, creativity, and edge needed to stretch a stubborn defense. Lennart Karl’s fearless approach could inject much-needed spark in the final third. With Serge Gnabry sidelined, the remaining attackers carry extra weight, while Konrad Laimer must drive Bayern’s intensity for all 90 minutes. Bayern do not need overcomplicated tactics or soul-searching over what went wrong in France. They need three points, a decisive display, and someone willing to seize control. title: Borussia Dortmund vs. Bayer Leverkusen preview: A heavyweight clash at the top
summary: Borussia DortmundMatchday 11 of the Bundesliga wraps up with one of the most anticipated games of the weekend as Borussia Dortmund host Bayer Leverkusen. Kick-off at the Westfalenstadion on Sunday is ...
content: Borussia Dortmund vs. Bayer Leverkusen preview: A heavyweight clash at the top Borussia Dortmund Matchday 11 of the Bundesliga wraps up with one of the most anticipated games of the weekend as Borussia Dortmund host Bayer Leverkusen. Kick-off at the Westfalenstadion on Sunday is scheduled for 19:30 CET. This fixture is undoubtedly a true test for BVB who currently sit top of the table with 2 points to spare. If they are to contend for silverware, getting the better of their in-form Rhineland opponents seems like an absolute must. Given their fine form, Niko Kovač's side should feel confident. Added to that, they secured a 1-1 draw away to Arsenal on Tuesday. Perhaps most impressive was their ability to fight back, grab parity and trouble the English champions. Their visitors, however, have proven to be a tricky nut to crack in recent years. Dortmund previously tended to dominate, but they have only extracted one win in their last five games against Leverkusen in front of the yellow wall. Team news: Emre Can, Giannis Konstantelias (both ACL tears), Justin Lerma (muscle injury) and Samuele Inácio (meniscus) are sidelined. Both Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka returned to fitness midweek against Arsenal. Bayer Leverkusen Bayer Leverkusen have seemingly put most of their late-October woes behind them. Things look to be clicking into gear under Carles Martínez who has been getting more of a tune out of his squad with each passing game. This short trip to face the Westphalian giants will equally test how much progress they truly have made. Up against an undefeated side who have only leaked three goals in five league games at home is as tough as it gets. Undoubtedly, fans and players alike of the Rhineland outfit will be confident in marksman Patrik Schick. The Czechia native has looked unstoppable at times, producing 9 goals in 10 Bundesliga outings already this campaign. Add that to the fact that the likes of Christian Kofane, Nathan Tella and Moussa Diaby are back in the mix, options are plentiful. Their 2-0 win over Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday ought not to have sapped to much energy either. Team news: Leverkusen's only major absentees as it stands are Kennet Eichhorn (fitness), Martin Terrier (hamstring) and Lucas Vasquez (knock). The trio are expected to play no part in the game as they focus on their recoveries. Click here to see our predicted starting lineups for the clash of Borussia Dortmund vs. Bayer Leverkusen.

title: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record
summary: Bournemouth are already dreaming on European glory under Marco Rose, and rightly so. After going 1-0 down against Celta Vigo in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night, having a man sent off and then...
content: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record Bournemouth are already dreaming on European glory under Marco Rose, and rightly so. After going 1-0 down against Celta Vigo in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night, having a man sent off and then scoring two goals, the Cherries’ 2-1 victory is their fifth straight win in their maiden European competition. With five wins from five and maximum points, Bournemouth became the first English team, and only the third in history, to win their first five European matches. Only Nuremberg (1961/62) and Ararat Yerevan (1972/73) are the only other teams to record such a feat. It was also their tenth straight victory across all competitions – a record matched only by Real Madrid. Speaking to the BBC Sport after Bournemouth’s latest victory, Rose, formerly of Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, said: “Dreaming is always allowed. When you participate in a competition like this, you want to achieve the best possible result.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder

title: Brest predicted XI v Paris FC: Noah Edjouma to continue in attack, Brendan Chardonnet remains sidelined
summary: Noah Edjouma, on loan from Lille OSC, has hit form in recent weeks and he is expected to retain his place in the team on the right of Stade Brestois’ attack as they prepare to host Paris FC on Frida...
content: Brest predicted XI v Paris FC: Noah Edjouma to continue in attack, Brendan Chardonnet remains sidelined Noah Edjouma, on loan from Lille OSC, has hit form in recent weeks and he is expected to retain his place in the team on the right of Stade Brestois’ attack as they prepare to host Paris FC on Friday night. There are no fresh absences for Julien Lachuer to contend with, however, he remains without defenders Raphael Le Guen and Brendan Chardonnet. The latter’s absence is particularly concerning, given how far behind schedule he now is in his recovery. He sustained a calf tear three months ago and has yet to feature for Brest this season. He is expected to play for the club’s youth side on Friday night. Ludovic Ajorque will continue to lead the line for Les Ty-Zéfs , with Pathé Mboup on the left and Kamory Doumbia continuing in the No.10 role. Brest likely line-up v Paris FC Egil Selvik; Bradley Locko, Gautier Lloris, Lucas Tousart, Kenny Lala; Joris Chotard, Hugo Magnetti; Pathé Mboup, Kamory Doumbia, Noah Edjouma; Ludovic Ajorque. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle

title: Cannavaro: Zidane’s headbutt helped me win the Ballon d’Or, Barcelona criticism makes me ‘smile’
summary: Italy legend Fabio Cannavaro admits Zinedine Zidane’s headbutt in the 2006 World Cup Final helped him win the Ballon d’Or: ‘It’s worth three times more now; I don’t see how a defender can wi...
content: Cannavaro: Zidane’s headbutt helped me win the Ballon d’Or, Barcelona criticism makes me ‘smile’ Italy legend Fabio Cannavaro admits Zinedine Zidane’s headbutt in the 2006 World Cup Final helped him win the Ballon d’Or: ‘It’s worth three times more now; I don’t see how a defender can win it again.’ The legendary defender won the Ballon d’Or 20 years ago today. Cannavaro, currently the Uzbekistan national team coach, remains the last defender and the last Italian player to have won the coveted award. “Now it’s worth three times more. No defender has won it since, and I don’t see how it can happen again,” he told Gazzetta. When the journalist argued that Pau Cubarsì might be the closest, Cannavaro replied. MILAN, ITALY – MAY 06: Lautaro Martinez of FC Internazionale is challenged by Pau Cubarsi of FC Barcelona which results in referee Szymon Marciniak (not pictured) awarding a penalty to FC Internazionale during the UEFA Champions League 2024/25 Semi Final Second Leg match between FC Internazionale Milano and FC Barcelona at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 06, 2025 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) “A Barcelona defender—the city that criticised my victory the most.” Catalan newspapers strongly criticised Cannavaro’s Ballon d’Or win 20 years ago, arguing that Barcelona striker Samuel Eto’o deserved it more. “Criticism has never annoyed me. Now I smile. It seems that it is my fault if Maldini, Baresi or Cubarsì have never won it,” Cannavaro replied. The former defender revealed how he learned he had won the Ballon d’Or. “I remember a France Football journalist stopped me in front of the Real Madrid training centre. He got into my car and said: ‘I must tell you something: Buffon can’t reach you; you have won, and we must do an interview.’ I thought: ‘Is this a joke?’ When I watch games of that season, I think: ‘Mamma mia! I was playing so well.’ But I knew, as I know today, that if Zidane had not given that headbutt, it would have been much more complicated.” TASHKENT, UZBEKISTAN – MARCH 30: Fabio Cannavaro, Head Coach of Uzbekistan, reacts during the international friendly match between Uzbekistan and Venezuela on March 30, 2026 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. (Photo by Anvar Ilyasov/Getty Images) Cannavaro was named the best player in the world in 2006 after helping Italy win the World Cup that year. The Final against France was one of the most epic games ever and saw Zidane sent off in extra time for headbutting Italy defender Marco Materazzi. That Final remains Italy’s last World Cup knockout game. What should Italian football do, especially defensively, to return to greatness? “We’ve only stopped working on individual technique, on running, and on the habit of defending with the ball frontally and laterally,” Cannavaro replied. “Each role has its characteristics, and sometimes they prefer a goalkeeper who can make a 70-meter pass to one who actually makes saves. It’s okay, but then don’t complain if he concedes at an important moment.” BOLOGNA, ITALY – APRIL 28: Fabio Cannavaro, Head Coach of Udinese Calcio, looks on prior to the Serie A TIM match between Bologna FC and Udinese Calcio at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on April 28, 2024 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) When asked whether his mentality has changed now that he has become a coach, Cannavaro replied: “For sure. When you start a coaching career, you think your ideas are the most important in the world; then you understand you have to adapt. I’ve seen coaches sacked because they wanted to change the team’s menu or train in the morning instead of the afternoon. Let’s say that I’ve become wiser and more experienced.” During the same interview, the former Juventus, Napoli, Parma and Inter defender said Liverpool defender Virgil Van Dijk told him during the 2026 World Cup that he’d like to play in Serie A one day.

title: Charlotte FC eye playoff history vs. Chicago Fire: "It's no easy task"
summary: By Cal MeachemCharlotte FC are on the doorstep of a historic moment as they enter Saturday's home match against Chicago Fire FC (12:30 pm ET | Apple TV).With Game 2 of their Eastern Conference Round ...
content: Charlotte FC eye playoff history vs. Chicago Fire: "It's no easy task" By Cal Meachem Charlotte FC are on the doorstep of a historic moment as they enter Saturday's home match against Chicago Fire FC (12:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). With Game 2 of their Eastern Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series looming, the Crown can advance past Round One of the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs for the first time in club history. Head coach Dean Smith and his squad are determined to ensure that dream becomes a reality. "All the work that they've had to put in, all the sacrifices, all the time they could have spent with their families, have been to get to this position now," said Smith. "If we win, we go through. The players know what is at stake." ⚽🏆 ALL FOR THE CUP Every match matters. Don't miss a moment of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. Watch on Apple TV Ready for more Since joining MLS as an expansion side in 2022, Charlotte have reached the postseason four times but never made a deep run. In fact, 2026 is the first season they've led an playoff series, after falling behind against New York City FC in 2025 and Orlando City in 2024. Now, thanks to their dramatic 2-1 road victory in Game 1, the Crown can eliminate the Fire in two games – and do so in front of a raucous home crowd at Bank of America Stadium. "We've won the first one, and now comes the tricky part of making sure we go and win the second game," Smith said. "It's no easy task. We've got home advantage; that's the big thing, and we've got to make sure we take advantage of that." Benin international forward Rodolfo Aloko praised the advantage Charlotte's fans provide: "I love the fans, how they bring energy. And then when I'm on the field, I want to bring them back this energy." Still, Smith preached composure and connectivity, understanding that you cannot let emotions slip. "You can't expect to just turn up and win because you're at home," the English manager added. "You've still got to do the hard yards. You've still got to work hard. You've got to outrun the opponents. You've got to outfight them. You've got to outthink them. "Don't lose your discipline." Fighting for their playoff lives Despite their 1-0 series advantage, Charlotte fully recognize the dangers posed by head coach Gregg Berhalter's side and, specifically, Robert Lewandowski . Hundreds of opponents have done their very best to stop the legendary Polish striker – one of the best No. 9s of this generation – from finding the back of the net, and few have ever had consistent success. Smith knows stopping Lewandowski, who scored the Fire's goal in Game 1 , won't be easy. "You could see that he's a top player," Smith said of the former FC Barcelona and Bayern Munich star. "I'm not sure many defenders could have defended him at the back post for that goal. ... You've just got to be aware of him because he can come alive at any moment." Nonetheless, Smith believes his side will be ready for the challenge. "I think we never lose focus," the former Premier League manager hailed. "We never lose sight of what we can do and what we can achieve. There's a great togetherness amongst the group, so that's been a pleasing thing." title: Cruz Azul crush Leon and look set to go thru to the Semifinals
summary: Cruz Azul demolished Leon by a 4-0 score and have almost settled their Quarterfinal series in their favor.
content: Cruz Azul's Argentine forward #20 Jose Paradela celebrate a goal during the Liga MX Apertura Liguilla quarter-final first-leg football match between Leon and Cruz Azul at the Leon Stadium in Leon, Mexico on November 26, 2026. (Photo by Mario ARMAS / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Cruz Azul demolished Leon by a 4-0 score in the first leg of the Quarterfinals series and looks to have settled the Quarterfinal series. Leon must not only win by 5 goals on Sunday but they must do so as the away team against the current Liga MX title. Cruz Azul was overly superior to a Leon team that looked rattled from the start, possibly because of the strong rainstorm that lasted all match. Cruz Azul looks likely to make if official in the return leg on Sunday. The 1st half started under incredibly rainy conditions. A run by Omar Campos ended with a dangerous cross into the area but Leon’s goalkeeper, Oscar Garcia, would get to the ball before a Cruz Azul attacker could reach it. After getting the ball in the area, Jose Paradela got off a left footed shot that went past Garcia to score and give Cruz Azul the 1-0 lead. Nicolas Ibañez got off a left footed shot in the area that forced a good save from Garcia. The match started to suffer as Leon tried to go on offense while Cruz Azul defended and counter, but neither team did either well on the wet conditions. Diber Cambindo went on a 1 vs 1 but his shot was blocked by Cruz Azul’s goalkeeper, Andres Gudiño, who made a good save. From outside the area, Nicolas Ibañez would get off a right footed shot that was deflected past Garcia and into the net to score and give Cruz Azul the 2-0 lead. Without being overly superior, Cruz Azul was once again very efficient and had a two goal lead with their few opportunities. A great pass in the area to Jeremy Marquez was wasted when he took too long to get off a shot and the ball was cleared. A shot from outside the area by Cambindo was blocked and would eventually easily reach Gudiño because of it. Off a free kick, a cross into the area was terribly cleared by Gudiño, which would fall to Sebastian Vega, but his close range chance was blocked by defender Willer Ditta. The halftime whistle blew as Cruz Azul looked like they were in control of the match and the series. The 2nd half started with Leon subbing Fernando Beltran, Ismael Diaz and Fernando Valadez for Juan Pablo Dominguez, Jose Alvarado and Jose Ivan Rodriguez. Ibañez got the ball in the area and got off a turn around right footed shot that forced a good save from Garcia. A left footed shot from outside the area by Erik Lira was saved by Garcia. Ibañez got the ball in the area for a 1 vs 1 but as he tried to get past Garcia, he would lose the ball to the goalkeeper. A cross into the area was headed from close range by Alvarado but the ball went wide. Cruz Azul subbed out Nicolas Ibañez, Carlos Rodriguez and Jeremy Marquez for Gabriel Fernandez, Carlos Rotondi and Alan Mozo. Leon subbed out Ivan Moreno for Edgar Guerra. Almost immediately after the changes, a combination play ended with Jose Paradela getting into the area and getting off a right footed shot past Garcia to score and give Cruz Azul the 3-0 lead. It was a goal that looked to have killed the match and series. Cruz Azul subbed out Erik Lira for Andres Montaño. After getting into the area, Gabriel Fernandez got off a left footed shot that was blocked by Garcia but the ball went right to Fernandez again, whose second left footed shot went past Garcia and into the net to score and give Cruz Azul the 4-0 lead over a terrible Leon. Leon subbed out Rodrigo Echeverria for Jordi Cortizo. Cruz Azul subbed out Jesus Orozco for Ralph Orquin. Alvarado got off a left footed shot that was well saved by Gudiño. Campos got into the area but his left footed shot went wide. The whistle blew and Cruz Azul had crushed Leon and looked to have booked their ticket to the Semifinals from just this first leg match. A great performance by Cruz Azul coupled with a terrible performance from Leon allowed for the only series to looked to have been settled after the first match. Cruz Azul were the better and more importantly looked like the side to have better taken advantage of the rainy conditions. Leon came into the Liguilla as one of the weakest team and so far have been by far the weakest of all sides. It would be one of the biggest upsets, if not the biggest, for Leon to go thru to the Semifinals. Cruz Azul should not only be heavy favorites but they could also rest players as they will probably be already thinking about their Semifinal series. And who can blame them?

title: ‘Use every ounce of quality you have’ – Jarell Quansah reacts to first European goal for Bayer Leverkusen
summary: Jarell Quansah doubled Bayer Leverkusen’s tally against Dinamo Zagreb in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night to secure his team’s fourth win of the competition.Collecting the ball from a neat...
content: ‘Use every ounce of quality you have’ – Jarell Quansah reacts to first European goal for Bayer Leverkusen Jarell Quansah doubled Bayer Leverkusen’s tally against Dinamo Zagreb in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night to secure his team’s fourth win of the competition. Collecting the ball from a neat flick from Moussa Diaby, the Englishman cut inside onto his weaker left foot before placing the ball into the bottom corner. “I told Moussa to pass me the ball, to flick it around the corner and as a player with so much quality, he can see the pitch and the opportunities ahead,” Quansah told Kicker , adding: “I’m happy he’s playing with us.” Diaby did, of course, return to Leverkusen for €28m in the summer after spending time at Aston Villa and Al-Ittihad between 2023 and 2026. Quansah channels his inner striker When asked about his finishing, and whether or not he played as a striker in his youth, Quansah replied: “Sometimes I can read the game quite well and can pick-up good positions. You obviously train small-sided games so it brings out the kid in you, and if you can just manage to keep composure and put it into the goal, using every ounce of quality you have.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder
