title: Haaland 'happy' at Man City despite outburst, says Maresca
summary: Enzo Maresca insisted on Friday that Erling Haaland is "happy" at Manchester City after the striker expressed frustration over his side's recent struggles.Maresca will need Haaland back to his best against Arsenal if third-placed City are to earn a vital victory over the champions.
content: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca (L) speaks with Erling Haaland (Odd ANDERSEN) Enzo Maresca insisted on Friday that Erling Haaland is "happy" at Manchester City after the striker expressed frustration over his side's recent struggles. Haaland gave a candid assessment of City's malaise following Tuesday's 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League. After winning 10 of their first 11 matches in all competitions this season, Maresca's men have won just two of their last seven. With a crucial trip to Premier League leaders Arsenal looming on Sunday, Haaland's criticism added to the growing sense that City's season is in danger of spiralling out of control. "We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way," Haaland said. "I have no idea what we were missing but you could feel it in the last few games that something was not clicking fully." Haaland has scored just once in his last five games for City and is without a league goal in his past three matches. The Norway star's body language has been noticeably angst-ridden in recent weeks, prompting suggestions that he is growing disillusioned with life at the Etihad Stadium. City are also awaiting the result of their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, with the punishment potentially including a huge points deduction. Despite City's woes, Maresca is adamant Haaland remains committed to the cause regardless of speculation that he could seek a move at the end of the season. "Erling is a nine, they live for goals and winning games. If they don't score they are upset. I think he gesticulates in the same way when we are winning games," Maresca told reporters on Friday. "For sure he is not happy because we are not winning games. But it is not just Erling. Everyone is on the same page. "He has been good. He has been normal since day one. Two or three weeks ago, he was dancing inside the pitch and in the training sessions. "He is happy. It is normal that results affect the mood a little bit but I don't see any problem with Erling. He is a winner." Maresca will need Haaland back to his best against Arsenal if third-placed City are to earn a vital victory over the champions. Already trailing six points behind Arsenal, a defeat in north London would be a huge blow to their title hopes. Maresca has come under fire during City's slump in his first season after replacing Pep Guardiola. The former Chelsea boss claimed teething problems were inevitable during the transition from Guardiola's dynastic reign. "Transition requires time. It's probably because we won seven games in a row, everyone was thinking at City there's no transition," Maresca said. "But I've said many times I'm not a magician. There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new. "For sure, when you don't win games, it's not the ideal situation. For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all." smg/td

title: What happened when Juventus last beat Como 1907?
summary: The Men's First Team travel east to face Como 1907 on Serie A Matchday 13, with the two sides sitting very close in the table.The match kicks off at 20:45 CET on Sunday, November 29. Having beaten Ven...
content: What happened when Juventus last beat Como 1907? The Men's First Team travel east to face Como 1907 on Serie A Matchday 13, with the two sides sitting very close in the table. The match kicks off at 20:45 CET on Sunday, November 29. Having beaten Venezia 4-0 in their last match, the Bianconeri will be trying to secure another important three points. Let’s take a look at the last time Juventus beat Como 1907. A TENSE NIGHT IN COMO The last time the Bianconeri took all three points against Como 1907 was February 2025, and it came in the midst of Randal Kolo Muani's incredible goal-scoring form in his first spell at the club. It was a tough game at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, and one that was settled by a late penalty for Juve. The hosts started the game well, but the opening goal came from Kolo Muani in the 34th minute. The Frenchman picked up the ball on the right, danced around a defender as he made his way into the box and then unleashed a superb strike into the roof of the net, making it 1-0. KOLO MUANI'S LATE WINNER As the first half was drawing to a close, though, Cesc Fabregas' side got themselves back on level terms. A seemingly innocuous cross from the left found Assane Diao unmarked in the box, and he made no mistake with the header. The hosts had the better of the second half action, but Juve were awarded a penalty with just minutes to go. Jean Butez flew out to meet a cross, but made contact with Federico Gatti and a spot-kick was given. Kolo Muani stepped up with confidence and scored in the 89th minute, ensuring that Juve took all three points from their trip to Lombardia. View this post on YouTube

title: Hermoso included in Champions League Team of the Week
summary: Mario Hermoso has received further recognition. The Roma defender has been included in UEFA’s Team of the Week for Matchday 5 of the Champions League domestic season, thanks to his performance in th...
content: Hermoso included in Champions League Team of the Week Mario Hermoso has received further recognition. The Roma defender has been included in UEFA’s Team of the Week for Matchday 5 of the Champions League domestic season, thanks to his performance in the 2-2 draw against Paris Saint-Germain at the Parc des Princes. The Spaniard was selected by UEFA’s technical observers, who recognized his performances in both defense and attack. Hermoso was the star of the match against PSG, scoring the goal that temporarily led 1-0 after just five minutes. The defender also stood out for his ability to counter the Parisian attackers, dominating duels and recording 11 recovered balls. Two other Serie A players are also included in the all-time starting lineup for matchday five: Inter’s Nicolò Barella and Como’s Luis Milla.

title: Hertha heading towards its rightful place
summary: Berlin: the Olympiastadion. German football’s spiritual home, current residence of Hertha BSC.Known affectionately as Die Alte Dame and visually defined by contrasting stripes, the club has found it...
content: Hertha heading towards its rightful place Berlin: the Olympiastadion. German football’s spiritual home, current residence of Hertha BSC. Known affectionately as Die Alte Dame and visually defined by contrasting stripes, the club has found itself somewhat stuck in 2. Bundesliga since demotion from the top tier in 2023. However, winds in the capital seem to be picking up as that eastward-flying flag now sits ten points clear at the summit. For over three years, that cavernous bowl of a stadium felt less like a sporting venue. In fact, it almost began to take on the appearance of a monument to unfulfilled promise and ambition. Relegation left its usual hangover, compounded even further by the absence of a much-needed rebound. In fear of becoming second-tier regulars, the hierarchy turned to Stefan Leitl for help. Baggage has been shed since his arrival on that pressured touchline. Not without trials and tribulations, that is. Sitting in seventh and closing out last season with a humiliating 6-1 defeat prompted calls for the coach to be given his marching orders. Major news outlets even raised the question, but instead public backing and guarantees were forthcoming from within. Continuity, it would appear, has paid off. Despite losing two of his most influential players, Leitl has pieced together a currently unbeaten team boasting an impressive cushion in the standings. Losing a promising Kennet Eichhorn to Leverkusen and the established Fabian Reese to newly relegated league rivals Wolfsburg left a bitter taste in the mouth, even considering the financial windfall. Other departures followed in what one might label a mass exodus, with cost-effective additions and loanees plugging seemingly unfillable gaps. Fast-forward six months and it now appears to have been good, hard business. As is often said in life, hindsight truly is a wonderful thing. Experience came at left-back in the form of Mads Pedersen for €150,000, while Austrian youth international Oluwaseun Adewumi arrived on a temporary basis from Burnley. Another loanee, this time Farid Alfa-Ruprecht, knows the division well having spent the previous campaign with VfL Bochum. Often deployed as a late substitute, the former Manchester City academy graduate has struck once and created another despite only being on the pitch for a combined total of 137 minutes. With unfamiliar faces contributing to the cause, Josip Brekalo is the one existing squad member who has stepped up following those notable changes. Scoring five while assisting six, the Croatian midfielder now brings quality and courage to even the biggest contests. In covering 129km across 12 outings, he also combines technical quality with immense work rate in Leitl’s pragmatic system. Fresh from a four-goal thrashing of Energie Cottbus, Leitl and his charges find themselves in an enviable position. You could even forgive Reese for potentially regretting the switch from blue and white to neon green. Saturday presents another opportunity to continue this astounding progress on home soil against a struggling Karlsruhe. Only three days later, Leitl will face the toughest possible test as the DFB-Pokal takes his side to the Allianz Arena. Earning a result in Munich, of all places, would send the loudest possible signal that Hertha BSC is ready to plant itself in the Bundesliga once again.

title: Injury-prone Real Madrid defender returns to squad for Alaves clash after 208 days
summary: Real Madrid will have a familiar face back in their squad for Saturday’s La Liga encounter against Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu as Ferland Mendy is set to return.Indeed, manager Jose Mourinho con...
content: Injury-prone Real Madrid defender returns to squad for Alaves clash after 208 days Real Madrid will have a familiar face back in their squad for Saturday’s La Liga encounter against Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu as Ferland Mendy is set to return. Indeed, manager Jose Mourinho confirmed that the left-back will be a part of the squad that will take on Quique Sanchez Flores’ team tomorrow night. A return after 208 days Now, as reported by AS , Mendy’s return to the squad for Real Madrid comes after a lengthy absence that has lasted for 208 days. The 30-year-old left-back has been out of action since May earlier this year, after suffering a rupture of the rectus femoris tendon in his right leg, an injury that required him to undergo surgery. The veteran left-back had been training with the senior squad for some time, but had yet to receive the green light to return to competitive action. Back in the squad. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) That wait is now over, with Mourinho confirming that the defender will be among the substitutes against Alaves. “Mendy will be on the bench tomorrow. And if he’s on the bench, it means he can play. We have three left-backs, but it’s great news for everyone that he’s back,” he said . Future remains complicated Mendy is currently behind Marc Cucurella and Alvaro Carreras in the competition for the left-back position at Real Madrid, with Cucurella seen as the first choice. However, the Frenchman offers a different profile to the other two players, especially with his defensive prowess and the solidity he brings to the table. Behind Cucurella and Carreras in the pecking order. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) If he can maintain his fitness, Mourinho could find opportunities to use Mendy’s qualities during the remainder of the campaign. However, his future at the club remains uncertain, considering that Real Madrid have invested more than €100 million on two new left-backs over the past two summers. Mendy, meanwhile, has a contract with Los Blancos until the summer of 2028, and and has no intention of leaving before that deal expires. So, it remains to be seen how Real Madrid handle his situation in the coming months. For now, though, the veteran defender’s focus will be on getting back on the pitch and regaining his rhythm.

title: Iraola on Liverpool trio’s fitness ahead of Merseyside derby
summary: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has delivered mixed injury news ahead of Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton, with Victor Muñoz not yet ruled out.The Spain international was forced off following...
content: Iraola on Liverpool trio’s fitness ahead of Merseyside derby Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has delivered mixed injury news ahead of Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton, with Victor Muñoz not yet ruled out. The Spain international was forced off following a collision during Wednesday’s Champions League win at Club Brugge , but subsequent assessment has shown no serious damage to his knee. “With Victor, I think the good news is that after assessing him, there is no disruption in the knee, everything is fine,” Iraola said. “But he has a big knock. It’s a big knock. “He hasn’t trained today but he wants to try tomorrow. We’ll see how the bruise is. But I cannot tell you right now.” Cody Gakpo will definitely miss the trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium with the muscle injury he sustained while playing for the Netherlands against Germany. “Cody definitely not,” Iraola said. “It’s a muscle injury so we have to wait a little bit until the process goes on and it heals. “Cody, this kind of injury is normally two or three weeks. He did it in the last game against Germany, so normally it’s this timeline. “It wasn’t a big injury but there is something there and you have to give the time to heal.” Ryan Gravenberch is also unlikely to be available as he continues to struggle with pain. “It’s going to be difficult,” Iraola admitted. “I cannot say no because these kinds of injuries are difficult. “They don’t look like a big thing but you have the pain, it doesn’t go. “The important thing is when he comes back he comes with no pain so he can play as free as possible.” Stay up to date with all the latest Liverpool news by joining our Liverpool WhatsApp channel .

title: When will Italy play their next game?
summary: Italy have been knocked out of the Nations League group phase, so when is their next match?The last international games of the year were played during the November break, so Italy, like most other cou...
content: When will Italy play their next game? Italy have been knocked out of the Nations League group phase, so when is their next match? The last international games of the year were played during the November break, so Italy, like most other countries worldwide, will return to action next year, precisely in March. The Azzurri finished third in their Nations League group, seeing winners France and runners-up Belgium progress to the quarter-finals. MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Nicolo Cambiaghi of Italy is challenged by Malo Gusto and Dayot Upamecano of France during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) Despite the disappointment of the elimination, which experts at BetPanda had widely predicted , it is fair to say the Azzurri must see the glass half full. Their Nations League campaign featured victories over Turkiye and France, and only their two losses to Belgium sealed the Nazionale’s elimination. Italy, however, still managed to secure a spot among the seeded teams in the Euro 2028 qualifying draw thanks to their Nations League results. As previously mentioned, the next international break is in March 2027, running from Monday 22 to Tuesday 30. As the Azzurri won’t be playing in the Nations League quarter-finals, they’ll start their Euro 2028 qualifying campaign straight away. Italy will learn their opponents on December 6, when the qualifying draw takes place. The first match will be played on March 26, 2027 and the second on March 29. The Azzurri will likely be placed in one of the four-team qualifying groups after their elimination from the Nations League. MILAN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 12: General view inside the stadium before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) Regardless of their opponents, the Azzurri will look to start their qualification campaign strongly and bounce back after a 4-1 loss to Belgium in their most recent match. “These nights can happen in the growth process; you need to learn from these experiences. Considering the way we got here, we had the chance to qualify, but we knew it would be tough, as Belgium are a strong team,” Mancini said at full time in Belgium. “We are sad, but this night will help us going forward.” Mancini returned for a second spell as Italy’s head coach in July. He has grabbed three wins, one draw and two defeats in his first six games in charge in his second spell. The Euro 2020 winner has signed a contract until 2030, when, hopefully, he’ll bring the Nazionale back to the World Cup. MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Adrien Rabiot of France runs with the ball under pressure from Sebastiano Esposito of Italy during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) Italy already know that their captain Gianluigi Donnarumma will miss the next international match after being booked in the most recent match against Belgium. Gigio was one yellow card away from suspension prior to the game in Belgium, so he’ll miss the next one. Predictably, Manchester City will replace the star with either Guglielmo Vicario (Juventus) or Marco Carnesecchi (Atalanta). The latter has recently suffered a knee injury, forcing him to undergo surgery, and the date of his return to action remains uncertain.

title: Jamal Musiala sidelined through the end of 2026 after aggravating muscle injury
summary: Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala has suffered another injury setback just days after returning to competitive football. According to Kicker, the 23-year-old appears to have aggravated ...
content: Jamal Musiala sidelined through the end of 2026 after aggravating muscle injury Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala has suffered another injury setback just days after returning to competitive football. According to Kicker , the 23-year-old appears to have aggravated the muscle injury that previously sidelined him for nearly two months. The German international will consequently miss Saturday’s Bundesliga away fixture against Hamburger SV. Musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September. After gradually working his way back to fitness, the Bayern star finally returned to competitive action in last Friday’s 1-1 draw against Köln. He also made a brief appearance in Wednesday’s 2-1 Champions League defeat against Lille. Kicker reports that the original muscle injury has apparently flared up again, although the full extent of the latest setback and the length of Musiala’s forthcoming absence remain unclear. Fußballtransfers claims Musiala’s absence will stretch out for several more weeks. Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg is reporting that Musiala will miss 4-6 weeks. Musiala setback compounds Bayern Munich’s growing injury problems The latest development comes during an exceptionally difficult period for Musiala, who has also been dealing with a neurological condition. Kicker and Sport Bild both report that the 23-year-old experienced another absence episode on Monday, November 23, his second reported recurrence since collapsing during August’s preparation campaign. Musiala has consequently made just six competitive appearances this season, completing the full 90 minutes on only one occasion. His ongoing health difficulties have also prompted considerable discussion surrounding his future at Bayern. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge recently expressed concerns about the midfielder’s ability to regain his previous performance levels . Earlier this week, Bayern also confirmed that constructive discussions had taken place with Musiala’s representatives . The club emphasized that the player’s health remained the priority and that both parties intended to continue their dialogue confidentially. For Kompany, Musiala’s latest absence also creates another selection headache amid a mounting injury crisis in Bayern’s attacking department. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of Saturday’s encounter with Hamburg. The French international continues to recover from bruising to his left foot sustained against Köln. Harry Kane, Serge Gnabry, and Ismael Saibari remain sidelined as well, leaving Bayern seriously depleted in attack. Luis Díaz at least returned to action against Lille following his own injury layoff. GGFN | Peter Weis

title: Juventus power past early wobble to put down Omonia Nicosia
summary: The Bianconeri pushed closer to a much-needed top eight finish.
content: TURIN, ITALY - NOVEMBER 26: Jeff Ekhator of Juventus celebrates with Francisco Conceicao after scoring an goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Juventus and Omonia FC at Juventus Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Alberto Gandolfo - Juventus/Juventus FC via Getty Images) | Juventus FC via Getty Images Thanksgiving is always a weird time when it comes to watching football for us here in the States. Europe couldn’t give a flying (redacted) about American holidays, so I got two doses of my favorite football teams—one European and one American. And strangely, both of those games ended up following a somewhat similar pattern. My beloved Philadelphia Eagles came out completely flat in their Thanksgiving game against the Dallas Cowboys, but scraped back from a 21-3 deficit to pull out a last second win. (Duck Fallas) Juventus were similarly bad in the first half of their Europa League contest against Omonia Nicosia. Some shockingly awful defense on a corner kick saw the Cyprian side score on Italian soil for the very first time in their history, leaving the fans at the J Stadium again scratching their heads and readying the jeers. But Juve’s heavily rotated lineup began to work things out. Andrea Cambiaso scored a phenomenal long-range goal eight minutes ahead of the break, and Francisco Concieção’s neat assist to Jeff Ekhator saw the 20-year-old open his account for Juventus to put Juve ahead after the break. A pair of second half goals gave Juve a much more comfortable end than my Birds had, ending the game with a 4-1 victory that propelled them to second place in the League Phase table and kept them in line for a vital bye to the round of 16. Likely with an eye to Sunday’s huge game against Como, Luciano Spalletti rotated heavily and put out a somewhat experimental lineup that looked more like a 3-4-3 than anything else. Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram, Nico González, and Pierre Kalulu were all still missing due to injury. Norberto Neto started in goal for Juventus for the first time since 2017, anchoring a back three of Federico Gatti, Jhon Lucumí, and Lloyd Kelly. Cambiaso and Juan Cabal sandwiched the double pivot midfield of Pape Matar Sarr and Douglas Luiz, while Conceição and Jérémie Boga flanked Ekhator up top. Henning Berg countered with a 4-2-3-1. He was missing Fotis Kitsos and Mihlali Mayambela to injury, while four players—Carel Eiting, Moses Odubajo, David Akintola and Giorgos Viktoros—were cup-tied. Thomas Kaminski started in goal, guarded by Loïc Nego, Senou Coulibaly, Lubomír Satka, and Jean-Kévin Duverne. Mateo Maric and Panagiotis Andreou started in midfield, while Florin Tanase, Muamer Tankovic, and Jaden Montnor supported Andronikos Kakoullis in attack. Conceição worked himself into a shooting opening by paradoxically drifting backward, forcing Kaminski into an early save, but that was about as threatening as Juve looked in the early going. But they couldn’t come up with any more shots until the 15 minute mark, when Omonia lined up for a corner kick. Everything went wrong on this play. Satka and Kakoullis both ended up without a marker on the back post, and the former had an easy header after Neto flapped at the air as he tried to go for a punch, stunning the J Stadium into silence. Things were still off as play resumed. It toosk almost 10 minutes for Juve to muster their first semblance of a response in the form of a blocked Conceição shot, and seconds later Cabal let fly from distance and forced Kaminski to parry the ball back into the middle and hope no one in a black Juve shirt was there. But it was Omonia who were still providing more danger as the clock ticked into the latter stages of the half. That’s when Cambiaso turned back the clock a little bit. He took a simple pass from Conceição, cut inside a few steps, and let loose a rocket from 25 yards out that wouldn’t have been saved by anyone. That finally lit a fire under the squad, and Juve were on top six minutes later thanks to their new young striker. Andreou made a mistake in midfield and was robbed by Boga. Ekhator and Gatti swiftly pushed the ball to Conceição. Ekhator made a beautiful run between the center backs, Conceição hit him in stride, and the 20-year-old nutmegged Kaminski with a first-time shot to put Juve ahead. The Portuguese winger almost helped make it 3-1 before the break with a good run and lay-back to a marauding Gatti, but Kaminski made a good kick-save to deny him. Cambiaso nearly made it two wonder-strikes seconds into the second half, but Kaminski got a hand to it and Duverne got a block on the rebound by Conceição. Not long after, Boga drilled a ball just wide making clear that the two-goal outburst at the end of the half had put the momentum firmly into Juve’s lap. At one point Omonia had a 20-minute gap between shot attempts—and right after that Concieção put the game on ice. After receiving a pass from Weston McKennie he fired on target. Kaminski denied his first attempt with another kick-save, but the rebound came right back to the diminutive attacker, who made no mistake to put the ball into an open goal on his second try. Five minutes later Boga put things beyond all doubt, taking a pass from Cambiaso, giving a little bit of ground to open his shooting lane, then cracking the ball into the top corner. He hit it so hard Kaminski barely had time to move. Neto had to make one save in garbage time, but the Cyprian side wasn’t going to be pulling any miracles on this night, and Juve headed into the weekend with the momentum of an eight-goal week behind them as they get set for Sunday’s crunch match at Como.

title: Lionel Messi embracing MLS supervillain role with Inter Miami CF
summary: Lionel Messi has drawn criticism for his behavior in Game 1 of a playoff series against the Columbus Crew, his supervillain persona is great theater.
content: It's been three years since Lionel Messi arrived in Miami, and he's done nothing but fortify himself as an MLS supervillain since. More: MLS may review Lionel Messi's actions against Columbus Crew's Gonzalo Tapia Beloved by many, backlash to the Argentinian's superstar has also grown, especially on social media. Since his arrival, Inter Miami CF has become the MLS equivalent to the NFL's Dallas Cowboys and baseball's New York Yankees, which casts Messi in the role of antihero or antagonist. Take your pick. Still brilliant at age 39, Messi is also petulant, brutish, brattish, arrogant and entitled. He's a virtuoso and diva, and now he's heading to ScottsMiracle-Gro Field on Nov. 27 for Game 2 against the Crew in a first-round playoff series Columbus leads 1-0. After avoiding a red card for smashing a ball off Gonzalo Tapia's face in the Crew's 3-0 blowout win to open the best-of-three series, Messi's superpowers will be tested in the face of elimination. Usually, that's trouble for those on the receiving end, but the Crew are no strangers to Messi's magic, as well as his "dark arts," as Crew captain Sean Zawadzki describes them. For every deft touch, there's a dive or foul. For every no-look pass, there's an incredulous grievance. If all sport is a stage, Messi is close to a one-man show. Lionel Messi vs Columbus Crew is great theater The Crew and Inter Miami have played three times this season, twice in the regular season and the opener of the playoffs, and Messi played in each game. All three produced must-see moments. Messi was featured in most. He scored a gorgeous tying goal Sept. 27 in Columbus and pumped his first at Crew fans. Before curving his free kick over a wall of defenders and into the goal, just over goalkeeper Patrick Schulte's outstretched hand, Messi pointed to his right eye while gesturing to a fan/heckler seated within earshot at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field. View this post on Instagram The message was clear: "Watch what I'm about to do here, OK?" After curving the ball perfectly off his left foot and into the goal, placed into the top left corner from far out on the right wing, Messi smiled before giving a pronounced fist pump in the same direction he'd called his shot. Many in the sold-out stadium cheered, and not all were Messi fans. It was fantastic theatre, Messi playing the role of polarizing antihero. In that same game, during a confrontation with Crew star Santiago Rodriguez, Messi angrily stomped on Rodriguez's foot. Fast forward to Nov. 21 in Miami, late in the first half of Game 1 at Nu Stadium. Columbus led 1-0 in added time when Messi's attempt to dribble past Tapia was stopped by the Crew forward's left foot. The ball rolled out of bounds with Tapia in pursuit, after a bump from Messi, and a moment later the ball is in the Miami superstar's hands. Tapia lingered in front of him, so Messi took the ball and bopped him on the nose with it before firing hard throw-in attempt straight into the Crew forward's grill. Stunned, Tapia grabbed his face and dropped to the grass in a gold-and-black heap. Gonzalo Tapia catches the wrong end of Lionel Messi’s throw-in (via @MLS ) pic.twitter.com/qj9Xpwo3xu — FOX Soccer (@FOXSoccer) November 22, 2026 Messi, meanwhile, put his right hand in the air while gesturing wildly that referee Allen Chapman missed call because Tapia had raised his left hand prior to the beaning. In the background, lying on the ground, a sports photographer laughed. Behind him, a fan who recorded it on his cellphone did the same. Others in the crowd, seated nearby, made faces covering a range of emotions. Eventually, Chapman showed yellow cards to both Messi and Tapia, which set off a wave of reaction on social media. Messi loyalists blamed Tapia for lingering too long in the king's airspace, while Messi's detractors cried foul about him escaping a red card. Soccer journalists and Crew interim coach Laurent Courtois agreed with the detractors, saying Messi's actions warranted ejection. Chapman disagreed, telling a pool reporter after the game that Messi's throw-in/beaning was done with "negligible" force and "did not reach the level of violent conduct." The MLS Disciplinary Committee could take a closer look to see if additional punishment (fine or suspension) is necessary, but anything more than a fine would be shocking before Game 2 of the series. Messi, the antihero/supervillain, will almost certainly lead the way for a Miami team facing possible elimination. What could possibly happen next? Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Lionel Messi embracing MLS supervillain role with Inter Miami CF

title: Liverpool plot ambitious summer window with Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala and Monza sensation Gustavo Varela on radar
summary: Liverpool are reportedly plotting an ambitious summer transfer window with Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala and Monza striker Gustavo Varela firmly on their radar. While the Reds are prepared to explore a costly move for the Germany international if he proves his fitness, they are also well-placed to pursue Serie A's breakout forward.
content: FC Bayern München v 1. FC Köln - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Liverpool are reportedly plotting an ambitious summer transfer window with Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala and Monza striker Gustavo Varela firmly on their radar. While the Reds are prepared to explore a costly move for the Germany international if he proves his fitness, they are also well-placed to pursue Serie A's breakout forward. Liverpool eye ambitious summer deals According to Football Insider , Liverpool are ready to explore a summer deal for Musiala alongside their interest in Monza sensation Varela . Reports in Germany suggest the 23-year-old Bayern midfielder has a release clause active next summer, putting long-term admirers on alert. However, sources warn it would be a "very expensive" move, meaning the Reds first need him to prove his fitness. Bayern worried about Musiala's future Musiala has endured a difficult campaign after developing a neurological condition that has occasionally caused seizures during matches. Despite featuring heavily for Germany at the World Cup in the summer, he has managed just one Bundesliga start so far this term as Bayern work to help him get to the bottom of the issue. The report states that the Bundesliga giants are "worried" about Musiala's future and remain sceptical over whether he can return to his best. Occupying a "huge contract" in Munich, the club are concerned about paying lofty wages to a player who is rarely available, sparking a controversial debate in German football that Liverpool are monitoring closely. Monza striker catches Reds' attention Alongside their pursuit of Musiala, Liverpool have also received encouragement in their hunt for attacking reinforcements in Italy. The outlet revealed that the Premier League side are well-placed to "tempt" 21-year-old Monza striker Varela into a switch to Anfield next summer. Varela has emerged as a surprise package in Serie A during the 2026-27 campaign, netting an impressive 11 goals in his opening 11 league appearances. With Liverpool already tracking his rapid progress closely, sources indicate that Monza are likely to entertain a sale at the end of the season, though the Italian club will not let their star man leave cheaply. Fitness and form will decide The coming months will prove decisive for both targets as Liverpool shape their summer recruitment plans. Bayern believe that ongoing health problems for Musiala would deter top clubs, leaving the Reds waiting for clear signs of improvement before committing to a bid. Meanwhile, Monza are prepared to drive up Varela's valuation if his prolific scoring run in Serie A continues.

title: Liverpool star expected to leave the club in 2027
summary: Federico Chiesa Transfer Latest as Liverpool Weigh January DecisionFederico Chiesa’s Liverpool future is moving back into focus ahead of the January transfer window, with fresh reporting from Daily ...
content: Liverpool star expected to leave the club in 2027 Federico Chiesa Transfer Latest as Liverpool Weigh January Decision Federico Chiesa’s Liverpool future is moving back into focus ahead of the January transfer window, with fresh reporting from Daily Mail suggesting an exit is again a realistic possibility. The Italy international has found minutes difficult to come by and that has shaped the conversation around his next step. Chiesa is now 29 and, after an encouraging reputation built in Serie A, his time at Anfield has yet to develop into anything close to a settled role. Injuries have disrupted him, selection opportunities have been limited, and life under Andoni Iraola has so far offered little sign of a breakthrough. His omission from Liverpool’s Champions League league-phase squad felt particularly significant. Decisions like that tend to sharpen thinking for all parties, especially when a player is already operating on the fringes and trying to rebuild momentum. This season he has made only one appearance in all competitions, which underlines how far down the pecking order he currently is. Photo: IMAGO January Transfer Window Set to Shape Chiesa Future There is still a degree of caution around any prediction because Chiesa has been close to leaving before without a move being completed. Even so, the direction of travel appears fairly clear. Liverpool will need to assess whether a permanent sale, a loan, or simply keeping him until the summer offers the cleanest solution. Contractually, there is no immediate pressure. Chiesa is tied to Liverpool until June 2028, which gives the club control and should help protect value. That could influence the structure of any deal, particularly if interested clubs in Italy push for favourable loan terms rather than a full transfer. Serie A Return Looks Logical for Liverpool Forward A return to Serie A feels the most natural outcome if movement comes. Regular football in familiar surroundings may appeal to the player, and Italian clubs would likely view him as a market opportunity if the financial package can be made workable. There is also mention of a lower-half Premier League loan or interest from Saudi Arabia, both of which would present very different sporting and financial calculations. For now, Liverpool’s stance will be key. Chiesa has made 51 appearances and scored five goals since arriving in 2024, but January may offer the clearest chance yet to reset a situation that has never fully taken off. Our View It feels like one of those transfers that made sense on paper but never really found rhythm. Chiesa has obvious talent, and there have been moments when it looked like he might still carve out something useful at Liverpool, but everything around him has felt stop-start from the beginning. The biggest issue now is clarity. If Iraola does not see him as part of the core group, there is little value in dragging this on until the summer and hoping circumstances suddenly change. A clean January solution would probably suit everyone. Liverpool can free up space in the squad and wages, and Chiesa can go somewhere he actually plays. A move back to Italy would be easy to understand. It feels like the best football fit and probably the best chance for him to enjoy the game again. A loan would not be a surprise if that is what it takes to get something done, especially with his contract length giving Liverpool a bit of cover. There is no real sense of drama here, just a player whose path at Anfield has stalled. Sometimes the right move is simply the obvious one. Source: Daily Mail

title: Malagò insists Italy players pushed for Mancini’s return
summary: Giovanni Malagò says Italy’s players were behind his decision to bring Roberto Mancini back as coach, and believes the Azzurri can rebuild around their young talent.According to La Gazzetta dello S...
content: Malagò insists Italy players pushed for Mancini’s return Giovanni Malagò says Italy’s players were behind his decision to bring Roberto Mancini back as coach, and believes the Azzurri can rebuild around their young talent. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the FIGC commissioner and presidential candidate was speaking at a debate organised by La Stampa at the MAUTO museum in Turin. Malagò took charge of Italian football after the national team failed to reach a third consecutive World Cup, beaten by Bosnia and Herzegovina in March. He then turned to Mancini, who had won Euro 2020 in his first spell in charge. “A federation president has to listen to everyone, but then the moment comes when it’s my face on the line,” Malagò said. “There’s an unwritten rule that if you don’t go to the World Cup, you go home. If we go out against Bosnia, it means we’re not exactly phenomenal. “There aren’t years to plan and programme. I chose Mancini because I know his ideas about young players, and I speak with the national team players, who tell me: ‘Mancini all the way.’” CORTINA D’AMPEZZO, ITALY – MARCH 05: Giovanni Malago, President of the Organising Committee for the 2026 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, speaks during the Paralympic Games Opening Press Conference ahead of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Paralympic Games at on March 05, 2026 in Cortina d’Ampezzo, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) Malagò backs Mancini’s youth project at Italy Italy’s Nations League campaign ended in disappointment. Despite beating France 3-1, the Azzurri lost 4-1 in Belgium and failed to progress. Malagò still sees reasons for optimism. “We have to rebuild around young players. We had a great Nations League group. We lost to Belgium, but there’s light at the end of the tunnel,” he said. “The senior team is only the peak of the movement, and Italy’s Under-21 side is very strong. We haven’t been to the Olympics with the Under-21s since 2008, and we’ve already laid all the right foundations to go back.” CORTINA D’AMPEZZO, ITALY – MARCH 5: Giovanni Malago, President of the Organising Committee for the 2026 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, speaks during the mural inauguration ahead of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Paralympic Games at the Cortina Paralympic Village on March 05, 2026 in Cortina d’Ampezzo, Italy. (Photo by Linnea Rheborg/Getty Images for IPC) The FIGC presidential election takes place in just over two weeks, with Malagò facing former Milan executive Adriano Galliani.

title: Man United handed unexpected route to finally land Jarrad Branthwaite in 2027
summary: A defensive rebuild is at the top of Manchester United’s agenda come 2027.United’s defensive frailties have been their major undoing this season. Wednesday’s draw with Sporting CP was a case in ...
content: Man United handed unexpected route to finally land Jarrad Branthwaite in 2027 A defensive rebuild is at the top of Manchester United’s agenda come 2027. United’s defensive frailties have been their major undoing this season. Wednesday’s draw with Sporting CP was a case in point, as defensive mistakes denied them the win. While Mauricio Pochettino will look to improve the Red Devils’ defensive play through his coaching, he could also use better defensive options. Meanwhile, INEOS are already looking at reinforcements, and The Athletic have now reported a clear opportunity to sign long-term defensive target Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite . Branthwaite: a dream Manchester United defensive target Back in 2024, the Red Devils were keen on adding the Everton star to their ranks, but the Toffees stood firm and knocked back two United bids. Seeing that the Merseyside outfit did not want to do business, INEOS therefore opted to pursue alternatives, signing Matthijs de Ligt from Bayern Munich. Two years on, however, United still hold an interest in Branthwaite, whose stock has continued to rise over the past two seasons. INEOS would jump at the chance to sign him and have him spearhead their defensive rebuild, and an opportunity seems to have presented itself to land the Everton star. Branthwaite has an exit clause The Athletic are reporting: “Manchester United are still keen on Jarrad Branthwaite, sources say, and people with knowledge of the situation say his contract does contain a timed exit clause at a significant fee, but it is not active in January. It can only be activated in summer but expires at a certain date. “If a club does make an approach, Everton are believed to want the terms met in full and up front, whereas United, in any deal, are likely to try to agree payments in instalments.” Ultimately, then, if United want Branthwaite and wish to avoid back-and-forth negotiations or a bidding war, they would be best advised to find out when his exit clause becomes active. While at it, they should also be ready to break the bank for him and make him their marquee 2027 signing, the face of their defensive rebuild. J. Branthwaite 2026/27 The Peoples Person Reliability Assessment Overall credibility: 8/10 Why? ✅ Update from a reliable transfer source TPP view We believe that if Branthwaite has an exit clause, United will definitely be keen to activate it as they look to pull off a defensive rebuild in 2027.

title: Man United trigger one-year extension to Bruno Fernandes' contract
summary: MANCHESTER, England (AP) — Manchester United has triggered an option to extend midfielder Bruno Fernandes' contract by 12 months, a person with knowledge of the deal told The Associated Press. The person spoke on the condition of anonymity because United has not publicly announced the extension.
content: MANCHESTER, England (AP) — Manchester United has triggered an option to extend midfielder Bruno Fernandes' contract by 12 months, a person with knowledge of the deal told The Associated Press. The person spoke on the condition of anonymity because United has not publicly announced the extension. Fernandes' deal was due to expire at the end of the season and the Portugal international said this week that talks were on hold. But United has ensured it is not in danger of losing its captain as a free agent next summer by triggering the option. The person said the option protected United from interested clubs being able to approach Fernandes in the new year and that negotiations would begin again in the future. Fernandes signed a three-year deal in 2024, which included the option of a further 12 months. Fernandes, meanwhile, raised doubts about his availability to play against Brentford after missing training Friday. United coach Mauricio Pochettino said the midfielder, who scored twice in a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, was absent from training because of illness. “He’s affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session,” Pochettino said. "We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we’ll see. We’re not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don’t feel (you can). “We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing.” Pochettino takes charge of his first home game as United coach on Saturday with his team second from last in the Premier League. Brentford coach Keith Andrews said he could already see the impact the Argentine was having after just two games. “You can see traits of what he is as a manager, but you have to balance that with where they are currently," Andrews said. "You can start to see the shift in terms of what he wants for sure, but we want to play our game. We will expect a very good and organised United side. “It’s Old Trafford, it’s Manchester United, it’s Mauricio Pochettino. He’s an incredibly impressive manager with what he’s achieved. So we have to expect Manchester United to be at their absolute best." ___ James Robson is at https://x.com/jamesalanrobson ___ See AP’s full soccer coverage here

title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
summary: Manchester United activate an option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract, extending it until 2028.
content: Bruno Fernandes joined Manchester United in 2020 [Getty Images] Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract. The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028. It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January. The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved. content: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has insisted he sees no behavioural problems with Erling Haaland ahead of this weekend's Premier League trip to Arsenal. Haaland, 26, has faced scrutiny over his recent performances, with City winning only one of their last six matches inside 90 minutes across all competitions. The striker spoke after Tuesday's 2-2 Champions League draw with Napoli, telling TNT Sports that the Blues were conceding too easily and that "you start questioning everything" when results do not go your way. Erling is upset, like I'm upset because we're not winning games: Maresca Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Maresca was asked about Haaland's mood in the wake of questions being raised over the Norway international's attitude as a member of Manchester City 's captaincy group. "Erling is a winner player. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games but not just Erling, it's everyone," Maresca said in defence of his number nine. Haaland also told TNT Sports that the squad has so much quality, and that the players need to regroup, stay positive and bring more energy onto the pitch ahead of what he called the most difficult game of the season in north London. The City manager added on Haaland: "But don't forget that two weeks or three weeks ago, he was dancing inside the pitch." Haaland scored the 78th minute winner in the 3-2 UEFA Champions League victory at RB Leipzig earlier this month, with Elliot Anderson setting up the decisive goal in Germany late in the second-half. "So, again, you can write or think many different things, but the reality is sometimes much more easy: Erling is upset, like I'm upset because we're not winning games," Maresca said. The Norway international has scored nine Premier League goals this season but has not found the net in his last four league appearances, with a goal against Fulham ruled out by VAR last weekend. Manchester City won their first seven Premier League games under Maresca, before defeats to Aston Villa , Brighton and Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest were followed by a 1-1 draw with Fulham. The Italian added: "And when we were winning games everyone was happy. But this is our job, this is football, that's why we need to maintain the balance. Don't forget that, again, we just started. This is not a sprint, it's a marathon." Maresca took charge in June as the successor to Pep Guardiola, with sporting director Hugo Viana overseeing a major rebuild that brought in Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi among others. On the title race, Maresca said: "The present is important, yes, we can be three points [behind] on Sunday, we can be six if we draw, we can be nine - yes, it's all a reality. But for us, we're building something. It's for the future." City sit six points behind leaders Arsenal heading into the weekend, with the leaders having won each of the last two Premier League titles. I don't see any problems at all with Erling, says Maresca Asked how Haaland has been away from the pitch, Maresca said: "He has been good, he has been normal like he has been since day one." Haaland told TV 2 Sport during the international break that he is incredibly happy at Manchester City , having signed a contract in January 2025 that runs until 2034. The striker joined from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022 and scored a record 36 Premier League goals in his debut season, as City won the treble under Guardiola. The City boss added: "Again, three weeks ago I think he was dancing inside the pitch, dancing in training sessions - he's happy!" He also saw a penalty appeal waved away against Napoli after being held as he attempted a header, as Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki twice brought City level at the Etihad Stadium. Maresca said: "It's normal that results affect a little bit the mood, that's why we need to win games. But I don't see any problems at all with Erling." Manchester City have taken ten points from five Champions League league-phase matches, with their only defeat a 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in October, while Antoine Semenyo is also expected back from his knee injury soon after Maresca issued an update on the Ghanian on Friday afternoon.

title: Manchester United reach Bruno Fernandes contract decision with talks on hold
summary: Manchester United have come to a decision regarding team captain Bruno Fernandes' contract, with the Portugal star's deal originally due to end in the summer of 2027
content: Manchester United have triggered a one-year extension in Bruno Fernandes' contract -Credit:Richard Sellers/Allstar, Getty Images Manchester United have activated the option to extend Bruno Fernandes' contract by one year. Fernandes had been set to become a free agent at the end of the season, but United held the option to prolong his deal by 12 months, which they have now triggered. The United captain has rejected two new contract proposals from the club, but both parties are now reportedly in agreement on resuming negotiations down the line, with an emphasis on improving United's current standing. Wrexham's unofficial 'One of Our Own' is paying back Phil Parkinson's faith perfectly Bruno Fernandes misses Manchester United training as Mauricio Pochettino provides update -Credit:Gualter Fatia - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images Club officials believe activating their one-year option makes sense given that European clubs could approach him regarding a pre-contract agreement in January. Addressing his future last week, Fernandes stated that his priority was helping United climb the Premier League table, according to the Manchester Evening News . "For us to start winning games, and then we can start speaking about contract. That's not important now, it's irrelevant," he said of potentially signing a new deal. "Obviously I know it's my future and I shouldn't probably look into that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that. I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "We're going to have time to speak about that. As I said, we had conversations. The conversations stopped in the moment that we thought that was not as important at the moment because results and performances have not been at the level we should be. So we're going to have time to think about that." Fernandes shattered the Premier League assist record last season and claimed the Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year award for an unprecedented fifth time, yet his performances have declined during this campaign. The Portugal international was also relegated to the bench against AFC Bournemouth last month following his public criticism of Michael Carrick's tactical approach after United's heavy defeat to Como in the UEFA Champions League. He was reinstated to the lineup by Carrick for the subsequent fixture and has featured in the starting eleven for both of Mauricio Pochettino's matches at the helm so far.

title: Manchester United set sights on a 2027 move for Argentine international amid Real Madrid return links
summary: The future of Nico Paz is going to become one of the hottest topics at the end of the season, with several teams expected to try to sign the Argentine international.After all, Paz has set the Serie A ...
content: Manchester United set sights on a 2027 move for Argentine international amid Real Madrid return links The future of Nico Paz is going to become one of the hottest topics at the end of the season, with several teams expected to try to sign the Argentine international. After all, Paz has set the Serie A on fire with his performances at Como. He has racked up six goals and eight assists in all competitions this term, impressing even in the UEFA Champions League. Paz’s future is a hot topic at Real Madrid as well, since Los Blancos have a buyback clause worth only €80 million. Manchester United eye move for Paz According to The Athletic , Manchester United have set their sights on a 2027 move for Nico Paz as they look to find a long-term replacement for Bruno Fernandes. Paz is the next big star in Argentine football. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The Portuguese international’s contract at Old Trafford expires at the end of the season, and the club anticipate the veteran playmaker to leave on a free transfer. Fernandes’ exit could accentuate the need for a new playmaker, and Paz fits the bill perfectly, having already made a statement against Man United in the Champions League this season by starring in a 4-1 victory for Como. Man United will make a move for Paz in the summer of 2027, but they will have to negotiate with Como. That is where Real Madrid, with their buyback clause, become important to the story. Will Paz return to Real Madrid? Paz wants a guaranteed starting role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) From a financial perspective, it makes every sense for Real Madrid to activate the €80 million buyback clause and re-sign Paz, who has shown potential to be a player worth way more than that. However, the report adds that Paz is not too keen on returning to the Bernabeu unless Real Madrid can assure him a guaranteed place in the starting eleven. Unfortunately, given the current squad build at Real Madrid, finding a place for Paz becomes impossible, especially given the way Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler have performed this season. Keeping that in mind, it will be interesting to see how this Paz transfer saga transpires come the summer of 2027.

title: Manchester United Trigger Option to Keep Bruno Fernandes Until 2028
summary: Manchester United have activated the one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, extending his stay at Old Trafford until the summer of 2028. The move, confirmed by club sources on Friday, comes at a moment of acute vulnerability for the club and a deliberate pause in longer-term talks. Fernandes’ previous deal was set to expire…
content: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Round of 16 - Portugal v Spain - Dallas Stadium, Arlington, Texas, U.S. - July 6, 2026 Portugal's Bruno Fernandes IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Maria Lysaker Manchester United have activated the one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, extending his stay at Old Trafford until the summer of 2028. The move, confirmed by club sources on Friday, comes at a moment of acute vulnerability for the club and a deliberate pause in longer-term talks. Fernandes’ previous deal was set to expire next summer. Without the option being exercised, overseas clubs would have been free to open pre-contract negotiations with him from January 1. By triggering the clause, United have protected the asset , preserved the possibility of a transfer fee, and removed an immediate external distraction. Sources indicate both sides view the step as mutually sensible while the team’s results remain the clear priority. The 32-year-old has already turned down two formal offers for a new long-term contract . In an interview with Sky Sports earlier this month, he was explicit: the club has shown it wants him to stay, but “because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side… The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.” He has also stressed he will not run down a deal if United decide his future lies elsewhere. That context is stark. United sit 19th in the Premier League after 11 matches (one win, five draws, five defeats), their worst start to a top-flight season in decades. New head coach Mauricio Pochettino is still searching for his first league win. Fernandes himself has been a pale imitation of the player who broke the Premier League assists record and swept the individual awards last season while United finished third. He has nonetheless contributed goals and assists this campaign, including a brace in Wednesday’s chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon. Complicating matters further, Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday’s home match against Brentford. He missed Friday’s training session with a virus contracted in Portugal and is being assessed carefully. Pochettino said the club will take no risks. Since his £47 million arrival from Sporting in January 2020, Fernandes has made 343 appearances and scored 115 goals for United. The one-year extension buys both parties time. It does not resolve the longer-term question. Talks on a fresh deal remain on hold until results improve, and a summer exit in 2027 cannot yet be ruled out. For now, United have simply ensured their captain cannot walk away for free while the rebuild continues.

title: Marco Rose hails 'relentless' Bournemouth after 10-man Cherries make European history against Celta Vigo
summary: Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose could not hide his admiration for his players after witnesssing a truly historic European night at the Vitality Stadium. Despite falling a goal behind and being reduced to ten men, the Cherries produced a stunning turnaround to defeat Celta Vigo 2-1 and cement their growing reputation on the continent.
content: FBL-EUR-C3-CELTA VIGO-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose could not hide his admiration for his players after witnesssing a truly historic European night at the Vitality Stadium. Despite falling a goal behind and being reduced to ten men, the Cherries produced a stunning turnaround to defeat Celta Vigo 2-1 and cement their growing reputation on the continent. Cherries roar back to sink Celta Bournemouth’s incredible transformation under Rose reached new heights on Thursday as the Premier League side secured their tenth consecutive victory in all competitions. Facing a difficult trip to Celta in the Europa League league phase, the Cherries appeared to be heading toward a frustrating evening after Bafode Diaktie was sent off during the first half. With a goal deficit to overcome and a player short, the odds were stacked heavily against the visitors. However, a spirited second-half performance saw Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan find the net to turn the game on its head. The manager was quick to credit the psychological fortitude of his players, who refused to accept defeat despite the circumstances. "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy,” the German manager said following the final whistle. “I’m really proud after being one player less, 1-0 down,” he told BBC Radio Solent . Tactical flexibility and individual brilliance The comeback was not just a product of willpower but also significant tactical adjustments that Rose implemented to balance the side after the red card. One of the standout performers in this regard was David Brooks, who was asked to fill a defensive void that few expected him to master. The versatility shown by the Welsh international allowed the Cherries to maintain their shape while still posing a threat on the counter-attack during the second period. Rose admitted that the victory was less about rigid systems and more about the players' ability to step up in difficult moments. "I said to Ty (Tyler Adams), sometimes it’s not about tactics and formations and stuff like this," Rose explained. "Brooksy did a great job when we got one player less, he played just right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment, everyone did his job on a really high level." Momentum shifts and belief The turning point arrived shortly after the interval when Bournemouth found their equalizer, a goal that completely altered the psychological dynamic of the match. With the scores level, the English side seemed to find a second wind, pressing Celta high up the pitch despite their numerical disadvantage. Rose highlighted that the early goal in the second half was the catalyst for the relentless pressure that eventually led to the winner. "We created the momentum after the half-time with the first goal and we were just relentless," the former RB Leipzig boss added. The manager noted that the squad’s conviction was the deciding factor: "We never stopped to believe in this win and that’s why big, big, big congratulations to the team." No rest for relentless Cherries There is little time for Rose and his squad to bask in their European heroics, as Bournemouth return to Premier League action on Sunday with a trip to Craven Cottage to face Fulham. Carrying the momentum of a 10-match winning streak, the Cherries will be eager to keep their domestic surge rolling. Attention will then turn back to the continent on Thursday, December 10, when Bournemouth host Viktoria Plzen in their next Europa League fixture. Another victory on home soil would put Rose’s side on the brink of locking down a coveted top-eight finish and automatic qualification for the knockout rounds.

title: Micky van de Ven: Man United retain interest in Tottenham Hotspur defender
summary: It is clear as daylight that Manchester United are in urgent need of defensive reinforcements. The Red Devils conceded 58 goals in the Premier League in the 2023/24 season, prompting INEOS to invest h...
content: Micky van de Ven: Man United retain interest in Tottenham Hotspur defender It is clear as daylight that Manchester United are in urgent need of defensive reinforcements. The Red Devils conceded 58 goals in the Premier League in the 2023/24 season, prompting INEOS to invest heavily in the backline. In came Matthijs de Ligt , Noussair Mazraoui and Leny Yoro in the summer of 2024, while Ayden Heaven joined the squad six months later. The English giants ended the season in 15th place, conceding 54 times in the league. Senne Lammens was signed to upgrade the goalkeeping department last summer. United went on to secure third place in the league, thanks to a resurgent run under Michael Carrick, but conceded 50 times in the league. This season, the Red Devils have already let in 23 goals in 11 Premier League games, managing just one win, and now sit 19th in the table. Mauricio Pochettino has replaced Carrick in the dugout as the English giants look to immediately climb up the table. However, the backline remains a concern for the Argentine as well, given that the team has conceded six goals in the two games since his arrival. United need a new defender in January United already have three senior centre-backs in their squad – Harry Maguire , Lisandro Martinez and De Ligt – but none of them inspire much confidence. Maguire and Martinez are out of contract next summer, while De Ligt has struggled with fitness issues. Heaven, meanwhile, had a positive start to his Old Trafford spell, but has looked off colour this season. Yoro has shown promise but has lacked consistency and perhaps could do better with an experienced head alongside him. This is where targeting a Premier League-proven central defender in January makes sense. United were linked with Micky van de Ven in recent times but a previous report suggests that the Dutchman has no desire to leave Tottenham Hotspur in January . However, that has not deterred the Red Devils, as the latest update outlines. Harry Maguire v Micky van de Ven: 2026/27 Stats Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 United retain Van de Ven interest According to journalist Dean Jones, Van de Ven remains on United’s wish list ahead of the January transfer window. In his column for Flashscore , Jones wrote: “(Nathan) Collins is not the only name under consideration. United retain a long-standing interest in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, as well as Tottenham’s Micky van de Ven and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey.” “United have doubts about the longer-term futures of several existing defensive options, particularly Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt. It is not expected that all three will leave, but there is a possibility that one could depart in January and another during the summer as the club looks to reshape their options.” “Defence was an area United had already intended to address in the summer, but the possibility of bringing plans forward has not been ruled out. If the right opportunities emerge, they would be prepared to consider strengthening earlier than originally intended.” The report, however, confirms that Pochettino “will have an important say in how the recruitment process develops, with the club keen to ensure any additions fit his requirements.” Van de Ven’s recovery pace, strength in tackles and Premier League experience make him a lucrative target for the Red Devils. However, prising the Dutchman away in mid-season may be next to impossible, given that the player signed a new deal in the summer that keeps him in north London until 2031. Why? ✅ Van de Ven matches the profile wanted by United ⚠️ The Dutchman is under a long-term contract at Tottenham Hotspur. TPP view We believe that while Van de Ven is likely to be on United’s wish list at the moment, convincing Tottenham to let him go could be very tough.

title: Mikel Arteta tight-lipped over whether David Raya will be fit for Man City clash
summary: Raya escaped a serious shoulder injury against Newcastle and could make a return for Arsenal’s mammoth clash with Man City
content: Mikel Arteta opted against giving a definitive answer over whether David Raya will be fit for Arsenal ’s mammoth clash with Manchester City this weekend - but indicated there was hope of the No 1’s return. Raya hurt his shoulder in a seemingly innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park last weekend, but the Spaniard escaped serious injury with Arteta confirming earlier in the week that he would not require surgery. Having initially feared the Spaniard would have been “out for months”, Raya has already returned to training and is in the picture for a return to the starting line-up. He nevertheless was not fit for the Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund in midweek and Arteta could not confirm if Sunday’s visit of City would come too soon for the 31-year-old. Questioned on his involvement, Arteta replied: “I don't know... we have a few more hours. We're trying to get everybody back.” Arteta was then asked if there was a “ray of hope” if Raya might play, to which he said: “Yeah.” Raya was instrumental in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season has carried his stellar form into the current campaign, boasting seven clean sheets in 10 matches prior to Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised for the injured David Raya against Borussia Dortmund (Getty) He was deputised by Kepa Arrizabalaga for the Dortmund clash and Arteta backed his goalkeeping understudy as a more than adequate alternative. “The experience that Kepa has is incredible, and for the teams he's been involved, the trophies that he's won,” he added.

title: At MorumBIS, São Paulo beat Remo in the Brasileirão
summary: On Thursday (26), São Paulo beat Remo 3–1 at MorumBIS in Matchweek 37 of the Brazilian Championship. Calleri (2) and Ryan scored for the Tricolor, while Gabriel Poveda pulled one back for the visit...
content: At MorumBIS, São Paulo beat Remo in the Brasileirão On Thursday (26), São Paulo beat Remo 3–1 at MorumBIS in Matchweek 37 of the Brazilian Championship. Calleri (2) and Ryan scored for the Tricolor, while Gabriel Poveda pulled one back for the visitors. With his two goals on the night, Calleri took his tally to 18 for the season, making him São Paulo's leading scorer this year. Meanwhile, academy graduate Ryan scored his fourth goal for the first team. The match began evenly, with both teams battling for possession and trying to find space. In the 19th minute, the defense only partially cleared a corner. Pedro Lima won the loose ball and fired a shot, forcing a good save from the goalkeeper. In the 38th minute, the Tricolor opened the scoring. Calleri picked up a loose ball, drove into the penalty area and slotted it into the back of the net. Eight minutes into the second half, Lucas threatened with a free kick, but his effort flew too high. In the ninth minute, Remo equalized through Gabriel Poveda. With chances few and far between, Dorival Júnior made changes, and the substitutions paid off. In the 41st minute, Bobadilla sent the ball into the box, the defense cleared it, and it fell to Ryan, who fired home to put São Paulo back in front. In the 49th minute, Bobadilla found Calleri, who chipped the goalkeeper to seal the 3–1 win. The Tricolor's next match is against Athletico Paranaense on Wednesday (02) at 9:30 p.m. at the Arena da Baixada in Curitiba, Paraná, in Matchweek 38 of the Brasileirão.
