title: Mourinho: “If a player is on the bench and doesn’t like it, that’s their problem, not mine”
summary: He spoke before the game against Alavés
content: Jose Mourinho, head coach of Real Madrid, speaks during a press conference ahead of the LaLiga EA Sports match against RC Celta de Vigo at Ciudad Real Madrid in Valdebebas, Spain, on November 20, 2025. (Photo by Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Real Madrid coach José Mourinho spoke to the media at Valdebebas on Friday morning ahead of a league encounter with Alavés on Saturday night, and played down any discontent with rotations, saying: “that’s their problem, not mine. Mbappé, Bellingham, and Vinicius, they’re all on the same level. If one day they end up on the bench and don’t like it, that’s their problem, not mine. The team has a collective goal that takes precedence over individual ones, and even they are capable of understanding that. Everything else is secondary. When you talk about Mbappé and Jude, you look at their playing time, they’ve played a lot, and I understand the question, but the fact that both have so many minutes isn’t a status symbol; it’s because of their performance, which is unmatched. That’s what makes the difference. We’ve felt the impact of playing without Jude, and we’ll also feel it when we play without Mbappé. We have Courtois, who makes an incredible difference, that’s why he plays every game except when he’s sick. And the player who stepped in for Courtois was also decisive. That’s the strength of this roster. There isn’t a single player I don’t like or don’t want here. I don’t want anyone on the transfer market, I’m saying this now, with two months to go before the transfer frenzy. Nor do I want anyone to leave, the door is closed. I don’t want any transfer activity; don’t report on transfer news because I don’t want it.” Mourinho on Alavés “Two days between games isn’t enough; three is good. We won’t have any trouble getting the players who played in the last game back in shape. I really like Quique Sánchez Flores’ work at Alavés; he did something important last year, and this year as well, with a very clear identity. Another tough game awaits us. Our goal is to win; we’ve already reached 15 points in the Champions League. We have to play and try to get the three points.” Mourinho on Dean Huijsen “Defending well means helping the team be better on offense. If you’re solid at the back, you can press higher up the field, and your defenders win their one-on-one battles… This is defensive work, but it has an impact on our offense. At Roma, he was just a kid and still had a long way to go, but England and its challenges helped him improve in many ways. My perspective from the outside, as someone who’s been there for a young player I care deeply about, is that last season wasn’t a good one for him. But he knows me, and I’ve helped him accelerate his growth. He’s young in age, but he’s much more mature. Rüdiger is an important teammate for him, he was last season, and he is this season as well. And Konaté, too. He’s growing a lot; he’s handled the frustration of not going to the World Cup well and took it in a positive light. But let’s not shower him with too much praise, that can end up doing him more harm than good. Still, I’m his coach, so I try not to be too lenient with him.” Mourinho on Bellingham and Zidane comparisons “I don’t like to compare players from different generations. Zidane was one of the best of his generation. Bellingham is already one of the best of his generation.” Mourinho on Vinícius Júnior “I have a hard time responding to some of these comments. If we’re looking for the ideal starting eleven, as far as I’m concerned, it doesn’t exist. Last week Vini had to be benched; then he was said to be incompatible with Diomande; now he shouldn’t be benched, now they both have to play together; now Arda is surplus to requirements; then Arda’s fans say he has to play… Things don’t work that way. Vini has improved, which is only natural. The hardest part is having the team love you, no matter how you play. And that was the foundation for Vini when he was getting torn apart by you guys and the fans. His character was shaped by his teammates; he loves his teammates and Madrid dearly. He wants to help, and he’s already at the level where he can make a difference. Whether he plays now is another story.” Mourinho on Vinícius and Diomande “They’re not competition; we’re all on the same side here, and we all have the same goal. It’s something we’ve worked very hard to achieve. You’re almost tempted to create this kind of competition. If they score, it’s a goal for Real Madrid, and nobody in the locker room cares who scores it.” Mourinho on the locker room “You always find some grumbling, but so far I haven’t had any problems with the team. We’ve been together for five months now, and I haven’t had any issues. It might happen, but if it does, the team will handle it on its own. I don’t even think it’ll reach me. I can see that they all share a common goal. The collective goal will overcome any grumbling.” Mourinho on whether Real Madrid can win the Champions League “I want to beat Alavés. I really like Quique; I have a lot of respect for him. It’s way too early to talk about the Champions League, we don’t know how we’ll all fare in the knockout rounds. I don’t want to have to go through the playoff round; we have so many games… Then there’s the Super Cup, in principle, two games, and the Copa del Rey, too. We’re close; with three or four points, we’ve got it. The Champions League comes down to the little things. Look at Bayern, who lost Kane; look at PSG… You can make it to the decisive matches without key players. Some people say we’re contenders, and then there’s that AI supercomputer… which is total crap.” Mourinho on injury updates “Mendy will be on the bench tomorrow. And if he’s on the bench, that means he can play. We have three left backs, but his return is great news for everyone. Trent is out because he’s sick. And Rodrygo is in pretty good form, but he’s sick too. And we want to keep sick players off the field. But Rodrygo is working really hard; he’s changed his mindset. He seemed to me like a guy who was still coming to terms with his injury. But now he’s working hard, I don’t see him playing against Arsenal or in La Liga before the end of the year. But he has incredible talent and will be another member of an incredible squad full of extraordinary players.” Mourinho on Spanish elections “We don’t have any Spanish players… So they can’t go vote or serve as poll workers.” Mourinho on starting games better “It’s my responsibility. But we’ve already started some games well, against Santander, Valencia, Sevilla, Málaga… We’ve wrapped up some of them within the first half-hour. In others, we started well but then let it slip and almost lost points, like in Elche. It’s a process, this idea of starting well, playing well, and finishing well, it’s a process. It feels like we’ve been here three years, but it’s only been five months, we’re lacking that consistency. I asked a couple of players to get a better understanding of things, and they gave me a funny answer: ‘Coach, if we always start off well, you’ll get bored on the bench. We give you a rush.’”

title: Muñoz Appears to Have Avoided Injury
summary: Per a report from Javier Mancebo Santos of MARCA, Liverpool FC’s Victor Muñoz appears to have avoided serious injury, and the issue that forced him off the pitch against Brugge is just a heavy knock. title: Music to Man United’s ears as Nico Paz’s stance on Old Trafford switch is confirmed
summary: Nico Paz, Como attacking midfielder, stance on a potential transfer to Manchester United has come to light, as interest in the midfielder mounts.United interestPaz has emerged as one of the best attac...
content: Music to Man United’s ears as Nico Paz’s stance on Old Trafford switch is confirmed Nico Paz, Como attacking midfielder, stance on a potential transfer to Manchester United has come to light, as interest in the midfielder mounts. United interest Paz has emerged as one of the best attacking midfielders in Europe this season, amid his electric performances for Como both in Serie A and the Champions League. He has notched three goals and as many assists in 11 top-flight appearances this term. He boasts eight contributions in Europe, the joint-most alongside Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappé. United have been named as admirers of Paz alongside Chelsea, Arsenal, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Inter Milan. Madrid are also said to be keen on a reunion, although it recently emerged that Los Blancos have little appetite in triggering his €80m buy-back clause. Paz provided United with a first-hand demonstration of his capabilities, dismantling the Red Devils at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. He scored two goals as United suffered a 4-0 defeat. Como · 2026/27 Page 1 of 2 1 2 David Ornstein of The Athletic has provided an update on Paz, and it will come as good news to United. Paz latest According to Ornstein, Paz has been identified by United as a potential replacement for Bruno Fernandes . The Portuguese playmaker’s terms expire at the end of the campaign and an agreement has yet to be struck. Fernandes has already rejected two offers from the club. United retain the option of extending his stay by an additional 12 months. Ornstein reports: “Sources privy to the matter, talking anonymously to protect relationships, suggest Paz does not currently favour rejoining Madrid. This stance might alter if he is assured of a prominent role — that has not been the case.” “Madrid declining to activate the clause would let Como sell Paz as normal, but no one has pushed as strongly as Tottenham Hotspur did in 2025, partly because of the circumstances surrounding his buy-back.” “Although it may not be his first-choice destination, and Champions League qualification is a major factor, sources confirm United’s project and enduring appeal are attractive to Paz — while sharing the same representatives as head coach Mauricio Pochettino may prove beneficial.” Ornstein notes that United also have alternative targets if Paz proves unattainable. title: ‘I nearly had a heart attack!’ - Thomas Frank celebrates first Crystal Palace win after dramatic Europa League comeback against Real Sociedad
summary: Thomas Frank has tasted his first victory as Crystal Palace manager, but the Danish coach admitted the frantic closing stages of their 2-1 win over Real Sociedad left him fearing for his health. The Eagles came from behind at Selhurst Park to secure a vital Europa League result that could act as a catalyst for their season.
content: FBL-EUR-C3-CRYSTAL PALACE-REAL SOCIEDAD - AFP Thomas Frank has tasted his first victory as Crystal Palace manager, but the Danish coach admitted the frantic closing stages of their 2-1 win over Real Sociedad left him fearing for his health. The Eagles came from behind at Selhurst Park to secure a vital Europa League result that could act as a catalyst for their season. Late goals and red card spark Selhurst Park turnaround Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr fired Real Sociedad ahead in the 66th minute of Frank's first home match, only for Jon Martin's second yellow card six minutes later to hand Palace a numerical advantage. Jean-Philippe Mateta converted from the penalty spot before Dwight McNeil poked home from fellow substitute Jorgen Strand Larsen's overhead kick. Unai Marrero saved Yeremy Pino's spot-kick, leaving goalkeeper Dean Henderson to make the last of his six stops against Orri Oskarsson late on. Frank hails brave attacking gamble after nervy finish Reflecting on bouncing back from Saturday's debut defeat to Coventry, Frank praised his squad's response to falling behind . “I think first and foremost to get it over the line, and [it was] an extremely important win for various reasons,” he said. “One, of course, confidence, and it relates to belief against an extremely good team. I think the first half we were compact and very disciplined in many ways. We missed the high-pressure situations we had, and I think we struggled to keep the ball well enough. “Second half I felt we were much better in the high pressure, and I felt we kept the ball much better. I actually felt we got a bit more momentum in the second half but then, out of the blue, they scored the 1-0 goal. But what I really like is the belief from the players, what they showed, and that we are threatening on set-pieces, we cannot underestimate that.” Frank also credited his bold substitutions once Real Sociedad went down to 10 men. “We know in football one moment can change the game,” he continued. “The penalty and the red card changed the game, then we still needed to score. To win still is important and we went brave, we went with the offensive substitutions and kept two strikers on the pitch, and that paid off. And then I think we were all close to getting a heart attack in the last five minutes.” European play-off boost offers hope amid relegation fight While Premier League survival remains the priority for the bottom-placed Eagles, Thursday's victory lifted them into the Europa League play-off spots, four places outside the top eight after five games. “I think we want to aim high,” the former Tottenham boss replied when asked about his continental ambitions. “We are ambitious for this tournament, and that’s why the win was so important.” Frank also agreed the comeback could prove a major turning point for his squad's morale. “That’s why it’s so important to keep doing the right things, keep believing, and keep going,” he said. Crucial Premier League test against Hull awaits Palace immediately switch focus back to domestic survival for Sunday's critical Premier League clash with Hull. Sitting bottom of the table after losing to Coventry, Frank's side must carry their second-half pressing, set-piece threat and newfound belief into the weekend to kickstart their climb to safety.

title: Nick Woltemade agent quizzed on transfer claim ‘These reports are completely untrue’
summary: Nick Woltemade continues to make headlines. The German international striker had a rollercoaster first season at Newcastle United, starting off in great form and then a bit like the team overall, found things more difficult as the 2025-26 campaign progressed and a 58 game season was far too much for a small squad to deal with.
content: Nick Woltemade Juventus v Omonia Nicosia Nick Woltemade continues to make headlines. The German international striker had a rollercoaster first season at Newcastle United, starting off in great form and then a bit like the team overall, found things more difficult as the 2025-26 campaign progressed and a 58 game season was far too much for a small squad to deal with. A lot of nonsense written and spoken about Nick Woltemade with ridiculous claims he had been a total flop, despite having 14 direct goal involvements including scoring 11. The decision was made for Nick Woltemade to spend the 2026-27 season with Juventus, Matthias Jaissle wanting to have pace as his main focus up front. The hope being that a year of regular football in Italy will help Nick Woltemade improve his skill set, become better at holding the ball up, polish his goalscoring technique and so on. Helping him then to come back and be a bigger asset for the Newcastle United team, or command a significant transfer fee boosted by his time with Juventus. Big Nick has had mixed fortunes with Juventus, not getting the amount of game time he would like (seven starts in all competitions, sub appearances) but doing very decently in the time he has spent on the pitch (five goals and three assists so far. Last weekend with Juventus drawing 0-0 at home and booed off at half-time, Nick Woltemade was introduced for the second half and within 14 minutes had turned the game around, scoring one and then getting an assist. Juventus finally winning 4-0 at the end against Venezia and the United loan star picking up the MOTM award. It was bench duties again last night, Nick Woltemade coming on in the second half with Juventus leading 3-1 against Omonia Nicosia in the second half and the Newcastle United loan striker helping his side to an eventual 4-1 victory. A lot of daft transfer claims floating about and now the United striker’s agent has shot down one of the daftest. Al-Maidan contacted Danny Bachmann, Nick Woltemade’s agent, to ask about media claims of Newcastle United doing a January 2027 swap deal, with 30-year-old Ivan Toney (reported to be on £20million a year/£400k a week, plus Toney has a court date to face in London after having been arrested and charged with an alleged serious assault in a nightclub) to come to United from Al Ahli and 24-year-old Nick Woltemade to join the Saudi club. Danny Bachmann dismissing this speculation as laughable nonsense: “These reports are completely untrue.” The player’s agent making clear what the obvious reality is: “The player’s future will be decided at the end of the season when he returns to Newcastle United . We don’t know yet whether he will stay or leave.”

title: Nico Paz Doesn’t Want to Go Back to Real Madrid!
summary: Nico Paz Currently Favors Staying Away From Real Madrid as Manchester United Circles Como’s rising Argentine star Nico Paz does not currently prefer a return to Real Madrid, according to a fresh update from The Athletic’s David Ornstein. Despite Madrid holding an exclusive €80 million buy-back option for next summer, the 22-year-old is prioritizing continued…
content: Oct 10, 2025; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Argentina midfielder Nico Paz (18) reacts against Venezuela during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Nico Paz Currently Favors Staying Away From Real Madrid as Manchester United Circles Como’s rising Argentine star Nico Paz does not currently prefer a return to Real Madrid, according to a fresh update from The Athletic’s David Ornstein. Despite Madrid holding an exclusive €80 million buy-back option for next summer, the 22-year-old is prioritizing continued development and a starring role over a move back to the Bernabéu for now. Ornstein reported Friday that sources close to the situation say Paz “does not currently favor rejoining Madrid.” That stance could shift if Real Madrid guaranteed him a prominent, regular role—but no such assurances have been offered. In the meantime, interest is building elsewhere. Manchester United have Paz on a shortlist of options should Bruno Fernandes leave Old Trafford. While United is not viewed as his preferred destination and Champions League qualification will be a major factor, the club’s project holds appeal. The shared representation with manager Mauricio Pochettino could also smooth any potential talks. The situation is a continuation of the path Paz chose last summer. Real Madrid were keen to bring the academy product back and even activated their low buy-back clause, but Paz made clear he wanted another season of consistent minutes under Cesc Fàbregas at Como rather than fight for playing time behind players such as Jude Bellingham, Arda Güler, and Bernardo Silva. Como paid roughly €60 million to make the move permanent, while Madrid retained the higher €80 million option for 2027. Paz later confirmed the choice after Como’s Champions League debut: “I thought this was where I would grow the most. I believe I made the right decision and I’m glad I did.” His form has justified the decision. Across 16 appearances this season, he has six goals and eight assists. The highlight was a Player of the Match masterclass against Manchester United in the Champions League, where he scored twice and assisted in Como’s 4-1 win. UEFA technical observer Roberto Martínez described the performance as “star material,” comparing the way Paz carried the team to Maradona-like influence. José Mourinho has been careful not to comment extensively, recently telling reporters, “This is not my player,” when asked about Paz. Madrid retain control through the buy-back, but the player’s preference currently points elsewhere—or at least toward remaining in Italy, where he is a central figure in a side that has already shown it can compete on the European stage.

title: OneFootball x Everything Everything: Newcastle are in for another tricky season
summary: As part of OneFootball's collaboration series with Shoot Music we're interviewing an artist about their love of football.This week it's Newcastle fan Michael Spearman, drummer of Ivor Novello and Mer...
content: OneFootball x Everything Everything: Newcastle are in for another tricky season As part of OneFootball's collaboration series with Shoot Music we're interviewing an artist about their love of football. This week it's Newcastle fan Michael Spearman, drummer of Ivor Novello and Mercury Prize nominated quartet Everything Everything. When did you start supporting Newcastle and why? I was around the age of five, a couple of years prior to Kevin Keegan becoming our manager. We lived about 20 miles from Newcastle and they were the only team to support in that area. It was a perfect storm of time and place for me since that era for NUFC in the 1990s was so exciting - there was a buzz around the city for years. What is your favourite childhood memory of supporting Newcastle? A lot of it is connected to my Grandpa who, although he was originally from Belfast, settled in Northumberland with the rest of my family and immediately loved NUFC. He was a goalie in his youth to a high standard (had trials for Spurs) and we used to play football a lot, taking turns in goal. I had my Pavel Srníček top and we went to the training ground where I got to meet Pavel and some of the other players and got photos and signatures. When possible I went to games with Grandpa as he had a season ticket and sometimes his mates around him couldn’t make it so I’d be allowed to go. I remember feeling quite overwhelmed at that age, but mainly hugely excited by the whole thing. The little memories like Grandpa giving local lads 50p to ‘look after’ his car, when he parked it at his favourite spot which was just a bit of wasteland in a rough part of town are as indelible to me just as much as the thrill of the matches. In 1992, after a letter sent by my Nana, I got to be a ballboy on Boxing Day for our match against Wolves and it was incredible to be rolling the ball to the players whose signatures I’d collected. I’m not sure I did a good job but it was amazing to actually be involved in a game, especially as we won 2-1. What would you consider a successful season for Newcastle this time around? It’s another tricky season for us, especially with so many of our best players leaving last season. I do feel though that we can be at our best as underdogs and I’m cautiously optimistic we can not only stay up but maybe finish at least mid table or even in a European place with some luck. It does feel on a knife edge at the moment though - we’ll need to get a lot more organised in defence and have a lot more threat going forward. I think we’re going to have to spend quite big in January but can’t afford to make more badly judged, rushed signings this time. What have been your thoughts on Matthias Jaissle's start as Newcastle boss? Do you think he's the right man? I think it still remains to be seen. I like his energy and attitude but my concern is whether the players are really playing for him and how much respect he’s getting as a young, unproven manager in the Premier League. It’s such an unforgiving league and he’s definitely got talent but it comes down to how quickly he can galvanise the team. I like the idea that he’s an underdog manager and could head up an underdog team and we battle hard but the dynamic and team spirit needs to be right for that to happen. I’m hopeful but not convinced yet. Which of your summer signings has impressed the most so far this season and which one needs to do more come 2027? We did a lot better last summer than the previous summer. Lukáš Horníček, Nico González, Amar Dedić, Aladji Bamba are all great signings with a lot more potential in future once the team gels better. I’m particularly excited about Sean Steur who, at 18-years-old, already looks to be a mature and clever footballer. We needed an injection of youth and we got that last summer but we need to find our best starting 11 quick. 'Poison Pop' by Everything Everything is out now. Their eighth studio album of the same name is set for release on March 12th 2027. You can follow the band on Instagram here: @e_e_

title: Pachuca defeat Chivas in the Oussama Idrissi match to take Quarterfinal series lead
summary: Pachuca got a 2-1 victory over Chivas and now only needs a tie in the 2nd leg to go thru to the Semifinals.
content: PACHUCA, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 26: Oussama Idrissi of Pachuca celebrates after scoring his team's second goal during the Liga MX Torneo Apertura 2026 quarterfinals first leg match between Pachuca and Chivas at Hidalgo Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Pachuca, Mexico. (Photo by Oscar Fuentes/Jam Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pachuca bounced back from an early goal to get an injury time winner and defeat Chivas by a 2-1 score. It was a wild and physical game in which Pachuca took advantage from a great game by Oussama Idrissi but that ended up marred in controversy at the end. Chivas will now have to win at home to go thru although their better record means that a win by any score will have thru to the semifinals. The return leg will take place Sunday. The 1st half started with both squads going out with their best. Alan Bautista got the ball in the area but his right footed shot went wide. Off a counter, Richard Ledezma got off a good cross that Eduardo Bauermann would slide to and deflect past Pachua’s goalkeeper, Carlos Moreno, to score an own goal and give Chivas the 1-0 lead. Chivas lost the ball to Salomon Rondon but Chivas’ goalkeeper, Raul Rangel, was able to get to the ball off his feet. Rodolfo Pizarro got off a right footed shot that went wide. Rondon got off a shot inside the area that was easily saved by Rangel. The match started to get chippy as both side started to commit harder and harder fouls. Off a corner kick the cross into the area was misjudged by Rangel and went off Daniel Aguirre into the net but after going to VAR, the referee judged the play was a foul and called off the goal. After a harsh foul by Oussama Idrissi, there was a scuffle that ended with Yellow cards to Moreno and Omar Govea. The halftime whistle blew and the match remained with a goal advantage in a game that had become extremely physical. The 2nd half started with neither team making a change during the break. Off a counter, Bryan Alonso Gonzalez got into the area but his left footed shot went wide. On a counter, Oussama Idrissi would make a run and from outside the area, he would get off a fantastic lobbed shot over Rangel and into the net to score a marvelous goal and tie the match at 1-1. It was a fantastic play and now Pachuca was back into the match. Of another counter, the ball would end up reaching Aguirre, who got off a left footed shot that went straight to Moreno. Chivas subbed out Efrain Alvarez, Santiago Sandoval and Richard Ledezma for Ricardo Marin, Angel Sepulveda and Brian Gutierrez. Pachuca subbed out Alan Bautista for Kenedy. A cross into the area was badly handled by Rangel and it bounced off Aguirre’s arm but no foul was called. After making a good move in the area, Idrissi got off a right footed shot that forced a great save from Rangel. Chivas subbed out Omar Govea for Miguel Gomez. After getting the ball in the area, Rondon got off a fantastic shot that forced a wonderful save from Rangel. Pachuca subbed out Francisco Venegas and Nicolas Vallejo for Mauricio Isaias and Sebastian Santos. Trying to clear the ball, Rangel instead sent it straight to Kenedy but his lobbed shot would be easily stopped by Rangel. Alonso Gonzalez got into the area but his left footed shot was saved by Moreno. Chivas subbed out Roberto Alvarado for Kevin Castañeda. A cross into the area was headed by Rondon but Rangel saved it. Pachuca subbed out Rodolfo Pizarro and Jorge Berlanga for Cristobal Hernandez and Pedro Budib. From outside the area, Oussama Idrissi would get off a fantastic right footed shot that went past Rangel to score and give Pachuca the 2-1 lead. It was another wonderful goal by Idrissi, who had completely changed the game. In a controversial move, Oussama Idrissi would make a controversial remark to the Chivas bench and Referee Fernando Hernandez would give him a second Yellow card and leave Pachuca with 10 players. Worse yet, it meant that Idrissi will miss the second leg. The whistle blew and the match ended with Pachuca taking a one goal lead to Guadalajara for the 2nd leg. Pachuca struck first in the Quarterfinal series with an important 2-1 lead. It was the Idrissi match as he would go from hero to villain, first by scoring the two wonderful goals that gave Pachuca the victory but also getting red carded at the end of the second one. It was a controversial decision as Referee Hernandez looked to have been “chasing” him but more controversial because of the fact that he failed to sanction anyone from Chivas’ bench, who were having the discussion with the Pachuca attacker. If he has to miss the return leg, it will be a huge miss for Pachuca but if they get to rescind the suspension, it could be the difference maker especially since Pachuca will have the ability to counter against a Chivas side that should go all out. Thus although Chivas doesn’t like the fact they are trailing, they should still be favored to go thru. It will be an interesting performance on Sunday as the leaders try to get the victory they need or it will be a truly disappointing finish to their Apertura 2026.

title: Would Paz Be A Good Successor To Fernandes For Manchester United?
summary: Nico Paz has been mentioned as a potential target for Manchester United as it considers Bruno Fernandes' future.
content: STADIO GIUSEPPE SINIGAGLIA, COMO, ITALY - 2026/11/24: Nico Paz of Como 1907 looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 league phase football match between Como 1907 and AEK Athens FC. Como 1907 won 1-0 over AEK Athens FC. (Photo by Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images) LightRocket via Getty Images Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s only world class player for a number of years. As the Old Trafford club has struggled to compete at the top of English and European soccer, the Portuguese midfielder has been a reliable performer. United hasn’t had enough of them. As things stand, though, Fernandes will be out of contract at the end of the season. The 32-year-old is believed to be the highest-paid player at Manchester United and the club has a big decision to make. Would signing Fernandes to a new contract be a good idea when United could use that money in other ways? LISBON, PORTUGAL - NOVEMBER 25: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United during the UEFA Champions League match between Sporting CP v Manchester United at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on November 25, 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. (Photo by Miguel Lemos/Soccrates/Getty Images) Getty Images The Athletic reports Manchester United is monitoring Nico Paz as a potential replacement for Fernandes. The Argentine is widely considered one of the brightest young attacking midfielders in the game at this moment in time and so it’s no surprise that United is watching his development. Paz has 10 goal contributions in his last 10 appearances for Como. The 22-year-old scored twice and registered an assist in a recent Champions League win over Manchester United with Paz the beating heart of a Como team that is making a profound impact in Europe and Serie A this season. Real Madrid reportedly has a buy-back clause on Paz who belonged to the Spanish club until recently. There is no suggestion, however, that the 22-year-old will return to the Santiago Bernabeu. Jose Mourinho already has Jude Bellingham as one of the best number 10s in the world. COMO, ITALY - OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como scores a goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Image Photo Agency/Getty Images) Getty Images Manchester United won’t be Paz’s only option and it’s debatable whether Old Trafford would be the best place for him to continue his development. Many young players have gone there in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson age and regretted it. Paz might be wise to look elsewhere for his next destination in the game. Alternatively, Manchester United could use the money it would save from not renewing Fernandes’ contract to strengthen other areas of its squad. Mauricio Pochettino’s team is desperately weak in defence and so United could spend big to add a dominant centre back rather than another attacking midfielder. Pochettino demonstrated how he is reshaping Manchester United in his own image in the Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Mistakes cost United in Lisbon, but its overall performance was positive and Fernandes was a big part of that, scoring twice in a 2-2 draw. How the Portuguese midfielder is replaced is becoming a bigger question. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Poole's 100-game Pompey adventure
summary: BBC Radio Solent's Andrew Moon on Regan Poole's 100 games at Portsmouth.
content: [Shutterstock] [BBC] In the summer of 2023 free agent Regan Poole turned down a higher salary elsewhere in League One to sign for Portsmouth. He did so believing the move to the south coast presented him with the best opportunity of reaching the Championship and furthering his career. Exactly 100 appearances later, he's been proved correct. Just like Poole's entire career trajectory, his time at Portsmouth has had plenty of ups and downs. After an excellent start and an international debut for Wales, he tore his anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during an FA Cup defeat at Chesterfield. When he returned, Pompey were struggling to adjust to life in the Championship and the transition wasn't straightforward for Poole. Not helped by having to play many games in quick succession following a serious injury. Poole and Pompey improved and maintained their Championship status. Portsmouth spent, by their standards, significant fees on centre-backs Hayden Matthews and Josh Knight. Neither have looked like dislodging Poole. Even this season Poole struggled at the start, affected by injury and then below Benji Arthur and Conor Shaughnessy in the pecking order. He's fought his way back into the side and now looks every inch the Championship centre-back he was hoping to become. Portsmouth fans always appreciate committed players. Fratton Park is a ground where big tackles get a louder cheers than great pieces of skills. Poole puts his body on the line the way the home fans crave to see. He wears his heart on his sleeve, celebrating great tackles and blocks. He's absolutely buzzing after wins and often has a face of thunder after defeats (although he will front up to the media). Likely in a similar way to fans leaving the ground. Supporters also love to go on a journey with a player. Poole has grown and improved with the team in the nearly three and half years he's been here. His journey through football has been fascinating , making his Newport County debut at just 16 before moving to Manchester United and then fighting his way back up through the EFL. He's now going into the final year of his contract and has made it clear he would love to sign a new one . The club retain an option year in his deal so it seems very unlikely he'll be departing anytime soon. I highly doubt John Mousinho and Richard Hughes mentioned the Premier League when trying to sell the club to Poole. It would still require something miraculous for Pompey to reach the top flight imminently. But the fact I'm even mentioning it highlights what an adventure the first 100 Pompey matches have been for Regan Poole. title: Premier League Giants Target Dortmund French Wonderkid
summary: Arsenal tracking Joane Gadou as Borussia Dortmund set £67m benchmarkRecruitment at the highest level often begins long before a transfer window opens. It starts in glances, in notes, in repeat viewin...
content: Premier League Giants Target Dortmund French Wonderkid Arsenal tracking Joane Gadou as Borussia Dortmund set £67m benchmark Recruitment at the highest level often begins long before a transfer window opens. It starts in glances, in notes, in repeat viewings of a player who seems to bend the usual timetable of development. Joane Gadou belongs in that category, a 19-year-old Borussia Dortmund defender whose early progress has already prompted sustained interest from Arsenal. According to BILD , Arsenal are among a cluster of elite clubs monitoring the French centre-back, alongside Liverpool, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain. That list tells its own story. It suggests a player who has moved beyond promise and into the more serious territory of strategic planning. Photo: IMAGO Joane Gadou’s rise at Borussia Dortmund Dortmund, as ever, appear to have identified value before the market fully caught up. Gadou arrived from Red Bull Salzburg last summer for around €19.5m and has since become a regular in Niko Kovac’s back three, lining up with Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton. For a teenager to earn that role at a club with Dortmund’s demands is significant in itself. His profile explains the fascination. At 6ft 5in, Gadou brings the scale modern clubs seek in central defence, though size alone no longer defines the position. What elevates him is the blend of recovery speed, calm distribution and the confidence to stride out with the ball. Arsenal saw much of that in the recent 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium, where he defended with authority and then supplied Maximilian Beier’s equaliser after driving forward from deep. Arsenal transfer interest and squad planning Arsenal’s interest reportedly stretches back months, which feels logical rather than reactive. Mikel Arteta already has an enviable range of central defenders, from William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes to Ezri Konsa, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie, with further versatility elsewhere in the squad. Gadou, then, would represent not emergency need but long-range squad design. That is why the asking price matters. Dortmund are said to value him at no less than €80m, or £67m, and with a contract running until 2031 and no release clause, they have little reason to soften. This is how the market now treats rare defensive prospects, especially those who combine physical command with technical assurance. Market logic behind £67m valuation There is a premium attached to youth, another to scarcity, and a further one to certainty of projection. Gadou seems to carry all three. He has already scored against Arsenal in the Emirates Cup, has settled swiftly in Germany after his PSG and Salzburg education, and appears the sort of defender clubs imagine anchoring the next six or seven years. For Arsenal, that does not make a deal inevitable. It makes it intelligible. The most ambitious sides recruit before the need becomes obvious. Gadou, at £67m, may prove expensive now, but that fee reflects a market belief that waiting could cost even more. Our View This is the sort of report that immediately makes sense. Arsenal have reached the point where recruitment is no longer about patching holes. It is about staying ahead, protecting standards and ensuring the next great player is in the building before everyone else realises quite how good he is. Gadou sounds exactly like that kind of target. Young, physically dominant, comfortable in space, assured on the ball, already trusted in a serious side, those are all markers of a defender with a huge ceiling. It also helps that Arsenal have become a place where top-level defenders improve. Any elite young centre-back can look at what has been built under Mikel Arteta and see a pathway towards becoming world class. There is no urgency because the squad is already stacked with quality, and that is what makes the link so encouraging. It suggests smart planning rather than panic buying. If the club decide to move, it will be because they believe Gadou can become one of the best in Europe, not because they are scrambling for numbers. £67m is a massive fee for a teenager, of course, but the market for exceptional defenders has changed. If Arsenal truly think he is special, acting early is often cheaper than arriving late. Watching a young centre-back with that blend of size, pace and technical quality develop at the Emirates would be hugely exciting. Even if nothing happens immediately, this feels like exactly the calibre of player Arsenal should be tracking.

title: 'Priceless' Duran proves 'the man' but is he papering over cracks at Celtic?
summary: Camilo Duran's 15-goal haul this season has made him an invaluable player for a Celtic side fighting for European progression.
content: "Duran is priceless for us at the moment". It would be difficult for a football manager to muster up a higher compliment for one of his players - given he should know exactly how much he did cost - but Celtic boss Martin O'Neill was rightly effusive in his praise for Camilo Duran. With 15 goals in 23 appearances, six assists, and another late European winner on Thursday, the Colombian was once again the main man for a struggling Celtic side. His double against Besiktas breathed life into their Europa League campaign last time out, and his late leap to nod in the winner against Torreense kept it alive. Duran, 24, started on the bench but was brought on with just over half an hour to go as O'Neill watched his side labour against a team currently 13th in the Portuguese second tier. Celtic would still be searching for their first European win were it not for their summer arrival from Qarabag, whose goals have played a key part in keeping his team within touching distance of a play-off spot with three fixtures to play. "He's taken on this mantle of being the man and he's been fantastic," said O'Neill, who started Duran on the bench. "We tried a similar approach against Besiktas. "Sometimes by the time Duran gets subbed on, you could be behind. But I think that's the sign of a brilliant player, he'll do something. "He's not a big guy but he's just a super footballer, a super, super footballer." Papering over cracks or quality in depth? Duran's summer arrival was overshadowed when, just over a fortnight later, a club-record fee was paid to Bodo Glimt for another striker, Kasper Hogh. While recent weeks have been dominated by debates over Duran or Hogh , the debate now seems settled, with the Colombian operating on a different level from his striking counterpart. Anyone watching Celtic in Portugal would have watched Hogh find space a handful of times in the area, but repeatedly fail to find a team-mate or trouble the goalkeeper. Duran didn't need to be asked twice. "I don't know how many touches he got, but he had the telling touch," James McFadden said on Sportsound post-match. Duran's goals have also proved decisive in securing domestic points against Falkirk and Hibernian, and with Celtic just a point clear of Rangers, he is indeed invaluable. Despite his late header giving the thousands of travelling Celtic fans a thrilling end to a relatively turgid game, the intervention is another significant moment in a season that is threatening to unravel if individual performances fail to continue papering over glaring deficiencies across the park. If the lively Jota - who lasted 74 minutes - was not creating chances, tormenting full-backs or digging out enticing crosses in the first half, Celtic seemed without any real plan of attack. Yang and Luke McCowan's involvements were limited at best, Hogh's chance to stake a claim was sub-par to be kind, and there was no driving force from the middle of the park to show some impetus. Arithmetically, Celtic can still finish in any position in the Europa League table. But if they are to claim a playoff or automatic qualification spot, they will need Duran to remain in such a rich vein of form. Duran spares Celtic's blushes against Portuguese second-tier side Torreense Celtic news, views and analysis all in one place What are the fans saying? Brian: Embarrassed by that performance, I know that there no easy games in Europe, couldn't pass the ball, not fit enough, no style of play and poorly coached. The club is in decline. John: Celtic are just an average side these days - there should be no expectation. Ted: That was just embarrassing. The 31st team in Portugal made us look ordinary. Go now Martin with dignity intact and preserve your achievements. Thus mob will drag you down. Allan: Outclassed and out paced by Torreense, Celtic played poorly with a lot of comedy of errors in their play. But Yippee hee, Celtic. Won with a late goal from Duran. Liam: This can't go on any further now, regardless of the result. MON is done and the coaching staff are done. Booing substitutions is the end, never mind a performance like this against second division opposition. The board can resign too. Alec: Total embarrassment. Barring Jota, there was a complete lack of creativity, quality, urgency and belief. Time for the board to make the right decisions, get a new manager in and get rid of at least 10 of those players on show tonight.

title: PSG is now a serious contenders to Arsenal for La Liga star
summary: Nico Williams remains one of the most highly regarded wingers in world football, and Arsenal continue to be linked with a move for the Spaniard as they look to strengthen their squad further. The Gunn...
content: PSG is now a serious contenders to Arsenal for La Liga star Nico Williams remains one of the most highly regarded wingers in world football, and Arsenal continue to be linked with a move for the Spaniard as they look to strengthen their squad further. The Gunners already have one of the strongest teams in Europe, but they are not prepared to become complacent and continue to monitor opportunities to improve their options. Williams remains on their radar as a potential addition who could bring further quality to their attack. His situation at Athletic Club is particularly interesting because, despite committing his future to the club until 2035, his contract includes a release clause that could allow him to leave if an interested team meets the required conditions. That clause offers encouragement to Arsenal as they consider whether to pursue a deal. However, the Gunners are far from alone in their interest, with several of Europe’s leading sides reportedly keen to add the winger to their squads. PSG emerge as Arsenal competition One of the clubs that could challenge Arsenal for Williams is Paris Saint-Germain. The French champions are also interested in securing his services, potentially setting up competition between two clubs with the financial resources to pursue a significant transfer. According to Fichajes , PSG are serious about beating Arsenal to the Spaniard’s signature. Their reported interest adds another complication for the Gunners, who would have to compete with other major European teams if they decide to make a formal approach. Williams remains happy at Athletic Club, meaning Arsenal and their rivals cannot assume that he is already looking for a way out. His current commitment to the Spanish side makes any potential transfer dependent on both his wishes and the opportunities available to him. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) Williams’ future remains open The winger was previously keen on joining Barcelona, showing that he has considered the possibility of moving to another major club. That interest suggests he could eventually become open to a new challenge, although there is no certainty about when he might decide to leave Athletic Club. Arsenal will therefore need to remain attentive to developments surrounding his future. Their interest could become more complicated if additional clubs make their intentions clear and begin competing for his signature. If Williams eventually decides that he wants to leave Spain, the Gunners will have to contend with growing competition from some of the biggest clubs in European football. PSG’s reported interest is another reminder that securing his services would not be straightforward. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. title: Rangers Boss in Favour of Keeping Findlay Curtis at Club
summary: Derek McInnes prepares to rebuff loan offers for Scotland’s youngest World Cup star as contract negotiations loom, prioritising the dynamic winger's long-term future at Rangers this winter.
content: According to a report by media outlet Football Insider , via TransferFeed , Scottish Premiership side Rangers manager Derek McInnes is not in favour of sending out 20-year-old Scottish winger Findlay Curtis on loan during the upcoming transfer window. The boss of the Glasgow club is reportedly in favour of retaining the player. In addition to this news by Football Insider, there was also a previous one reported by TransferFeed which said that talks of a contract extension were underway between Rangers and Curtis. However, the news in question also mentioned that even after negotiating for several months, a definitive conclusion could not be reached by the parties involved. The report stated, “Curtis stated that he will leave the matter with his agent and the football club.” Born in 2006, Curtis joined the academy of Rangers in 2012, at the age of 6, and came up through the hierarchy of the club to make his first-team debut in 2025. Ten days after making his debut, he signed a contract extension with Rangers, the length of which has remained undisclosed. Since then, the player has made 22 official league appearances for the Gers and has netted 1 goal, an equaliser scored against St Mirren. He has also played 2 Scottish Cup, 4 League Cup, and 9 European games for Rangers. In 2026, Curtis joined fellow Premiership side Kilmarnock on a loan deal, where he further featured in 14 league games and scored 5 goals. In addition to his club career, the 20-year-old has also made 6 official appearances for the senior squad of the Scotland National Football Team, after playing a mere 2 games for the U-21 squad of The Tartan Army. He became Scotland’s youngest ever player to feature on the field in a World Cup when he came on as a second-half substitute during Scotland's game against Haiti at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, overtaking the record of teammate Ben Gannon-Doak. As things stand, it does not look like Findlay Curtis would be going out on loan during the upcoming January transfer window. However, if the club indeed wants to retain the player, it will have to provide him with regular playing time. A contract extension is also necessary to bind the player to the club, and a definitive conclusion to the negotiations would have to be reached quickly before other clubs show their interest and the youngster decides to leave.

title: RBL aiming to take “the next step” in Freiburg
summary: Sunday’s trip to Freiburg will pit third against fourth, with three important points and a chance to overtake SC Freiburg at stake. Having won each of their last four Bundesliga games, RBL are headi...
content: RBL aiming to take “the next step” in Freiburg Sunday’s trip to Freiburg will pit third against fourth , with three important points and a chance to overtake SC Freiburg at stake . Having won each of their last four Bundesliga games, RBL are heading into the match with plenty of confidence.We’ve gathered all the key quotes from head coach Martín Demichelis ahead of the match. RBL’s points tally against top teams “We lost away at Bayern München and Bayer 04 Leverkusen – both top teams. But, we’re a different team now. We have grown and developed in different areas. Now, we have another big game ahead of us . It’s also an opportunity for us to grow. We will travel to Freiburg with a lot of respect for our opponents , but also knowing that we want to win. It’s an opportunity for us to take a huge step forward .” SC’s strengths “They are a very consistent and hard-working side . Freiburg have a strong spirit. All their players work together on the pitch. We saw yesterday how they all celebrated the winning goal [in their Conference League tie against Twente]. That’s significant. Freiburg had rotated their squad and still managed to put in a strong performance. I have a lot of respect for that .” Reasons for David Raum’s good form “David is our captain and a very important player for us . Everyone has seen the performances he’s put in over the last weeks. I’m very happy for him. It hasn’t just been individual players that have needed some time to develop, but our team as a whole. He’s in good form and needs to continue on like this.” The importance of the next few weeks: “The tough part of the season is coming up. Not only has the weather turned cold, but we will also have many games right after another. We’re nearing the winter break and some time off. Now, we also have to think of what we can achieve come March. That’s why I’m looking forward to this phase of the season. We need every player to be at their best .” Discover more Fixtures Red Bull Arena Men's first team Tickets Fan Zone

title: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine
summary: As we near the halfway point of the season, it is safe to say that Kylian Mbappe has emerged as one of the best performers in Europe.The Frenchman has continued his goalscoring exploits at Santiago Be...
content: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine As we near the halfway point of the season, it is safe to say that Kylian Mbappe has emerged as one of the best performers in Europe. The Frenchman has continued his goalscoring exploits at Santiago Bernabeu, having racked up as many as 19 goals across all competitions. Mbappe has looked quite fit in doing so as well, as he has played in every single one of Real Madrid’s matches so far, leading the club to believe that the player is at the peak of his physical performance. Mbappe’s bid to win Ballon d’Or Mbappe has embraced the number nine role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Given the sheer productivity Mbappe has provided to the table at Real Madrid this season, it goes without saying that he will once again be one of the candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. Keeping that in mind, El Chiringuito has recently claimed that Mbappe himself is aware of the fact that he has more chances of winning the Ballon d’Or if he continues to operate as a number nine. This comes against the backdrop of earlier allegations against Mbappe that he enjoys operating more as a left-winger. In the months since, Mbappe has now fully embraced the role of a number nine, and this has been quite evident in his performances this season. Although the Frenchman still has the tendency to drift out wide, he has done so far less frequently in recent weeks and his overall combination play with other attackers has improved tenfold. Real Madrid, as a result, have dominated their opponents. Can Mbappe win the Ballon d’Or? Mbappe finished second in the 2026 Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Mbappe’s numbers so far this season make it obvious that he will be one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. However, the Frenchman’s fate will once again depend on whether or not Real Madrid can secure any silverware this season. Los Blancos have not won a single major trophy in two seasons, so breaking that rut could go a long way in boosting Mbappe’s chances of winning his first Ballon d’Or. Fortunately, with Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid now have a seasoned coach who has shown exceptional decision-making skills and has the technical know-how in competitions such as the Champions League. Mbappe, to that end, will play an integral part of Mourinho’s war machine as they look to break Real Madrid’s trophy rut during the second half of the campaign.

title: Roma inquire about Hudson-Odoi on loan
summary: Roma continues to look to the Premier League to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attacking lineup in the winter transfer window. Among the players being monitored by the Giallorossi management is C...
content: Roma inquire about Hudson-Odoi on loan Roma continues to look to the Premier League to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attacking lineup in the winter transfer window. Among the players being monitored by the Giallorossi management is Callum Hudson-Odoi, a 2000-born winger from Nottingham Forest. According to Football Insider, the English player is ready to ask for a January transfer if he doesn’t find more playing time in the coming weeks. The former Chelsea player has been marginalized by Oliver Glasner’s coaching project, partly due to the nature of the manager’s playing system. This season, Hudson-Odoi has played just 45 minutes in the Premier League, without ever starting in any competition. Roma would like to secure the winger’s services on loan, guaranteeing him the prospect of a starting spot. Hudson-Odoi’s contract with Nottingham Forest expires in 2028, and a loan move could represent a solution ahead of a possible permanent move next summer. Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens remains among the Giallorossi’s targets to strengthen their attack.

title: I said to Azaz it wasn't a good move - Hellberg
summary: Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg spoke BBC Radio Tees following their 2-0 defeat at Southampton.
content: Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg spoke BBC Radio Tees following their 2-0 defeat at Southampton. "It's a tough one to take when you [produce] that type of performance and create so many chances, but it also gives us a lot of energy and fuel to work harder," he said. "That's what the players and I love - a challenge in terms of getting disappointed. "It's always a thing that you have as a footballer and a coach to try to be a role model, be better. I know it's sometimes tough with emotions sometimes. I said to [Azaz that] it wasn't a good move. "I know players, whatever they are, are young people and sometimes get their emotions into it, which you sometimes have to have respect for. But you can handle it and should handle it in a better way." Latest Middlesbrough news, analysis and fan views

title: SC Paderborn vs. FC Schalke 04 preview: Promoted sides aim to escape relegation zone
summary: SC Paderborn and Schalke hope to end their respective poor run of results in Bundesliga when they lock horns on Saturday.SC PaderbornAfter getting knocked out of the cup with a late Deniz Undav strike...
content: SC Paderborn vs. FC Schalke 04 preview: Promoted sides aim to escape relegation zone SC Paderborn and Schalke hope to end their respective poor run of results in Bundesliga when they lock horns on Saturday. SC Paderborn After getting knocked out of the cup with a late Deniz Undav strike, Ralf Kettemann's men are winless in three league games. Draws with Borussia Mönchengladbach and Eintracht Frankfurt followed by their heaviest defeat of the early season at Bayer Leverkusen. Last season's 2. Bundesliga runners-up conceded another late goal in their last home game against Frankfurt. However, they did pick up seven of their ten points in front of their fans at Home Deluxe Arena. Team News Timur Gayret and Marcel Hoffmeier, who are both yet to feature this season, are the only guaranteed absentees for the hosts. Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant could make his first appearance, but Stuttgart loanee Laurin Ulrich is a doubt with gastrointestinal problems. Schalke 04 In contrast, Schalke are yet to even score at their home. Miron Muslić’s troops also picked up only a single point on the road since their solitary win of the season at Union Berlin on matchday 3. On average, the newly-promoted side only found the net once every two games. Although it's somehow expected considering their poor attacking numbers even in their promotion 2. Bundesliga season, Schalke would be in real danger of relegation if they don't improve their efficiency in front of goal. Team News Ron Schallenberg needs a bit more time to return to action, while Timo Becker, Maximilian Wöber, Emil Højlund and Bryan Lasme are also still on the sidelines. Head-to-head Schalke were victorious in both of their 2. Bundesliga games against Paderborn last season. Dejan Ljubicic was the star in the matchday 31 clash in Paderborn as they came from an early two-goal deficit to win 3-2 with his goals either side of the half-time break. Schalke also came from an early blow the last time the two teams met in Bundesliga for a resounding 5-1 away win in 2019. title: Schalke 04’s Loris Karius plays coy on Bayern Munich transfer links
summary: Bayern are yet to contact Karius and his agent.
content: Photo by Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images | Getty Images Loris Karius’s career hit a downward spiral following his 2017/18 Champions League Final mishap with Liverpool. After losing confidence, he had a two-year loan spell at Beşiktaş, followed by stints at Union Berlin, Newcastle United, and a return to Liverpool. Eventually, Karius landed at 2. Bundesliga side Schalke 04, where he rebuilt his confidence. Last season, he helped Die Königsblauen capture the 2. Bundesliga title and earn promotion back to Germany’s top flight for the first time since the 2022/23 season. Now, the German shot-stopper is putting together a strong campaign with Schalke—and has caught Bayern Munich’s attention. The rumors linking Karius to Bavaria caught many off guard, including the goalkeeper himself. “I heard about it just like you did,” Karius said (as reported by @iMiaSanMia ). “It’s not my place to comment on rumors, and this isn’t the right occasion for that either. I haven’t spoken to anyone. My day-to-day work here is demanding enough as it is. I feel very comfortable at Schalke and really enjoy playing here. We have a lot to look forward to in the coming weeks, so my full focus is on that.” Karius m ay not know much about Bayern’s interest right now, though he’ll have plenty to think about if Die Rekordmeister decides he’s the right veteran option to back up Jonas Urbig next season. title: Scott McTominay: Ex-Man United ace makes major decision on January Napoli exit
summary: Manchester United’s plans to immediately bring Scott McTominay back to Old Trafford appear to have hit a standstill. The midfield was at the centre of INEOS’ squad rebuild this summer, but their i...
content: Scott McTominay: Ex-Man United ace makes major decision on January Napoli exit Manchester United’s plans to immediately bring Scott McTominay back to Old Trafford appear to have hit a standstill. The midfield was at the centre of INEOS’ squad rebuild this summer, but their investment has yet to bear fruit. The Red Devils spent over €150 million on Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans, but the trio have hardly improved the team. Tielemans has been heavily involved, while Santos has been in and out of the starting XI. Baleba , meanwhile, remains sidelined with a hamstring injury after already missing the beginning of the campaign with an ankle issue. With United languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table after 11 games, new manager Mauricio Pochettino could seek further reinforcements in midfield in 2027. Recent reports suggest that the Red Devils have been offered the chance to re-sign their former academy graduate McTominay next year. McTominay has been a hit in Serie A United made the surprise decision to allow McTominay to leave Old Trafford in the summer of 2024, and it has since been proven to be a poor move. The Scottish midfielder has hit a higher gear since moving to Napoli, helping them win Serie A in his debut campaign. McTominay has continued his upward trajectory with the Italian club and has already scored 33 goals and registered 10 assists in 93 appearances across competitions. For the record, the 29-year-old, who rose through the ranks at Old Trafford, has 29 goals and eight assists in 255 appearances for the Red Devils in his career. However, with the player’s contract set to expire in 2028 and a renewal yet to materialise, he has been linked with an exit from the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that the player would prefer to return to Old Trafford rather than join Chelsea, who are also in the race. It was suggested that McTominay’s camp held a meeting with Napoli sporting director Giovanni Manna to discuss his future. However, an update on the saga has now emerged that could complicate matters for United. Scott McTominay: 2026/27 Stats Napoli · 2026/27 Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 McTominay unlikely to leave Napoli in January According to Il Mattino , as cited by Sport Witness , McTominay has no desire to leave Napoli in January, and this was communicated in the meeting with Manna. While the development certainly puts a dent in United’s plans, it does not effectively rule out a move next summer. McTominay’s renewal remains a complicated affair, especially given the finances involved. If the Scot does not sign a new deal by the end of this season, the Red Devils could have the chance to bring their prodigal son home. Overall credibility: 5/10 Why? ✅ Scott McTominay has been linked with a return to Old Trafford for ages. ✅ Napoli could be willing to let him go if a renewal fails to materialise. ⚠️ The player could wait to see how the season unfolds before making a decision about rejoining United. TPP view We believe that McTominay is unlikely to leave in the middle of the season, although much could depend how United’s midfield performs in the next few weeks. title: SCU Torreense 1-2 Celtic – It’s not ’embarrassing’, it’s a valuable victory
summary: A win is a win. It’s certainly not embarrassing as some have suggested. So stop the whining, it’s time to take a reality check…Players of Celtic celebrate after Javi Vazquez of SC Uniao Torreens...
content: SCU Torreense 1-2 Celtic – It’s not ’embarrassing’, it’s a valuable victory A win is a win. It’s certainly not embarrassing as some have suggested. So stop the whining, it’s time to take a reality check… Players of Celtic celebrate after Javi Vazquez of SC Uniao Torreense scored an own goal to make it the first goal for Celtic during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) Celtic massively boosted our chances of qualification from the Europa League group stage by recording a hard fought 2-1 win in Portugal over SCU Torreense to move up to 25th place in the Europa League group standings. It was a fixture seen by many as a potential banana skin, due to our history of away clashes in European competition, but the players dug deep and showed their determination to grind out a win on a difficult playing surface. It’s the kind of result that could prove ever vital in the long run as Martin O’Neill’s side look forward to the next away day challenge in Cyprus next month. Kasper Hogh of Celtic receives medical attention during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) Right now I’d bite your hands off for a repeat of last night’s result, even with a similar performance. However, it doesn’t seem to be enough for a section of our supporters who have still found time to be critical of the manager and players in-spite of a win on the road in European competition. The headline I saw this morning was about how Celtic’s embarrassing run in Europe continues and had I not know the score then I would have thought reading that nonsense that we had lost to the Portuguese second tier side. Fans of Celtic show their support in the stands during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) I thought it must have been a headline from one of the mainstream media sites but incredibly it was actually a fan media outlet making the point that the club has continued it’s ’embarrassing’ run of conceding in every Europa League game this season. Was it embarrassing the first time we won in Portugal by the same score as last night? I wonder…. Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) An early own goal, then a headed goal from Camilo Duran from a wonderful James Forrest cross gave Celtic a second successive victory in the Europa League, just weeks after the 3-2 win over Besiktas at Celtic Park. Admittedly it wasn’t pretty, and we looked lacklustre at times, but the main target on the night was to win, and that’s just what we did thus keeping our hopes of qualification alive. SCU Torreense may be a mid table second tier side, but they’ve already won twice in the group stages, and ran EPL side Sunderland close in the same ground that Celtic just triumphed, so they are far from the ‘pub team’ that some have been suggesting. Callum McGregor and Sam Johnstone of Celtic interact after the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) The main aim on the night was to win, and we did just that meaning we’ve now won four games on the bounce in all competitions. That breeds confidence, and just what we need as we travel to Tynecastle on Sunday to face Hearts in an ever so vital league fixture. Will it be embarrassing if we concede against Hearts but win anyway, like the last time we played them and won 3-1. Can’t remember anyone in our support being particularly embarrassed that afternoon! So instead of moaning about the performance, or being embarrassed about the failure to keep a clean sheet or any other negative issue that spring to mind, let’s take the positives and look forward with growing confidence. It’s not that difficult is it? Rant over! title: Solidity missing from Burnley - Celestini
summary: Burnley boss Fabio Celestini says it is important his side show more solidity at Millwall.
content: Burnley boss Fabio Celestini says it is important his side show more solidity at Millwall on Saturday following a damaging defeat in midweek. The Clarets' 2-0 loss at home to Birmingham City on Wednesday was seen as a new low by some fans as the club set an unwanted English record of 24 league matches without a win at home. Celestini is yet to taste victory having been appointed Burnley boss last month but will be looking to leave their dreadful home form behind them when they visit The Den. "In this moment, it is very important to be more solid and not concede so easily," Celestini told BBC Radio Lancashire. "The reaction when we went 1-0 down [against Birmingham, was good], we had three very clear chances to score. "In our situation, every goal we concede is very difficult to accept, and to come back and fight. "That's concentration, aggressivity, more inside of the game details and tactics. In the end, it's about being more brave and aggressive." After the goal we were fragile - Celestini EFL preview: Happy Potters and the deathly Hammers The midweek defeat means Burnley have won just one of their past 29 league games in both the Premier League and Championship dating back to February. Celestini's side have shipped nine goals in their past three matches but the 51-year-old says he will continue to instruct his side to play out from the back. After struggling to keep the ball in the chaotic 5-4 defeat by Cardiff, in which they led 4-1 with half an hour remaining, Burnley have registered 56% of possession in their past two matches. The Swiss coach strongly believes that keeping possession is the best solution to tightening up at the back to help his side end their current slump and climb up the table. "We need the ball. In the last two games, we've seen another Burnley with the ball," he said. "The better way not to concede a goal is to have a little bit more of the ball. When we were at Cardiff, we only had 30% of the ball. "For Cardiff, we were running 60 minutes, 65 minutes without the ball. This team cannot defend for 60 minutes, it is just impossible." title: Southend United legend awarded Freedom of the City
summary: Frankie Banks admits feeling emotional as he accepts the prestigious civic honour.
content: Frankie Banks has been involved with the Shrimpers for almost 60 years [Warren Muggleton/BBC] A legendary ex-Southend United footballer has been awarded the Freedom of the City for his lifelong service to the Shrimpers. Frankie Banks was granted the prestigious civic honour at a meeting of Southend-on-Sea City Council on Thursday evening. The 81-year-old's love affair with Roots Hall began in 1958 and has continued for almost 60 years, in the form of playing, coaching and community outreach roles. He was visibly moved as Blues supporters gave him a standing ovation from the council chamber's public gallery. "It was emotional and that's me, I'm afraid. This football club is a very important part of my life," Banks told the BBC. He was first spotted by Southend while playing football in a park near Roots Hall in 1958, and went on to make 79 appearances for the first team across two stints. Banks enjoyed two spells at Roots Hall, before spending time in the dugout [Tom Larsen-Wright/BBC] Banks signed for Hull City in 1966 but returned to the Essex coast in 1976, playing for three more years before his retirement. The steely right-back, who was born in Hull but grew up in Southend, then transitioned into a youth coach and rose to become the club's assistant manager. "The club means so much to me. They gave me the opportunity to become a professional footballer," he said. "The reason I love this club [is] the supporters… They're fantastic, really fantastic people." Banks became Southend United's first football in the community officer in 1991 and, despite retiring in 2007, has continued to serve the foundation. He still coaches multiple teams, including the Shrimpers' walking football team, and volunteers at after-school clubs. Daniel Cowan, the council's Labour leader, nominated Banks for the award and said it was "high time we made a little more noise about our unsung hero". Conservative councillor James Courtenay, who backed the motion, added: "Generations of Southenders have been touched by his work." Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below.
