title: Sunderland Have The Tools To Make Themselves Safe
summary: With their best eleven Sunderland have enough to climb the table, but they must get their recruitment right in January.
content: Two clean sheets and four points from two of the better teams in the Premier League has been a welcome reversal in what had been a slump that took us to the bottom of the table. To put it bluntly and trying not to talk like David Moyes, but if anyone had been in any doubt before our trip to Coventry a couple of weeks ago, we are at this point in a relegation battle. The points tally doesn’t lie, the goals conceded tally doesn’t lie, nor the goal difference. If anyone wants to argue that we are too good to be in one, then that is the kind of complacency which sees such supposedly ‘ too good to go down ‘ suffer the dreaded drop. However, if anything the win at home against Chelsea and the point gained from the trip to Aston Villa have shown that we do have the tools to get out of trouble. Against Chelsea we looked the better team. Villa were restricted at arms length until the last ten minutes of the game. These two performances were more like the Sunderland of last season which fought for every point. The problem this Sunderland squad has, and which has played a part in the slump that took us to the bottom of the table is that they badly miss key players when they are injured. Glaringly obvious in the case of Brian Brobbey, but just as importantly in the case of Nordi Mukiele. With his return, the defensive mistakes which had been handing goals on a plate to our opponents in the previous games came to a halt and his knack of making the vital interceptions and clearances made all the difference at the back in the last two matches. Similarly with Brian Brobbey, Sunderland are a different team with him in the team not just because of the constant threat he brings, but also the ball is held up when it is played forward to him and an attack built around him. When he isn’t in the side we struggle to find that outlet. For all the repeated criticism of our summer recruitment of players we brought in, you have to cast an eye on two players who we didn’t keep hold of for different reasons this summer – Lutsharel Geertruida and Eilezer Mayenda. Geertruida would surely have been a starter in our back four with the likes of Ballard and Mukiele out and others out of form. If we were looking for a ball player who could play in the back four, why didn’t we sign up the one who had proven he could do the job? Mayenda didn’t get much game time last season, but in my opinion – and this is just the opinion of this fan – Wilson Isidor is a player who has to be playing at his maximum to be an effective starter in the Premier League. He was used to great effect as an impact sub last season, and scored quite a few important goals, but I always felt Mayenda had the greater potential, not least because he had the ability to play a perfectly timed through ball which was simply priceless. One position where we have found a very able deputy for an injured player is in Granit Xhaka’s anchor role in midfield where Jules Ahoka has added to his growing catalogue of impressive performances. All fingers crossed that we have no more injuries to key positions in the coming weeks, that Brobbey returns soon along hopefully with Dan Ballard. Two games a week is the reality this season, and injuries are part of that reality. Regis Le Bris has actively tried to rotate his team, but factor in a World Cup hangover where we had 13 players present and an AFCON in January which no Premier League club sent more players to than Sunderland, then some of our squad have been playing football non stop since June 2025 with two major tournaments thrown in. Little wonder there have been injuries and loss of form among so many. Our January shopping list surely must be for a centre back and striker to confidently cover the key areas, because we have shown that with a strong eleven on the pitch we can compete and take points off the better teams in the Premier League, what we need is quality cover for the key areas when our best players are injured.

title: Video shows Levski fan caught giving Nazi salute before Marseille match
summary: Violent clashes marred Marseille’s Europa League win over Levski Sofia, with a filmed Nazi salute, flares, injuries and condemnation from both presidents.
content: A Levski Sofia supporter has been filmed appearing to perform a Nazi salute in the stands during Marseille’s Europa League tie against the Bulgarian side, in footage that has circulated widely online. The clip emerged amid chaotic scenes at the Stade Vélodrome , where flares and other projectiles were thrown and rival supporters clashed before and during Thursday’s match. Around 500 Levski fans were housed in the away section. About ten minutes before kick-off , several Marseille supporters ran from a home stand and breached the away enclosure, apparently targeting the Bulgarian fans. Projectiles and flares were thrown between the two groups, and further disturbances broke out during the half-time break. Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital with injuries including eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder, according to the Marseille police prefecture . Around a dozen Bulgarian fans were reportedly injured in total. Despite the disturbances, the match kicked off as scheduled, with Marseille securing a 1-0 victory over the Bulgarian side. The violence drew condemnation from French President Emmanuel Macron and his Bulgarian counterpart, Iliana Iotova . Levski Sofia coach Julio Velázquez also condemned the incidents, describing the scenes as “unacceptable for football” . The disturbances overshadowed the European fixture and renewed concerns over spectator safety at international club matches.

title: Virgil van Dijk praises ‘outstanding’ Liverpool teammates after Club Brugge win
summary: Liverpool 3-0 Club Brugge: Van Dijk Praises Champions League ResponseLiverpool did what good sides are supposed to do after a bad European result. They went away from home, kept control, took their ch...
content: Virgil van Dijk praises ‘outstanding’ Liverpool teammates after Club Brugge win Liverpool 3-0 Club Brugge: Van Dijk Praises Champions League Response Liverpool did what good sides are supposed to do after a bad European result. They went away from home, kept control, took their chances and left with a clean 3-0 win over Club Brugge in the Champions League. After the frustrating defeat to Fenerbahce, when Liverpool had led twice and still came away empty-handed, there was a need for a proper response. They got one in Belgium. Alexander Isak scored twice, Florian Wirtz added the third, and the game was effectively a demonstration of efficiency. Photo IMAGO Van Dijk Sees Right Reaction Virgil van Dijk started on the bench, which remains an unusual sight in any major Liverpool fixture, and came on for the final 15 minutes. Even without starting, his influence was obvious. He said: “I am in the game, encouraging and trying to do the type of things I usually do when I’m playing.” He added: “Off the pitch, in the warm-up, in the dressing room, I try to do all the same things but obviously you have a bit less influence.” That is the point with senior players. If they are switched on, they matter whether they play 90 minutes or 15. Alexander Isak And Florian Wirtz Deliver Club Brugge arrived in form and posed a tactical problem with aggressive man-marking all over the pitch. Liverpool handled it well. They moved the ball cleanly, punished openings and never let the game drift into chaos. Van Dijk summed it up plainly: “Overall it was a very good performance against a team who have been in form. They can be tricky to play against as they go with man-marking all over the pitch. “But our guys were so clinical, so good in the way we kept the ball. Defensively, we were solid as well. A great night.” Van Dijk reserved special praise for the younger players and the defence, saying: “The whole back line did so good, Trey [Nyoni] as well in front of them. The whole team were outstanding.” That is the real takeaway. Liverpool did not overcomplicate the evening. They corrected the mistakes of the Fenerbahce loss, stayed compact, stayed sharp and got the result they needed. As Van Dijk put it: “It was important to show a reaction away after what happened away to Fenerbahce. That was a disappointing night for us. But it’s about how you deal with what’s coming next and we’ve done that pretty well.”

title: Wanderers acquire Meadowbank stadium leasehold
summary: A Dorking Wanderers spokesperson says it will give the club "greater control over its future".
content: The Wanderers have played at Meadowbank since 2018, after it was refurbished [Getty Images] The proposed transfer of ownership of Meadowbank Stadium from Surrey County Football Association to Dorking Wanderers Football Club has been approved by Mole Valley District Council. The Wanderers have played there since 2018 after it was refurbished. It had previously been home to Dorking FC prior to their disbanding. The club said it "marks a significant milestone" following several years of hard work to reach this point. Completion of the lease arrangements remains subject to approval from the East Surrey Shadow Authority executive, according to the district council, due to local government reorganisation in the county. A club spokesperson said: "Taking responsibility for Meadowbank will give the club greater control over its future, creating opportunities to develop additional income streams and build on the stadium's role as a hub for the community." The acquisition is being supported by new co-owners Frank Villares and Debra Tucker. The pair recently bought a stake in the sixth-tier club , which was formed and is owned and managed by Marc White. The club said it has provided the funding necessary to complete the deal. Villares said: "Getting involved in Dorking Wanderers was about several things for Debra and me. "Of course we want to see success on the pitch and we're sure we will, but creating income streams for the club is crucial. "I'd like to thank everyone at Mole Valley District Council and Surrey County Football Association for their cooperation and support throughout this process. "We're looking forward to taking over the operation of Meadowbank and building on what is already a fantastic hub for the community." title: Big Ten partners with STRAUSS workwear. You won't see name on OSU game days
summary: Though unrelated, the German retailer shares a name with Dr. Richard Strauss, the former OSU physician that sexually abused hundreds of male students.
content: Workwear company STRAUSS is a new official brand partner with the Big Ten Conference, but you won't see their name on Ohio State University game days. The German retailer planted its United States headquarters in Columbus in December 2025 and on Nov. 23, the conference announced STRAUSS as its "official workwear partner." The Big Ten Conference said in a news release that STRAUSS branding will run in venues and on broadcasts all season, including bench branding, replay hoods, sideline officials' bibs, broadcast graphics and halftime shows. That branding, however, will not include an appearance in the company's domestic headquarters hometown. "The Ohio State University appreciates the Big Ten Conference’s work in developing innovative partnership opportunities that benefit the conference and its member institutions," Ohio State spokesperson Chris Booker said in an emailed statement. "However, Ohio State elected not to participate in its gameday activations in our home venues or on our sidelines or team bench areas while we are the visiting team." The company, while completely unrelated, shares a name with Dr. Richard Strauss, the former OSU physician who sexually abused hundreds of male students during his tenure as an OSU professor and team doctor from 1978 to 1998, as well as through a private off-campus practice. In 2018, former OSU wrestler Michael DiSabato came forward about the sexual abuse he suffered from Strauss, which prompted an investigation by Ohio State. More: Who was Richard Strauss? A look at the OSU doctor at the center of abuse scandal The university has paid survivors of Strauss' abuse millions of dollars in settlements in recent years. OSU's board of trustees approved a $100 million settlement for 279 of 280 individual remaining survivors at a June 3 meeting. OSU President Ravi Bellamkonda said at the meeting that the university is "grateful" to the Strauss survivors "for their courage in coming forward" and that they "will always be a part of our family and our community." Prior to the June meeting, Ohio State had reached settlements with more than half of the outstanding plaintiffs, paying out more than $61 million to 317 survivors since March 2020. The board also settled with over a dozen survivors in April 2026. A spokesperson for STRAUSS did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment Nov. 25. The Big Ten's agreement with STRAUSS includes football, volleyball and men's and women's basketball. STRAUSS was founded in 1948 as a small, family-owned company in Germany and is currently operated by brothers Henning and Steffen Strauss. According to the company, they serve a "wide range of industries" including agriculture, construction, and trades, among others. Current products on their site include toe-protected work boots, cargo pants, tool bags, high visibility jackets and more. title: Andrey Rublev shares his honest opinion about Mirra Andreeva as both a tennis player and person
summary: Andrey Rublev experienced playing alongside Mirra Andreeva at the US Open this year. Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals this year, in...
content: Andrey Rublev experienced playing alongside Mirra Andreeva at the US Open this year. Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals this year, in what has been a big breakthrough season for the Russian teenager, who has a big opportunity to become world number one at the start of the 2027 season. Although they had played an exhibition set together before, the US Open mixed doubles was the first time Andreeva and Rublev had played together in a professional setting. Andreeva and Rublev made it all the way to the semi-finals, beating two-time defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori en route, before they were beaten by eventual champions Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik . Three months on from playing with Andreeva, Rublev has revealed what he really thinks about his compatriot. Andrey Rublev backs Mirra Andreeva to achieve a lot more in her career While Andreeva has mostly had success this year, it has been a mixed season for former world number five Rublev, who dropped outside the top 20 for the first time in six years this season. Following the conclusion of his 2026 season, Rublev appeared on the The Blueprint , where he was asked about Andreeva and his experience of playing with her at the US Open this year. Rublev was full of praise for Andreeva, who he predicted would go on to achieve a lot more success in her career. “She’s such a good, joyful, bright, sunny child, incredibly talented, who has already achieved a lot and will achieve even more,” said Rublev. “I knew right away it would be a great atmosphere [US Open mixed doubles], so yeah, I think we had a blast. We also managed to show a good level of play, considering neither Mirra nor I are doubles players. It left behind some great memories that I’ll definitely cherish.” Andreeva has played with both Rublev and Daniil Medvedev , the latter of whom she lost in the first round with, in US Open mixed doubles since the event was overhauled in 2025. It will be interesting to see if Andreeva partakes in the event again in 2027 and if she reunites with either Rublev or Medvedev, or if she has a new partner.

title: Carlos Alcaraz claimed to have made a change to his game inspired by Pete Sampras ahead of 2027
summary: One of the many things that makes Carlos Alcaraz so great is his constant willingness to improve. Time and time again, he has proven himself...
content: One of the many things that makes Carlos Alcaraz so great is his constant willingness to improve. Time and time again, he has proven himself the best player in the world, having strolled to major titles or beaten his rivals with minimal fuss. Normally, that could encourage complacency, and he would have been forgiven for occasionally succumbing to that notion. However, that has yet to happen. Every time it feels like the 23-year-old simply cannot get any better, he manages it, with his current run of form no different. Carlos Alcaraz spent nearly five months sidelined due to injury this year, but even that has not prevented him from improving a key area of his game, which has now been compared to one of the sport’s greatest-ever players. Carlos Alcaraz discusses his changes to his serve Alcaraz’s serve has been a much-discussed topic for years now. After all, if a weakness had to be selected in the Spaniard’s game, this used to be it, with it more than capable, but far from a lethal weapon. Photo by Darren Carroll/USTA via Getty Images Then, last year, he served his way to US Open glory once again, reaching the final without dropping a set and getting broken just three times en route to the title. Even that was not enough, with Alcaraz reportedly having made further tweaks to this all-important shot. According to Marca , the latest changes are inspired by Pete Sampras, one of the greatest servers in tennis history, with particular focus on his raised foot movement during the motion. Samu Lopez, his coach, added: “We were looking for him to have more balance at the beginning of the movement, and that would help him to be more fluid and that he could push himself upwards.” Then, at a Davis Cup press conference earlier this week, Alcaraz directly addressed these changes, admitting: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. 🎙️Carlos on his serve improvements: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. “I don't usually look at stats during practice. I do… https://t.co/BK02s8kU8T pic.twitter.com/cT7b0gk1kt — Alcaraz Daily (@alcarazdaily) November 26, 2026 “I don’t usually look at stats during practice. I do look at them after matches, because they matter for the next round. We know how important the serve is. It’s something we’ve improved and put a lot of focus on. “Since the US Open, this is the hardest I’ve worked on my serve. Accuracy was a big part of it, and we’ve worked on it more because I’m not very tall and can’t serve like some other players.” Earlier this year, Alcaraz’s serve was accused of ‘not doing enough damage’ . It’s incredible how he has managed to combat those complaints despite spending so long out injured with a wrist injury.

title: Jack Draper’s ex-coach tipped to replace Leon Smith as Britain’s Davis Cup captain
summary: Great Britain secured a hugely impressive victory in the Davis Cup yesterday, defeating Alexander Zverev’s Germany to reach the semi-finals. It is the first time...
content: Great Britain secured a hugely impressive victory in the Davis Cup yesterday, defeating Alexander Zverev’s Germany to reach the semi-finals. It is the first time they have reached this stage in seven years, and they will now face the unenviable task of trying to topple a stacked Spain side led by Carlos Alcaraz. Regardless of what happens from here, it has been a fine campaign from Smith’s men, who have done him proud in what will be his final year as captain of the team . And, whilst his tenure is not officially over just yet, the Scotsman’s successor has already been predicted by journalist Russell Fuller and former Davis Cup star Kyle Edmund. James Trotman backed to replace Leon Smith as Great Britain’s Davis Cup captain Speaking on BBC 5 Live just last night, it was Fuller who began, insisting that there is one outstanding option to take over from Smith. “I think there is one obvious candidate,” he began, prefacing his claim by noting that there remain many former players who also have strong claims. However, Fuller then settled by stating: “I am pretty sure that the LTA are going to decide to go for James Trotman. “He has a lower profile, but he’s currently Leon Smith’s lead Davis Cup coach; he coached Jack Draper to the top four in the world and the US Open semi-finals and the Indian Wells title. I think that relationship with Draper could be crucial, because if Jack Draper can get fit again next season and is able to return to being a top 10 player once again, then getting him to commit to Davis Cup on a regular basis will be vital to Britain’s chances over the next few years.” Reacting to this prediction was Edmund, who outlined his excitement at the prospect, whilst also sharing one potential reservation over the potential appointment. He claimed: “It’s a really interesting one. I don’t doubt that James Trotman could do an amazing job because he is inside the system; he is at the LTA, he knows the players and the players know him as well. Ultimately, they know what he is about, and they trust him. “The only thing that would be different from a Davis Cup captain point of view is if Trots wants to deal with the media side of things, or the political side, where he has been a coach behind the player, and now he has got to be in front of everyone and lead the team. “If that is something that he wants to do, then that would make a lot of sense, because he has that relationship with Jack. “I spent a few years working with Trots as well, and he is a really world-class coach. He knows the game; he is very clever and smart, and it’s almost that next generation with Arthur and Jack coming through. We have always had very good doubles players, so it would be a very smart choice. “The great thing is that I think, as Great Britain, we have options with past players like Andy, Jamie, and I know Greg would want to do it. I did junior Davis Cup with Greg as well, and he is very passionate about supporting the players. “Either way, I think there is some really good options there for the team.” What did Jack Draper achieve with James Trotman as his coach? If Jack Draper were to get back to full fitness , he would likely revel in the opportunity to work with Trotman again, given all they accomplished as a player-coach partnership. And, this coach’s ability to nurture young talent and get them to perform to the best of their abilities at the highest level would surely make him a good fit for Davis Cup duties. Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images Trotman began working with Jack Draper in 2021, guiding the Brit from outside the world’s top 250 to world number four. During that period, they won three ATP titles, with Stuttgart and Vienna making way for his ultimate accomplishment: winning Indian Wells in 2025. However, in October of last year, Trotman decided to step back, opting to prioritise family life and return to his role as an LTA men’s national coach.

title: Madison Keys believes Alex Eala is going to reach a Grand Slam final in 2027
summary: Madison Keys has high hopes for Alex Eala at Grand Slam tournaments in 2027. Eala has enjoyed the best season of her career in 2026,...
content: Madison Keys has high hopes for Alex Eala at Grand Slam tournaments in 2027. Eala has enjoyed the best season of her career in 2026 , having won her first WTA title in Washington D.C. and broken into the top 20, ending the year as the world number 15. The Filipina has also achieved her best Grand Slam result this year, with Eala beating defending champion Iga Swiatek en route to reaching the fourth round of Wimbledon . Eala has never been past the fourth round of a major tournament, but 2025 Australian Open winner Keys believes she can make it all the way to a Grand Slam final next year. Madison Keys backs Alex Eala to reach a major final next year Keys was part of the Sky Sports review show of the 2026 season on both the ATP and WTA Tours, and earlier on in the show she had praised both Eala and Victoria Mboko as two young stars for the future. “Absolutely, I would throw her [Eala] into the mix,” said Keys. “She has such a unique style that really disrupts rhythm and I think she is going to be able to do that against a lot of the big hitters “…I would also say I think we can look forward to Mboko coming back, coming back from injury. She obviously was playing very, very good tennis, unfortunately had that injury that stalled her a little bit, but she’s already working on coming back and if she continues to find the form that she was playing with, we will definitely be seeing more of her.” Later on in the review show, Keys was asked to pick a surprise Grand Slam finalist for 2027 from both the WTA and ATP Tours. Keys started by choosing Roland Garros semi-finalist Jakub Mensik to go one step further next year, before backing Eala to do the same on the women’s side. “I’m going with Mensik on the men’s side,” said Keys. “I think he’s a fantastic player and I think we’re only going to see more. On the women’s side, I’m going to go with Alex Eala.” Keys was not the only person to make their prediction on this, as former world number four Tim Henman chose Arthur Fils and Iva Jovic for his two picks. “Arthur Fils,” answered Henman. “He’s still scratching the surface, I think the influence of Goran Ivanisevic has been very positive. I see big upside in his game and his attitude, so I will go with Arthur Fils.” Henman added, “Jovic. I’ve been so impressed with the way she’s played. I hadn’t seen a massive amount of her until Australia and she was into the quarter-finals. Her game, her ball-striking, her athletic ability and her attitude are brilliant and I’d love to see her in a Grand Slam final.” Former British number one Laura Robson had two different names on her mind, as she named the aforementioned Mboko and rising Belgian star Alexander Blockx. “I’m going to go Vicky Mboko for the women,” said Robson. “I know you’ve spoke about her as the season unfolded as a whole, but absolutely. And I’m going to go Alexander Blockx on the men’s side, maybe a little bit random but he’s had an incredible run this year.” Another former British WTA player turned commentator Naomi Cavaday also chose a Czech man to reach his first Grand Slam final next year, but in the form of Jiri Lehecka instead, before backing former US Open champion Bianca Andreescu to return to the big stage after her recent resurgence. “Jiri Lehecka,” picked Cavaday, before adding, “I settled on a return to the top and the return to a Grand Slam final and that’s Bianca Andreescu. She has just won 23 out of 24 matches, she’s back in the top 100 and you put her on a stadium, she’s spent two years not on stadium courts, battling it out, battling her body. She’s the healthiest she’s ever been, put her on a stadium and you see what she does.” Sky Sports commentator Jonathan Overend also had Jovic reaching her first Grand Slam next year, alongside three-time US Open semi-finalist Frances Tiafoe . “I’m going to go with someone like Tiafoe, I’ve been so impressed with his reset this year,” said Overend. “Can he keep that going next year? Made a couple semi-finals before, maybe it’s time for him to make a final…Women’s I will go for Jovic, I think she’s ready.” Grand Slam Men’s singles final result in 2026 Women’s singles final result in 2026 Australian Open Carlos Alcaraz beat Novak Djokovic, 2-6 6-2 6-3 7-5 Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka, 6-4 4-6 6-4 Roland Garros Alexander Zverev beat Flavio Cobolli, 6-1 4-6 6-4 6(5)-7 6-1 Mirra Andreeva beat Maja Chwalinska, 6-3 6-2 Wimbledon Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev, 6(7)-7 7-6(2) 6-3 6-4 Linda Noskova beat Karolina Muchova, 6-2 5-7 6-3 US Open Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton, 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka, 6-4 5-7 6-2 This year saw two first-time Grand Slam finalists from the ATP Tour, with both Flavio Cobolli and Ben Shelton finishing as the runner-up at Roland Garros and the US Open, respectively. There were even more first-time major finalists from the WTA Tour, with Mirra Andreeva , Maja Chwalinska and Linda Noskova all breaking new ground. Andreeva would beat Chwalinska for the Roland Garros title , while Noskova would also be victorious after beating her compatriot Karolina Muchova at Wimbledon.

title: Tallahassee Tennis Association Championships draw 100 players of all ages
summary: A local tournament highlights how tennis builds community and may even help you live a longer, healthier life.
content: Tennis players often joke that few sports offer the humbling experience of losing to a teenager and a retiree in the same afternoon. At the Tallahassee Tennis Association Championships, where players ranged in age from 13 to 74, that was a possibility worth considering. A total of 100 players from the Tallahassee area and South Georgia competed in the three-day tournament at Forest Meadows Tennis Complex. The Tallahassee Tennis Association (TTA) hosted the tournament in partnership with the City of Tallahassee Parks, Recreation & Neighborhood Affairs and its tennis division. Competition began Friday evening, Nov. 13, with a sold-out mixed doubles event, followed by men’s and women’s doubles on Saturday. The tournament concluded on Sunday, Nov. 15, with singles play. The competition was strong, and the weekend brought together players from different generations who might never have crossed paths on the court otherwise. Sometimes, the best thing to come out of a tournament is simply finding someone to hit with the following Saturday. That’s part of what TTA has worked to make possible since its founding in 1986. For events like the TTA Championships, the goal is to give members and others in the tennis community more chances to get on the court together, whether players are looking for a place to further develop their skills, get back into the game after time away, or find new competition after years of playing. Tournaments and recreational matches can help players feel more at home in their community, too. In a 2025 Kinetica survey , tennis players reported feeling more connected to their communities than people who took part in other sports and recreational activities. While tennis is certainly a great way to meet people and stay active, its benefits extend further than many realize. The United States Tennis Association (USTA) has called tennis the world's healthiest sport, and research suggests there's good reason for that distinction. A 2018 Mayo Clinic Proceedings study examined the relationship between participation in recreational sports and life expectancy among more than 8,500 adults. Researchers found that tennis players had an estimated 9.7-year greater life expectancy compared with sedentary participants, the largest difference among the eight sports studied. Playing tennis just three hours per week — the duration of play for many participants during Friday's mixed doubles event — can also reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease by 56% according to research in the British Journal of Sports Medicine . TTA’s efforts to bring those benefits to the local community align closely with a broader push by USTA Florida to expand access to tennis across the state and advocate for investment in public courts and opportunities to play. TTA has contributed funding toward improvements at the city’s public courts while providing annual support for the Tallahassee Tennis Challenger and other community initiatives. Whether the goal is to win a local tournament or simply find someone to hit with, Tallahassee’s public tennis courts have a place for both. The Tallahassee Tennis Association is a volunteer-led nonprofit organization dedicated to organizing, promoting, and growing the sport of tennis. Learn more about membership, events, and opportunities to play at ttatennis.org , on Instagram at @tallytennis, and on Facebook. Melissa Powell is a long-time recreational tennis player and a member of the Tallahassee Tennis Association’s board of directors. title: How the WNBA’s First Union Chief Sees Its Billion-Dollar Growth
summary: Washington described the new CBA as “monumental.”
content: The first president of the Women’s National Basketball Players Association heaped praise on the union’s ability to secure a “monumental” collective bargaining agreement, saying it solidified nearly three decades of work. “It goes back to the beginning when we thought this is about making sure the WNBA is a career and is a place for players to spend their working lives as a professional athlete,” Coquese Washington, now an assistant coach for the SMU women’s basketball team, told Front Office Sports . “That ethic, that mindset, you see in this new collective bargaining agreement.” Washington joined the WNBA in 1998, the league’s second season. After her rookie season, she helped establish the league’s first union. The players earned as little as $15,000 per season then, and the union had the far-fetched goal of turning the league into a primary source of income for players. “We were really focused on, ‘Let’s make this league stick,’” Washington said. “We have a great opportunity here to make being a professional athlete, professional women’s basketball player in this country stick.” Washington, like most players, balanced her WNBA career with other jobs. The early WNBA seasons were only around 30 games—the league will play 50 next year—and ran for only two to three months, so many would spend the majority of their years playing basketball overseas or working other jobs to make more money. Washington earned her law degree at Notre Dame and spent her first year practicing law in New York City, a background she leveraged to lead the union. She also became an assistant coach at her alma mater—which she said provided most of her income. “While most of my peers were playing overseas, I jumped into coaching in the offseason out of necessity,” Washington said. “I don’t remember what my salary was, but I definitely was making more as an assistant coach than I was as a player.” In 1999, Washington led the union in securing its first collective bargaining agreement, raising minimum salaries to $25,000, and adding maternity leave, health and dental care, and a 401(k) plan for the first time. The union made incremental gains over the next few decades, but as fan interest waned and several teams shut down, many players continued to work second or third jobs overseas while playing in the WNBA. For the first time, though, every WNBA player makes enough money to just play in the one domestic league if they prefer. After a protracted standoff with owners, the union—led by outgoing president Nneka Ogwumike— agreed to a new CBA in March that raised the minimum salary to $270,000, nearly five times more than the previous deal. (The league says the new agreement will pay players more than a billion dollars in salary over the life of the deal, which runs through 2032.) More than 30 players made over a million dollars this past season—one year after the salary cap was $1.5 million per team. The WNBPA announced Tuesday that Elizabeth Williams, who has been the union’s secretary since 2018, will take over for Ogwumike after she announced her retirement in August . Washington, who said she continues to speak with Ogwumike about the union, credits the “metrics” that have been established in recent years that show that the W is a viable business. She said the union had to use “intangible” arguments when pitching the first CBA since the league had just started. The WNBA has experienced steady growth over the past decade, but it exploded in 2024 upon the arrival of the rookie class led by Caitlin Clark as women’s sports boomed in the United States. Over the last three years, the league has consistently broken attendance and viewership records and has become a part of mainstream sports dialogue. “We can show that women’s sports and women’s basketball in particular is highly regarded in the fan space,” Washington said. The result is exactly what Washington initially envisioned in 1998: Few players spend the offseason playing abroad or working a non-basketball job. The addition of lucrative domestic offseason leagues like Unrivaled have also allowed many to stay in the U.S. year-round. Superstars like Clark, A’ja Wilson, and Angel Reese don’t even play professional basketball in the offseason, making enough money from the WNBA and endorsement opportunities. On NCAA Changes Washington finished her WNBA career in 2003, and she has spent the last 23 years working in college basketball. Her most successful years came as the head coach of Penn State, a 12-year run until 2019 that included three conference championships in the early 2010s. She recognizes that she’s had some down moments in her coaching career as well; Washington was fired by Rutgers earlier this year after four consecutive losing seasons. The NCAA has changed drastically since her years at Penn State, with the introduction of legal pay for players in 2021 and the continued evolution of revenue sharing and the transfer portal . Washington said it’s basically become professional sports. “Many programs have folks on staff, regardless of their title, with their role to really figure out and impact roster management and how do you build a roster and salary cap management and how do you utilize your resources,” Washington said. She said she even reached out to Eagles GM Howie Roseman and Chiefs head coach Andy Reid about how to manage a professional team since the NCAA was moving in that direction. However, she still refers to the changes in NCAA women’s basketball as “exciting,” especially as the sport continues to grow. And she’s hopeful she can lead a program again eventually. “I’m looking forward to continuing to impact the game as an assistant, and if the opportunity arises to do it again as a head coach, I’m absolutely open to that as well,” Washington said. title: Arsenal women's coach Renée Slegers leaves 'by mutual consent,' 18 months after Champions League win
summary: LONDON (AP) — Arsenal women's coach Renée Slegers has left the club by mutual consent, the club said Friday, 18 months after she led the team to a surprise Women’s Champions League title against Barcelona.Arsenal is sixth in the Women’s Super League without a home win, and eighth in the 18-team Women’s Champions League standings.
content: LONDON (AP) — Arsenal women's coach Renée Slegers has left the club by mutual consent, the club said Friday, 18 months after she led the team to a surprise Women’s Champions League title against Barcelona. Arsenal is sixth in the Women’s Super League without a home win, and eighth in the 18-team Women’s Champions League standings . “After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level and change is necessary,” director of women’s football Clare Wheatley said in a statement. The team trails 12 points behind league leader Chelsea and is eight points back of third place, which secures a spot in next season’s Women’s Champions League. The team has drawn all six home games. The 37-year-old Dutch coach was an assistant at Arenal when promoted to be interim head coach in October 2024 after Jonas Eidevall resigned. Slegers was given the job full-time three months later in a season that ended with a first European title. ___ See AP’s full soccer coverage here

content: Exclusive: Mandy Rose has nothing to say to Triple H about WWE release appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A few years ago, in 2022, Mandy Rose was released by WWE In Dec. 2022, after losing her NXT Women’s title to Roxanne Perez, Rose was let go the day after . Rose was one of the most popular names on the roster and enjoyed a long and notable title reign with the NXT Women’s Championship. However, WWE took swift steps and released her after her FanTime content work became public. Recently, answering a few questions from ClutchPoints, Rose opened up about her WWE run as well as shared comments about her former colleagues. When asked what she would like to ask Triple H about her previous run, exit, or a future appearance, Rose claimed that she has nothing to ask about her previous tenure. However, she is open to conversations about a future run. “That’s a good question. Honestly, I don’t really know what I would say. Like I’ve said, I had great relationships with everyone, and I feel like it was just one of those decisions they felt they had to make, whether it was to make a statement or something else. I don’t really know. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There are certain things I might have my own thoughts about, but I can’t necessarily say them. Maybe that’ll be something for my book one day! But honestly, I don’t know what I’d say to him. I don’t think there would be much to discuss unless it involved a future business opportunity. “I’m someone who understands business, and I get it. We wouldn’t need to sit there and go over everything that happened. And if you think about it, there are people who have done far worse things in that company, without naming any names, who’ve been welcomed back or forgiven. It’s almost like those situations are never even talked about again. So when I look at my situation, I think it’s nothing compared to some of the things that have gone on in that company, if you know what I mean. I’m sure you know,” she finished. However, since losing to Perez in Dec. 2022, Rose has not returned to pro-wrestling. However, she is open to it if she receives creative control. Ex-WWE star Mandy Rose comments on fellow Toxic Attraction member Jacy Jayne’s current run Further answering ClutchPoints’ questions via Casino.ca , Rose asked about her thoughts on former fellow Toxic Attraction member Jacy Jayne’s current run. While Jayne was still relatively new during her alliance with Rose, she has grown immensely since. “I’m extremely proud of Jacy Jayne, especially because I was there with her from the beginning. I always knew she had so much discipline, grit, and genuine passion for the business. I love seeing her succeed because I know how genuine she is, but I also remember there were times early on when people doubted her. Some of the producers and coaches would question her character and ask, ‘Well, who are you?’ And she’d be trying to figure that out. “We knew who she was, but it’s not always easy when you’re put into a faction with two other women who are completely different from you. The three of us were very different. I already had a bit of a name from the main roster, and Gigi [Dolin] was probably a little more established at the time, so Jacy was still trying to find herself. “Seeing how much she’s grown and the work she’s put in has been amazing because she’s always been such a hard worker. When it came to her in-ring work, she would stay until the very end of training and help everyone else. She’s always been a great worker and already had plenty of wrestling experience. “I genuinely believe she deserves the spotlight she’s getting now, and it’s so rewarding to see someone like her succeed. I still reach out to congratulate her and check in to see how she’s doing because I know she’s killing it. I’m just really happy for her,” she finished. Mandy Rose opens up about former WWE rival Roxanne Perez Rose’s last in-ring match was against Roxanne Perez, who defeated her to win her first NXT Women’s Championship. Talking about Perez’s growth, Rose added that she was definitely the next in line. “My last match was against Roxanne, and I have to say, out of all the women at that time, I’m actually grateful it worked out that way. Not only because she deserved that championship, and I’m sure she was next in line, as we would say, but also because she’s so easy to work with. We were good friends at the time, which made the whole situation a little easier. “She was just as confused as everyone else about what was going on. Nobody knew anything, and she was in shock that this huge change was suddenly happening on a random Tuesday night with absolutely no build-up. She was probably thinking, “What the—?” “But I’m really grateful it was her because we worked so well together and had already faced each other before. We had to put together this banger of a match in just a couple of hours, with all that pressure on us. “I’m really happy it was Roxanne, and it’s great to see her thriving and killing it now. I always knew she was going to do well. She’s one of the best workers I’ve ever worked with and just a genuinely amazing person,” Rose concluded. Perez right now is a part of the Judgment Day faction on the WWE roster and is a former two-time WWE NXT Women’s Champion.
